MAJAZ:v1p14/r9.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p14/r9.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p14/r9.claim: The construction implies omitted prepositions: ‘to the path’ and ‘for the path.’
MAJAZ:v1p14/r9.anchor: قال: «اهدنا الصراط المستقيم» (1/ 5) ، وإلى الصراط وللصراط.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p108/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p108/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p108/r4.claim: The transition at the worship-and-help petition is a graceful bridge because it mixes the preceding and following sections.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p108/r4.anchor: محسن التخلص في قوله فإذا قال : إياك نعبد وإياك نستعين

BIQAI-FULL:v1p28#s002/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p28#s002/r1.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p28#s002/r1.claim: Al-Harali maps al-Fatiha's verses to the seven letters: praise, lawful and forbidden, command and prohibition, clear and ambiguous, then the corresponding petitions; its opening gathers all seven.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p28#s002/r1.anchor: فالآية الأولى تشتمل على حرف الحمد السابع

BURSEVI:v1p7/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p7/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p7/r1.claim: The seeker advances from the darkness of the self to certainty that no one owns or rules except the Owner of Judgment Day, then addresses Him directly in worship.
BURSEVI:v1p7/r1.anchor: فيشاهد بعين اليقين بل يكاشف حق اليقين أن الملكولا مالك إلا مالك يوم الدين

BURSEVI:v1p7#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p7#2/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v1p7#2/r1.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says an unjust governor will be cast onto Hell's bridge; if disobedient, it breaks and he falls for fifty years.
BURSEVI:v1p7#2/r1.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم "يجاء بالوالي يوم القيامة فينبذ به على جسر جهنم

BURSEVI:v1p7#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p7#2/r2.speaker: السعدي
BURSEVI:v1p7#2/r2.claim: Sa'di's verses warn that a tyrant's injustice will not endure and leaves a lasting curse upon him.
BURSEVI:v1p7#2/r2.anchor: قال السعدي قدس سره : مهازور مندى مكن برجهان

BURSEVI:v1p7#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p7#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p7#2/r3.claim: The surah moves from signs and reflection on divine names to the endpoint of the knower's journey: direct witnessing and intimate address.
BURSEVI:v1p7#2/r3.anchor: بنى الله سبحانه أول الكلام على ما هو مبادي حال العارف من الذكر والفكر والتأمل في أسمائه

BURSEVI:v1p7#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p7#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p7#2/r4.claim: The worshipper should attend first to God, seeing worship as a noble connection to Him rather than as a deed owned by the self.
BURSEVI:v1p7#2/r4.anchor: أن العابد ينبغي أن يكون نظره إلى المعبود أولا وبالذات ومنه إلى العبادة

BURSEVI:v1p7#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p7#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p7#2/r5.claim: The intimate assurance that God is with the Prophet in the cave surpasses Moses' statement that his Lord will guide him.
BURSEVI:v1p7#2/r5.anchor: ولذلك فضل ما حكى عن حبيبه حين قال : {لا تحزن إن الله معنا}

BURSEVI:v1p7#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p7#2/r6.speaker: عكرمة
BURSEVI:v1p7#2/r6.claim: Ikrima says worship wherever used in the Qur'an means monotheism, tasbih means prayer, and qunut means obedience.
BURSEVI:v1p7#2/r6.anchor: وعن عكرمة : جميع ما ذكر في القرآن من العبادة التوحيد

BURSEVI:v1p8/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p8/r1.speaker: جبريل عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v1p8/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Gabriel told the Prophet to understand You alone we worship as placing hope in God alone.
BURSEVI:v1p8/r1.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أن جبريل عليه السلام قال للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قل يا محمد

BURSEVI:v1p8/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p8/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p8/r2.claim: The plural pronoun can include the prayer leader and those present, including recording angels, or all monotheists whose worship and needs the reciter joins.
BURSEVI:v1p8/r2.anchor: والضمير المستكن في {نعبد} وكذا في {نستعين} للقارىء ومن معه

BURSEVI:v1p8/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p8/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p8/r3.claim: This collective form helps explain why congregational prayer was prescribed: the individual folds his worship and need into the community's.
BURSEVI:v1p8/r3.anchor: أوله ولسائر الموحدين أدرج عبادته في تضاعيف عبادتهم وخلط حاجته بحاجتهم

BURSEVI:v1p8/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p8/r4.speaker: الشيخ الأكبر
BURSEVI:v1p8/r4.claim: Ibn Arabi explains the plural as gathering the human person's subtle center with its body and parts, each of which owes fitting worship to God.
BURSEVI:v1p8/r4.anchor: قال الشيخ الأكبر والمسك الأذفر قدسنا الله بسره الأطهر في كتاب "العظمة"

BURSEVI:v1p8/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p8/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p8/r5.claim: Worship belongs exclusively to God because its ultimate reverence is due only to the greatest benefactor, who creates the beneficiary and gives life.
BURSEVI:v1p8/r5.anchor: وإنما خصص العبادة به تعالى لأن العبادة نهاية التعظيم فلا تليق إلا بالمنعم في الغاية

BURSEVI:v1p9/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p9/r1.speaker: الصدر القونوي
BURSEVI:v1p9/r1.claim: Qunawi calls the servant sincere when he witnesses God as the source of action and attribution, and fully realized when that witness encompasses every state without heedlessness.
BURSEVI:v1p9/r1.anchor: كذا في تفسير الفاتحة للصدر القنوي قدس سره

BURSEVI:v1p9/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p9/r2.speaker: النجمي
BURSEVI:v1p9/r2.claim: The Najmiyya reading says the shift from speaking of God to addressing Him directly occurs when the seeker crosses the veil of owning the self.
BURSEVI:v1p9/r2.anchor: قال في "التأويلات النجمية" في قوله : {إياك نعبد} رجع إلى الخطاب من الغيبة

BURSEVI:v1p9/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p9/r3.speaker: أبو يزيد
BURSEVI:v1p9/r3.claim: Abu Yazid's unveiling gives the way to God as abandoning the self and coming to Him.
BURSEVI:v1p9/r3.anchor: كما قال أبو يزيد في بعض مكاشفاته : إلهي كيف السبيل إليك؟

BURSEVI:v1p9/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p9/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p9/r4.claim: Bursevi relays the Najmiyya interpretation that the self has four faculties, matched by four divine attributes that draw the servant toward God.
BURSEVI:v1p9/r4.anchor: فللنفس أربع صفات : أمارة ، ولوامة ، وملهمة ، ومطمئنة

BURSEVI:v1p9/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p9/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p9/r5.claim: God remembers the tranquil soul as promised in 2:152, calls it back to Him, and draws it from absence of self into witnessing its Lord's ownership.
BURSEVI:v1p9/r5.anchor: ويناديه ويخاطب نفسه {يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة}

BURSEVI:v1p10/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p10/r1.speaker: النجمي
BURSEVI:v1p10/r1.claim: A person who reaches witnessing his Lord sees the beauty of his true Owner and addresses Him as a humbled, helpless servant; some read Malik as a vocative.
BURSEVI:v1p10/r1.anchor: فيشاهد جمال مالكه ويناديه نداء عبد خاضع خاشع ذليل عاجز

BURSEVI:v1p10/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p10/r2.speaker: النجمي
BURSEVI:v1p10/r2.claim: The soul serves worldly desire, the heart serves Paradise, the spirit seeks nearness, and the secret worships God alone.
BURSEVI:v1p10/r2.anchor: واعلم أن النفس دنيوية تعبد هواها الدنيوي لقوله تعالى : {أفرءيت من اتخذ إلاهه هوااه} (الجاثية : 23) والقلب أخروي يعبد الجنة لقوله تعالى :

BURSEVI:v1p10/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p10/r3.speaker: النجمي
BURSEVI:v1p10/r3.claim: A sacred report calls sincerity a secret between God and His servant that no angel or messenger can enter.
BURSEVI:v1p10/r3.anchor: لقوله تعالى على لسان نبيه عليه السلام : "الإخلاص سر بيني وبين عبدي

BURSEVI:v1p10/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p10/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v1p10/r4.claim: A sacred report says prayer is divided between God and His servant, who receives what he asks.
BURSEVI:v1p10/r4.anchor: قسمت الصلاة بيني وبين عبدي نصفين فنصفها لي ونصفها لعبدي ولعبدي ما سأل

BURSEVI:v1p10/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p10/r5.speaker: النجمي
BURSEVI:v1p10/r5.claim: The servant approaches through praise and gratitude, while God draws him away from other attachments into divine unity and witnessing.
BURSEVI:v1p10/r5.anchor: فتقرب العبد بنصفه إلى حضرة كماله بالحمد والثناء والشكر على صفات جماله وجلاله

BURSEVI:v1p10/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p10/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p10/r6.claim: Seeking help means asking God for aid in worship, in what exceeds our power, against Satan, and in the needs of worldly and religious life.
BURSEVI:v1p10/r6.anchor: والاستعانة طلب العون ويعدى بالباء وبنفسه أي : تطلب العون على عبادتك

BURSEVI:v1p10#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p10#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p10#2/r1.claim: The two phrases mean serving and asking help from God alone.
BURSEVI:v1p10#2/r1.anchor: ثم تحقيقهما من العبد أن لا يخدم غير الله ولا يسأل إلا من الله

BURSEVI:v1p10#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p10#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p10#2/r2.claim: Placing worship before the request follows the verse endings and teaches that presenting a means before asking a need is more likely to bring an answer.
BURSEVI:v1p10#2/r2.anchor: أدعى إلى الإجابة وإياك نعبد لما أورثه العجب

BURSEVI:v1p10#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p10#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p10#2/r3.claim: Pairing worship with dependence combines pride in serving God with humility about needing His aid, and removes worshipper's conceit.
BURSEVI:v1p10#2/r3.anchor: إياك نعبد لما أورثه العجب أردف إياك نستعين إزالة له وإفناء للنخوة

BURSEVI:v1p10#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p10#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p10#2/r4.claim: The pairing expresses Sunni teaching: the servant performs actions while God creates and grants success, rejecting both Jabriyya denial of human action and Mu'tazila denial of divine aid.
BURSEVI:v1p10#2/r4.anchor: إذ فيه إثبات الفعل من العبد والتوفيق من الله كالخلق

BURSEVI:v1p10#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p10#2/r5.speaker: سفيان الثوري
BURSEVI:v1p10#2/r5.claim: Sufyan fainted while leading prayer at this verse, fearing that his appeal to God alone would be contradicted by seeking physicians' or rulers' doors.
BURSEVI:v1p10#2/r5.anchor: حكي عن سفيان الثوري رحمه الله أنه أم قوما في صلاة المغرب فلما قال : {إياك نعبد

BURSEVI:v1p10#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p10#2/r6.speaker: الخليل عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v1p10#2/r6.claim: Abraham declined Gabriel's offer of help in the catapult, saying God already knew his state; the author likens his own restraint and reliance to Abraham's.
BURSEVI:v1p10#2/r6.anchor: اقتداء بالخليل عليه السلام في قيد النمرود حيث قال له جبريل

SULAMI:v1p36#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p36#4/r1.speaker: author
SULAMI:v1p36#4/r1.claim: Worship is sincere action without attachments or compensation; one seeks God's help to remain in that state because worship is through Him, not oneself.
SULAMI:v1p36#4/r1.anchor: وأيضا إياك نعبد بالعمل الخالص أي : إياك نعبد بقطع العلائق والأعواض

SULAMI:v1p36#4/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p36#4/r2.speaker: author
SULAMI:v1p36#4/r2.claim: The paired clauses can mean worship with sincerity and seeking help to unveil one's secrets.
SULAMI:v1p36#4/r2.anchor: إياك نعبد بالإخلاص وإياك نستعين على المكاشفة لأسرارنا

SULAMI:v1p36#4/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p36#4/r3.speaker: author
SULAMI:v1p36#4/r3.claim: Another reading pairs worship through intention with divine aid in aspiration.
SULAMI:v1p36#4/r3.anchor: إياك نعبد بالإرادة وإياك نستعين عليه بالهمة

SULAMI:v1p36#4/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p36#4/r4.speaker: author
SULAMI:v1p36#4/r4.claim: One worships through knowledge and seeks help for gnosis.
SULAMI:v1p36#4/r4.anchor: إياك نعبد بالعلم وإياك نستعين عليه بالمعرفة

SULAMI:v1p36#4/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p36#4/r5.speaker: author
SULAMI:v1p36#4/r5.claim: True worship recognizes that God enabled it; divine help is needed for its acceptance and correction.
SULAMI:v1p36#4/r5.anchor: إياك نعبد عبادة من يعلم أنه بتوفيقك وتيسيرك قد عبدك

SULAMI:v1p36#4/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p36#4/r6.speaker: author
SULAMI:v1p36#4/r6.claim: Worship is performed by God's command and depends on His grace.
SULAMI:v1p36#4/r6.anchor: إياك نعبد بأمرك وإياك نستعين عليها بفضلك

SULAMI:v1p36#4/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p36#4/r7.speaker: author
SULAMI:v1p36#4/r7.claim: The servant asks to be freed from spiritual claims and carried from them into the gardens of realities.
SULAMI:v1p36#4/r7.anchor: إياك نعبد بالدعاوى وإياك نستعين أن تسقط عنا الدعاوى

SULAMI:v1p36#4/r8.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p36#4/r8.speaker: author
SULAMI:v1p36#4/r8.claim: Worship is outward and reliance inward; repeating You removes the perception that either worship or reliance belongs to the self.
SULAMI:v1p36#4/r8.anchor: إياك نعبد ظاهرا وإياك نستعين عليها باطنا ، إياك نعبد فأسقط

SULAMI:v1p36#4/r9.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p36#4/r9.speaker: author
SULAMI:v1p36#4/r9.claim: The prayer asks God to qualify, purify, and aid worshippers while protecting them from self-regard about their worship.
SULAMI:v1p36#4/r9.anchor: فأهلنا لعبادتك وإياك نستعين فلا تحرمنا معونتك

SULAMI:v1p36#4/r10.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p36#4/r10.speaker: author
SULAMI:v1p36#4/r10.claim: Worship is by direct witnessing, while divine help is sought for affliction.
SULAMI:v1p36#4/r10.anchor: إياك نعبد على المشاهدة ، وإياك نستعين على النازلة

SULAMI:v1p36#4/r11.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p36#4/r11.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v1p36#4/r11.claim: Those granted knowledge of servanthood first devote worship to God, then recognize that He alone enables and helps them give thanks for worship.
SULAMI:v1p36#4/r11.anchor: قال الجنيد : إن الله عز وجل خص قوما بمعرفة عبوديته

SULAMI:v1p36#4/r12.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p36#4/r12.speaker: القاسم
SULAMI:v1p36#4/r12.claim: Worship is by divine enablement, and help is sought to thank God for enabling it.
SULAMI:v1p36#4/r12.anchor: وقال القاسم : إياك نعبد بالتوفيق ، وإياك نستعين على شكر ما وفقتنا له

SULAMI:v1p36#4/r13.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p36#4/r13.speaker: أبو جعفر الفرغلي
SULAMI:v1p36#4/r13.claim: Whoever affirms the verse is absolved of both determinism and the opposing doctrine of human self-determination.
SULAMI:v1p36#4/r13.anchor: سمعت أبا جعفر الفرغلي يقول : من أقر بإياك نعبد وإياك نستعين فقد برىء من الجبر والقدر

IBNABIHATIM:v1p29#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p29#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p29#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says Gabriel commanded Muhammad to say that God alone is worshipped, unified, feared, and hoped in, with no other lord.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p29#2/r1.anchor: عن الضحاك ، عن ابن عباس قال : قال جبريل عليه السلام : قل يا محمد ، وهو جماع اياك ننعبد

IBNABIHATIM:v1p29#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p29#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v1p29#2/r2.claim: Qatada says the wording itself indicates God's exclusive claim: worshippers should say it as instructed.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p29#2/r2.anchor: عن حسين بن واقد عن مطر ، عن قتادة اياك نعبد واياك نستعين دل على نفسه انه كذا فقولوا

IBNABIHATIM:v1p29#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p29#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v1p29#2/r3.claim: Qatada says God commands sincere worship and asks people to seek His help in their affairs.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p29#2/r3.anchor: عن قتادة قي قوله : اياك نعبد واياك نستعين قال : يامركم ان تخلصوا له العبادة ، وان تستعينوه على امركم

IBNABIHATIM:v1p29#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p29#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p29#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says help is sought for obedience to God and for all one's affairs.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p29#2/r4.anchor: عن الضحاك ، عن ابن عباس : واياك نستعين قال : على طاعتك وعلى امورنا كلها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r1.claim: He reads the sura's annexation to Fatihat al-Kitab as descriptive: it means a sura characterized as the Book's opening, with no separate title needed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r1.anchor: إضافة السورة إلى فاتحة الكتاب من إضافة الموصوف إلى الصفة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r2.claim: By contrast, Fatihat al-Kitab is a true annexation: al-Kitab here means the remainder of the Book apart from the sura called the Opening.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r2.anchor: إضافة فاتحة إلى الكتاب فإضافة حقيقية باعتبار أن المراد من الكتاب بقيته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r3.claim: The names Umm al-Qur'an and Umm al-Kitab are established in the Sunna; “mother” denotes a thing's origin and source.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r3.anchor: وأما تسميتها أم القرآن وأم الكتاب فقد ثبتت في السنة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r4.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r4.claim: A report in Sahih al-Bukhari says Abu Sa'id al-Khudri recited Umm al-Qur'an over a person suffering from a sting as a healing prayer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r4.anchor: أن أبا سعيد الخدري رقى ملدوغا فجعل يقرأ عليه بأم القرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r5.speaker: النبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r5.claim: A sound hadith calls a prayer without Umm al-Qur'an deficient.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r5.anchor: كل صلاة لم يقرأ فيها بأم القرآن فهي خداج

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r6.claim: One explanation of Umm al-Qur'an is that it begins and opens the Qur'an, making it like its origin.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r6.anchor: أنها مبدؤه ومفتتحه فكأنها أصله ومنشؤه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r7.claim: A second explanation is that the sura gathers the Qur'an's three main aims: praise, commands and prohibitions, and promise and warning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r7.anchor: تشتمل محتوياتها على أنواع مقاصد القرآن وهي ثلاثة أنواع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r9.claim: The worship clause represents the Qur'an's commands and prohibitions; the path clause represents promise and warning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r9.anchor: والأوامر والنواهي من قوله : { إياك نعبد } ، والوعد والوعيد من قوله : { صراط الذين } إلى آخرها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r11.claim: The sura's three aims together represent the Qur'an's original purposes, while its remaining material elaborates them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r11.anchor: فهذه هي أنواع مقاصد القرآن كله ، وغيرها تكملات لها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r12.claim: He also supports the sura's comprehensiveness by citing the sound report that al-Ikhlas counts as a third of the Qur'an because all its wording praises God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r12.anchor: وقد يؤيد هذا الوجه بما ورد في الصحيح في : { قل هو الله أحد }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p133/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p133/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p133/r1.claim: A third explanation of Umm al-Qur'an is that it contains the Qur'an's theoretical wisdom and practical rulings, including theology, prophecy, admonition, worship, transactions, morals, and law.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p133/r1.anchor: تشتمل معانيها على جملة معاني القرآن من الحكم النظرية والأحكام العملية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p133/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p133/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p133/r6.claim: “You alone we worship” gathers the meaning of religion and sacred law, while “You alone we ask for help” gathers sincerity in deeds.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p133/r6.anchor: يجمع معنى الديانة والشريعة ، و { إياك نستعين } يجمع معنى الإخلاص لله في الأعمال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p133/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p133/r7.speaker: عز الدين بن عبد السلام
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p133/r7.claim: Ibn Abd al-Salam divides the path to God into outward bodily practice (Sharia) and inward heart practice (Haqiqa), both aiming at servitude as required of the responsible person.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p133/r7.anchor: قال عز الدين بن عبد السلام في كتابه ( حل الرموز ومفاتيح الكنوز )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p133/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p133/r8.speaker: عز الدين بن عبد السلام
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p133/r8.claim: Ibn Abd al-Salam identifies “You alone we worship” with Sharia and “You alone we ask for help” with Haqiqa.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p133/r8.anchor: فإياك نعبد شريعة وإياك نستعين حقيقة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p133/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p133/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p133/r11.claim: Taken explicitly and by implication, the sura gives a general outline of the Qur'an's aims and prompts readers to seek their fuller detail as able.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p133/r11.anchor: يحصل من معاني الفاتحة تصريحا وتضمنا علم إجمالي بما حواه القرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p133/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p133/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p133/r12.claim: Requiring al-Fatiha in every rak'ah preserves recollection of the Qur'an's purposes contained within it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p133/r12.anchor: فرضت قراءة الفاتحة في كل ركعة من الصلاة حرصا على التذكر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r10.speaker: النبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r10.claim: A hadith in both Sahihs from Abu Hurayra has God divide prayer between Himself and the servant, answering each portion of al-Fatiha and granting the servant's request.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r10.anchor: قسمت الصلاة نصفين بيني وبين عبدي فنصفها لي ونصفها لعبدي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r11.claim: The verse division differs by region: Medinans exclude the basmala and count “those You favored” as a verse; Meccans and Kufans include the basmala and combine that phrase with its verse; Hasan counts both separately.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r11.anchor: فعند أهل المدينة لا تعد البسملة آية وتعد : { أنعمت عليهم } آية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r1.claim: Important guidance requires preparing listeners, stirring their attention, and removing stubbornness, false assumptions, and satanic impulses that block learning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r1.anchor: ما بقي يخالجها العناد والبهتان ، وتخامر رشدها نزغات الشيطان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r2.claim: Placed first by the Prophet's instruction, al-Fatiha trains readers in inner purification through its supplication from “You alone we worship” onward.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r2.anchor: نبه الله تعالى قراء كتابه وفاتحي مصحفه إلى أصول هذه التزكية النفسية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r3.claim: The declaration of worship frees the supplicant from denial and idolatry.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r3.anchor: أولها التخلية عن التعطيل والشرك بما تضمنه { إياك نعبد }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r4.claim: Asking God alone for help rejects imagined self-sufficiency and admits human beings have no power before His greatness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r4.anchor: التخلي عن خواطر الاستغناء عنه بالتبرىء من الحول والقوة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r10.claim: As a Qur'anic preface, al-Fatiha models an Arabic literary opening that improves understanding and attentive reception.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r10.anchor: وهذا الأسلوب له شأن عظيم في صناعة الأدب العربي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p153/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p153/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p153/r5.claim: Because the Qur'an guides people and reforms both worldly and future life, listeners must prepare by removing stubbornness, error, and low impulses before receiving its wisdom.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p153/r5.anchor: فلا مناص لها قبل استقبال تلك الحكمة والنظر من الاتسام بميسم الفضيلة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p153/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p153/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p153/r7.claim: The declaration of exclusive worship purges associationism.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p153/r7.anchor: وعن الإشراك بما تضمنه { إياك نعبد وإياك نستعين }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p153/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p153/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p153/r10.claim: These aims help explain why al-Fatiha is called Umm al-Qur'an.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p153/r10.anchor: ولأجل هذا سميت هاته السورة أم القرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p177#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p177#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p177#2/r1.claim: After completing praise, the speaker turns to God in an initial independent address, showing exclusive devotion through worship and seeking help in recognition of God's due.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p177#2/r1.anchor: انتقالا من الإفصاح عن حق الرب إلى إظهار مراعة ما يقتضيه حقه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p177#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p177#2/r2.speaker: حسان بن ثابت
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p177#2/r2.claim: Al-Isfahani transmits Hassan's story of a poet calling out praise around al-Numan's pavilion; al-Numan recognized al-Nabigha and admitted him, illustrating the Arabic custom of praising a ruler before addressing him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p177#2/r2.anchor: روى أبو الفرج الأصفهاني عن حسان بن ثابت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p177#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p177#2/r3.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p177#2/r3.claim: Most rhetoricians define iltifat as shifting the same referent among first, second, and third person; al-Sakkaki instead defines it as choosing a person-form other than the contextually apt one.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p177#2/r3.anchor: أحدهما رأي من عدا السكاكي من أئمة البلاغة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p177#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p177#2/r4.speaker: السكاكي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p177#2/r4.claim: Al-Sakkaki counts apostrophe to one's own heart as iltifat, whereas other rhetoricians classify Alqama's example as tajrid; Ibn Ashur explains the difference in their definitions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p177#2/r4.anchor: فهذا ليس بالتفات عند الجمهور وهو معدود من الالتفات عند السكاكي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p177#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p177#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p177#2/r5.claim: A proper name counts as third-person reference on both definitions, so the turn from God's name and attributes to إياك is iltifat for both schools.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p177#2/r5.anchor: أن الاسم الظاهر معتبر من قبيل الغائب على كلا الرأيين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p179/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p179/r1.speaker: السكاكي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p179/r1.claim: Iltifat refreshes listeners by varying expression, like varying flavors for guests; rhetoricians also find additional contextual subtleties in individual shifts.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p179/r1.anchor: بتجديد الأسلوب تجديد نشاط السامع كي لا يمل من إعادة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p179/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p179/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p179/r2.claim: Here the worshipper, carried to the limit of reflection by praising God's greatness, imagines himself in the divine presence and turns to address Him directly.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p179/r2.anchor: فتخيل نفسه في حضرة الربوبية فخاطب ربه بالإقبال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p179/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p179/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p179/r3.claim: Muhammad ibn Bashir's poem illustrates the reverse shift: after addressing himself, the speaker describes his deficient judgment in third person, as if the self had receded from view.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p179/r3.anchor: فالتفت من خطابه إلى التعبير عنه بضمير الغيبة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p179/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p179/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p179/r4.claim: The Quran's shift in 29:23 stigmatizes the disbelievers by naming their rejection of God's signs before reporting their despair of His mercy.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p179/r4.anchor: بأنهم كفروا بآيات صاحب ذلك الاسم الجليل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p179/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p179/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p179/r5.claim: The address also moves naturally from praise into supplication, which requires direct address and leads into the request guide us to the path.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p179/r5.anchor: أنه تخلص من الثناء إلى الدعاء ولا شك أن الدعاء يقتضي الخطاب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p179/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p179/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p179/r6.claim: The shift from third person into first person is natural because the first person is the normal form for things attributed to the speaker.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p179/r6.anchor: إذ هو الأصل في التعبير عن الأشياء المضافة إلى ذات المتكلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p179#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p179#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p179#2/r1.claim: إياك is an accusative independent pronoun; the stronger analysis treats إيا as a support for a separated pronoun, explaining the attached forms and its use in warnings when the verb is omitted.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p179#2/r1.anchor: والأظهر أن كلمة إيا جعلت ليعتمد عليها الضمير عند انفصاله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p179#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p179#2/r2.speaker: النحاة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p179#2/r2.claim: Grammarians offer alternatives: إيا alone is the pronoun and its endings reinforce it; إيا is the pronoun and the following letters clarify it; or it is a noun annexed to pronouns.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p179#2/r2.anchor: ومن النحاة من جعل ( إيا ) ضميرا منفصلا ملازما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p179#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p179#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p179#2/r3.claim: Ordinary العبادة is submissive or exceptionally reverent action; obedience is a figurative extension. In religious usage it is whatever pleases God through submission, compliance, and avoidance, including all law.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p179#2/r3.anchor: وأما إطلاقها على الطاعة فهو مجاز

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p179#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p179#2/r4.speaker: الرازي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p179#2/r4.claim: Al-Razi says worship means honoring God's commands and caring for creation, the shared purpose of revealed laws despite their differing forms and details.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p179#2/r4.anchor: العبادة تعظيم أمر الله والشفقة على الخلق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p179#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p179#2/r5.speaker: الصوفية
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p179#2/r5.claim: Sufis distinguish worship, doing what pleases God, from servitude, accepting what God does; other definitions describe servitude as keeping promises and limits, contentment, and patience.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p180/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p180/r1.speaker: الفخر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p180/r1.claim: Fakhr al-Razi ranks worship for reward or fear as low, worship for the honor of belonging to God as intermediate, and worship because God alone deserves it as highest, calling the last servitude.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p180/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p180/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p180/r2.claim: Ibn Ashur rejects devaluing reward-and-fear worship as a Sufi excess: Islam repeatedly encourages it and it is the practice of most believers, though rare people may reach higher motives.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p180/r2.anchor: قد غلب عليه فيه اصطلاح غلاة الصوفية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p180/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p180/r3.speaker: رسول الله
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p180/r3.claim: Asked why he labored in worship after forgiveness, the Prophet answered that he should be a grateful servant; Ibn Ashur cites this as worship motivated by gratitude, not hope or fear.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p182/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p182/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p182/r1.claim: Worship trains individual and social perfection: it recalls God and recompense, disciplines the self, sustains just relations, and keeps thought on the Creator; this explains the purpose of creation stated in 51:56.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p182/r1.anchor: ظهر أن العبادة هي طريق الكمال الذاتي والاجتماعي مبدأ ونهاية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p182/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p182/r2.speaker: ابن سينا
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p182/r2.claim: Ibn Sina explains that people need one another, so justice must be maintained by revealed law and a rightful lawgiver; knowledge of the one who rewards good and evil needs repeated worship to preserve it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p182/r2.anchor: ففرضت عليهم العبادة المذكرة للمعبود ، وكررت عليهم ليستحفظ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p182#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p182#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p182#2/r1.claim: Worship arises from reverence through love or fear; love is higher because it pleases the worshipper and entails fear of displeasing the beloved, as the cited poems and 3:31 express.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p182#2/r1.anchor: وأهمه ما كان عن محبة لأنه يرضي نفس فاعله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p182#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p182#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p182#2/r2.claim: Love-based worship underlies revealed religions and even idolaters' devotion to their gods; some instead worship from fear alone, such as Manicheans who worship Ahriman to avert harm.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p182#2/r2.anchor: ومن الأمم من عبدت عن خوف دون محبة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p182#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p182#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p182#2/r3.claim: The fronted object in إياك نعبد gives true exclusivity: believers reciting this praise worship God alone.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p182#2/r3.anchor: حصر حقيقي لأن المؤمنين الملقنين لهذا الحمد لا يعبدون إلا الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p182#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p182#2/r4.speaker: ابن الحاجب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p182#2/r4.claim: Ibn al-Hajib argues that fronting the object in إياك نعبد marks emphasis only, not exclusivity, and says the cited exclusivity proofs are weak.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p182#2/r4.anchor: وزعم ابن الحاجب في ( إيضاح المفصل )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p183/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p183/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p183/r1.claim: Ibn Ashur says Ibn al-Hajib's appeal to فاعبد الله is unconvincing because wording must be judged in its particular context, not treated as equivalent in every passage.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p183/r1.anchor: لا يليق بمقامه العلمي إذ لا يظن أن محامل الكلام متماثلة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p183/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p183/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p183/r2.claim: وإياك نستعين coordinates with إياك نعبد; the clauses are not separated as in a sequence of petitions because the worshippers emphasize both acts in the same exclusive commitment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p183/r2.anchor: للإشارة إلى خطور الفعلين جميعا في إرادة المتكلمين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p183/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p183/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p183/r3.claim: Seeking help means asking another to ease a difficult act through tools, physical cooperation, teaching, advice, or money; seeking God's help concerns what a person cannot achieve alone while still exerting their own ability.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p183/r3.anchor: والاستعانة طلب العون . والعون والإعانة تسهيل فعل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p183/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p183/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p183/r4.claim: Scholars divide divine aid into essential capacity and means required for an act, and additional facilitation; the latter is sometimes called tawfiq, which with capacity means creating ability and desire to obey.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p183/r4.anchor: فتنقسم قسمين ضرورية أي ما يتوقف الفعل عليها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p183/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p183/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p183/r5.claim: The general object of seeking aid is omitted to include all important acts, especially receiving religion and disciplining the soul; the needed knowledge, guidance, laws, and sciences also come from God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p183/r5.anchor: والمقصود هنا الاستعانة على الأفعال المهمة كلها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p185/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p185/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p185/r1.claim: Fronting إياك نستعين gives hyperbolic, claimative exclusivity: people do help one another, but great matters beyond human aid are sought from God alone. This indirectly rebukes polytheists who worship other beings or use them as intermediaries.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p185/r1.anchor: حصر ادعائي للمبالغة لعدم الاعتداد بالاستعانات المتعارفة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p185/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p185/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p185/r2.claim: The indirect rebuke fits those who worship celestial bodies, animals, idols, or other gods and seek their aid as intermediaries to God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p185/r2.anchor: فهؤلاء جمعوا العبادة والاستعانة بهم لأن جعلهم وسيلة إلى الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p185/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p185/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p185/r3.claim: The Prophet taught Ibn Abbas: when asking, ask God; when seeking help, seek God's help. The grandfather commentator says omitting an explicit exclusivity formula implies that requesting help properly admits no partner, and an explicit restriction would be redundant.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p185/r3.anchor: إذا سألت فاسأل الله وإذا استعنت فاستعن بالله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p185#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p185#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p185#2/r1.claim: The opening of revelation and legislation needed an emphatic exclusive claim, which also rebukes idolatry; conditional answers to any request carry the same restriction.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p185#2/r1.anchor: مقام هذه الآية فمقام مفتتح الوحي والتشريع واستهلال الوعظ والتقريع ، فناسب تأكيد الحكم بالقصر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p185#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p185#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p185#2/r2.claim: The exclusivity repudiates polytheists who sought help from their gods, including drawing lots with arrows placed beside idols.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p185#2/r2.anchor: كانوا يستعينون بآلهتهم . ومن ذلك الاستقسام بالأزلام الموضوعة عند الآلهة والأصنام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p185#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p185#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p185#2/r3.claim: The plural pronouns include the reciter with the believers; their collective praise signals Muslim strength and is more eloquent than a solitary confession.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p185#2/r3.anchor: وضميرا { نعبد ونستعين } يعودان إلى تالي السورة ذاكرا معه جماعة المؤمنين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p185#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p185#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p185#2/r4.claim: The communal voice keeps praising God during the move from praise to intimate address, like al-Nābigha's enumeration of nations to suggest al-Nuʿmān's greatness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p185#2/r4.anchor:
قول النابغة في رثاء النعمان بن الحارث الغساني :
قعودا له غسان يرجون أوبة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p185#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p185#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p185#2/r5.claim: Worship precedes aid because it draws near to God, aid serves the creature and can assist worship, and the order also suits the surah's cadence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p185#2/r5.anchor: العبادة تقرب للخالق تعالى فهي أجدر بالتقديم في المناجاة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p186/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p186/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p186/r1.claim: Repeating إياك marks distinct restrictions: worship is truly exclusive to God, while aid is only rhetorically exclusive because people may help one another; ultimate aid belongs to God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p186/r1.anchor: فالحصر في { إياك نعبد } حقيقي والقصر في { إياك نستعين ادعائي فإن المسلم قد يستعين غير

TUSTARI:1:5/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:1:5/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:1:5/r1.claim: Worship means submission, humility, confession of God's lordship, affirming His unity, and serving Him; the word servant derives from this sense.
TUSTARI:1:5/r1.anchor: أي نخضع ونذل ونعترف بربوبيتك ونوحدك ونخدمك، ومنه اشتق اسم العبد.

TUSTARI:1:5/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:1:5/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:1:5/r2.claim: Seeking help asks God to enable sincere fulfillment of His obligations, since will, knowledge, sincerity, and all power depend on His support.
TUSTARI:1:5/r2.anchor: ولن نقدر على ذلك إلا بالمعونة والتسديد لنا منك، إذ لا حول لنا ولا قوة إلا من عندك.

TUSTARI:1:5/r3.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:1:5/r3.speaker: author
TUSTARI:1:5/r3.claim: Asking for guidance requests an increase in divine support and empowerment, even after God has already guided the servant.
TUSTARI:1:5/r3.anchor:
ولكن طلب الزيادة منه كما قال:
ولدينا مزيد
[ق:35] فكان معنى قوله: " اهدنا ": أمددنا منك بالمعونة والتمكين.

TUSTARI:1:5/r4.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:1:5/r4.speaker: author
TUSTARI:1:5/r4.claim: Another sense of guidance is direction to Islam, the path to God, through divine insight, since guidance comes only from Him.
TUSTARI:1:5/r4.anchor: معناه أرشدنا إلى دين الإسلام الذي هو الطريق إليك بمعونة منك، وهي البصيرة،

TUSTARI:1:5/r5.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:1:5/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TUSTARI:1:5/r5.claim: A report from Thawban says prayer is divided between God and the servant: praise and glorification are for God, then the servant receives what he asks.
TUSTARI:1:5/r5.anchor:
عن ثوبان قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:
" يقول الله عز وجل: قسمت الصلاة بيني وبين عبدي

TUSTARI:1:5/r6.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:1:5/r6.speaker: author
TUSTARI:1:5/r6.claim: Sahl explains God's saying He is praised as describing Him through abundant beneficence and generosity.
TUSTARI:1:5/r6.anchor: قال سهل: معنى قوله: " مجدني عبدي " أي وصفني بكثرة الإحسان والإنعام،

TUSTARI:1:5/r7.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:1:5/r7.speaker: مجاهد
TUSTARI:1:5/r7.claim: Mujahid reports that Amin is one of God's names.
TUSTARI:1:5/r7.anchor: وروي عن مجاهد أنه قال: آمين اسم من أسماء الله تعالى،

TUSTARI:1:5/r8.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:1:5/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
TUSTARI:1:5/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says Christians envy Muslims for saying Amin.
TUSTARI:1:5/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما: ما حسدتكم النصارى على شيء كما حسدتكم على قولكم آمين.

TUSTARI:1:5/r9.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:1:5/r9.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TUSTARI:1:5/r9.claim: A report from Jabir urges steadfastness despite its difficulty, calls prayer the best deed, and says saying Amin after the imam brings God's approval, accepted prayer, and answered supplication.
TUSTARI:1:5/r9.anchor:
عن جابر بن عبدالله رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:
" استقيموا ولن تحصوا، واعلموا أن خير أعمالكم الصلاة،

TUSTARI:1:5#2/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:1:5#2/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TUSTARI:1:5#2/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that when the imam says the final phrase, worshippers should say Amin; agreement with the angels' Amin brings forgiveness for past sins.
TUSTARI:1:5#2/r1.anchor: إذا قال الإمام: " ولا الضالين " قولوا: آمين، فإن الملائكة يقولون آمين،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p71#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p71#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p71#2/r6.claim: Saying “You alone we worship” is a believer's confession of God's lordship, submission, and true worship, in contrast to those who worship idols.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p71#2/r6.anchor: نطق المؤمن به إقرار بالربوبية وتذلل وتحقيق لعبادة الله، إذ سائر الناس يعبدون سواه من أصنام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p71#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p71#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p71#2/r7.claim: The object is fronted to give it emphasis and priority, a normal Arabic ordering when the object is most important.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p71#2/r7.anchor: وقدم المفعول على الفعل اهتماما، وشأن العرب تقديم الأهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p72/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p72/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p72/r1.claim: An anecdote illustrates fronting for emphasis: an insulted man answers “You I ignore” after being told “You are the one I mean.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p72/r1.anchor: «وعنك أعرض» فقدما الأهم. وقرأ الفضل الرقاشي:

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p72/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p72/r2.speaker: الفضل الرقاشي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p72/r2.claim: Al-Fadl al-Raqqashi reads iyyaka with fatḥa on the initial hamza, a well-known dialect form.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p72/r2.anchor: وقرأ الفضل الرقاشي: «أياك» بفتح الهمزة، وهي لغة مشهورة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p72/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p72/r3.speaker: عمرو بن فائد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p72/r3.claim: ʿAmr ibn Faʾid reads iyyaka with kasra on the hamza and a light yāʾ to avoid a doubled yāʾ after kasra.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p72/r3.anchor: وقرأ عمرو بن فائد: «إياك» بكسر الهمزة وتخفيف الياء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p72/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p72/r4.speaker: أبو السوار الغنوي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p72/r4.claim: Abu al-Sawwar al-Ghanawi reads hiyyaka with hāʾ, another dialect form.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p72/r4.anchor: وقرأ أبو السوار الغنوي: «هياك نعبد وهياك نستعين» بالهاء، وهي لغة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p72/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p72/r5.speaker: الخليل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p72/r5.claim: Al-Khalil analyzes iyyā as an independent pronoun compounded with the following element for clarification rather than identification.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p72/r5.anchor: فقال الخليل: إيا اسم مضمر أضيف إلى ما بعده للبيان لا للتعريف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p72/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p72/r6.speaker: المبرد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p72/r6.claim: Al-Mubarrad calls iyyā an indefinite pronoun made specific, not definite, by what follows.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p72/r6.anchor: وقال المبرد: إيا اسم مبهم أضيف للتخصيص لا للتعريف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p72/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p72/r7.speaker: بعض الكوفيين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p72/r7.claim: Some Kufans treat the complete iyyāka as the pronoun, an exceptional one whose ending changes.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p72/r7.anchor: عن بعض الكوفيين أن إياك بكماله اسم مضمر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p72/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p72/r8.speaker: بعضهم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p72/r8.claim: Another analysis makes the attached kāf, hāʾ, or yāʾ the pronoun and iyyā a supporting base when the pronoun precedes its verb.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p72/r8.anchor: وحكي عن بعضهم أنه قال: الكاف والهاء والياء هي الاسم المضمر،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p72/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p72/r9.speaker: بعضهم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p72/r9.claim: A further view treats ayyā as an obscure form for the accusative, with suffixes distinguishing addressee, absent person, and speaker but carrying no case role.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p72/r9.anchor: أن أيا اسم مبهم يكنى به عن المنصوب، وزيدت الكاف والياء والهاء تفرقة بين المخاطب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p72/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p72/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p72/r10.claim: Worship means observing the law and commands with humility and submission; maʿbad describes a well-trodden path or a tamed camel, as in Tarafa's line.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p72/r10.anchor: ونعبد معناه نقيم الشرع والأوامر مع تذلل واستكانة، والطريق المذلل يقال له معبد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p72/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p72/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p72/r11.claim: Iyyaka is repeated because each of the two different verbs requires its own emphasis and focus.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p72/r11.anchor: وتكررت إياك بحسب اختلاف الفعلين، فاحتاج كل واحد منهما إلى تأكيد واهتمام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p72/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p72/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p72/r12.claim: We seek God's help in all our affairs; this is also a repudiation of idols.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p72/r12.anchor: ونستعين معناه نطلب العون منك في جميع أمورنا، وهذا كله تبرؤ من الأصنام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p72/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p72/r13.speaker: الأعمش وابن وثاب والنخعي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p72/r13.claim: Al-Aʿmash, Ibn Waththab, and al-Nakhaʿi read نستعين with kasra on its initial nūn, a dialect of some Quraysh in certain augmented verbs.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p72/r13.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش وابن وثاب والنخعي: «ونستعين» بكسر النون، وهي لغة لبعض قريش

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73/r1.claim: Nastaʿīn derives from nastaʿūn by moving the wāw's vowel to the ʿayn and changing wāw to yāʾ after kasra.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73/r1.anchor: ونستعين أصله نستعون نقلت حركة الواو إلى العين وقلبت ياء لانكسار ما قبلها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73/r2.claim: The verbal noun istiʿāna derives from istiʿwānan; the wāw shifts its vowel, then a long vowel is dropped and hāʾ compensates for it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73/r2.anchor: والمصدر استعانة أصله استعوانا نقلت حركة الواو إلى العين فلما انفتح ما قبلها وهي في نية الحركة انقلبت ألفا

AKHFASH:v1p3#2/r5.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p3#2/r5.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p3#2/r5.claim: The same waṣl rule applies to initial alifs in verbs or verbal nouns whose imperfect form begins with a fatḥa vowel on its yāʾ, as in the cited imperatives.
AKHFASH:v1p3#2/r5.anchor: وكذلك كل الف كانت في اول فعل او مصدر

AKHFASH:v1p15#2/r4.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p15#2/r4.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p15#2/r4.claim: The shift to addressing God as iyyāka is by revelation: God instructs the Prophet to say the praise and then to say iyyāka naʿbudu.

AKHFASH:v1p15#2/r5.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p15#2/r5.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p15#2/r5.claim: Iyyāka is used instead of anta because the pronoun is an object of naʿbudu; object position takes ka, hi, or the iyyā form.
AKHFASH:v1p15#2/r5.anchor: لان هذا موضع نصب. واذا لم يقدر في موضع النصب

AKHFASH:v1p16/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p16/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p16/r1.claim: Iyyāka in both naʿbudu and nastaʿīn is accusative as the object; nominative positions instead take forms such as anta, antum, huwa, or hiya.
AKHFASH:v1p16/r1.anchor: اذا كان موضع رفع جعلت فيه

AKHFASH:v1p17/r6.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p17/r6.speaker: العرب
AKHFASH:v1p17/r6.claim: Some Arabs say hiyyāka for iyyāka, treating the initial alif as h, like ih or hih and haraqtu for araqtu.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14/r1.speaker: الحسن وأبو المتوكل وأبو مجلز
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Abū al-Mutawakkil, and Abū Majlaz read the verb with yāʾ and ḍamma on the yāʾ, making the sense “him alone they worship.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14/r1.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وأبو المتوكل وأبو مجلز يعبد بضم الياء وفتح الباء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14/r2.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14/r2.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī explains that reading as an instruction to Muḥammad: say that they worship You alone.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14/r2.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري المعنى قل يا محمد إياك يعبد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14/r3.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14/r3.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī says Arabic can shift from third person to address and back, citing Yunus 10:32 and al-Insān 76:21–22; Labīd's line illustrates the idiom.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14/r3.anchor: والعرب ترجع من الغيبة إلى الخطاب ومن الخطاب إلى الغيبة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14/r4.speaker: علي وابن عباس في آخرين
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14/r4.claim: One interpretation of worship is affirming God's oneness, reported from ʿAlī and Ibn ʿAbbās among others.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14/r4.anchor: أحدهما أنها بمعنى التوحيد روي عن علي وابن عباس في آخرين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14/r5.claim: A second meaning is obedience, as in the command not to worship Satan in Yā Sīn 36:60.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14/r6.claim: A third meaning is supplication, as in the warning about those too proud to worship God in Ghāfir 40:60.

IBNKATHIR:1:5/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r1.speaker: القراء السبعة والجمهور
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r1.claim: The seven readers and the majority pronounce the yāʾ in iyyāka with gemination.

IBNKATHIR:1:5/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r2.speaker: عمرو بن فايد
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r2.claim: Amr ibn Fayd's light yāʾ with kasra is a rejected anomalous reading because iyā means sunlight.
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r2.anchor: وقرأ عمرو بن فايد بتخفيفها مع الكسر

IBNKATHIR:1:5/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r3.speaker: بعض القراء
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r3.claim: Some read ayyaka with an open hamza and geminated yāʾ, while others substitute hāʾ for hamza, as illustrated by a poetic line.
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r3.anchor: بالهاء بدل الهمزة ، كما قال الشاعر

IBNKATHIR:1:5/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r4.speaker: يحيى بن وثاب والأعمش
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r4.claim: All readers open the initial nūn of nastaʿīn except Yahya ibn Waththab and al-A'mash, who use kasra, a dialect of several Arab tribes.
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r4.anchor: وهي لغة بني أسد وربيعة وبني تميم وقيس

IBNKATHIR:1:5/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r5.claim: In ordinary language ʿibādah is rooted in humility, as in a subdued road or camel; in religious usage it combines complete love, submission, and fear.

IBNKATHIR:1:5/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r6.claim: Fronting and repeating iyyāka marks special concern and restriction: worship is for God alone and reliance is on Him alone, the perfection of obedience.

IBNKATHIR:1:5/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r7.speaker: بعض السلف
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r7.claim: Some early authorities call this the secret of the Fatiha, itself the secret of the Qur'an: the first clause renounces shirk and the second renounces self-power through surrender to God.
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r7.anchor: قال بعض السلف : الفاتحة سر القرآن

IBNKATHIR:1:5/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r8.claim: Worship and reliance recur together elsewhere in the Qur'an, including commands to worship God and trust Him.
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r8.anchor: وهذا المعنى في غير آية من القرآن

IBNKATHIR:1:5/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r9.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r9.claim: The speech shifts from speaking of God in the third person to addressing Him directly because praise brings the worshipper near and present before Him.
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r9.anchor: وتحول الكلام من الغيبة إلى المواجهة بكاف الخطاب

IBNKATHIR:1:5/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r10.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r10.claim: The opening is God's praise of Himself and instruction to servants to praise Him; the Prophet says prayer is invalid without reciting the Opening of the Book when able.
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r10.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

IBNKATHIR:1:5/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r11.speaker: الله تعالى
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r11.claim: In a divine report, God divides the prayer between Himself and His servant, responds to each recited section, calls 1:5 shared between them, and grants the servant's request.
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r11.anchor: قال : هذا بيني وبين عبدي ولعبدي ما سأل

IBNKATHIR:1:5/r12.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas says the servant worships, fears, and hopes in God alone, and seeks His help for obedience and every affair.

IBNKATHIR:1:5/r13.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r13.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r13.claim: Qatadah says God commands His servants to devote worship sincerely to Him and seek His help for their affairs.
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r13.anchor: وقال قتادة : { إياك نعبد وإياك نستعين }

IBNKATHIR:1:5/r14.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r14.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r14.claim: Worship precedes asking for help because worship is the intended end while seeking help is its means; sound judgment puts the more important matter first.

IBNKATHIR:1:5/r15.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r15.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r15.claim: One explanation of the plural nūn is that the speaker represents the whole class of worshippers, including fellow believers, especially in congregational prayer or when leading them.
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r15.anchor: بأن المراد من ذلك الإخبار عن جنس العباد

IBNKATHIR:1:5/r16.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r16.speaker: بعضهم
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r16.claim: Another explanation allows a plural of honor: the servant is noble while worshipping, but should not claim collective standing outside worship because everyone depends on God.
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r16.anchor: ومنهم من قال : يجوز أن تكون للتعظيم

IBNKATHIR:1:5/r17.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r17.speaker: بعضهم
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r17.claim: A third view says we is more humble than I worship because the singular could imply that one person alone can fully worship or properly praise God.
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r17.anchor: ومنهم من قال : ألطف في التواضع من إياك أعبد

IBNKATHIR:1:5/r18.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r18.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r18.claim: Servanthood is an exalted station; God calls His Messenger His servant at the revelation, public worship, and night journey, and directs him to worship amid rejection.
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r18.anchor: يشرف به العبد لانتسابه إلى جناب الله

IBNKATHIR:1:5/r19.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r19.speaker: بعضهم
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r19.claim: Some argue that servanthood is nobler than messengerhood because worship proceeds from creation to God, while the messenger's mission proceeds from God to creation; Ibn Kathir rejects the claim and its reasoning.
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r19.anchor: عن بعضهم : أن مقام العبودية أشرف من مقام الرسالة

IBNKATHIR:1:5/r20.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r20.speaker: بعض الصوفية
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r20.claim: Some Sufis criticize worship motivated by reward or avoidance of punishment, and even worship as honor through religious duties, arguing that the highest worship is for God's own perfection.
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r20.anchor: وقال بعض الصوفية : العبادة إما لتحصيل ثواب ورد عقاب

IBNKATHIR:1:5/r21.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r21.speaker: آخرون
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r21.claim: Others rebut the Sufi criticism: worship directed to God can still seek reward and protection from punishment, as the Prophet affirms to a Bedouin asking for Paradise and refuge from Hell.
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r21.anchor: وقد رد ذلك عليهم آخرون وقالوا

JISHUMI:v1p210/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p210/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p210/r3.claim: The common reading has kasra on the first vowel of iyyāka and fatḥa on the first nūn of nastaʿīn; another Arabic dialect is possible but not an accepted reading.
JISHUMI:v1p210/r3.anchor: قراءة العامة (إياك) بكسر الألف، (ونستعين) بفتح النون الأولى

JISHUMI:v1p210/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p210/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p210/r4.claim: Iyyāka is derived as iwyāka, with wāw changed and assimilated into yāʾ, and is associated with seeking refuge; as a detached pronoun it precedes its verb unless a separator intervenes.
JISHUMI:v1p210/r4.anchor: أصله إوياك، قلبت الواو ياء وأدغمت في الياء، فصار إياك

JISHUMI:v1p210/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p210/r5.speaker: أبو حاتم
JISHUMI:v1p210/r5.claim: Abū Ḥātim classifies iyyāka as a detached pronoun, as opposed to connected or implicit pronouns.
JISHUMI:v1p210/r5.anchor: قال أبو حاتم: إياك ضمير منفصل، والضمير ثلاثة

JISHUMI:v1p213/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p213/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p213/r1.claim: The second kind of divine assistance brings a person closer to doing a duty or choosing it, as with divine لطف; it belongs to one known to have such help and may precede or accompany action.
JISHUMI:v1p213/r1.anchor: المعلوم أن له لطفا، ثم اللطف قد يتقدم الفعل وقد يقارنه

JISHUMI:v1p213/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p213/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p213/r2.claim: Though assistance from God is obligatory in this account, asking for it remains meaningful: one who knows an act is good wants help to do it, and supplication can itself be worship or a لطف occasioned by the request.
JISHUMI:v1p213/r2.anchor: من علم حسن فعل أحب أن يعان عليه، ولأن الطلب قد يكون عبادة وإن كان واجبا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p55#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p55#2/r1.speaker: الأخفش
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p55#2/r1.claim: Al-Akhfash and the verified grammarians treat the attached kāf, hā, and yā on iyya as markers of address, absence, or speech, not inflected pronouns.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p55#2/r1.anchor: وليست بأسماء مضمرة وهو مذهب الأخفش وعليه المحققون

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p55#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p55#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p55#2/r2.claim: Putting the object first expresses exclusivity: worship and the request for help are directed to God alone.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p55#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p55#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p55#2/r3.claim: The reading has variants in the yā, hamza, and initial letter; Tufayl's verse witnesses the hā form.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p55#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p55#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p55#2/r4.claim: Worship is the utmost submission and humility, reserved for God because He is the giver of the greatest blessings.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p55#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p55#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p55#2/r5.claim: The shift from third-person praise to direct address is rhetorical iltifat; the explanation of its purpose continues in the next segment.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p55#2/r5.anchor: هذا يسمى الالتفات في علم البيان قد يكون من الغيبة إلى الخطاب ومن الخطاب إلى الغيبة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p56/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p56/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p56/r1.claim: Iltifat shifts among speech styles, as Quranic examples and Imru al-Qays's three successive shifts show; changing style renews attention and can carry special benefits.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p56/r1.anchor: ولأن الكلام اذا نقل من أسلوب إلى أسلوب كان ذلك أحسن تطرية لنشاط السامع وايقاظا للإصغاء اليه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p56/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p56/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p56/r2.claim: Direct address here makes the one already described as worthy of praise vivid, so worship and help are confined to the God whose qualities make Him deserving.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p56/r2.anchor: فقيل إياك يا من هذه صفاته نخص بالعبادة والاستعانة لا نعبد غيرك ولا نستعينه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p56/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p56/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p56/r3.claim: Joining worship with help unites what servants offer in drawing near to God with what they need from Him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p56/r3.anchor: ليجمع بين ما يتقرب به العباد إلى ربهم وبين ما يطلبونه ويحتاجون اليه من جهته

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p56/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p56/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p56/r4.claim: Worship comes first because presenting a means before making a request makes a response more likely.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p56/r4.anchor: لأن تقديم الوسيلة قبل طلب الحاجة ليستوجبوا الاجابة اليها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p56/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p56/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p56/r5.claim: The request for help is general, but its best sense is seeking God's aid and enabling grace to perform worship; the next verse specifies that request.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p56/r5.anchor: والأحسن ان تراد الاستعانة به وبتوفيقه على أداء العبادة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p57/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p57/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p57/r1.claim: The request for guidance explains the help being sought: when asked how He should assist, the servants answer, guide us to the straight path.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p57/r1.anchor: بيانا للمطلوب من المعونة كأنه قيل كيف أعينكم فقالوا اهدنا الصراط المستقيم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p57/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p57/r2.speaker: ابن حبيش
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p57/r2.claim: Ibn Hubaysh reads nasta'in with kasra on the initial nūn.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p57/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن حبيش ( نستعين ) بكسر النون

MAJAZ:v1p22/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p22/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p22/r2.claim: The direct address in iyyāka naʿbudu is evidence for the vocative accusative analysis.
MAJAZ:v1p22/r2.anchor: لأنه يخاطب شاهدا، ألا تراه يقول: «إياك نعبد» (4) فهذه حجة لمن نصب،

MAJAZ:v1p22/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p22/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p22/r4.claim: After referring to the absent, the discourse returns to direct address in ‘You alone we worship, You alone we ask for help, guide us.’
MAJAZ:v1p22/r4.anchor: ثم رجع فخاطب شاهدا فقال: «إياك نعبد وإياك نستعين اهدنا» (5) ، قال عنترة بن شداد العبسى:

MAJAZ:v1p22/r6.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p22/r6.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p22/r6.claim: The shift between absent and present address is illustrated by ʿAntara ibn Shaddād’s cited verse.
MAJAZ:v1p22/r6.anchor: قال عنترة بن شداد العبسى: شطت مزار العاشقين فأصبحت ... عسرا على طلا بك ابنة مخرم

MAJAZ:v1p22/r7.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p22/r7.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p22/r7.claim: Abū Kabīr al-Hudhalī’s cited address likewise illustrates a turn from speaking about someone to addressing them.
MAJAZ:v1p22/r7.anchor: وقال أبو كبير الهذلى: يا لهف نفسى كان جدة خالد ... وبياض وجهك للتراب الأعفر

MAJAZ:v1p22/r8.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p22/r8.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p22/r8.claim: Placing the object pronoun before the verb is grammatical; al-ʿAjjāj’s ‘iyyāka adʿū’ exemplifies the order.
MAJAZ:v1p22/r8.anchor: كقولك: نعبد إياك، قال العجاج: إياك أدعو فتقبل ملقى

MAJAZ:v1p22/r9.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p22/r9.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p22/r9.claim: Putting the pronoun after a verb-first clause, as in adʿū iyyāka, is impossible, but adding it after the verb’s object suffix, adʿūka iyyāka, is allowed.
MAJAZ:v1p22/r9.anchor: ولو بدأت بالفعل لم يجز كقولك: أدعو إياك، محال، فإن زدت الكناية فى آخر الفعل جاز الكلام: أدعوك إياك.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p57#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p57#2/r1.speaker: الخليل
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p57#2/r1.claim: He parses iyyaka as God's name annexed to the second-person suffix kāf.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p57#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p57#2/r2.speaker: الأخفش
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p57#2/r2.claim: He parses iyyaka as one word used as a pronoun for God, since a pronoun cannot be annexed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p57#2/r2.anchor: لأن المضمر لا يضاف , وهذا قول الأخفش

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p57#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p57#2/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p57#2/r3.claim: One meaning of worship is submission, the highest form of submission, due only to the giver of greatest blessings such as life and the senses.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p57#2/r3.anchor: إلا الله تعالى , لأنها أعلى مراتب الخضوع

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p57#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p57#2/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p57#2/r4.claim: A second definition of worship is obedience.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p57#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p57#2/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p57#2/r5.claim: A third definition of worship is drawing near through obedience.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p57#2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p57#2/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p57#2/r6.claim: The submission definition is clearest: Christians worshiped Jesus without obeying him, while the Prophet is obeyed but is not an object of worship.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p57#2/r6.anchor: عبدَت عيسى عليه السلام , ولم تطعه بالعبادة , والنبي

MUQATIL:1:5-7/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:1:5-7/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:1:5-7/r1.claim: To worship God alone means to affirm His oneness, as the feminine participle in another verse means monotheists.
MUQATIL:1:5-7/r1.anchor: يعنى نوحد، كقوله سبحانه في المفصل

MUQATIL:1:5-7/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:1:5-7/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:1:5-7/r2.claim: The servant asks God for help in carrying out worship.

MUQATIL:1:5-7/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:1:5-7/r8.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MUQATIL:1:5-7/r8.claim: A report from Abū Hurayra says the Prophet related that God divided this sūra between Himself and the servant: praise is thanks, the two mercy names are praise, the King verse is glorification, and the rest belongs to the servant; seeking help is God's special acknowledgment of the servant's plea.
MUQATIL:1:5-7/r8.anchor: عن أبى هريرة، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

NASAFI-FULL:v1p7#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p7#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p7#3/r1.claim: Sibawayh treats iya as a detached pronoun and the kaf as an address particle without syntactic position; al-Khalil treats iya as the pronoun with the kaf attached to it.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p7#3/r1.anchor: ايا عند الخليل وسيبويه اسم مضمر والكاف حرف خطاب عند سيبويه ولا محل له من الاعراب

NASAFI-FULL:v1p7#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p7#3/r2.speaker: الكوفيون
NASAFI-FULL:v1p7#3/r2.claim: The Kufans treat the whole form iyaka as one pronoun.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p7#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p7#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p7#3/r3.claim: Fronting the object marks exclusivity: worship and the seeking of aid are directed to God alone; worship is the utmost submission and abasement.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p7#3/r3.anchor: وتقديم المفعول لقصد الاختصاص والمعنى نخصك بالعبادة وهى أقصى غاية الخضوع والتذلل

NASAFI-FULL:v1p7#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p7#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p7#3/r4.claim: The shift from third-person reference to direct address is iltifat; Arabic rhetoric uses such shifts to refresh attention and heighten reception, and the cited Qur'anic and poetic examples illustrate its forms.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p7#3/r4.anchor: وعدل عن الغيبة إلى الخطاب للالتفات وهو قد يكون من الغيبة إلى الخطاب ومن الخطاب إلى الغيبة

NASAFI-FULL:v1p7#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p7#3/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p7#3/r5.claim: Direct address follows the great descriptions of God: the one worthy of praise, humility, and aid is addressed as the uniquely distinguished Lord described above.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p7#3/r5.anchor: أنه لما ذكر الحقيق بالحمد والثناء وأجرى عليه تلك الصفات العظام تعلق العلم بمعلوم عظيم الشأن

NASAFI-FULL:v1p7#3/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p7#3/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p7#3/r6.claim: Worship precedes asking for aid because presenting the means before a request brings a response closer; alternatively, the order follows the preceding arrangement of the verses.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p7#3/r6.anchor: وقدمت العبادة على الاستعانة لأن تقديم الوسيلة قبل طلب الحاجة أقرب إلى الإجابة

NASAFI-FULL:v1p7#3/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p7#3/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p7#3/r7.claim: The request for aid is unrestricted and covers every need; alternatively it asks for God's help and enabling grace in performing acts of worship, which the following request for guidance specifies.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p7#3/r7.anchor: وأطلقت الاستعانة لتنناول كل مستعان فيه ويجوز أن يراد الاستعانة به وبتوفيقه على أداء العبادات

QURTUBI-FULL:1:5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:1:5/r1.speaker: ثعلب
QURTUBI-FULL:1:5/r1.claim: Thaʿlab says dāna has opposite meanings: to obey, disobey, become powerful, become low, and subdue; din can also mean habit, affair, a ruler’s way, or illness.
QURTUBI-FULL:1:5/r1.anchor: قال ثعلب: دان الرجل إذا أطاع، ودان إذا عصى، ودان إذا عز، ودان إذا ذل

QURTUBI-FULL:1:5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:1:5/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:1:5/r2.claim: Poetry uses din for obedience, habit or custom, a ruler’s way of life, and illness, with examples from ʿAmr ibn Kulthum, al-Muthaqib, Zuhayr, and al-Lihyani.
QURTUBI-FULL:1:5/r2.anchor: ويطلق الدين على العادة والشأن، كما قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:1:5/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:1:5/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:1:5/r3.claim: Iyyaka naʿbudu shifts from third-person praise to direct address; worship means obedient submission, and speaking the verse confesses God’s lordship amid others worshipping idols.
QURTUBI-FULL:1:5/r3.anchor: رجع من الغيبة إلى الخطاب على التلوين لأن من أول السورة إلى ها هنا خبرا عن الله تعالى وثناء عليه

QURTUBI-FULL:1:5/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:1:5/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:1:5/r4.claim: Iyyaka nastaʿin asks for help, support, and success; one report says confessing both worship and dependence escapes both fatalism and the Qadariyya.

QURTUBI-FULL:1:5/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:1:5/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:1:5/r5.claim: The object is fronted for emphasis and because Arabs put the important item first; the repeated pronoun prevents reading the clause as seeking aid from someone else.
QURTUBI-FULL:1:5/r5.anchor: قدم اهتماما، وشأن العرب تقديم الأهم

QURTUBI-FULL:1:5-6/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:1:5-6/r1.speaker: العجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:1:5-6/r1.claim: Al-ʿAjjaj’s line uses an object pronoun before the verb, illustrating the Quranic word order.

QURTUBI-FULL:1:5-6/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:1:5-6/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:1:5-6/r2.claim: The line “to You until I reached iyāka” is anomalous and cannot serve as a grammatical model.
QURTUBI-FULL:1:5-6/r2.anchor:
وأما قول الشاعر:
إليك حتى بلغت إياكا
فشاذ لا يقاس عليه.

QURTUBI-FULL:1:5-6/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:1:5-6/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:1:5-6/r3.claim: Waraq means dirhams when pronounced with kasra on rāʾ and wealth when pronounced with fatḥa.
QURTUBI-FULL:1:5-6/r3.anchor: والورق بكسر الراء من الدراهم، وبفتحها المال.

QURTUBI-FULL:1:5-6/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:1:5-6/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:1:5-6/r4.claim: The pronoun is repeated so readers do not infer that worship is directed to God but aid is sought from someone else.
QURTUBI-FULL:1:5-6/r4.anchor: وكرر الاسم لئلا يتوهم إياك نعبد ونستعين غيرك.

QURTUBI-FULL:1:5-6/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:1:5-6/r5.speaker: الجمهور من القراء والعلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:1:5-6/r5.claim: Most readers double the yāʾ in iyyaka at both occurrences.
QURTUBI-FULL:1:5-6/r5.anchor: الجمهور من القراء والعلماء على شد الياء من «إياك» في الموضعين

QURTUBI-FULL:1:5-6/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:1:5-6/r6.speaker: عمرو بن فائد
QURTUBI-FULL:1:5-6/r6.claim: ʿAmr ibn Faʾid reads iyyaka with a light yāʾ and kasra on the hamza; the author rejects it because it would mean “your sun” or its light.
QURTUBI-FULL:1:5-6/r6.anchor: وهذه قراءة مرغوب عنها، فإن المعنى يصير: شمسك نعبد أو ضوءك

QURTUBI-FULL:1:5-6/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:1:5-6/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:1:5-6/r7.claim: Iāʾ means sunlight, like the halo around the moon; a cited line says sunlight struck the animal’s lip.
QURTUBI-FULL:1:5-6/r7.anchor:
وإياة الشمس بكسر الهمزة: ضوءها وقد تفتح. وقال:
سقته إياة الشمس إلا لثاته

QURTUBI-FULL:1:5-6/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:1:5-6/r8.speaker: الفضل الرقاشي
QURTUBI-FULL:1:5-6/r8.claim: Al-Fadl al-Raqqashi reads ayyaka with an open hamza, a well-known dialect.
QURTUBI-FULL:1:5-6/r8.anchor: وقرأ الفضل الرقاشي: «أياك» بفتح الهمزة وهي لغة مشهورة.

QURTUBI-FULL:1:5-6/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:1:5-6/r9.speaker: أبو السوار الغنوي
QURTUBI-FULL:1:5-6/r9.claim: Abu al-Sawwar al-Ghanawi reads hiyyaka in both places, a dialect supported by a poetic line.
QURTUBI-FULL:1:5-6/r9.anchor: وقرأ أبو السوار الغنوي: «هياك» في الموضعين، وهي لغة قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:1:5-6/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:1:5-6/r10.speaker: يحيى بن وثاب والأعمش
QURTUBI-FULL:1:5-6/r10.claim: The clause is coordinated with the preceding one; these readers use a kasra on the nūn in nastaʿīn, a dialect of several tribes, deriving it from nastaʿawn through sound changes.
QURTUBI-FULL:1:5-6/r10.anchor: عطف جملة على جملة. وقرأ يحيى بن وثاب والأعمش: «نستعين» بكسر النون

NAHHAS:v1p171/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p171/r10.speaker: الفضل بن عيسى الرقاشي
NAHHAS:v1p171/r10.claim: Al-Faḍl ibn ʿĪsā al-Raqāshī reads iyyāka with fatḥa on the hamza.
NAHHAS:v1p171/r10.anchor: وقرأ الفضل بن عيسى الرقاشي فتح الهمزة

NAHHAS:v1p171/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p171/r11.speaker: عمرو بن فائد
NAHHAS:v1p171/r11.claim: ʿAmr ibn Fāʾid reads iyyāka in a shortened form.
NAHHAS:v1p171/r11.anchor: وقرأ عمرو بن فائد ( إياك ) مخففا

NAHHAS:v1p171/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p171/r12.speaker: الخليل وسيبويه
NAHHAS:v1p171/r12.claim: Al-Khalīl and Sībawayh treat iyā as the noun and the attached kāf as genitive; the Kufans treat iyyāka as one complete noun.
NAHHAS:v1p171/r12.anchor: الاسم من إياك عند الخليل وسيبويه إيا والكاف موضع خفض وعند الكوفيين إياك اسم بكمالها

NAHHAS:v1p171/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p171/r13.speaker: الخليل
NAHHAS:v1p171/r13.claim: Al-Khalīl calls iyā a pronoun; Abū al-ʿAbbās objects that pronouns are not annexed and calls it an ambiguous expression like kull.
NAHHAS:v1p171/r13.anchor: وزعم الخليل رحمه الله أنه اسم مضمر قال أبو العباس هذا خطأ لا يضاف المضمر

NAHHAS:v1p171/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p171/r14.speaker: الخليل
NAHHAS:v1p171/r14.claim: Al-Khalīl says naʿbudu is indicative because it resembles nouns.
NAHHAS:v1p171/r14.anchor: ( نعبد ) فعل مستقبل وهو مرفوع عند الخليل

NAHHAS:v1p171/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p171/r15.speaker: سيبويه
NAHHAS:v1p171/r15.claim: Sībawayh says the imperfect is indicative because it resembles nouns.

NAHHAS:v1p171/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p171/r16.speaker: الكسائي
NAHHAS:v1p171/r16.claim: Al-Kisāʾī says the imperfect is indicative because of its prefixes.
NAHHAS:v1p171/r16.anchor: وقال الكسائي الفعل المستقبل مرفوع بالزوائد التي في أوله

NAHHAS:v1p171/r17.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p171/r17.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v1p171/r17.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says the imperfect is indicative because it is free of jussive and subjunctive particles.
NAHHAS:v1p171/r17.anchor: وقال الفراء هو مرفوع بسلامته من الجوازم والنواصب

NAHHAS:v1p171/r18.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p171/r18.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p171/r18.claim: Iyyāka is also the object of nastaʿīn, and the two clauses are coordinated.
NAHHAS:v1p171/r18.anchor: و إياك منصوب بنستعين عطف جملة على جملة

NAHHAS:v1p171/r19.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p171/r19.speaker: يحيى بن وثاب والأعمش
NAHHAS:v1p171/r19.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb and al-Aʿmash read nastaʿīn with kasra on the nūn, a Tamīm, Asad, Qays, and Rabīʿa usage.
NAHHAS:v1p171/r19.anchor: وقرأ يحيى بن وثاب والأعمش ( نستعين ) بكسر النون وهذه لغة تميم وأسد وقيس وربيعة

NAHHAS:v1p171/r20.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p171/r20.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p171/r20.claim: The form derives from istaʿwana: the wāw shifts its vowel to the preceding consonant and becomes yāʾ; istiʿāna similarly derives from istiʿwān, with a compensatory tāʾ after a long vowel is deleted.
NAHHAS:v1p171/r20.anchor: والأصل في نستعين نستعون قلبت حركة الواو على العين فلما انكسر ما قبل الواو صارت ياء

QUTB-ZILAL:1:1/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:1:1/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:1:1/r1.claim: Al-Fatiha is Meccan and has seven verses; Muslims recite it at least seventeen times daily, more with voluntary prayers, and may repeat it without limit.

QUTB-ZILAL:1:1/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:1:1/r2.speaker: رسول الله [ ص ]
QUTB-ZILAL:1:1/r2.claim: The Prophet says prayer is invalid without reciting the Opening of the Book; the report is in both Sahih collections.
QUTB-ZILAL:1:1/r2.anchor: لا صلاة لمن لم يقرأ بفاتحة الكتاب

QUTB-ZILAL:1:1/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:1:1/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:1:1/r3.claim: The short surah gathers core Islamic creed, worldview, feelings, and guidance, explaining its repetition in every rakʿa and why prayer without it is invalid.
QUTB-ZILAL:1:1/r3.anchor: ما يشير إلى طرف من حكمة اختيارها للتكرار

QUTB-ZILAL:1:5/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:1:5/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:1:5/r1.claim: The preceding principles entail that worship and reliance belong to God alone.
QUTB-ZILAL:1:5/r1.anchor: وهذه هي الكلية الاعتقادية التي تنشأ عن الكليات السابقة في السورة

QUTB-ZILAL:1:5/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:1:5/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:1:5/r2.claim: Exclusive worship liberates people from subjection to other people, systems, social arrangements, superstition, and delusion.
QUTB-ZILAL:1:5/r2.anchor: وهذه الكلية تعلن ميلاد التحرر البشري الكامل الشامل

QUTB-ZILAL:1:5/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:1:5/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:1:5/r3.claim: Muslims should support and cooperate for good with human forces that believe in God and follow His way, and resist and change those disconnected from God and His way.
QUTB-ZILAL:1:5/r3.anchor: وهذه يجب أن يؤازرها ، ويتعاون معها على الخير والحق والصلاح

QUTB-ZILAL:1:5/r4.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:1:5/r4.speaker: author
