QUTB-ZILAL:1:5/r4.claim: A misguided human power may look immense but loses its true strength when severed from God, while even a small force connected to Him retains power.
QUTB-ZILAL:1:5/r4.anchor: تفقد الغذاء الدائم الذي يحفظ لها طاقتها

QUTB-ZILAL:1:5/r5.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:1:5/r5.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:1:5/r5.claim: A small faithful group can overcome a larger one through connection to the first source of strength, as the Qur'an says in 2:249.

QUTB-ZILAL:1:5/r6.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:1:5/r6.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:1:5/r6.claim: Muslims should approach natural powers through understanding and friendship, since human and natural forces share God's will and cooperate under it.
QUTB-ZILAL:1:5/r6.anchor: وأما القوى الطبيعية فموقف المسلم منها هو موقف التعرف والصداقة

QUTB-ZILAL:1:5/r7.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:1:5/r7.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:1:5/r7.claim: God made natural forces helpful allies; people gain their aid by observation, knowledge, and cooperation, while harm often follows ignorance of their laws.
QUTB-ZILAL:1:5/r7.anchor: إن عقيدة المسلم توحي إليه أن الله ربه قد خلق هذه القوى كلها

QUTB-ZILAL:1:5/r8.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:1:5/r8.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:1:5/r8.claim: The Western phrase “conquer nature” reflects a worldview severed from God; Muslims see nature's forces as created under one law for cooperative ends and thank God for their service.
QUTB-ZILAL:1:5/r8.anchor: ولهذا التعبير دلالته الظاهرة على نظرة الجاهلية المقطوعة الصلة بالله

QUTB-ZILAL:1:5/r9.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:1:5/r9.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:1:5/r9.claim: God, not humanity, subjects natural forces to human use; the Qur'an says He subjected all that is on earth for people.

QUTB-ZILAL:1:5/r10.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:1:5/r10.speaker: رسول الله [ ص ]
QUTB-ZILAL:1:5/r10.claim: Looking toward Mount Uhud, the Prophet said that the mountain loves the Muslims and they love it, exemplifying intimacy with nature.
QUTB-ZILAL:1:5/r10.anchor: وما أروع قول الرسول [ ص ] وهو ينظر إلى جبل أحد

QUTB-ZILAL:1:7/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:1:7/r2.speaker: رسول الله
QUTB-ZILAL:1:7/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra reports in Sahih Muslim that God calls al-Fatiha a prayer divided between Himself and His servant: praise, mercy, and glorification are the Lord's; worship and aid are shared; guidance and the servant's request belong to the servant, who receives what he asks.
QUTB-ZILAL:1:7/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة عن رسول الله [ ص ] :  "  يقول الله تعالى : قسمت الصلاة بيني وبين عبدي نصفين

RAZI-FULL:v1p151/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p151/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p151/r4.claim: Razi moves from lordship to servitude: the body is an instrument for the soul, and worship is its best state and the first stage of human felicity; divine aid and guidance are the next stages.
RAZI-FULL:v1p151/r4.anchor: فأحسن أحوال العبد في هذه الدنيا أن يكون مواظبا على العبادات

RAZI-FULL:v1p153#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p153#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p153#2/r4.claim: Razi maps worship to three stages: outward observance is the law, seeking the unseen through divine support is the path, and seeing all affairs as God's is the reality.
RAZI-FULL:v1p153#2/r4.anchor: وهو أن يواظب على الأعمال الظاهرة وهو قوله ﴿ إياك نعبد ﴾

RAZI-FULL:v1p154/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p154/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p154/r2.claim: The law, path, and reality complete human ascent: worship, reliance on God, and guidance culminate in fellowship with the pure and distance from the wretched.
RAZI-FULL:v1p154/r2.anchor: أعني الشريعة المدلول عليها بقوله إياك نعبد والطريقة المدلول عليها بقوله وإياك نستعين

RAZI-FULL:v1p155/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p155/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p155/r6.claim: As the servant ceases serving rulers and relying on them for wealth or rank, he turns instead to worshipping God and seeking guidance and knowledge from Him.
RAZI-FULL:v1p155/r6.anchor: فعند زوال ذلك التعلق يعلم أنه لما كان مشتغلا بخدمة الأمير والوزير فلأن يشتغل بخدمة المعبود كان أولى

RAZI-FULL:v1p161/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p161/r2.speaker: أم سلمة عن النبي
RAZI-FULL:v1p161/r2.claim: Umm Salama reports that the Prophet recited al-Fatiha while counting the basmala as its first verse, followed by the rest of its verses.
RAZI-FULL:v1p161/r2.anchor: روى الشافعي رضي الله عنه عن مسلم عن ابن جريج عن ابن أبي مليكة عن أم سلمة أنها قالت

RAZI-FULL:v1p162/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p162/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي
RAZI-FULL:v1p162/r2.claim: In the divided-prayer report, God calls the basmala glorification, al-Hamd praise, the two mercy names extolling, the Master of Judgment entrustment, and the remaining response a sharing and a request granted.
RAZI-FULL:v1p162/r2.anchor: فإذا قال العبد بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم قال الله سبحانه مجدني عبدي وإذا قال الحمد لله رب العالمين

SAMIN-DURR:1:5/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:5/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:5/r1.claim: Iyyaka is the object placed before na'budu for exclusivity and must be a detached form.
SAMIN-DURR:1:5/r1.anchor: إياك " مفعول مقدم على " نعبد " ، قدم للاختصاص، وهو واجب الانفصال

SAMIN-DURR:1:5/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:5/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:5/r2.claim: Most grammarians classify iyyaka as a pronoun, while al-Zajjaj treats it as an overt noun.
SAMIN-DURR:1:5/r2.anchor: واختلفوا فيه: هل هو من قبيل الأسماء الظاهرة أو المضمرة؟ فالجمهور على أنه مضمر

SAMIN-DURR:1:5/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:5/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:5/r3.claim: Pronoun analyses differ: the whole form is a pronoun; only iyya is; iyya plus suffix marker is; or iyya is support and the suffix is the pronoun.
SAMIN-DURR:1:5/r3.anchor: والقائلون بأنه ضمير اختلفوا فيه على أربعة أقوال، أحدها: أنه كله ضمير

SAMIN-DURR:1:5/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:5/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:5/r4.claim: The rare phrase iyaha al-shawab annexes iyya to an overt noun, supporting the analysis that suffixes are genitive annexes.
SAMIN-DURR:1:5/r4.anchor: وشذت إضافته إلى الظاهر في قولهم: " إذا بلغ الرجل الستين فإياه وإيا الشواب

SAMIN-DURR:1:5/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:5/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:5/r5.claim: Some derive iyyā from aw or āya and debate its pattern, but the author says this is useless because morphology does not apply to deeply frozen forms.
SAMIN-DURR:1:5/r5.anchor: وقد أبعد بعض النحويين فجعل له اشتقاقا، ثم قال: هل هو مشتق من " أو

SAMIN-DURR:1:5/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:5/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:5/r6.claim: The common form has kasra and doubled y; other forms open the hamza or replace it with hā', with doubled or plain y, as a poem shows.
SAMIN-DURR:1:5/r6.anchor: وفيه لغات: أشهرها كسر الهمزة وتشديد الياء، ومنها فتح الهمزة وإبدالها هاء

SAMIN-DURR:1:5/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:5/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:5/r7.claim: Some reject the light pronunciation because it could sound like we worship your sun; the text notes irregular readings among the variants without detailing them.
SAMIN-DURR:1:5/r7.anchor: وقال بعضهم: إياك بالتخفيف مرغوب عنه]، لأنه يصير " شمسك نعبد

RAZI-FULL:v1p196#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p196#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p196#2/r1.claim: Worship is an act performed to magnify another; the word is related to a well-trodden, level road, طريق معبد.
RAZI-FULL:v1p196#2/r1.anchor: العبادة عبارة عن الفعل الذي يؤتى به لغرض تعظيم الغير وهو مأخوذ من قولهم

RAZI-FULL:v1p196#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p196#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p196#2/r2.claim: God alone deserves worship because ultimate reverence belongs only to the source of greatest benefaction: life and the creation of what sustains life, both traced to God.
RAZI-FULL:v1p196#2/r2.anchor: الحياة التي تفيد المكنة من الانتفاع وخلق المنتفع به

RAZI-FULL:v1p196#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p196#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p196#2/r3.claim: Rāzī's second proof begins by mapping God's names to the servant's past: God brought him from nonexistence, death, incapacity, and ignorance into being, life, ability, and knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v1p196#2/r3.anchor: انتقل من العدم إلى الوجود ومن الموت إلى الحياة ومن العجز إلى القدرة

RAZI-FULL:v1p196#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p196#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p196#2/r4.claim: The servant's needs multiply upon entering existence, setting up the claim that present provision depends on God as Lord, Merciful, and Compassionate.
RAZI-FULL:v1p196#2/r4.anchor: لما دخل في الوجوه انفتحت عليه أبواب الحاجات وحصلت عنده أسباب الضرورات

RAZI-FULL:v1p197/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p197/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p197/r1.claim: God's names cover all three stages of the servant's life: deity for his origin, Lord and the two Merciful names for present needs, and Owner of Judgment Day for the afterlife; all welfare depends on Him alone.
RAZI-FULL:v1p197/r1.anchor: جميع مصالح العبد في الماضي والحاضر والمستقبل لا يتم ولا يكتمل إلا بالله

RAZI-FULL:v1p197/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p197/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p197/r2.claim: Because divine power, knowledge, generosity, and forbearance are certain while natural, astral, or mental causes may also be effects of God's power, only God is certainly worthy of worship.
RAZI-FULL:v1p197/r2.anchor: العلم بكون الإله تعالى معبودا للخلق أمر يقيني وأما كون غيره معبودا للخلق فهو أمر مشكوك فيه

RAZI-FULL:v1p197/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p197/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p197/r3.claim: Although servitude is lowly, service to the highest and most excellent Lord is most fitting; God's superior power, knowledge, and generosity make His worship preferable to any rival's.
RAZI-FULL:v1p197/r3.anchor: لما كان الله تعالى أشرف الموجودات وأعلاها فكانت عبوديته أولى من عبودية غيره

RAZI-FULL:v1p197/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p197/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p197/r4.claim: Everything contingent is needy and occupied with its own needs, so only the self-sufficient God can meet the needs of others and deserves their worship.
RAZI-FULL:v1p197/r4.anchor: والغني لذاته هو الله تعالى فدافع الحاجات هو الله تعالى فمستحق العبادات هو الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v1p197/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p197/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p197/r5.claim: God's extraordinary acts—holding the sky, moving celestial bodies, producing lightning, wind and rain, bringing water from stone and ice from water, and raising or lowering mountains and people—show why no created thing can share His worship.
RAZI-FULL:v1p197/r5.anchor: استحقاق العبادة يستدعي قدرة الله تعالى بأن يمسك سماء بلا علاقة وأرضا بلا دعامة

RAZI-FULL:v1p197#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p197#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p197#2/r1.claim: God's miracles, including raising the mountain over Moses and splitting the sea, make it foolish to equate Him in worship with inert, base, or finite creatures.
RAZI-FULL:v1p197#2/r1.anchor: وجعل البحر يبسا لموسى عليه السلام فمن كانت قدرته هكذا كيف يسوى في العبادة

RAZI-FULL:v1p197#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p197#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p197#2/r2.claim: The exclusive address “You alone we worship” amounts to pure monotheism and the confession that there is no deity but God.
RAZI-FULL:v1p197#2/r2.anchor: قوله إياك نعبد يدل على أنه لا معبود إلا الله ومتى كان الأمر كذلك ثبت أنه لا إله إلا الله

RAZI-FULL:v1p197#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p197#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p197#2/r3.claim: Among lower composite bodies, polytheists worship mineral idols of stone, gold, or silver, a particular tree, the calf, or humans claimed to be God's son, such as Ezra and Christ.
RAZI-FULL:v1p197#2/r3.anchor: يتخذون الأصنام إما من الأحجار أو من الذهب أو من الفضة ويعبدونها

RAZI-FULL:v1p197#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p197#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p197#2/r4.claim: The Magians worship fire, which Rāzī classifies among simple lower bodies.

RAZI-FULL:v1p197#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p197#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p197#2/r5.claim: The Ṣābiʾa and most astrologers worship the sun, moon, and other stars and attribute fortune and misfortune to them.
RAZI-FULL:v1p197#2/r5.anchor: يعبدون الشمس والقمر وسائر الكواكب ويضيفون السعادة والنحوسة إليها

RAZI-FULL:v1p197#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p197#2/r6.speaker: المانوية والثنوية
RAZI-FULL:v1p197#2/r6.claim: Manichaeans and dualists posit Light and Darkness as the world's managers and partners with God.
RAZI-FULL:v1p197#2/r6.anchor: الذين قالوا مدبر العالم هو النور والظلمة وهؤلاء هم المانوية والثنوية

RAZI-FULL:v1p197#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p197#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p197#2/r7.claim: A group treats angels as planetary spirits assigned to regions and kinds, fashions images of them, and worships those images.
RAZI-FULL:v1p197#2/r7.anchor: لكل إقليم روح معين من الأرواح الفلكية يدبره ولكل نوع من أنواع هذا العالم روح فلكي

RAZI-FULL:v1p197#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p197#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p197#2/r8.claim: Another group posits two sibling gods, one good and one evil, assigning worldly good to God and evil to Iblīs.
RAZI-FULL:v1p197#2/r8.anchor: الذين قالوا للعالم إلهان : أحدهما خير والآخر شر

RAZI-FULL:v1p197#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p197#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p197#2/r9.claim: Every polytheist worships a partner to seek benefit or escape harm, while strict monotheists place hope, fear, desire, and dread in God alone and worship and ask help only from Him.
RAZI-FULL:v1p197#2/r9.anchor: فكان رجاؤهم من الله وخوفهم من الله ورغبتهم في الله ورهبتهم من الله

RAZI-FULL:v1p198/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p198/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p198/r1.claim: The preceding taxonomy concludes that “You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help” functions as the confession “There is no deity but God.”
RAZI-FULL:v1p198/r1.anchor: فكان قوله إياك نعبد وإياك نستعين قائما مقام قوله لا إله إلا الله

RAZI-FULL:v1p198/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p198/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p198/r2.claim: The familiar remembrance combines glorification, praise, monotheism, divine greatness, and dependence; “praise belongs to God” already entails glorifying Him because only the perfect can perfect others.
RAZI-FULL:v1p198/r2.anchor: والشيء لا يكون مكملا متمما لغيره إلا إذا كان قبل ذلك تاما كاملا في ذاته

RAZI-FULL:v1p198/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p198/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p198/r3.claim: The sūrah elaborates the five formulas of the familiar remembrance: praise establishes God's qualities, exclusive worship states monotheism, and asking His help expresses that no aim is fulfilled without Him.
RAZI-FULL:v1p198/r3.anchor: فثبت أن سورة الفاتحة من أولها إلى آخرها منطبقة على ذلك الذكر

RAZI-FULL:v1p198/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p198/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p198/r4.claim: Putting “You” first identifies the true object of worship and produces reverent attention; Rāzī illustrates this with an expert wrestler who lost to a rustic until he recognized his opponent.
RAZI-FULL:v1p198/r4.anchor: قدم ذكر نفسه ليتنبه العابد على أن المعبود هو الله الحق

RAZI-FULL:v1p198/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p198/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p198/r5.claim: Remembering God's greatness before undertaking difficult prayer makes its burdens easier, like taking strength before lifting weight or accepting pain for a beloved.
RAZI-FULL:v1p198/r5.anchor: فاذكر أولا قوله إياك نعبد لتذكرني وتحضر في قلبك معرفتي

RAZI-FULL:v1p198/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p198/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p198/r6.claim: When satanic laziness or heedlessness arises, recalling God's presence restores insight and readiness for worship, as 7:201 describes the God-conscious remembering and seeing clearly.
RAZI-FULL:v1p198/r6.anchor: إن الذين اتقوا إذا مسهم طيف من الشيطان تذكروا فإذا هم مبصرون

RAZI-FULL:v1p198/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p198/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p198/r7.claim: Naming God before the act prevents the devil from claiming the worship was directed to idols, celestial bodies, or another object; the order makes monotheism explicit.
RAZI-FULL:v1p198/r7.anchor: أما إذا غيرت هذا الترتيب وقلت أولا إياك ثم قلت ثانيا نعبد كان قولك أولا إياك صريحا

RAZI-FULL:v1p198/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p198/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p198/r8.claim: Since the necessarily existent precedes contingent beings in existence, mention of the Eternal should precede all other speech.
RAZI-FULL:v1p198/r8.anchor: القديم الواجب لذاته متقدم في الوجود على المحدث الممكن لذاته

RAZI-FULL:v1p198/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p198/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p198/r9.claim: The discerning worshiper attends to the giver, not the gift, and in hardship to God, not the affliction; this keeps the heart absorbed in knowledge of God rather than worldly circumstances.
RAZI-FULL:v1p198/r9.anchor: من كان نظره في وقت النعمة إلى المنعم لا إلى النعمة كان نظره في وقت البلاء إلى المبتلي لا إلى البلاء

RAZI-FULL:v1p200/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p200/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p200/r1.claim: The servant's continuing approach through supererogatory worship until God loves him illustrates the state of being absorbed in God's presence.
RAZI-FULL:v1p200/r1.anchor: لا يزال العبد يتقرب إلي بالنوافل حتى أحبه فإذا أحببته كنت له سمعا وبصرا

RAZI-FULL:v1p200/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p200/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p200/r2.claim: Saying “we worship You” would not exclude worship of others, as polytheists do; saying “You alone we worship” clearly denies every rival.
RAZI-FULL:v1p200/r2.anchor: لو قيل نعبدك لم يفد نفي عبادتهم لغيره

RAZI-FULL:v1p200/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p200/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p200/r3.claim: The nūn of majesty portrays God's servants together as His subjects, whose service makes them rulers of this world and the next.
RAZI-FULL:v1p200/r3.anchor: أن هذه النون نون العظمة فكأنه قيل له متى كنت خارج الصلاة فلا تقل نحن

RAZI-FULL:v1p200/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p200/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p200/r4.claim: The plural “we worship” is humbler than “I worship”: it presents the speaker as one servant among God's servants rather than as a self-important individual.
RAZI-FULL:v1p200/r4.anchor: لو قال إياك أعبد لكان ذلك تكبرا ومعناه أني أنا العابد أما لما قال إياك نعبد

RAZI-FULL:v1p200/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p200/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p200/r5.claim: Although the same reasons might seem to favor putting God before “praise,” praise can be given to others, so “for God” must restrict it; worship can never go to another, so “You alone” comes first.
RAZI-FULL:v1p200/r5.anchor: الحمد لما جاز لغير الله في ظاهر الأمر كما جاز لله لا جرم حسن تقدم الحمد

RAZI-FULL:v1p200/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p200/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p200/r6.claim: Rāzī asks whether the nūn in “we worship” is plural or divine majesty, since attributing greatness to oneself seems unfitting during humble worship; he says each answer has wisdom.
RAZI-FULL:v1p200/r6.anchor: النون في قوله نعبد إما أن تكون نون الجمع أو نون التعظيم

RAZI-FULL:v1p200#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p200#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p200#2/r1.claim: To explain the plural nūn, Rāzī cites a report that the first congregational takbīr is worth more than the world and all it contains.
RAZI-FULL:v1p200#2/r1.anchor: التكبيرة الأولى في صلاة الجماعة خير من الدنيا وما فيها

RAZI-FULL:v1p200#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p200#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p200#2/r2.claim: The great reward for congregational prayer does not justify harming Muslims with garlic or onion odor, much less by slander, backbiting, or denunciation.
RAZI-FULL:v1p200#2/r2.anchor: فإذا كان هذا الثواب لا يفي بذلك فكيف يفي بإيذاء المسلم

RAZI-FULL:v1p200#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p200#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p200#2/r3.claim: In congregational prayer “we” means the worshipers together; when praying alone it includes the worshiper and the angels who join him in worship.
RAZI-FULL:v1p200#2/r3.anchor: وإن كان يصلي وحده كان المراد أني أعبدك والملائكة معي في العبادة

RAZI-FULL:v1p200#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p200#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p200#2/r4.claim: The plural also includes all believers across east and west, so the worshiper seeks the welfare of fellow Muslims as well as his own.
RAZI-FULL:v1p200#2/r4.anchor: كان قد ذكر عبادة نفسه وعبادة جميع المؤمنين شرقا وغربا

RAZI-FULL:v1p200#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p200#3/r1.speaker: رسول الله
RAZI-FULL:v1p200#3/r1.claim: The Prophet promises that God will fulfill all the needs of one who fulfills a Muslim's need.
RAZI-FULL:v1p200#3/r1.anchor: من قضى لمسلم حاجة قضى الله له جميع حاجاته

RAZI-FULL:v1p200#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p200#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p200#3/r2.claim: After the servant praises God through the whole opening sūrah, God raises his standing and asks him to care for all Muslims rather than only his own needs.
RAZI-FULL:v1p200#3/r2.anchor: فلا تقتصر على إصلاح مهماتك وحدك ولكن أصلح حوائج جميع المسلمين

RAZI-FULL:v1p200#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p200#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p200#3/r3.claim: Because an individual's worship is mixed with shortcomings, he joins it to the worship of all worshipers; like a sale of ten slaves accepted all together or rejected all together, God may accept it with the worship of angels, prophets, and saints.
RAZI-FULL:v1p200#3/r3.anchor: فإما أن يرد الكل وهو غير جائز لأن قوله إياك نعبد دخل فيه عبادات الملائكة

RAZI-FULL:v1p200#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p200#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p200#3/r4.claim: Knowing worship's benefits makes it sweet: it is human perfection, illuminates the heart, ennobles speech, beautifies the limbs, and brings the greatest happiness now and in the future.
RAZI-FULL:v1p200#3/r4.anchor: هذه الأحوال أشرف المراتب الإنسانية والدرجات البشرية فإذا كان حصول هذه الأحوال أعظم السعادات

RAZI-FULL:v1p200#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p200#3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p200#3/r5.claim: Worship is a trust: fulfilling it is required and intrinsically excellent, and faithfulness in one direction brings God's faithfulness in return; 33:72 and 4:58 support the duty.
RAZI-FULL:v1p200#3/r5.anchor: أن العبادة أمانة بدليل قوله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v1p200#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p200#3/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p200#3/r6.claim: An Arab leaves his camel outside, fulfills worship calmly, and asks God to return His trust; after the camel is stolen, its injured robber returns it, illustrating God's preservation of the worshiper's trust.

RAZI-FULL:v1p200#3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p200#3/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p200#3/r7.claim: Rāzī says that the camel story illustrates a saying of the Prophet to Ibn ʿAbbās, whose wording follows in the next segment.
RAZI-FULL:v1p200#3/r7.anchor: وهو المراد من قوله عليه السلام لابن عباس

RAZI-FULL:v1p201/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p201/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p201/r1.claim: Worship transfers a person from the deceptive world and preoccupation with creatures into joy and the presence of God, bringing complete delight.
RAZI-FULL:v1p201/r1.anchor: الاشتغال بالعبادة انتقال من عالم الغرور إلى عالم السرور ومن الاشتغال بالخلق إلى حضرة الحق

RAZI-FULL:v1p201/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p201/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p201/r2.claim: Rāzī recounts that a snake fell near Abū Ḥanīfa during prayer, but he did not notice as people scattered.
RAZI-FULL:v1p201/r2.anchor: أن حية سقطت من السقف وتفرق الناس وكان أبو حنيفة في الصلاة ولم يشعر بها

RAZI-FULL:v1p201/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p201/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p201/r3.claim: ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr's diseased limb was amputated while he prayed, and he felt nothing.
RAZI-FULL:v1p201/r3.anchor: فلما شرع في الصلاة قطعوا منه ذلك العضو فلم يشعر عروة بذلك القطع

RAZI-FULL:v1p201/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p201/r4.speaker: رسول الله
RAZI-FULL:v1p201/r4.claim: The Prophet's chest made a rumbling sound like a boiling cauldron when he began prayer; Rāzī compares this absorption to women cutting their hands while captivated by Joseph's beauty.
RAZI-FULL:v1p201/r4.anchor: وعن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه كان حين يشرع في الصلاة كانوا يسمعون من صدره أزيزا

RAZI-FULL:v1p201/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p201/r5.speaker: أهل التحقيق
RAZI-FULL:v1p201/r5.claim: The first rank worships for reward or to avoid punishment; Rāzī calls it very low because it treats God as a means to a worldly or created goal.
RAZI-FULL:v1p201/r5.anchor: أن يعبد الله طمعا في الثواب أو هربا من العقاب وهذا هو المسمى بالعبادة

RAZI-FULL:v1p201/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p201/r6.speaker: أهل التحقيق
RAZI-FULL:v1p201/r6.claim: The second rank worships to gain honor through service, accepted duties, or affiliation with God; it is higher but incomplete because its real aim remains something other than God.
RAZI-FULL:v1p201/r6.anchor: أن يعبد الله لأجل أن يتشرف بعبادته أو يتشرف بقبول تكاليفه

RAZI-FULL:v1p202/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p202/r1.speaker: أهل التحقيق
RAZI-FULL:v1p202/r1.claim: The highest rank worships God because He is God and Creator and the worshiper is His servant; this joins awe with humility, and intending prayer for God keeps it valid.
RAZI-FULL:v1p202/r1.anchor: أن يعبد الله لكونه إلها وخالقا ولكونه عبدا له

RAZI-FULL:v1p202/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p202/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p202/r2.claim: The command to worship until death in 15:99 shows worship must never lapse and attests its rank; its four elements—glorification, praise, prostration, and worship—also ease sorrow by turning the heart from creatures to God.
RAZI-FULL:v1p202/r2.anchor: فأمر محمدا عليه الصلاة والسلام بالمواظبة على العبادة إلى أن يأتيه الموت

RAZI-FULL:v1p202/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p202/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p202/r3.claim: Calling Muhammad God's servant at the supreme Ascension shows servitude's honor; some say it exceeds prophethood because it turns from creation to God, while prophethood turns back to people and their affairs.
RAZI-FULL:v1p202/r3.anchor: ولولا أن العبودية أشرف المقامات وإلا لما وصفه الله بهذه الصفة في أعلى مقامات المعراج

RAZI-FULL:v1p202/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p202/r4.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v1p202/r4.claim: Some authorities rank servitude above prophethood because servitude turns from people toward God and withdraws from managing affairs, while a messenger turns from God toward people and manages their needs.
RAZI-FULL:v1p202/r4.anchor: ومنهم من قال : العبودية أشرف من الرسالة

RAZI-FULL:v1p202/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p202/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p202/r5.claim: Jesus first calls himself God's servant; that declaration vindicates his mother, brings good and averts harm, and precedes God's raising him, so sustained practical servitude deserves hope of Paradise.

RAZI-FULL:v1p202/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p202/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p202/r6.claim: After establishing God's oneness, God commands Moses to worship Him: monotheism is the root or tree, and servitude its branch or fruit; neither stands without the other.
RAZI-FULL:v1p202/r6.anchor: أمره بعد التوحيد بالعبودية ؛ لأن التوحيد أصل

RAZI-FULL:v1p202/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p202/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p202/r7.claim: Rationally, contingent beings receive existence and every perfection through God's creative power; thus every honor, joy, and virtue comes through servitude, the key to all good.
RAZI-FULL:v1p202/r7.anchor: فلما تعلقت قدرة الحق به وفاضت عليه آثار جوده وإيجاده حصل له الوجود وكمالات الوجود

RAZI-FULL:v1p202/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p202/r8.speaker: علي
RAZI-FULL:v1p202/r8.claim: Rāzī introduces a saying from ʿAlī in which the following segment calls servanthood an honor and God’s lordship a distinction.
RAZI-FULL:v1p202/r8.anchor: وكان علي كرم الله وجهه يقول

RAZI-FULL:v1p203/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p203/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p203/r1.claim: The spiritual stations are knowledge of lordship and servitude; together they fulfill the covenant of 2:40. The opening praise establishes lordship, worship begins servitude, reliance completes it, and guidance is its fruit.

RAZI-FULL:v1p203/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p203/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p203/r2.claim: The transition from third person praise to direct address can be understood as God lifting the veil and drawing near after the worshiper has praised and acknowledged His attributes.
RAZI-FULL:v1p203/r2.anchor: حمدتني وأقررت بكوني إلها ربا رحمانا رحيما مالكا ليوم الدين

RAZI-FULL:v1p203/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p203/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p203/r3.claim: Direct address suits requests and service in God’s presence; the sūrah uses third person for praise and shifts to direct address for supplication, as prophets do.
RAZI-FULL:v1p203/r3.anchor: من أول السورة إلى قوله إياك نعبد ثناء والثناء في الغيبة أولى

RAZI-FULL:v1p203/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p203/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p203/r4.claim: Rāzī then quotes a prayer exalting servitude as honor and recognizing God as Lord.
RAZI-FULL:v1p203/r4.anchor: كفى بي فخرا أن أكون لك عبدا وكفى بي شرفا أن تكون لي ربا

RAZI-FULL:v1p204/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p204/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p204/r1.claim: Rāzī divides the case for reliance on God into rational proofs and transmitted evidence, then begins with the rational proofs.
RAZI-FULL:v1p204/r1.anchor: ويدل عليه وجوه من العقل والنقل أما العقل فمن وجوه

RAZI-FULL:v1p204/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p204/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p204/r2.claim: No act of obedience can be performed without God's protection from sin and enabling grace; Rāzī supports reliance on both rational and transmitted proofs.
RAZI-FULL:v1p204/r2.anchor: لا حول عن معصية الله إلا بعصمة الله ولا قوة على طاعة الله إلا بتوفيق الله

RAZI-FULL:v1p204/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p204/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p204/r3.claim: Human capacity is equally disposed to acting or abstaining; action needs a preponderating motive, which cannot come from the servant without regress, so God must assist.
RAZI-FULL:v1p204/r3.anchor: فما لم يحصل المرجح لم يحصل الرجحان وذلك المرجح ليس من العبد

RAZI-FULL:v1p204/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p204/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p204/r4.claim: People with similar ability, intellect, effort, and desire seek true belief, yet only some attain it; the needed aid must come from God rather than a human or angel, which would restart the question.
RAZI-FULL:v1p204/r4.anchor: فوز البعض بدرك الحق لا يكون إلا بإعانة معين وما ذاك المعين إلا الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v1p204/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p204/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p204/r5.claim: A person may delay an act until a decisive motive enters the heart and opposing motives are removed; God creates these motives, which is the meaning of assistance.
RAZI-FULL:v1p204/r5.anchor: إلقاء تلك الداعية في القلب وإزالة الدواعي المعارضة لها ليست إلا من الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v1p204/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p204/r6.speaker: الجبرية
RAZI-FULL:v1p204/r6.claim: The Jabriyya argue that if people acted independently, asking God for help with their actions would be pointless.
RAZI-FULL:v1p204/r6.anchor: لو كان العبد مستقلا بالفعل لما كان للاستعانة على الفعل فائدة

RAZI-FULL:v1p204/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p204/r7.speaker: القدرية
RAZI-FULL:v1p204/r7.claim: The Qadariyya argue that seeking assistance only makes sense if the servant can already perform the basic act; otherwise another's help is useless.
RAZI-FULL:v1p204/r7.anchor: الاستعانة إنما تحسن لو كان العبد متمكنا من أصل الفعل

RAZI-FULL:v1p204/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p204/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p204/r8.claim: Rāzī resolves the dispute by saying capacity affects action only alongside a decisive motive; divine assistance creates that motive and removes the contrary one.
RAZI-FULL:v1p204/r8.anchor: القدرة لا تؤثر في الفعل إلا مع الداعية الجازمة

RAZI-FULL:v1p204#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p204#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p204#2/r1.claim: Although assistance is usually sought before work begins, the worshiper asks God to help complete worship already begun and protect it from death, illness, or changed motives.
RAZI-FULL:v1p204#2/r1.anchor: شرعت في العبادة فأستعين بك في إتمامها فلا تمنعني من إتمامها بالموت ولا بالمرض

RAZI-FULL:v1p204#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p204#2/r2.speaker: رسول الله
RAZI-FULL:v1p204#2/r2.claim: A Prophetic saying that the believer's heart lies between two fingers of the Merciful supports the worshiper's request for God to make his wandering heart present.
RAZI-FULL:v1p204#2/r2.anchor: قلب المؤمن بين أصبعين من أصابع الرحمن

RAZI-FULL:v1p204#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p204#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p204#2/r3.claim: The worshiper asks God alone, not Gabriel or Michael, following Abraham's refusal of Gabriel's offer while tied by Nimrod and his trust that God knows his state; Rāzī compares his own helplessness before Hell and God's promised rescue.
RAZI-FULL:v1p204#2/r3.anchor: فقال : أما إليك فلا فقال : سله فقال : حسبي من سؤالي علمه بحالي

RAZI-FULL:v1p204#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p204#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p204#2/r4.claim: Help from any intermediary itself depends on God's help, so the worshiper should cut out that intermediary and ask God directly.
RAZI-FULL:v1p204#2/r4.anchor: فإذا كانت إعانة الغير لا تتم إلا بإعانتك فلنقطع هذه الواسطة

RAZI-FULL:v1p204#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p204#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p204#2/r5.claim: Following worship with a request for help prevents pride: the rank achieved through worship came from God's support, not the servant's own strength.
RAZI-FULL:v1p204#2/r5.anchor: المقصود من ذكر قوله وإياك نستعين إزالة العجب وإفناء تلك النخوة والكبر

RAZI-FULL:v1p214#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p214#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p214#2/r5.claim: The seven Fatiha verses remove seven vices: praise dispels desire, Lord of the worlds greed, Judgment Day anger, worship and aid pride and vanity, guidance caprice, the favored path unbelief and doubt, and the final phrase innovation.
RAZI-FULL:v1p214#2/r5.anchor: فثبت أن هذه الآيات السبع دافعة لتلك الأخلاق القبيحة السبعة

RAZI-FULL:v1p215#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p215#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p215#2/r8.claim: The servant's obligations comprise the act of worship and recognition that worship is only possible with God's aid; the latter opens the question of determinism and free will.
RAZI-FULL:v1p215#2/r8.anchor: الأعمال التي يأتي بها العبد والآثار المتفرعة على تلك الأعمال

RAZI-FULL:v1p217/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p217/r1.speaker: الله تعالى
RAZI-FULL:v1p217/r1.claim: In a divine report transmitted by the Prophet, God responds to each Fatiha phrase: the opening remembers Him, praise praises Him, the mercy names magnify Him, Judgment Day glorifies Him or is entrusted to Him, worship belongs to Him, aid relies on Him, and guidance is the servant's request.
RAZI-FULL:v1p217/r1.anchor: فإذا قال العبد : بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم يقول الله تعالى ذكرني عبدي

RAZI-FULL:v1p217/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p217/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p217/r2.claim: Calling the Fatiha “prayer” shows that religious law serves human interests: people most need knowledge of God's lordship and servitude, which the surah's two halves provide to fulfill the covenant.
RAZI-FULL:v1p217/r2.anchor: مدار الشرائع على رعاية مصالح الخلق

RAZI-FULL:v1p217/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p217/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p217/r3.claim: Since God names the Fatiha “prayer,” prayer without its recitation does not occur; Razi takes this to establish that reciting it is a pillar, as his school holds.
RAZI-FULL:v1p217/r3.anchor: أن عند عدم قراءة الفاتحة وجب أن لا تحصل الصلاة

RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r1.claim: Razi supports obligatory Fatiha recitation because the Prophet consistently recited it and commands require following him.

RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r2.claim: The rightly guided caliphs also consistently recited it, and the Prophet commanded Muslims to follow their sunna.
RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r2.anchor: أن الخلفاء الراشدين واظبوا على قراءتها

RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r3.claim: Muslims everywhere recite it in prayer, and the Qur'an commands following the path of believers.
RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r3.anchor: أن جميع المسلمين شرقا وغربا لا يصلون إلا بقراءة الفاتحة

RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r4.claim: The prophetic statement “no prayer without the Opening of the Book” directly supports the requirement.

RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r5.claim: The command to recite what is easy from the Qur'an is obligatory; because reciting other passages is not, the obligatory recitation must be the Fatiha.
RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r5.anchor: وظاهره الوجوب فكانت قراءة ما تيسر من القرآن واجبة

RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r6.claim: Reciting the Fatiha is the safer course, following the prophetic instruction to leave what causes doubt for what does not.
RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r6.anchor: أن قراءة الفاتحة أحوط فوجب المصير إليها

RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r7.claim: The Prophet's constant practice makes abandoning his command forbidden, and Muslims agree that the Fatiha is better and more complete than another recitation.
RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r7.anchor: وسابعها : أن الرسول عليه السلام واظب على قراءتها فوجب أن يكون العدول عنه محرما

RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r8.claim: If the superior prayer with the Fatiha discharges the obligation, it does not follow that the inferior prayer with another passage does; the obligation remains due.
RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r8.anchor: ولا يلزم من الخروج عن العهدة بالعمل الكامل الخروج عن العهدة بالعمل الناقص

RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r9.claim: Prayer seeks remembrance of the heart, and this concise surah gathers lordship and servitude and is equated with the mighty Qur'an; nothing else can replace it.
RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r9.anchor: المقصود من الصلاة حصول ذكر القلب

RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r10.claim: The transmitted report itself says that prayer is not established without the Fatiha.
RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r10.anchor: أن هذا الخبر الذي رويناه يدل على أن عند فقدان الفاتحة لا تحصل الصلاة

RAZI-FULL:v1p218#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p218#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p218#2/r3.claim: The report that worship and aid belong between God and servant expresses determinism: a balanced capacity acts only when a decisive motive tips it, and that motive must be created by God.

RAZI-FULL:v1p218#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p218#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p218#2/r4.claim: Creating a decisive motive without an opposing one is God's aid; the request not to let hearts swerve means not creating motives toward false belief and corrupt action, while mercy creates motives to good.
RAZI-FULL:v1p218#2/r4.anchor: فخلق تلك الداعية الخالصة عن المعارض هو الإعانة

RAZI-FULL:v1p218#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p218#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p218#2/r5.claim: God's share is creating the decisive motive; the servant's share is that the action issues from him when capacity and motive coincide, a subtle account of agency.
RAZI-FULL:v1p218#2/r5.anchor: أما الذي منه فهو خلق الداعية الجازمة وأما الذي من العبد فهو أن عند حصول مجموع القدرة والداعية يصدر الأثر عنه

RAZI-FULL:v1p219/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p219/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p219/r4.claim: The seven Fatiha verses correspond to the seven bodily prayer acts—standing, bowing, rising, first prostration, rising between prostrations, second prostration, and sitting—as soul to body.
RAZI-FULL:v1p219/r4.anchor: أن آيات الفاتحة سبع والأعمال المحسوسة أيضا في الصلاة سبعة

RAZI-FULL:v1p220/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p220/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p220/r5.claim: Worship recalls the preceding prostration while seeking aid asks God to grant success in reaching the second; both match the sitting between prostrations.
RAZI-FULL:v1p220/r5.anchor: إياك نعبد إخبار عن السجدة التي تقدمت

RAZI-FULL:v1p220/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p220/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p220/r8.claim: The seven Fatiha verses are the soul of the seven prayer acts, themselves the soul of seven stages of human formation; God is the soul of souls and light of lights.
RAZI-FULL:v1p220/r8.anchor: روح الأرواح ونور الأنوار هو الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v1p221/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p221/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p221/r1.claim: Muhammad's ascent has a bodily journey from Mecca to Jerusalem and then the high kingdom, and a spiritual journey from the visible to the unseen and from the unseen to the unseen of the unseen.
RAZI-FULL:v1p221/r1.anchor: أما ما يتعلق بعالم الأرواح فله معراجان

RAZI-FULL:v1p221/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p221/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p221/r2.claim: The spiritual ascent rises through human spirits, the spirits of the heavens, angels, throne-bearers, and pure spirits detached from bodies, whose worship and love of God exceed human comprehension.
RAZI-FULL:v1p221/r2.anchor: ثم تترقى فتنتهي إلى الأرواح المقدسة عن التعلقات بالأجسام

RAZI-FULL:v1p221/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p221/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p221/r3.claim: The ascent continues through ever-higher spiritual ranks until God, the source of all good and mercy; thus the spirit-world is the unseen and God's presence the unseen of the unseen.
RAZI-FULL:v1p221/r3.anchor: فثبت أن عالم الأرواح هو عالم الغيب وحضرة جلال الربوبية هي غيب الغيب

RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r1.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r1.claim: A prophetic report says God has seventy veils of light; if unveiled, the splendor of His face would burn everything perceived by sight, and only prophetic light reveals the number.
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r1.anchor: إن لله سبعين حجابا من النور لو كشفها لأحرقت سبحات وجهه كل ما أدرك البصر

RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r2.claim: Prayer was given to Muhammad as a gift for his community because it joins bodily ascent through actions with spiritual ascent through remembrances.
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r2.anchor: إن تحفة أمتك الصلاة وذلك لأنها جامعة بين المعراج الجسماني وبين المعراج الروحاني

RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r3.claim: Before beginning the ascent, the worshipper purifies body and clothing for the holy presence and chooses which of opposing companions—angel or devil, reason or desire, truth or falsehood, and so forth—to follow, since settled companionship is hard to break.
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r3.anchor: فإنه إذا استحكمت المرافقة تعذرت المفارقة

RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r4.claim: Raising the hands signals leaving both worlds and directing all inner faculties toward God; “God is greatest” means He exceeds all beings, knowledge, comparison, and even the claim that He is simply greater.
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r4.anchor: فاقطع نظرك عنهما بالكلية ووجه قلبك وروحك وسرك وعقلك وفهمك

RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r5.claim: The opening glorification reveals the lights of divine majesty and moves from declaring God's transcendence to praising Him.
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r5.anchor: ثم قل : سبحانك اللهم وبحمدك وفي هذا المقام تجلى لك نور سبحات الجلال

RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r6.claim: “Blessed is Your name” unveils pre-eternity and eternity, since blessing here indicates abiding beyond extinction and nonexistence.
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r6.anchor: لأن قوله تبارك إشارة إلى الدوام المنزه عن الإفناء والإعدام

RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r7.claim: “Exalted is Your majesty” signifies that God's knowledge and greatness exceed every stated measure.
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r7.anchor: أعلم وأعظم من أن تكون صفات جلاله ونعوت كماله محصورة في القدر المذكور

RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r8.claim: “There is no god but You” means every attribute of majesty and perfection belongs only to God; ultimately reason, speech, understanding, and imagination fail before Him.
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r8.anchor: كل صفات الجلال وسمات الكمال له لا لغيره

SAMIN-DURR:1:5#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#2/r1.claim: The present verb is nominative because it has no governing subjunctive or jussive; Basran grammarians also explain this by its occupying a noun's position and resembling nouns in form and distribution.
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#2/r1.anchor: ونعبد: فعل مضارع مرفوع لتجرده من الناصب والجازم

SAMIN-DURR:1:5#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#2/r2.claim: The subject of naʿbudu is obligatorily implicit.
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#2/r2.anchor: وقيل: لوقوعه موقع الاسم، وهذا رأي البصريين

SAMIN-DURR:1:5#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#2/r3.claim: Worship is ultimate submission, due only to the ultimate benefactor, and is stronger than ʿubūdiyya, which is outwardly showing submission.
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#2/r3.anchor: والعبادة غاية التذلل، ولا يستحقها إلا من له غاية الإفضال

SAMIN-DURR:1:5#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#2/r4.claim: The root denotes submission: a trodden road is called muʿabbad, as are a subdued camel and a person made submissive by tar.
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#2/r4.anchor: ويقال: طريق معبد، أي مذلل بالوطء

SAMIN-DURR:1:5#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#2/r5.speaker: طرفة
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#2/r5.claim: Ṭarafa's line uses muʿabbad for a road, illustrating the sense of a road trodden smooth.
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#2/r5.anchor: قال طرفة: 63 تباري عتاقا ناجيات وأتبعت

SAMIN-DURR:1:5#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#2/r6.claim: The phrase shifts from speaking about God in the third person to addressing Him directly, a rhetorical turn; Yūnus 10:22 offers the reverse direction.
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#2/r6.anchor: وفي قوله تعالى: { إياك نعبد } التفات من الغيبة إلى الخطاب

SAMIN-DURR:1:5#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#2/r7.speaker: بعضهم
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#2/r7.claim: Some critics correct al-Zamakhsharī's count to two shifts, rather than three; the author answers that the opening address itself shifts from the expected first person.
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#2/r7.anchor: وقد خطأ بعضهم الزمخشري في جعله هذا ثلاثة التفاتات، وقال: بل هما التفاتان

SAMIN-DURR:1:5#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#2/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#2/r8.claim: The Imruʾ al-Qays example has three shifts: first person to address, then to third person, then back to first person.
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#2/r8.anchor: ثم من الخطاب إلى الغيبة، ثم من الغيبة إلى التكلم الذي هو الأصل

SAMIN-DURR:1:5#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#3/r1.claim: A rare reading has a third-person passive form, analyzed as borrowing an accusative pronoun for a nominative subject, with the underlying sense أنت تعبد.
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#3/r1.anchor: وقرئ شاذا: " إياك يعبد " على بنائه للمفعول الغائب

SAMIN-DURR:1:5#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#3/r2.claim: The anomalous form also shifts from direct address in إياك to third person in يعبد; the author calls this an unusual shift within one clause.
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#3/r2.anchor: إلا أن هذا التفات غريب، لكونه في جملة واحدة

SAMIN-DURR:1:5#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#3/r3.speaker: الآخر
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#3/r3.claim: A poet uses the second-person suffix in عصيكا where the expected first-person form would be عصيت, illustrating a pronoun substitution parallel.
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#3/r3.anchor: وقول الآخر: 65 يابن الزبير طالما عصيكا

SAMIN-DURR:1:5#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#3/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#3/r4.claim: A fronted object pronoun is obligatory when a delayed object would have to attach to its verb; this rule does not apply when attachment is optional.
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#3/r4.anchor: و " إياك " واجب التقديم على عامله، لأن القاعدة

SAMIN-DURR:1:5#3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#3/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#3/r5.claim: The syntax of إياك نستعين parallels إياك نعبد, and the conjunction coordinates both inflection and meaning.
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#3/r5.anchor: والكلام في " إياك نستعين " كالكلام في " إياك نعبد " والواو عاطفة

SAMIN-DURR:1:5#3/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#3/r6.speaker: الجمهور
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#3/r6.claim: Most grammarians say the conjunction does not establish sequence; a group of Kufans disagrees.
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#3/r6.anchor: ولا تقتضي ترتيبا على قول الجمهور، خلافا لطائفة من الكوفيين

SAMIN-DURR:1:5#3/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#3/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#3/r7.claim: Nastaʿīnu derives from nastaʿwinu: a preceding kasra changes the quiescent wāw to yāʾ, as in mīzān and mīqāt.
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#3/r7.anchor: وأصل نستعين: نستعون مثل نستخرج في الصحيح

SAMIN-DURR:1:5#3/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#3/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#3/r8.claim: The sīn marks requesting help, while استفعل also conveys adoption, transformation, finding or deeming, causative and related meanings, and sometimes replaces other verb patterns.
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#3/r8.anchor: والسين فيه معناها الطلب، أي: نطلب منك العون على العبادة

SAMIN-DURR:1:5#4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#4/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#4/r1.claim: A dialect reads the imperfect prefix with kasra under stated conditions: not before yāʾ, and with a past stem having medial kasra, initial hamzat al-waṣl, or a reflexive tāʾ; ordinary forms such as yaḍribu lack these conditions.
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#4/r1.anchor: وقرئ " نستعين " بكسر حرف المضارعة، وهي لغة مطردة

SAMIN-DURR:1:5#4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#4/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#4/r2.claim: The supposed restriction against yāʾ is challenged by the reported form ييلمون, while ييجل is offered as an attempted sound-easing exception.
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#4/r2.anchor: وقد قرئ: فإنهم ييلمون [النساء: 104]، وهي هادمة لهذا الاستثناء

SAMIN-DURR:1:5#4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#4/r3.speaker: النابغة الجعدي
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#4/r3.claim: Al-Nābigha asks Laylā al-Akhyaliyya whether they take shelter from severe cold; her kasra-prefix reply نكتني prompts his bawdy joke and demonstrates the dialect.
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#4/r3.anchor: فقال لها النابغة الجعدي وعرف أنها تقع فيما أراد: فكيف تصنعون؟

SAMIN-DURR:1:5#4/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#4/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#4/r4.claim: Seeking help is requesting assistance and support.
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#4/r4.anchor: والاستعانة: طلب العون، وهو المظاهرة والنصرة

SAMIN-DURR:1:5#4/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#4/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#4/r5.claim: Worship precedes the request for help because worship is the means leading to a requested need.
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#4/r5.anchor: وقدم العبادة على الاستعانة لأنها وصلة لطلب الحاجة

SAMIN-DURR:1:5#4/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#4/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#4/r6.claim: Neither verb names an object, allowing the wording to encompass every object of worship or aid, or to focus on performing the acts without regard to an object.
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#4/r6.anchor: وأطلق كلا من فعلي العبادة والاستعانة فلم يذكر لهما مفعولا ليتناولا كل معبود به وكل مستعان

SAMIN-DURR:1:5#4/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#4/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#4/r7.claim: The objectless wording can also present eating and drinking simply as acts to perform.
SAMIN-DURR:1:5#4/r7.anchor: أو يكون المراد وقوع الفعل من غير نظر إلى مفعول نحو: كلوا واشربوا

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r1.claim: Most scholars place al-Fātiḥah among the earliest sūrahs revealed in Makkah.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r1.anchor: to have been revealed in Makkah

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r2.speaker: Mujāhid
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r2.claim: Mujāhid says al-Fātiḥah was revealed in Madinah.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r2.anchor: According to Mujāhid (d. 104/722–23), one of the leading scholars among the second generation of Muslims, this sūrah was revealed in Madinah

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r3.claim: Most scholars reject a Medinan origin because Muslims needed the sūrah to perform obligatory prayers.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r3.anchor: Most scholars claim that this is impossible, however, as the Muslims would not have been able to perform their required prayers without it

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r4.claim: Al-Fātiḥah means The Opening: it opens the Book, each prayer cycle, many everyday acts, and may open the breast to faith.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r4.anchor: The primary meaning of al-Fātiḥah is “The Opening,” which indicates the sūrah’s function as “the opening of the Book”

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r5.claim: The sūrah is seen as a synthesis and the Quran’s most important chapter, hence Umm al-kitāb; the title also refers to 3:7 and the celestial archetype of scripture.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r5.anchor: has been given the title Umm al-kitāb, “Mother of the Book,” a

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r6.claim: It is called the Mother of the Quran because it contains the meaning of the entire Quran.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r6.anchor: It is also known as “The Mother of the Quran” (IK, Ṭ), a reference to its containing the meaning of the entire Quran

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r7.claim: Another title, The Seven Oft-Repeated, is linked to 15:87.

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r8.claim: The title The Cure reflects its reputed healing power for body and soul.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r8.anchor: is said to have healing powers for both body and soul

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r9.claim: The title The Foundation reflects the Fātiḥah’s role as a foundation for the whole Quran.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r9.anchor: because it serves as a foundation

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r10.claim: As Sūrat al-Ḥamd and Sūrat al-Ṣalāh, the Fātiḥah begins each prayer cycle for Sunnis and many Shiites.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r10.anchor: the Fātiḥah is recited at the beginning of each

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r11.claim: Shiite law permits reciting the Fātiḥah in the third and fourth cycles or an alternative formula praising God.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r11.anchor: In Shiite law one is allowed to recite the Fātiḥah

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r12.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r12.claim: Muslims recite the Fātiḥah at diverse life events; funeral services are called fātiḥah in some lands as an opening from one life to another.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r12.anchor: It is also recited by Muslims on occasions as diverse as a funeral, a wedding, the birth of a child, the inauguration of an official event

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r13.speaker: Prophet Muhammad
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r13.claim: The Prophet identifies the Fātiḥah as the greatest sūrah, calling it Praise be to God and the seven oft-repeated, and linking it to 15:87.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r13.anchor: the Prophet told a man that he would teach him the greatest sūrah; when asked what it was, the Prophet responded

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r14.speaker: God
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r14.claim: In a hadith qudsī, God responds to the servant’s praise, magnification, and glorification during the prayer, which is divided between them.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r14.anchor: I have divided the prayer between Myself and My

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r15.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r15.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r15.claim: The Fātiḥah is a prayer encapsulating metaphysical and eschatological realities and teaches the proper human disposition toward God.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r15.anchor: the Fātiḥah is more than the confessional prayer of Muslims. It is a prayer that encapsulates all the metaphysical and eschatological realities

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r16.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r16.claim: Its structure moves from God’s nature in the first three verses, through the God-human relationship, to human states in the final three.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r16.anchor: The Fātiḥah thus has a threefold structure: the first three verses deal with the nature of God, the middle verse deals with the relationship between God and human beings

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r17.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r17.speaker: Prophet Muhammad
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r17.claim: A report says nothing like the Fātiḥah was revealed in the Torah, Psalms, Gospel, or Quran.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r17.anchor: In one the Prophet says, “By Him in Whose Hand lies my soul, in neither the Torah, the Psalms, the Gospel, nor the Quran was the like of it revealed”

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r18.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r18.speaker: Mujāhid
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r18.claim: One attribution says Satan was frightened when the Fātiḥah was revealed, among four events; others attribute the saying to the Prophet.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r18.anchor: attributed by some to Mujāhid (Q) and by

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r19.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r19.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r19.claim: The Fātiḥah’s exalted status generated many independent commentaries, often showing how the Quran as a whole is contained in it.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r19.anchor: The exalted status of the Fātiḥah has resulted in numerous independent commentaries upon it, some numbering hundreds of pages

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r20.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r20.speaker: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r20.claim: A saying attributed to ʿAlī compresses the Quran into the Fātiḥah, the basmalah, its opening bāʾ, and the diacritical point beneath it.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r20.anchor: a famous saying attributed to ʿAlī ibn AbīṬālib

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r21.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r21.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r21.claim: The point beneath bāʾ can symbolize the Divine Pen’s first drop of ink, which inscribed all archetypes on the Preserved Tablet before creation; thus basmalah marks both Quranic and cosmic beginnings.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r21.anchor:
This point can be understood to represent the first
drop of ink

STUDYQURAN:1:5/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:5/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:5/r1.claim: Verse 5 shifts from describing God to direct second-person address; the first-person plural represents people and creation, expressing humility before God.
STUDYQURAN:1:5/r1.anchor: In v. 5 begins the direct address of God in the second person, a marked change from the praise and description of God in vv. 1–4

STUDYQURAN:1:5/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:5/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:5/r2.claim: Naʿbudu means worship, servitude, obedience, and adoration; the verse acknowledges all creation as God’s servants and places the direct object before the verb to express complete servitude.
STUDYQURAN:1:5/r2.anchor: We worship renders the verb naʿbudu, which also indicates servitude, obedience, and adoration

STUDYQURAN:1:5/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:5/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:5/r3.claim: Direct second-person address establishes an I-Thou relation and gives every person access to God without a priestly intermediary; worshippers should be fully present and devote religion solely to Him.
STUDYQURAN:1:5/r3.anchor: Addressing God in the second person rather than the third person indicates a direct I-Thou relationship

STUDYQURAN:1:5/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:5/r4.speaker: Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq
STUDYQURAN:1:5/r4.claim: Jaʿfar distinguishes worship from fear, for reward, and from love; worship out of love is free worship and most excellent.
STUDYQURAN:1:5/r4.anchor: Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq is reported to have said

STUDYQURAN:1:5/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:5/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:5/r5.claim: Some define true servitude as maximal humility and self-effacement; it acknowledges human poverty and reliance on God (47:38).
STUDYQURAN:1:5/r5.anchor: the greatest degree of humility and self-effacement before God

STUDYQURAN:1:5/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:5/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:5/r6.claim: Servitude precedes seeking help because one first recognizes the sovereign’s power; help is requested for worship and all affairs, since people never act independently or worship by their own strength.
STUDYQURAN:1:5/r6.anchor: The expression of servitude necessarily precedes the statement that one “seeks help” from God

TAB-FULL:v1p155/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p155/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p155/r2.claim: Ṭabarī says the accusative is unnecessary: revelation commands Muhammad to say both the descriptions of God and then the direct address, and Arabic allows this shift within reported speech.
TAB-FULL:v1p155/r2.anchor: قل أيضا يا محمد: {إياك نعبد وإياك نستعين} [الفاتحة: 5]

TAB-FULL:v1p157/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p157/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p157/r1.claim: Poetry by Abū Kabīr al-Hudhalī and Labīd, and Qurʾān 10:22, show that Arabic can move from third-person report to direct address without requiring a vocative construction.
TAB-FULL:v1p157/r1.anchor: حتى إذا كنتم في الفلك وجرين بهم بريح طيبة

TAB-FULL:v1p159/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p159/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p159/r1.claim: The worship clause means humbling, submitting, and lowering ourselves to God in acknowledgment of His lordship, exclusively; al-Ṭabarī prefers this sense to fear and hope because servitude is rooted in abasement.
TAB-FULL:v1p159/r1.anchor: وإنما اخترنا البيان عن تأويله بأنه بمعنى نخشع ونذل ونستكين، دون البيان عنه بأنه بمعنى نرجو ونخاف

TAB-FULL:v1p159/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p159/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p159/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports Gabriel's gloss to Muhammad: worship means affirming God's oneness, fearing and hoping in Him alone.
TAB-FULL:v1p159/r2.anchor: إياك نوحد ونخاف ونرجو يا ربنا لا غيرك

TAB-FULL:v1p159/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p159/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p159/r3.claim: Arabic calls a road trodden and subdued by feet maʿbad, and a camel subdued for errands maʿbad; the servant's name reflects subjection to its master, supporting worship as abasement.
TAB-FULL:v1p159/r3.anchor: الطريق المذلل الذي قد وطئته الأقدام وذللته السابلة

TAB-FULL:v1p161/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p161/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p161/r1.claim: The supplication seeks God's help alone for worship, obedience, and every affair; unlike idolaters who seek aid from their idols, believers serve God sincerely.
TAB-FULL:v1p161/r1.anchor: وإياك ربنا نستعين على عبادتنا إياك وطاعتنا لك وفي أمورنا كلها، لا أحد سواك

TAB-FULL:v1p161/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p161/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p161/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the request as seeking God's help in obeying Him and in all affairs.
TAB-FULL:v1p161/r2.anchor: قال: إياك نستعين على طاعتك وعلى أمورنا كلها

TAB-FULL:v1p161/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p161/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p161/r3.claim: Help is requested for the remaining lifetime and future obedience, not completed past deeds; enabling the limbs and granting success are divine favor and لطف, whose unequal bestowal is neither mismanagement nor injustice.
TAB-FULL:v1p161/r3.anchor: أن يعينه فيما بقي من عمره على ما كلفه من طاعته، دون ما قد تقضى ومضى من أعماله الصالحة فيما خلا من عمره

TAB-FULL:v1p161/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p161/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p161/r4.claim: The prayer for help refutes Qadariyyah proponents of tafwīḍ, who claim God must grant each commanded person the assistance needed to act or refrain; otherwise asking help would amount to asking God not to commit injustice.
TAB-FULL:v1p161/r4.anchor: أدل الدليل على فساد قول القائلين بالتفويض من أهل القدر

TAB-FULL:v1p161/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p161/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p161/r5.claim: Worship may precede the request for help because worship and its enabling aid necessarily accompany one another, like saying either that someone fulfilled a need and thereby helped, or helped and thereby fulfilled it.
TAB-FULL:v1p161/r5.anchor: كان سواء تقديم ما قدم منهما على صاحبه، كما سواء قولك للرجل إذا قضى حاجتك فأحسن إليك

TAB-FULL:v1p161/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p161/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p161/r6.claim: He rejects the suggestion that the sequence uses a fronted phrase whose intended meaning comes later, a proposal attributed to some inattentive readers and illustrated by Imruʾ al-Qays.
TAB-FULL:v1p161/r6.anchor: وقد ظن بعض أهل الغفلة أن ذلك من المقدم الذي معناه التأخير، كما قال امرؤ القيس

TAB-FULL:v1p163/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p163/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p163/r1.claim: The Imruʾ al-Qays analogy fails: having enough money does not entail giving up desire for more, whereas worship and the aid enabling it necessarily coexist, so their order is not semantic reversal.
TAB-FULL:v1p163/r1.anchor: ومن مشابهة بيت امرئ القيس بمعزل؛ من أجل أنه قد يكفيه القليل من المال ويطلب الكثير

TAB-FULL:v1p163/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p163/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p163/r2.claim: The repeated second-person object is idiomatic and more eloquent: Arabic repeats a pronoun with each verb, whether attached after the verb or fronted within iyyāka, though omission is possible when attached.
TAB-FULL:v1p163/r2.anchor: كان كذلك إذا قدمت كناية اسم المخاطب قبل الفعل موصولة بإيا، كان الأفصح إعادتها مع كل فعل

TAB-FULL:v1p163/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p163/r3.speaker: بعض من لم يمعن النظر
TAB-FULL:v1p163/r3.claim: Some inattentive readers compare the repeated iyyāka before nastaʿīn to paired repetitions in poetic expressions such as between one person and another.
TAB-FULL:v1p163/r3.anchor: وقد ظن بعض من لم يمعن النظر أن إعادة إياك مع نستعين بعد تقدمها في قوله:

TAB-FULL:v1p164/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p164/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p164/r1.claim: The analogy to paired phrases with bayna is mistaken: bayna requires two complements, so omitting one makes the sentence defective, while iyyāka nعبد is already a complete clause.
TAB-FULL:v1p164/r1.anchor: ليس ذلك حكم بين لأنها لا تكون إذا اقتضت اثنين إلا تكريرا إذا أعيدت

TAB-FULL:v1p164/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p164/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p164/r2.claim: Each clause independently needs its object pronoun, just as every verb may repeat its attached object; therefore iyyāka properly recurs before nastaʿīn.
TAB-FULL:v1p164/r2.anchor: فكان معلوما بذلك أن حاجة كل كلمة كانت نظيرة

TAB-FULL:v1p199/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p199/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p199/r2.claim: Answering why al-Fātiḥa has seven verses if two contain its meanings: earlier scriptures each included only some meanings, while the Qur'an gathers all of them for Muhammad's community and adds many more.
TAB-FULL:v1p199/r2.anchor: إن الله تعالى ذكره جمع لنبينا محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ولأمته بما أنزل إليه من كتابه معاني لم يجمعهن بكتاب

TAB-FULL:v1p199/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p199/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p199/r3.claim: The Torah is admonition and detailed instruction, Psalms praise and glorification, and Gospel admonition and reminder, but none has a miracle proving its recipient; the Qur'an contains these meanings and more.
TAB-FULL:v1p199/r3.anchor: كالتوراة التي هي مواعظ وتفصيل، والزبور الذي هو تحميد وتمجيد، والإنجيل الذي هو مواعظ وتذكير؛ لا معجزة في واحد منها

TAB-FULL:v1p199/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p199/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p199/r4.claim: Among the Qur'an's distinctive merits is its miraculous arrangement and composition: rhetoricians cannot compose even a sura as short as one of its chapters.
TAB-FULL:v1p199/r4.anchor: نظمه العجيب، ورصفه الغريب، وتأليفه البديع، الذي عجزت عن نظم مثل أصغر سورة منه الخطباء

TAB-FULL:v1p203/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p203/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة عن رسول الله
TAB-FULL:v1p203/r2.claim: The Prophet reports God praises the servant’s recitation of praise, mercy, and sovereignty, then says the invocation from You alone we worship through the end belongs to the servant.
TAB-FULL:v1p203/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " إذا قال العبد: {الحمد لله رب العالمين}

TABATABAI:1:1-5/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:1-5/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:1-5/r3.claim: Rahim guides believers to Gods special mercy, their happiness in the afterlife and meeting their Lord.
TABATABAI:1:1-5/r3.anchor: وهو الرحيم يبين لهم سبيل رحمته الخاصة بالمؤمنين وهو سعادة آخرتهم ولقاء ربهم

TABATABAI:1:5#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:5#3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:5#3/r2.claim: A servant is a human or any conscious being in a state of ownership; worship is setting oneself in the position of one's Lord's possession.
TABATABAI:1:5#3/r2.anchor: فكأن العبادة هي نصب العبد نفسه في مقام المملوكية لربه

TABATABAI:1:5#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:5#3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:5#3/r3.claim: Worship differs from mere humility in grammar and meaning: the lexicographer's account of servitude as submission captures an implication, since worship takes a direct object while submission takes li.
TABATABAI:1:5#3/r3.anchor: فالخضوع متعد باللام والعبادة متعدية بنفسها

TABATABAI:1:5#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:5#3/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:5#3/r4.claim: Worship is incompatible with arrogance but can be shared, as shown by the prohibition on associating another in worship; arrogance, by contrast, cannot coexist with worship.
TABATABAI:1:5#3/r4.anchor: فمن الجائز أن يشترك أزيد من الواحد في ملك رقبة أو في عبادة عبد

TABATABAI:1:5#3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:5#3/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:5#3/r5.claim: Human masters own only some voluntary acts and have limited rights, but God owns every aspect of servants without condition; thus God alone is owner and every other being wholly owned.
TABATABAI:1:5#3/r5.anchor: فهو تعالى مالك على الاطلاق من غير شرط ولا قيد وغيره مملوك على الاطلاق من غير شرط ولا قيد

TABATABAI:1:5#3/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:5#3/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:5#3/r6.claim: This absolute ownership on both sides creates a twofold exclusivity: God alone is master and the servant is wholly devoted, expressed by fronting the object and leaving worship unrestricted.
TABATABAI:1:5#3/r6.anchor: الرب مقصور في المالكية، والعبد مقصور في العبودية

TABATABAI:1:5#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:5#4/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:5#4/r1.claim: Because everything besides God is wholly owned by Him, nothing can truly veil Him; God is universally present to every thing.

TABATABAI:1:5#4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:5#4/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:5#4/r2.claim: True worship requires God's presence as the addressed object and the servant's undivided attention, rather than a lifeless outward form or divided inward focus.
TABATABAI:1:5#4/r2.anchor: فأن يكون عبادته عبادة عبد حاضر من غير أن يغيب في عبادته

TABATABAI:1:5#4/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:5#4/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:5#4/r3.claim: Worship that shares attention with idols, other aims, Paradise as a bargain, or fear of Hell is shirk; sincere religion belongs to God alone.
TABATABAI:1:5#4/r3.anchor: فإن ذلك كله من الشرك في العبادة الذي ورد عنه النهي

TABATABAI:1:5#4/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:5#4/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:5#4/r4.claim: The plural first-person pronoun humbles the individual by dissolving a sense of separate selfhood and independence into the wider community of worshippers.
TABATABAI:1:5#4/r4.anchor: فإن فيه هضما للنفس بإلغاء تعينها وشخوصها وحدها

TABATABAI:1:5#5/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:5#5/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:5#5/r1.claim: The author defers discussion of the changed address in the request for guidance to a later passage.
TABATABAI:1:5#5/r1.anchor: فسيجيء الكلام فيه إن شاء الله تعالى

TABATABAI:1:5#5/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:5#5/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:5#5/r2.claim: The prior discussion explains the shift to direct address, object-fronting for exclusivity, unrestricted worship, the plural pronoun, and the relation of the two clauses.
TABATABAI:1:5#5/r2.anchor: الوجه في الحصر الذي يفيده تقديم المفعول، والوجه في إطلاق قوله نعبد

TABATABAI:1:5#5/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:5#5/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:5#5/r3.claim: The author notes that other commentators give additional subtleties and sends readers to their books.
TABATABAI:1:5#5/r3.anchor: وقد ذكر المفسرون نكات أخرى في أطراف ذلك من أرادها فليراجع كتبهم

TABATABAI:1:6-7#10/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#10/r2.speaker: الصادق
TABATABAI:1:6-7#10/r2.claim: Al-Sadiq distinguishes worship from fear, which is servitude, and reward-seeking, which is hired labor; worship from love is free worship and best.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#10/r2.anchor: وقوم عبدوا الله عز وجل حبا، فتلك عبادة الأحرار، وهي أفضل العبادة

TABATABAI:1:6-7#10/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#10/r3.speaker: علي
TABATABAI:1:6-7#10/r3.claim: Ali describes worship from desire as merchants' worship, fear as slaves' worship, and gratitude as free people's worship.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#10/r3.anchor: وإن قوما عبدوا الله شكرا فتلك عبادة الأحرار

TABATABAI:1:6-7#10/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#10/r4.speaker: الصادق
TABATABAI:1:6-7#10/r4.claim: Al-Sadiq says reward-seeking is the worship of the greedy, fear of Hell the worship of slaves, and loving God the worship of the noble; one who loves God is loved and made secure.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#10/r4.anchor: ولكني أعبده حبا له عز وجل فتلك عبادة الكرام

TABATABAI:1:6-7#10/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#10/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7#10/r5.claim: Love and gratitude in these reports converge: gratitude places a gift where it belongs, and worship belongs to God for His own perfection and beauty, which is inherently lovable.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#10/r5.anchor: فليس الحب إلا الميل إلى الجمال والانجذاب نحوه

TABATABAI:1:6-7#10/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#10/r6.speaker: الصادق
TABATABAI:1:6-7#10/r6.claim: A report through a general transmission from al-Sadiq reads You alone we worship as seeking only God, without a substitute or reward, unlike those ignorant of His presence.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#10/r6.anchor: لا نريد منك غيرك ولا نعبدك بالعوض والبدل
