TABATABAI:1:6-7#10/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#10/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7#10/r7.claim: The report confirms that worship requires attentive presence and sincerity, with no substitutionary aim.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#10/r7.anchor: من استلزام معنى العبادة للحضور وللإخلاص الذي ينافي قصد البدل

TABATABAI:1:6-7#10/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#10/r8.speaker: الصادق
TABATABAI:1:6-7#10/r8.claim: Al-Sadiq rejects worship through an attribute detached from perception as addressing an absent object, and rejects worship of both attribute and described essence as violating tawhid.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#10/r8.anchor: ومن زعم أنه يعبد بالصفة لا بالإدراك فقد أحال على غائب

TABATABAI:1:6-7#11/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#11/r6.speaker: النبي
TABATABAI:1:6-7#11/r6.claim: The Prophet transmits God's division of al-Fatiha between Himself and the servant: each phrase receives divine acknowledgement and a tailored promise of blessing, mercy, ease of judgment, reward, help, and fulfillment of the servant's requests.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#11/r6.anchor: قسمت فاتحة الكتاب بيني وبين عبدي فنصفها لي ونصفها لعبدي، ولعبدي ما سأل

TABRISI:1:5/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:5/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:1:5/r1.claim: Worship linguistically means abasement, as in a road worn smooth by traffic or a camel coated with tar; seeking assistance means asking for help.
TABRISI:1:5/r1.anchor: العبادة في اللغة هي الذلة يقال: طريق معبد أي: مذلل بكثرة الوطء

TABRISI:1:5/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:5/r2.speaker: أبو إسحاق الزجاج
TABRISI:1:5/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj parses iyyaka as an accusative pronoun stem with the following kaf in genitive annexation.
TABRISI:1:5/r2.anchor: موضع إياك نصب بوقوع الفعل عليه وموضع الكاف في إياك خفض بإضافة إيا إليها

TABRISI:1:5/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:5/r3.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
TABRISI:1:5/r3.claim: Abu Ali rejects treating iyyā as a noun: its form changes and it cannot stand in nominative or genitive contexts like an ordinary noun.
TABRISI:1:5/r3.anchor: إن إيا ليس بظاهر بل هو مضمر يدل على ذلك تغير ذاته وامتناع ثباته في حال الرفع والجر

TABRISI:1:5/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:5/r4.speaker: المبرد عن الأخفش
TABRISI:1:5/r4.claim: Al-Akhfash, transmitted by al-Mubarrad, treats iyyā as a singular pronoun whose ending changes with person and number; kaf marks address and has no case role.
TABRISI:1:5/r4.anchor: وحكى السراج عن المبرد عن أبي الحسن الأخفش أنه اسم مفرد مضمر يتغير آخره كما تتغير أواخر المضمرات

TABRISI:1:5/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:5/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:1:5/r5.claim: The author treats yā, hā, and the other suffixes in iyyā as person markers attached to a pronoun, and allows emphatic pronouns after it.
TABRISI:1:5/r5.anchor: وهكذا الحكم في إياي وإيانا وإياها في أنها حروف تلحق إيا فالياء في إياي دليل على التكلم

TABRISI:1:5/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:5/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:1:5/r6.claim: Nastaʿīn originally had waw from maʿūna; the waw changed to yā under the preceding kasra, with its vowel shifted to the preceding consonant.
TABRISI:1:5/r6.anchor: والأصل في نستعين: نستعون لأنه من المعونة والعون لكن الواو قلبت ياء لثقل الكسرة عليها

TABRISI:1:5/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:5/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:1:5/r7.claim: Naʿbudu and nastaʿīn are indicative because they occupy positions that can be filled by nouns; the present tense takes inflection because it resembles a noun.
TABRISI:1:5/r7.anchor: وقوله نعبد ونستعين مرفوع لوقوعه موقعا يصلح للاسم ألا ترى أنك لو قلت أنا عابدك وأنا مستعينك لقام مقامه

TABRISI:1:5#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:5#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:1:5#2/r1.claim: Fronting iyyaka makes the worship and request exclusive: we worship You alone and ask help from You alone.
TABRISI:1:5#2/r1.anchor: أدل على الاختصاص من أن نقول نعبدك ونستعينك لأن معناه نعبدك ولا نعبد سواك ونستعينك ولا نستعين غيرك

TABRISI:1:5#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:5#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:1:5#2/r2.claim: Worship is the highest gratitude: utmost submission joined with utmost reverence, owed only to God as giver of life's foundational blessings.
TABRISI:1:5#2/r2.anchor: والعبادة ضرب من الشكر وغاية فيه لأنها الخضوع بأعلى مراتب الخضوع مع التعظيم بأعلى مراتب التعظيم

TABRISI:1:5#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:5#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:1:5#2/r3.claim: The author rejects defining worship simply as obedience: obeying a parent or master does not itself make a person their worshiper, and idolaters worship without receiving commands from idols.
TABRISI:1:5#2/r3.anchor: وقول من قال: إن العبادة هي الطاعة للمعبود يفسد بأن الطاعة موافقة الأمر

TABRISI:1:5#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:5#2/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:1:5#2/r4.claim: Nastaʿīn means asking God for success and assistance in worship and all affairs; tawfiq combines all causes needed for an act to occur.
TABRISI:1:5#2/r4.anchor: ومعنى قوله إياك نستعين إياك نستوفق ونطلب المعونة على عبادتك وعلى أمورنا كلها والتوفيق هو أن يجمع بين جميع الأسباب

TABRISI:1:5#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:5#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:1:5#2/r5.claim: One explanation for repeating iyyaka is to prevent the mistaken impression that worship and seeking help cannot be separated.
TABRISI:1:5#2/r5.anchor: لو اقتصر على واحد ربما توهم متوهم أنه لا يتقرب إلى الله تعالى إلا بالجمع بينهما

TABRISI:1:5#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:5#2/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:1:5#2/r6.claim: Another explanation treats the repetition as emphasis, though the author questions that account because the second iyyaka is governed by a second verb.
TABRISI:1:5#2/r6.anchor: وقيل إنه جمع بينهما للتأكيد كما يقال الدار بين زيد وبين عمرو

TABRISI:1:5#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:5#3/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:1:5#3/r1.claim: A further explanation is that the verse teaches renewing mention of God whenever a new need arises.
TABRISI:1:5#3/r1.anchor: وقيل أيضا إنه تعليم لنا في تجديد ذكره تعالى عند كل حاجة

TABRISI:1:5#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:5#3/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:1:5#3/r2.claim: Although divine aid is necessary, the verse puts worship before asking for help: it requests the appeal for aid, which can follow an act of worship, not the aid itself.
TABRISI:1:5#3/r2.anchor: فالجواب: أنه قدم العبادة على الاستعانة لا على الإعانة وقد تأتي بغير استعانة

TABRISI:1:5#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:5#3/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:1:5#3/r3.claim: The prayer seeks help for future worship, and asking remains fitting under obligation because the servant shows dependence; prayer may also be needed before God grants a further grace.
TABRISI:1:5#3/r3.anchor: وقيل إن السؤال للمعونة إنما يقع على عبادة مستأنفة لا على عبادة واقعة منهم وإنما حسن طلب المعونة

TABRISI:1:5#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:5#3/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:1:5#3/r4.claim: The author rejects using this prayer to prove that ability coincides with the act: one may ask for unprovided divine favors that strengthen motivation and ease obedience.
TABRISI:1:5#3/r4.anchor: وقد أخطأ من استدل بهذه الآية على أن القدرة مع الفعل من حيث إن القدرة لو كانت متقدمة لما كان لطلب المعونة وجه

TABRISI:1:5#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:5#3/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:1:5#3/r5.claim: A second reason to ask is to retain capacity for future obedience over time or to avoid acts that would cancel capacity, depending on one's theory of its persistence.
TABRISI:1:5#3/r5.anchor: والثاني: أن يطلب بقاء كونه قادرا على طاعته المستقبلة بأن تجدد له القدرة حالا بعد حال

TABRISI:1:5#3/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:5#3/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:1:5#3/r6.claim: The move from third-person reference to direct address is a familiar Arabic rhetorical shift, illustrated by Labid and Abu Kathir al-Hudhali.
TABRISI:1:5#3/r6.anchor: وأما العدول عن الخبر إلى الخطاب في قوله إياك نعبد إلى آخر السورة فعلى عادة العرب المشهورة وأشعارهم من ذلك مملوءة

TABRISI:1:5#4/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:5#4/r1.speaker: الكسائي
TABRISI:1:5#4/r1.claim: Al-Kisa'i supplies an implicit command to say these words, as in Qur'anic scenes where people say 'Our Lord, we have seen' and 'Peace'.
TABRISI:1:5#4/r1.anchor: وقال الكسائي: تقديره قولوا إياك نعبد أو قل يا محمد هذا

THALABI:v1p103/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p103/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v1p103/r4.claim: In the divine report dividing prayer between God and the servant, the basmala glorifies God, al-ḥamdu praises Him, al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm extols Him, Mālik delegates the matter, the worship-and-help verse is shared, and guidance is granted to the servant.
THALABI:v1p103/r4.anchor: عن أبي هريرة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «يقول الله: قسمت الصلاة بيني وبين عبادي نصفين

THALABI:v1p117/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p117/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p117/r1.claim: The verse shifts from third-person report to direct address, an instance of rhetorical turn; another analysis supplies the omitted command “say: You alone.”
THALABI:v1p117/r1.anchor: رجع من الخبر الى الخطاب على التلوين. وقيل فيه إضمار، أي قولوا: إياك

THALABI:v1p117/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p117/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p117/r2.claim: Iyyāka is an object-case pronoun, with the kāf in a genitive relation to the pronoun; its attachment to a pronoun is illustrated by poetry and ordinary speech.
THALABI:v1p117/r2.anchor: وإيا كلمة ضمير، لكنه لا يكون إلا في موضع النصب، والكاف في محل الخفض بإضافة إيا إليها

THALABI:v1p117/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p117/r3.speaker: الخليل
THALABI:v1p117/r3.claim: Al-Khalīl reports that Arabs say “iyyāhu wa-iyyākum” when a man reaches sixty.
THALABI:v1p117/r3.anchor: وحكى الخليل عن العرب: إذا بلغ الرجل الستين فإياه وإياكم

THALABI:v1p117/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p117/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p117/r4.claim: Iyyāka normally precedes the verb, as in “You I mean”; after the verb it occurs only under restriction, as in “I worship none but You.”
THALABI:v1p117/r4.anchor: ويستعمل مقدما على الفعل مثل (إياك أعني) و (إياك أسأل)

THALABI:v1p117/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p117/r5.speaker: أبو ميثم سهل بن محمد
THALABI:v1p117/r5.claim: Abū Maytham classifies pronouns as attached, detached, or implicit, giving examples of each and explaining their labels.
THALABI:v1p117/r5.anchor: وقال أبو ميثم سهل ابن محمد: إياك ضمير منفصل، والضمير ثلاثة أقسام

THALABI:v1p117/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p117/r6.speaker: أبو زيد
THALABI:v1p117/r6.claim: Abū Zayd analyzes iyyā as two yāʾs, one relational and one vocative, originally ay yā and merged.
THALABI:v1p117/r6.anchor: وقال أبو زيد: إنما هما ياءان: الأولى للنسبة والثانية للنداء

THALABI:v1p117/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p117/r7.speaker: أبو عبيد
THALABI:v1p117/r7.claim: Abū ʿUbayd derives iyyāka from awyāka, with wāw changed to yāʾ, connecting it to seeking refuge and turning toward an aim.
THALABI:v1p117/r7.anchor: وقال أبو عبيد: أصله (أوياك) ، فقلبت الواو ياء

THALABI:v1p117/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p117/r8.speaker: الفضل الرقاشي
THALABI:v1p117/r8.claim: Al-Faḍl al-Raqāshī reads the first alif of iyyāka with fatḥa, describing it as a dialect form.
THALABI:v1p117/r8.anchor: وقرأ الفضل الرقاشي (أياك) بفتح الألف وهي لغة

THALABI:v1p117/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p117/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p117/r9.claim: The fronted object is clearer and rhetorically better than naʿbuduka because attention turns from the worship to God, not from the worshiper toward the act.
THALABI:v1p117/r9.anchor: وإنما لم يقل: نعبدك [لأنه] يصح في العبارة، وأحسن الإشارة

THALABI:v1p117/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p117/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p117/r10.claim: The author glosses worship as affirming oneness, devoting oneself sincerely, obeying, and submitting; it is disciplining the self to bear hardship in obedience and originally means humility and submission.
THALABI:v1p117/r10.anchor: وقوله: نعبد أي نوحد ونخلص ونطيع ونخضع

THALABI:v1p117/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p117/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p117/r11.claim: The Arabic root of worship connotes humility and being trodden down, as in a leveled path; Ṭarafa’s verse supplies poetic evidence.
THALABI:v1p117/r11.anchor: والعبادة رياضة النفس على حمل المشاق في الطاعة

THALABI:v1p118/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p118/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p118/r1.claim: A camel described as maʿbad is coated with tar; Ṭarafa's verse illustrates the usage.
THALABI:v1p118/r1.anchor:
وبعير معبد إذا كان مطليا بالقطران، قال طرفة:
إلى أن تحامتني العشيرة كلها

THALABI:v1p118/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p118/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p118/r2.claim: The word ʿabd reflects a servant's abasement and submission to his master.
THALABI:v1p118/r2.anchor: وسمي العبد عبدا لذلته وانقياده لمولاه

THALABI:v1p118/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p118/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p118/r3.claim: Seeking help means asking aid for worship and for all one's affairs.
THALABI:v1p118/r3.anchor: نستوفي ونطلب المعونة على عبادتك وعلى أمورنا كلها

THALABI:v1p118/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p118/r4.speaker: الفراء
THALABI:v1p118/r4.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Riʾāb reads نستعين with a kasra; al-Farrāʾ says several tribes kasrate future markers except yāʾ, while Quraysh and Kināna open them, the more eloquent and common form.
THALABI:v1p118/r4.anchor: قال الفراء: تميم وقيس وأسد وربيعة يكسرون علامات المستقبل إلا الياء

THALABI:v1p118/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p118/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p118/r5.claim: Repeating إياك strengthens sincerity, exclusivity, and emphasis; the author adduces repeated phrasing in scripture and poetry.
THALABI:v1p118/r5.anchor: وإنما كرر إياك ليكون أدل على الإخلاص والاختصاص والتأكيد

THALABI:v1p118/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p118/r6.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
THALABI:v1p118/r6.claim: Worship is owed because God created people, and help is sought because God guided them.
THALABI:v1p118/r6.anchor: وقال أبو بكر الوراق: إياك نعبد لأنك خلقتنا، وإياك نستعين لأنك هديتنا

THALABI:v1p118/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p118/r7.speaker: أبو الحسن علي بن عبد الرحمن الفران
THALABI:v1p118/r7.claim: Al-Farrān gives several paired reasons: God is maker and people made, worship earns Paradise, help averts Fire, people are servants and God generous, and God alone is truly worshipped.
THALABI:v1p118/r7.anchor: إياك نعبد لأنك الصانع، وإياك نستعين لأن المصنوع لا غنى به عن الصانع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p505#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p505#2/r1.speaker: الخليل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p505#2/r1.claim: Al-Khalīl analyzes iyyā as a pronoun with kāf attached in genitive; Abū ʿUthmān is also said to hold this view.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p505#2/r1.anchor: ذهب الخليل # إلى أن (إيا) اسم مضمر، مضاف إلى (الكاف) وهذا -أيضا- مذهب أبي عثمان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p505#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p505#2/r2.speaker: أبو الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p505#2/r2.claim: Abū al-Ḥasan treats iyyā itself as a pronoun whose ending changes with the number and person addressed; kāf merely marks address, as in dhālika.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p505#2/r2.anchor: وحكى أبو بكر (¬2) عن أبي العباس (¬3) عن أبي الحسن (¬4) أنه اسم مفرد مضمر يتغير آخره

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p505#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p505#2/r3.speaker: أبو الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p505#2/r3.claim: According to the transmitted account, Abū al-Ḥasan disallows combinations such as iyyā-ka with iyyā of Zayd or falsehood.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p505#2/r3.anchor: لا يجيز أبو الحسن فيما يحكى عنه: (إياك وإيا زيد) و (إياي وإيا الباطل)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p505#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p505#2/r4.speaker: سيبويه
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p505#2/r4.claim: Sibawayh reports hearing an Arab say that after sixty a man should beware of himself and young women.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p505#2/r4.anchor: وقال سيبويه: حدثني من لا أتهم عن الخليل أنه سمع أعرابيا يقول:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p505#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p505#2/r5.speaker: ابن كيسان
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p505#2/r5.claim: Ibn Kaysān attributes to some grammarians the view that the full form iyyāka is a noun; others take its final yāʾ, kāf, or hāʾ as the pronoun and iyyā as support.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p505#2/r5.anchor: وحكى ابن كيسان عن بعض النحويين أنه قال: (إياك) بكمالها: اسم.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p505#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p505#2/r6.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p505#2/r6.claim: Abū Isḥāq says kāf is genitive by adding it to iyyā, which can also take the other attached pronouns.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p505#2/r6.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: (الكاف) في (إياك) في موضع جر بإضافة (¬3) (إيا) إليها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p505#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p505#2/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p505#2/r7.claim: The author accepts only Abū al-Ḥasan's account: a pronoun is already maximally definite and has no need for the specificity of annexation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p505#2/r7.anchor: وليس يصح من هذه الأقوال إلا قول أبي الحسن (¬5). أما قول الخليل:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p505#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p505#2/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p505#2/r8.claim: The author rejects the full-word analysis as weak: like anta, iyyā is the pronoun, while the kāf's vowel marks masculine or feminine address.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p505#2/r8.anchor: فكما أن ما قبل التاء في (أنت) هو الاسم، والتاء حرف خطاب، كذلك (إيا) هو الاسم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p511/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p511/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p511/r1.claim: Pronouns divide into independent, attached, and hidden forms; they may be nominative, accusative, or genitive, though genitive pronouns have no independent form.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p511/r1.anchor: واعلم: أن الضمير ينقسم إلى ثلاثة أقسام (¬9): ظاهر منفصل، وظاهر # متصل، ومستكن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p511/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p511/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p511/r2.claim: A hidden pronoun is understood in a verb such as sat or stood because a verb cannot stand without a subject.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p511/r2.anchor: وأما المستكن فهو ما كان مستكنا في الفعل كقولك: قعد، وقام، فالضمير

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p511/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p511/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p511/r3.claim: Iyyā is built on sukūn because it resembles a particle; its final alif is original, like the alifs in lā, mā, ḥattā, and kallā.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p511/r3.anchor: واعلم: أن (إيا) مبنية على السكون؛ لأن فيها شبه الحرف، فهي مثل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p511/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p511/r4.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p511/r4.claim: Abū Isḥāq reportedly glosses iyyā-ka naʿbud as we worship Your reality and derives iyyā from āya, a sign.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p511/r4.anchor: عن أبي إسحاق قال (¬2): سمعته يقول وقد سئل عن معنى قوله: {إياك نعبد}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p511/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p511/r5.speaker: أبو الفتح
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p511/r5.claim: Abū al-Fatḥ rejects that derivation: pronouns are built forms, not derived words; since iyyā is a pronoun it should not be considered derived.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p511/r5.anchor: قال أبو الفتح: وحكى لي حاك عن أبي إسحاق قال (¬2): سمعته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p511/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p511/r6.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p511/r6.claim: The author of al-Naẓm explains iyyā as exclusivity: iyyā-ka ḍarabtu directs the act specifically to you, which also explains its use in warnings such as beware the lion.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p511/r6.anchor: وقال صاحب "النظم" (¬8): معنى (إيا) الاختصاص، وقول القائل: (إياك ضربت)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p516/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p516/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p516/r1.claim: Worship is obedience joined to submission and humility, a form of abasement due only to God; ʿabd reflects a servant's lowliness and a well-trodden road is muʿabbad.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p516/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {نعبد} معنى العبادة: الطاعة مع الخضوع والتذلل، وهو جنس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p516/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p516/r2.speaker: أبو بكر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p516/r2.claim: Abū Bakr says iyyā-ka is repeated for emphasis, like repeating bayna in the phrase between Zayd and ʿAmr.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p516/r2.anchor: قال أبو بكر: وإنما كرر (إياك) للتوكيد، كما تقول: بين زيد وبين عمرو خصومة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p516/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p516/r3.speaker: أبو بكر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p516/r3.claim: He also notes that each verb independently selects an object: if placed after the verbs the phrase would be naʿbuduka wa-nastaʿīnuka, and both take the fronted iyyā-ka.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p516/r3.anchor: قال: ولأن كل واحد من الفعلين يطلب مفعولا على حدته،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p516/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p516/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p516/r4.claim: The author prefers emphasis as the reason for repeating iyyā-ka, since Arabic can leave the shared object unspoken after the first coordinated verb.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p516/r4.anchor: والقول هو الأول (¬3)؛ لأن العرب إذا جمعت فعلين واقعين اكتفت بوقوع أحدهما من وقوع الآخر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p516/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p516/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p516/r5.claim: The omitted object in 93:3, mā qalā, means mā qalāka and illustrates that coordination can share an object without repeating it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p516/r5.anchor: قال الله تعالى: {ما ودعك ربك وما قلى} [الضحى: 3] أراد (وما قلاك)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p516/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p516/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p516/r6.claim: Putting worship before asking for help does not establish chronological order: the conjunction wāw joins things without requiring sequence.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p516/r6.anchor: والجواب: أن الواو عند النحويين لا توجب ترتيبا (¬6)، وإنما هي للجمع

WAHIDI-QT:1:5/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:1:5/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:1:5/r1.claim: Worship is obedience with submission; worship is reserved for God alone, and help is sought from Him.
WAHIDI-QT:1:5/r1.anchor: إياك نعبد أي نخصك ونقصدك بالعبادة وهي الطاعة مع الخضوع وإياك نستعين ومنك نطلب المعونة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:1:5-7/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:1:5-7/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:1:5-7/r1.claim: Worship means singling God out and directing oneself to Him in obedience joined with humility.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:1:5-7/r1.anchor: نخصك ونقصدك بالعبادة، وهي الطاعة مع الخضوع.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:1:5-7/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:1:5-7/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:1:5-7/r2.claim: The worshippers ask God alone for help.

ELMALILI:1:5/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5/r1.claim: Elmalılı renders the verse as worshipping and serving God alone and seeking aid and care from Him alone.
ELMALILI:1:5/r1.anchor: Meâl: Sâde sana ederiz kulluğu, ibadeti ve sâde senden dileriz ʿavni, inâyeti yâ Rab!

ELMALILI:1:5/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5/r2.claim: The imperative meaning 'say this' is implicit; placing the independent pronoun before the verb expresses exclusivity: to You alone, not another.
ELMALILI:1:5/r2.anchor: gelmesi kasr ve ihtisas ifade ettiğinden “başkasına değil ancak sana” demek olur

ELMALILI:1:5/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5/r3.claim: In legal usage, worship is a special act of obedience that earns reward, depends on intention, and expresses nearness to God.
ELMALILI:1:5/r3.anchor: “ibadet”, niyete mütevakkıf olarak yapılmasında sevab olan ve Cenâb-ı Allah’a kurbet ifade eden tâ‘at-i mahsûsadır

ELMALILI:1:5/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5/r4.claim: Taat is an act rewarded whether or not it depends on intention or the doer knows for whom it is done.
ELMALILI:1:5/r4.anchor: “Tâat”, niyete mütevakkıf olsun olmasın ve kimin için yapıldığı bilinsin bilinmesin yapılması sevab olan fiili yapmaktır

ELMALILI:1:5/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5/r5.claim: Qurbat is a rewarded act performed with awareness of the person one seeks to approach, even when intention is not required.
ELMALILI:1:5/r5.anchor: “Kurbet”, niyete mütevakkıf olmasa bile yapılması sevab olan fiili kime yapıldığını bilerek

ELMALILI:1:5/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5/r6.claim: Every worship act is both qurbat and taat, and every qurbat is taat, but the reverse implications do not hold.
ELMALILI:1:5/r6.anchor: Binâen‘aleyh her ibadet Allah’a bir kurbet

ELMALILI:1:5/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5/r7.claim: Reflection to know God is taat but not qurbat while its intended object remains unknown, and without intention it is not worship.
ELMALILI:1:5/r7.anchor: Meselâ ma‘rifetullah için fikr ü nazar bir

ELMALILI:1:5/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5/r8.claim: Qur'an recitation, charity, aid, endowment, and freeing slaves without required intention are qurbat and taat but not ibadat; prayer, fasting, alms, pilgrimage, and jihad with intention are all three.
ELMALILI:1:5/r8.anchor: Kur’an okumak, muhtaçlara yardım etmek, sadaka vermek, vakıf yapmak, köle azat etmek

ELMALILI:1:5/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5/r9.claim: Legal worship is conscious obedience and nearness directed only to God through the person's whole spiritual and bodily, outward and inward existence.
ELMALILI:1:5/r9.anchor: Demek ki ibâdet-i şer‘iye, insanın rûhen ve cismen, zâhiren ve bâtınen bütün mevcûdiyetiyle yalnız Allah’a yapılan şuurlu bir tâat ve kurbettir

ELMALILI:1:5/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5/r10.claim: Intention is a present, created will to obey God and draw near through the act; resolve comes before action, purpose accompanies it, and intention joins knowledge to the act.
ELMALILI:1:5/r10.anchor: Niyet ise yapılacak fiilin îcâdında ancak Allah’a tâat ve tekarrub kast etmek demek olan irâde-i hâdisedir

ELMALILI:1:5/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5/r11.claim: Full awareness, containing both knowledge and will, belongs to the soul and heart.
ELMALILI:1:5/r11.anchor: Hem ilim ve hem iradeyi ihtivâ eden bu şu‘ûr-i tâm rûh ve kalbin bir işidir

ELMALILI:1:5/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5/r12.claim: Worship also requires an outwardly manifested act of obedience; inward reflection alone may be taat and qurbat but does not become worship.
ELMALILI:1:5/r12.anchor: ind-i ilâhîde tâat olan bir fiil izhâr edilmiş olmak lâzımdır ki ibadet olsun

ELMALILI:1:5/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5/r13.claim: Faith requires at least verbal confession as well as inward assent, while an unexpressed inner thought is insufficient as worship.
ELMALILI:1:5/r13.anchor: imanda sadece tasdîk-i kalbî kifayet etmez de bunun hiç olmazsa lisânen ikrar ile zâhire ihrâc edilmesi dahi lâzım gelir

ELMALILI:1:5/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5/r14.claim: External ritual acts without intention are not worship: sleep is not prayer, hunger is not fasting, giving is not alms, travel is not pilgrimage, and fighting is not jihad.
ELMALILI:1:5/r14.anchor: Niyetsiz yatıp kalkmak namaz değil, niyetsiz aç durmak oruç değil, niyetsiz sadaka vermek, i‘âne yapmak zekât değil

ELMALILI:1:5/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5/r15.claim: A bad intention, meaning an aim other than obedience and nearness to God, prevents an act from counting as worship.
ELMALILI:1:5/r15.anchor: sû’-i niyetle, yani Allah’a itaat ve kurbet kasdından mâ‘adâ bir maksadla yapılan fiiller hiç ibadet olmaz

ELMALILI:1:5/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5/r16.claim: Turkish tapmak and tapınmak suggest indiscriminate or unconscious obedience and are associated with idols and the cross, so translating worship that way debases the language; kulluk is more aware but weaker than worship.
ELMALILI:1:5/r16.anchor: “tapmak” ve “tapınmak” kelimelerinde az çok ne yaptığını bilmemek gibi bir şuursuzluk mânası anlarız

ELMALILI:1:5/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5/r17.claim: Before later legal convention, the shared lexical root meaning of worship should be considered; its broadest sense appears in ubudet or abed and includes worshipper and object of worship.
ELMALILI:1:5/r17.anchor: Bu mâna (ع ب د) madde-i asliyesinin en umûmî olan mânası ne ise odur ki bu da “ubûdet” veya “abed” masdarlarındandır

ELMALILI:1:5/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5/r18.claim: Ubudet is the broadest term, while ibadat is narrower; ubudiyet displays humility and ibadat expresses its strongest form, including awe and reverence.
ELMALILI:1:5/r18.anchor: “ubûdet” lisân-ı Arab’da tezellül mânasını mutazammındır. “Ubûdiyet” izhâr-ı tezellül, “ibadet” bunun daha kuvvetlisi

ELMALILI:1:5/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5/r19.speaker: cumhûr-i müfessirîn
ELMALILI:1:5/r19.claim: The majority of exegetes define worship as the utmost degree of humility, which entails complete obedience without asking the reason.
ELMALILI:1:5/r19.anchor: cumhûr-i müfessirîn bunu “gāye-i hudû‘un aksâsı” diye tefsir ederler

ELMALILI:1:5/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5/r20.speaker: İbn Sikkît
ELMALILI:1:5/r20.claim: Ibn Sikkit is reported in Abu Hayyan's tafsir as deriving ibadat from the sense of tajrid, or detachment.
ELMALILI:1:5/r20.anchor: Tefsîr-i Ebû Hayyân’da İbn Sikkît’ten ibâdetin tecrid mânasından me’huz olduğu da nakledilmiştir

ELMALILI:1:5/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5/r21.speaker: Şârih-i Kāmûs
ELMALILI:1:5/r21.claim: The commentator on the Qamus says ibadat derives from the root abed, associated with greed or anger.
ELMALILI:1:5/r21.anchor: Şârih-i Kāmûs’un beyânına göre de ibadet, hırs veya gazab mânalarına gelen “abed” maddesinden me’huzdur

ELMALILI:1:5/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5/r22.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5/r22.claim: Another explanation says worship is doing what God approves while ubudiyet is being content with what God does; its usage can be narrower or broader, and Prophetic ubudiyet is more specific than ibadat.
ELMALILI:1:5/r22.anchor: “İbadet”, Allah’ın râzı olduğu şeyi yapmak, “ubudiyet” de Allah’ın yaptığına râzı olmak diye de tefsir edilmiştir

ELMALILI:1:5/r23.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5/r23.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5/r23.claim: Human life travels between pleasure and pain: fear and hope repeatedly shape action, while despair extinguishes activity and absence of fear leads to transgression and waste.
ELMALILI:1:5/r23.anchor: Kesb-i beşerin nâzımı da işte hâlden istikbâle bu korku ile ümidin mütevâlî tekabül ve tesâdümüdür

ELMALILI:1:5/r24.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5/r24.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5/r24.claim: Hope needs some fear and fear some hope for a sense of duty; the hungry work to become full and the full work from fear of hunger.
ELMALILI:1:5/r24.anchor: Ümidin içinde bir korku, korkunun içinde bir ümit yoksa vazife hissi atâlete düşer

ELMALILI:1:5/r25.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5/r25.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5/r25.claim: Human life is an exchange between inner and outer conditions, many of whose causes lie outside us or were not chosen by us; this makes each person sense their own incapacity.
ELMALILI:1:5/r25.anchor: Hayât-ı beşer dâhil ile hâricin bir muâmelesidir

ELMALILI:1:5/r26.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5/r26.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5/r26.claim: Even intelligent people cannot escape dependence on hope and fear, and no individual can leave this field of helplessness alone.
ELMALILI:1:5/r26.anchor: Fakat ne olursa olsun hiçbir ferd kendi kendine bu acz sahasından çıkamaz

ELMALILI:1:5#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#2/r1.claim: Human hope and fear have no ultimate limit; alongside particular hopes and fears, the soul is affected by boundless possibilities that converge in one ultimate source.
ELMALILI:1:5#2/r1.anchor: rûh-i beşerde ne ümidin nihâyeti vardır ne de korkunun

ELMALILI:1:5#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#2/r2.claim: The soul's attachment to an ultimate source of hope and fear is the origin of the innate ideas of worship and the object of worship, and moral character and future fortune depend on its seriousness.
ELMALILI:1:5#2/r2.anchor: İşte rûh-i insânînin böyle külliyetiyle müteessir olduğu mutlak bir havf u recâ âmiline karşı duyduğu bu alâka fıtrattaki mâbud ve ibadet fikrinin menşe’idir

ELMALILI:1:5#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#2/r3.claim: A person may become wholly captive to one limited pleasure or fear, treating its finite cause as the goal of all love or the limit of all fear and humbling themselves before it.
ELMALILI:1:5#2/r3.anchor: Artık o bu ümidin âmilini öyle sevmiş veya o korkunun âmilinden öyle yılmıştır ki bunlar ona bütün sevgilerin gayesi veya bütün korkuların müntehâsı gibi görünür

ELMALILI:1:5#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#2/r4.claim: Such attachment to a created finite cause is the source of shirk and the many false idols, whether animate or inanimate.
ELMALILI:1:5#2/r4.anchor: İnsanlara ma‘bûd-ı hakīkī ve ‘ubûdiyyet-i hakīkiye alâkasını unutturarak

ELMALILI:1:5#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#2/r5.claim: Even those who claim no concern with worship continually replace one object of worship with another and live in uncertainty without considering death.
ELMALILI:1:5#2/r5.anchor: kendilerini mâbud ve ibadet fikriyle hiç alâkadar değil gibi zannedenler her lahza böyle bir mâbud değiştirirler

ELMALILI:1:5#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#2/r6.claim: Any heart tied wholly to mortal things is at risk of ruin because that attachment will eventually break; only the Ever-Living Sustainer can guarantee what creatures cannot.
ELMALILI:1:5#2/r6.anchor: Bütün mevcûdiyetini fânîlere bağlayan her gönül

ELMALILI:1:5#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#2/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#2/r7.claim: Worship belongs to God alone; worshippers who serve Him are not wholly captured by other hopes and fears and can remain steady in their duties.
ELMALILI:1:5#2/r7.anchor: Ve fi’l-hakīka ibadet O’nun hakkıdır ve ancak O’na ibadet edenlerdir ki diğer ümitlere, korkulara kendini tamamen kaptırmaz

ELMALILI:1:5#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#2/r8.speaker: Aleyhi’s-salâtü ve’s-selâm Efendimiz
ELMALILI:1:5#2/r8.claim: The Prophet compares a believer to fresh grain that bends in wind and rises again, but a disbeliever to a pine that breaks once and never rises.
ELMALILI:1:5#2/r8.anchor: Aleyhi’s-salâtü ve’s-selâm Efendimiz buyurmuştur ki “Mü’min taze ekin gibidir, rüzgâr estikçe yatar, fakat yine doğrulur kalkar

ELMALILI:1:5#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#2/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#2/r9.claim: The believer is attached to the Everlasting Living God, while the disbeliever is attached to what perishes.
ELMALILI:1:5#2/r9.anchor: Çünkü kâfir fâniye, mü’min ise Hayy-i Bâkī’ye merbuttur

ELMALILI:1:5#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#2/r10.speaker: Hazret-i Ömeru’l-Fârûk
ELMALILI:1:5#2/r10.claim: After the Prophet's death, Umar was so shaken that he denied the Prophet had died and threatened anyone who said otherwise.
ELMALILI:1:5#2/r10.anchor: Hazret-i Ömeru’l-Fârûk bile “Peygamber vefat etmedi ve etmez, her kim öyle derse vururum” demeye kadar varmıştı

ELMALILI:1:5#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#2/r11.speaker: Sıddîk-i A‘zam Efendimiz
ELMALILI:1:5#2/r11.claim: Abu Bakr recited Qur'an 3:144 to remind the Companions that Muhammad was a messenger who had died before messengers, and to restore their composure.
ELMALILI:1:5#2/r11.anchor: Sıddîk-i A‘zam Efendimiz derhâl وَمَا مُحَمَّدٌ إِلَّا رَسُولٌۭ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِن قَبْلِهِ ٱلرُّسُلُ

ELMALILI:1:5#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#2/r12.speaker: Sıddîk-i A‘zam Efendimiz
ELMALILI:1:5#2/r12.claim: Abu Bakr tells them that worship of Muhammad cannot continue after his death, whereas the God who sent him is the Living One who never dies.
ELMALILI:1:5#2/r12.anchor: Ey mü’minler! Eğer Muhammed’e ibadet ediyorsanız işte o vefat etti ve eğer onu gönderen Allah teâlâ’ya ibadet ediyorsanız O Hayy-i lâ-yemûttur

ELMALILI:1:5#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#2/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#2/r13.claim: When mortal attachments divide the sources of hope and fear, hearts pursue separate love-idols and fear-idols through irrational humiliations and cannot find calm.
ELMALILI:1:5#2/r13.anchor: bir tarafta dilber sevgi mâbudları, bir tarafta da kahraman korku mâbudları dizilmiştir

ELMALILI:1:5#2/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#2/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#2/r14.claim: Hope and fear must be positive and negative effects of one source so the heart can replace one with the other and find contentment; if they come from unrelated sources, pursuit yields endless exhaustion.
ELMALILI:1:5#2/r14.anchor: Ümit ve korku bir mebde’den gelen ve yine onda birleşen müsbet ve menfî birer sûret-i te’sîr olarak duyulmalıdır

ELMALILI:1:5#2/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#2/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#2/r15.claim: The water and fire analogy shows that alternating between hope and fear from unrelated sources is futile; the one Lord is what binds self, consciousness, and the external world.
ELMALILI:1:5#2/r15.anchor: Fakat bunların biri suyun, diğeri ateşin eserleri ise su ile ateş beyninde hâkim bir mebde’-i müşterek de yok ise

ELMALILI:1:5#2/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#2/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#2/r16.claim: Worship is obedient action born from the collision of supreme love and fear, seeking ascent from total helplessness to absolute power and seeking tranquility through ultimate humility and reverence.
ELMALILI:1:5#2/r16.anchor: Hâsılı fıtrat-ı beşerde ibadet, rûhu teshir eden en yüksek mahabbet ile en yüksek mehâfetin

ELMALILI:1:5#2/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#2/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#2/r17.claim: True worship unites outward and inward submission without pride or ostentation; arrogant people, heedless optimists, and despairing pessimists are excluded from its honor.
ELMALILI:1:5#2/r17.anchor: Bunun için kibr ü riya ile birleşmez ve zâhir ü bâtına inkisâmı kabul etmez

ELMALILI:1:5#3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#3/r1.speaker: e‘âzım-ı müfessirîn
ELMALILI:1:5#3/r1.claim: The great exegetes paraphrase worship as bowing and humbling oneself only to God, finding tranquility through obedience because He alone is the source of all fear and hope.
ELMALILI:1:5#3/r1.anchor: Bu hakikatleri telhis için e‘âzım-ı müfessirîn

ELMALILI:1:5#3/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#3/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#3/r2.claim: God alone controls fear, hope, pleasure, pain, body, soul, and the inner capacities of perception and volition; these gifts should be devoted to His command with gratitude.
ELMALILI:1:5#3/r2.anchor: Rûh Senin milkin, cisim Senin milkin, bütün vücûd Senin milkin

ELMALILI:1:5#3/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#3/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#3/r3.claim: The proud objector asks whether worship's humility is degrading for a soul that wants to rise or believes it has already risen.
ELMALILI:1:5#3/r3.anchor: Rûh ve vicdan tezellül değil yükselmek ister, ibadet ise ma‘nâ-yı tezellülü mutazammın olduğuna göre yükselecek olan

ELMALILI:1:5#3/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#3/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#3/r4.claim: Wanting to rise admits one's own need and the value of a higher state, which worship recognizes most fully.
ELMALILI:1:5#3/r4.anchor: Yükselmek istemek, yükselmek ihtiyâcını teslim etmektir

ELMALILI:1:5#3/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#3/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#3/r5.claim: Claiming to have risen already falsely treats progress as finite and decline as impossible; ascent is limitless and the danger of falling remains, so worship is pride's remedy.
ELMALILI:1:5#3/r5.anchor: merâtib-i te‘âlî nâmütenâhîdir, tehlike-i sukūt ise her zaman bâkīdir

ELMALILI:1:5#3/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#3/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#3/r6.claim: Humility and reverence toward God provide the highest possible elevation for the human conscience through affiliation with Him.
ELMALILI:1:5#3/r6.anchor: Allah teâlâ’ya ibadetteki tezellül ve ta‘zîm vicdân-ı beşer için mümkin olan her türlü i‘tilânın fevkinde bir ulviyet temin eden bir vesîka-i intisabdır

ELMALILI:1:5#3/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#3/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#3/r7.claim: The imagined worshipper pledges freedom from all but God, obedience to His commands, moral effort, and even sacrifice of life and worlds in God's path.
ELMALILI:1:5#3/r7.anchor: Âlemde ben Allah’tan başkasına hürriyetimi veremem ve ancak O’na ve O’nun emrine inkıyad ederim

ELMALILI:1:5#3/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#3/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#3/r8.claim: Such faithful affiliation is the greatest human power and nobility; the Fatiha asks the speaker to say 'we,' making the pledge communal.
ELMALILI:1:5#3/r8.anchor: Ma‘amâfîh bu babda Fâtiha “ben” değil “biz” deyiniz diyor

ELMALILI:1:5#3/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#3/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#3/r9.claim: The first Muslims lived this spirit and spread God's exaltation across the world, whereas those who lost it bowed to worldly power.
ELMALILI:1:5#3/r9.anchor: ilk Müslümanlar bütün bu rûhun içinde idiler, bu rûhu kaybedenler de dünyaya boyun eğdiler

ELMALILI:1:5#3/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#3/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#3/r10.claim: The pledge is a heavy burden, but the dignity of God's exaltation is no light goal; human beings cannot undertake it through their own power, so seeking God's aid is necessary.
ELMALILI:1:5#3/r10.anchor: abdin ‘acz-i zâtîsi kudret-i zâtiyesiyle böyle bir taahhüde girişmesine mâni‘dir

ELMALILI:1:5#3/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#3/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#3/r11.claim: Isti‘ana means asking for aid or assistance; giving help is i‘ana, and mutual assistance is ta‘awun, so the terms must be distinguished.
ELMALILI:1:5#3/r11.anchor: “İsti‘âne”, ‘avn talep etmek, ta‘bîr-i âhârla me‘ûnet istemek, daha Türkçesi yardım dilemektir

ELMALILI:1:5#3/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#3/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#3/r12.claim: The exclusive restriction here concerns asking for help; the omitted complement permits three readings: aid itself, aid in every matter, or aid in a specific matter.
ELMALILI:1:5#3/r12.anchor: Bu isti‘ânenin ne gibi hususta olduğu zikr olunmamıştır. Böyle olan yerlerde de üç mâna muhtemel olur

ELMALILI:1:5#3/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#3/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#3/r13.claim: The first and universal readings converge in meaning, though the first is more eloquent and the second more explicit.
ELMALILI:1:5#3/r13.anchor: Bu ikisi meâlen birleşir. Fakat evvelki eblağ, bu sarih olur

ELMALILI:1:5#3/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#3/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#3/r14.claim: Although worship could suggest a specific request for aid, the verse's monotheistic emphasis and context of God's exclusive praise require a general meaning.
ELMALILI:1:5#3/r14.anchor: hepsi Allah’a mahsus olan hamdin beyânı siyâkında îrâd edilmiş bulunması

ELMALILI:1:5#3/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#3/r15.speaker: İbn Abbas
ELMALILI:1:5#3/r15.claim: Ibn Abbas's transmitted view supports the general scope of seeking aid, in worship and all other affairs.
ELMALILI:1:5#3/r15.anchor: her hâlde İbn Abbas hazretlerinden de rivayet edildiği üzere umûmu muktezîdir

ELMALILI:1:5#3/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#3/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#3/r16.claim: The resulting meaning is that believers ask God alone for help both in worship and every other matter, unlike disbelievers who seek help elsewhere.
ELMALILI:1:5#3/r16.anchor: Biz gerek sana ibadet ve itaatımızda ve gerek sâir umûrumuzun hepsinde ancak Senden isti‘âne ederiz

ELMALILI:1:5#3/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#3/r17.speaker: Beyzâvî
ELMALILI:1:5#3/r17.claim: Beydawi distinguishes necessary aid, without which an act cannot occur, from nonessential aid that makes it easier; necessary aid includes ability, conception, instruments, and material.
ELMALILI:1:5#3/r17.anchor: Beyzâvî’nin beyânına göre me‘ûnet iki nevidir. Birisine “me‘ûnet-i zarûriye”, diğerine “me‘ûnet-i gayr-i zarûriye” denilir

ELMALILI:1:5#3/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#3/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#3/r18.claim: Legal theory calls these two kinds of aid enabling power and facilitating power.
ELMALILI:1:5#3/r18.anchor: Bu taksim ilm-i usûlde “kudret-i mümekkine” ve “kudret-i müyessire” nâmları tahtında yapılır

ELMALILI:1:5#4/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#4/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#4/r1.claim: All enabling aid belongs to God, but the request is ours; capability arises when human seeking and divine assistance coincide with the act, which is called acquisition or partial will.
ELMALILI:1:5#4/r1.anchor: bütün me‘ûnet Allah’ındır, fakat talep bizimdir. Ve buna “kesb” veya “irâde-i cüz’iye” dahi tâbir olunur

ELMALILI:1:5#4/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#4/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#4/r2.claim: Humans are given authority to request; intended and unintended acts alike are attributed to us because they occur in and through us as their locus.
ELMALILI:1:5#4/r2.anchor: bizden birisi talebimizle, diğeri talebimiz olmayarak iki fiil sâdır olur ve her ikisi de bizden sâdır olduğu

ELMALILI:1:5#4/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#4/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#4/r3.claim: In voluntary acts we are the proximate cause through our request, but not the complete cause, since we depend on necessary aid; the Creator makes the total causal set.
ELMALILI:1:5#4/r3.anchor: Fakat bütün sebebi ve ‘illet-i tâmmesi biz değiliz, çünkü biz bunda me‘ûnet-i zarûriyeye muhtâcız

ELMALILI:1:5#4/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#4/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#4/r4.claim: Voluntary action expresses a relation between a requesting agent and a creating agent; bodies are inherently passive, while the soul is inherently desirous and God's action is creative.
ELMALILI:1:5#4/r4.anchor: Demek ki ef‘âl-i ihtiyâriyemiz bir fâ‘il-i tâlib ile bir fâ‘il-i hâlık arasındaki

ELMALILI:1:5#4/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#4/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#4/r5.claim: The engine analogy distinguishes the machine as the locus of motion, the operator as the one who wants and initiates it, and God as the creator of the motion from nonexistence.
ELMALILI:1:5#4/r5.anchor: İşleten, o hareketi isteyen makinisttir. Yaratan, o hareketi baştan nihâyete, ‘ademden vücûda getiren Hak teâlâ’dır

ELMALILI:1:5#4/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#4/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#4/r6.claim: The account rejects both Jabriyya or materialist views that reduce people to soulless machines and the idea that humans create like God.
ELMALILI:1:5#4/r6.anchor: ne Cebriyye veya Maddiyye gibi insanı rûhsuz bir makine farz ettirmeye çalışmalı, ne de onu rûh ve cismin hâlıkı olan Hak teâlâ gibi

ELMALILI:1:5#4/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#4/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#4/r7.claim: Overindulging in metaphysical speculation until one loses the path and denies obvious truths leads to endless error.
ELMALILI:1:5#4/r7.anchor: hakīkat-i zâhireyi inkâr eyleyecek bir surette dalıp gitmek sonu gelmeyen bir dalâlet olur

ELMALILI:1:5#4/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#4/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#4/r8.claim: The request of existence is not existence itself: seeking is a relation among existents, not a created existent, so it entails neither infinite regress nor compulsion nor creation.
ELMALILI:1:5#4/r8.anchor: Cebr lâzım gelmez, çünkü fiil araba sürükler gibi yapılmış değildir. Halk da lâzım gelmez, çünkü taleb bir mevcud değil

ELMALILI:1:5#4/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#4/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#4/r9.claim: Universal will is created, while partial will, seeking, and choice called kasb are an uncreated relation belonging to us.
ELMALILI:1:5#4/r9.anchor: irâde-i külliye denilen kuvve-i irâdiye mahluktur. Fakat irâde-i cüz’iye ve taleb ve ihtiyarla “kesb” dediğimiz karar gayr-i mahluktur

ELMALILI:1:5#4/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#4/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#4/r10.claim: The limits of understanding human willing reflect our inability to comprehend God's reality.
ELMALILI:1:5#4/r10.anchor: taleb ve irâdenin hadd-i vücûdîsini, inniyyetini tamamen ihâta edemiyor isek o da Hak teâlâ’nın hakikatini muhît olmadığımızdan

ELMALILI:1:5#4/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#4/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#4/r11.claim: The verse itself assigns the capacity to seek to us and assistance and power to God, excluding both Jabriyya compulsion and Qadariyya denial of destiny.
ELMALILI:1:5#4/r11.anchor: Fâtiha’da نَسْتَعِينُ cümlesinin içinde taleb salâhiyeti bizim

ELMALILI:1:5#4/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#4/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#4/r12.claim: It is mistaken to infer that every partial will succeeds; when people fail, they may wrongly swing toward compulsion by treating willing as creation and assuming God cannot intervene.
ELMALILI:1:5#4/r12.anchor: bunu yanlış anlıyorlar da bizim her irâde-i cüz’iyemizin her zaman iş görmekte kâfi olduğunu zannediyorlar

ELMALILI:1:5#4/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#4/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#4/r13.claim: God can create outcomes that match or diverge from our seeking, grant extra favor to those on His path, or let others face loss, punishment, or reminders.
ELMALILI:1:5#4/r13.anchor: o müvâzâtı ref‘ederek lehimize veya aleyhimize bizzat icrâ-yı tasarrufa ve ta‘bîr-i şer‘îsiyle nusret u hızlâna dahi kādir olduğunda şüphe edilemez

ELMALILI:1:5#4/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#4/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#4/r14.claim: The verse about entrusting one's affair to God illustrates this subtlety concerning delegated trust.
ELMALILI:1:5#4/r14.anchor: Dünyada dahi mükâfat ve mücâzat veya irâdesine ihtâr ve tenbih mânasını ifade eden bu noktalara müte‘allik birçok âyetler göreceğiz

ELMALILI:1:5#4/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#4/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#4/r15.claim: A hadith says that when God wills to enact His decree, He removes the reason of people of understanding; this concerns good or bad seeking, not compulsion.
ELMALILI:1:5#4/r15.anchor: “Allah teâlâ kazâ ve kaderini infâz etmek murad ederse zevi’l-‘ukūlün akıllarını alıverir”

ELMALILI:1:5#4/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#4/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#4/r16.claim: The verse says people may dislike what is good for them and love what is harmful, since God knows while they do not.
ELMALILI:1:5#4/r16.anchor: âyet-i celîlesi de bu nüktede diğer bir mâna ifade eyler

ELMALILI:1:5#5/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#5/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#5/r1.claim: The two declarative clauses also perform an implied act of commitment, like conventional oaths, covenants, or contracts; the prior speech signaled the obligation this acceptance entails.
ELMALILI:1:5#5/r1.anchor: Görülüyor ki إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ iki kelâm-ı ihbârîden müteşekkil bir âyettir

ELMALILI:1:5#5/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#5/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#5/r2.claim: The verse records a profound covenant between God and servants, a mutual legal agreement that summarizes a fundamental practical and social law of nature.
ELMALILI:1:5#5/r2.anchor: gayet derin ve gayet şümullü bir ‘akd-i bey‘at, bir mukāvele-i hukūkiye takrîr u tescîl edilmiş oluyor

ELMALILI:1:5#5/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#5/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#5/r3.claim: All living beings are carried by this covenantal law; disbelievers follow it unconsciously, while believers experience it consciously as well as bodily.
ELMALILI:1:5#5/r3.anchor: ehl-i küfr bunun ardından lâ-şu‘ûrî olarak vücûden sürüklenir. Ehl-i iman da bunu vücûdundan başka vicdan ve şuuruyla dahi yaşar

ELMALILI:1:5#5/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#5/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#5/r4.claim: At the center of the Fatiha, speech and the covenant are voiced through the collective conscience and worshipful tongue, pointing to conscience as a locus for divine speech.
ELMALILI:1:5#5/r4.anchor: Ne latîftir ki Fâtiha’nın tam ortasında hakk-ı tekellüm

ELMALILI:1:5#5/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#5/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#5/r5.claim: The author links this point to the trustworthy Spirit bringing revelation to Muhammad's heart and to God's speaking to humans by revelation or from behind a veil.
ELMALILI:1:5#5/r5.anchor: Bunda vicdân-ı ‘ubûdiyetin kelâm-ı ilâhîye tecellîgâh olduğuna büyük bir tenbih vardır

ELMALILI:1:5#5/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#5/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#5/r6.claim: Human speech and communication are gifts from the Creator, so people should hear, understand, and apply God's revealed eternal speech through their shared conscience.
ELMALILI:1:5#5/r6.anchor: söylemek, teblîğ-i merâm etmek kudret ve sıfatını Hâlıkınızdan ve O’nun me‘ûnetinden ahz ediyorsunuz

ELMALILI:1:5#5/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#5/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#5/r7.claim: God models gracious reciprocal dealing: after creating and nurturing people, He gives worldly gifts as if their property and makes them eternal, granting them a nearly equal standing in the agreement.
ELMALILI:1:5#5/r7.anchor: dünyada muvakkaten ihsan buyurduğu ‘atâyâsını bizim milk-i hakīkīmiz imiş gibi ebedîleştirmek ve ebediyyen tenmiye etmek için

ELMALILI:1:5#5/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#5/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#5/r8.claim: Although humans have no inherent rights before God, He recognizes their rights and assumes them under His mercy; worship is His right and the servant's duty, while aid, reward, and punishment become human claims by His own commitment.
ELMALILI:1:5#5/r8.anchor: zâtında hiçbir hukūku olmayan bizlere dahi milk ve hukūk tanıyarak ikisini mübâdele ediyor ve bizim hukūkumuzu da ‘uhde-i rahmetine alıyor

ELMALILI:1:5#5/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#5/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#5/r9.claim: Rights of people receive even greater care than God's rights; mercy precedes worship, worship precedes asking for help, and duty precedes the claim to a right, though divine mercy establishes the right first.
ELMALILI:1:5#5/r9.anchor: Rahmet ubûdiyete mütekaddim, lâkin ubûdiyet de isti‘âneye mütekaddim

ELMALILI:1:5#5/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#5/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#5/r10.claim: The author connects this reciprocal moral pattern to the Prophetic hadith, 'Adopt the character traits of God.'
ELMALILI:1:5#5/r10.anchor: hadîs-i şerîfinde işaret buyurduğu ahlâk-ı ilâhiyenin en şâyân-ı hayret tecellîlerinden biridir

ELMALILI:1:5#5/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#5/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#5/r11.claim: The plural 'we worship / we ask help' gives social community special importance, since the pledge is not expressed in the singular.
ELMALILI:1:5#5/r11.anchor: akid “ibadet ederim, isti‘âne ederim” gibi mütekellim vahde, yani ferd sîgasıyla yapılmıyor da, نَعْبُدُ / نَسْتَعِينُ diye cemi‘yani

ELMALILI:1:5#5/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#5/r12.speaker: müfessirîn
ELMALILI:1:5#5/r12.claim: Exegetes see an indication here of the virtue of congregational worship.
ELMALILI:1:5#5/r12.anchor: Müfessirîn burada cemaatle ibadetin faziletine işaret vardır diyorlar

ELMALILI:1:5#5/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#5/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#5/r13.claim: A congregation is not a mere crowd but an organized body able to act with one spirit, formed through a shared social covenant, so there is no true circularity in the verse.
ELMALILI:1:5#5/r13.anchor: cemaat kuru bir kalabalık demek değil, rûh-i vâhidle hareket edebilen bir hey’et-i muntazama-i vahdâniye demektir

ELMALILI:1:5#5/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#5/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#5/r14.claim: Social spirit first takes root in individuals when fraternity widens conscience beyond pride, narrowness, and selfishness; this breadth can support anything from a family to an empire.
ELMALILI:1:5#5/r14.anchor: Rûh-i ictimâ‘î evvelâ ferdde teessüs eder, vicdân-ı ferde ne vakit hiss-i uhuvvet girer

ELMALILI:1:5#5/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#5/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#5/r15.claim: Narrowness of conscience accompanies ignorance and pride, while an expanded conscience accompanies elevated understanding, humility, mercy, patience, and forbearance; the narrow-hearted person loves and fears only himself.
ELMALILI:1:5#5/r15.anchor: Vicdan darlığı cehalet ve kibir ile mütelâzımdır. İnşirâh-ı sadr dahi denilen vicdan vüs‘ati ise hafv u recâda

ELMALILI:1:5#6/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#6/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#6/r1.claim: When a person shares another’s welfare and harm as their own, social feeling and brotherhood begin; practiced empathy strengthens community and reduces pride.
ELMALILI:1:5#6/r1.anchor: Bir vicdanda bu mahabbet u mehâfet yükselip de bir diğerini dahi kendisi gibi, lâekal kendisine müsâvî bir kıymetle görmeye

ELMALILI:1:5#6/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#6/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#6/r2.claim: The breadth and strength of shared feeling set the scale of brotherhood, society, and civilization; narrow particular affiliations fragment wider bonds.
ELMALILI:1:5#6/r2.anchor: Bu his, bu câmi‘a ne kadar vüs‘at peydâ eder ve ne kadar kuvve bulursa kibir o nisbette tenâkus eder

ELMALILI:1:5#6/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#6/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#6/r3.claim: A community needs both breadth in its common bond and strength in conscience: breadth without strength dissolves it, while strength without breadth prevents its growth.
ELMALILI:1:5#6/r3.anchor: Câmi‘ada vüs‘at var da vicdanda kuvvet yoksa o cem‘iyyet idare edilemez, dağılmaya, küçülmeye mahkum olur

ELMALILI:1:5#6/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#6/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#6/r4.claim: Social feeling is first a divine innate gift and second a reflection of one's surroundings, and it is shaped by both innate and acquired upbringing.
ELMALILI:1:5#6/r4.anchor: Bu rûh-i ictimâ‘înin teessüsü evvelemirde fıtratta bir mevhibe-i rabbâniye ve derece-i sâniyede muhîtin bir in‘ikâsıdır

ELMALILI:1:5#6/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#6/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#6/r5.claim: Only God, without counterpart, equal, or partner, can encompass all human love and fear; devotion to Him grounds universal brotherhood and a worldwide community.
ELMALILI:1:5#6/r5.anchor: Şerîki, nazîri mevcud olmayan da ancak Hak teâlâ’dır. Çünkü mukabili li-zâtihi bâtıl ve li-zâtihi mümteni‘olan ancak O’dur

ELMALILI:1:5#6/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#6/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#6/r6.claim: God trains and strengthens social feeling by taking a covenant from each rational individual in the plural, so each represents all humanity and the worlds.
ELMALILI:1:5#6/r6.anchor: Fâtiha’da Hak teâlâ kendisini evvelâ zevi’l-‘ukūl ferdlere duyurarak vicdanlarında bu rûh-i ictimâ‘îyi terbiye ve takviye etmek için

ELMALILI:1:5#6/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#6/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#6/r7.claim: The first-person plural is grammatically spoken by one individual who represents fellow believers; a congregation speaks through a representative rather than each member saying “I.”
ELMALILI:1:5#6/r7.anchor: çünkü cemi‘mütekellim, muhatab ve gāib cemi‘lere benzemez, bunda hakikaten söyleyen yine bir müfreddir

ELMALILI:1:5#6/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#6/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#6/r8.claim: Saying “we worship” makes the individual represent those he feels as brothers, beginning with guardian angels and extending to present or envisaged congregations.
ELMALILI:1:5#6/r8.anchor: Binâen‘aleyh cemi‘mütekellim hakikatte nefs-i mütekellim me‘a’l-gayr demektir. Ve bu suretle إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ diyen bir ferd olacak

ELMALILI:1:5#6/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#6/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#6/r9.claim: In the author's school, followers behind the prayer leader recite neither Fatiha nor anything else because the imam recites for them; a person praying alone recites as imam of a potential congregation.
ELMALILI:1:5#6/r9.anchor: mezhebimizde imamın arkasında namaz kılan cemaat ne Fâtiha ne sâire hiçbir şey kıraat etmez de hepsinin hesabına imam okur

ELMALILI:1:5#6/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#6/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#6/r10.claim: As like-minded individuals meet, an actual congregation forms readily and follows an imam; its collective power corresponds to that imam.
ELMALILI:1:5#6/r10.anchor: bu gibi ferdler tekessür edip tanıştıkça bilfiil cemaat de kendiliğinden ve kolayca teşekkül ediverir de derhâl içlerinden birini imam tanıyarak ona iktidâ ederler

ELMALILI:1:5#6/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#6/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#6/r11.claim: Social spirit precedes the social body, so an individual can carry and represent the conscience of a community before it exists without circularity.
ELMALILI:1:5#6/r11.anchor: rûh-i ictimâ‘î, cism-i ictimâ‘îye mütekaddim olduğundan bir ferd, bir cemaatin bütün vicdânını onun teşekkülünden evvel dahi taşıyarak onu temsil eder

ELMALILI:1:5#6/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#6/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#6/r12.claim: Islam is an unsurpassed social and civil bond; narrow-minded people seek small gods and think restricted brotherhood easier, yet cannot attain a Muslim's firmness and serenity.
ELMALILI:1:5#6/r12.anchor: İşte İslâm bu büyük ve lâ-nazîr rûh-i ictimâ‘îdir ve onun muhtevî olduğu ma‘nâ-yı ictimâ‘î ve medenî fevkinde hiçbir câmi‘a tasavvuruna imkân bulunamaz

ELMALILI:1:5#6/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#6/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#6/r13.claim: The Muslim community's strength depends on the number of its members and the strength of their Islamic conscience; sustaining this universal spirit without an existing community is a prophetic station, especially that of the final Prophet, by divine support.
ELMALILI:1:5#6/r13.anchor: bu makam makām-ı enbiyâ ve bilhassa makām-ı Hâtemü’l-enbiyâ’dır

ELMALILI:1:5#7/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#7/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#7/r1.claim: God first established this covenant in Muhammad's prophetic heart through revelation; he is the complete, truthful servant and representative individual able fully to say the verse, and the model of servanthood.
ELMALILI:1:5#7/r1.anchor: tam mânasıyla إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ diyebilen sâdık ve masdûk ‘abd-i ekmel, ferd-i câmi‘, Hâtemü’l-enbiyâ Efendimiz’dir

ELMALILI:1:5#7/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#7/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#7/r2.claim: The faith declaration pairs God's oneness with Muhammad's being His servant and messenger; at Hira the Prophet's worship represented the universal spirit and his communal conscience became imam to all worlds.
ELMALILI:1:5#7/r2.anchor: أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لاَ إِلٰهَ إِلاَّ اللّٰهّٰ وَأَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا عَبْدُهُ وَرَسُولُهُ düstûr-ı îmânı teşkil eder

ELMALILI:1:5#7/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#7/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#7/r3.claim: Communities sincerely following the Prophet's Sunna can collectively uphold the covenant, submit to no one besides God, and seek aid from no one else; this spirit drove early Islamic conquests and expansion.
ELMALILI:1:5#7/r3.anchor: bu ‘akd-i ‘ubûdiyeti bihakkın söyleyebilmişler, ne Allah’tan başkasına boyun eğmişler ne de ‘arz-ı isti‘âne eylemişlerdir

ELMALILI:1:5#7/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#7/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#7/r4.claim: Replacing the plural with singular wording in prayer invalidates it because God requires a communal conscience covenant, not an individual-only promise; worshippers should consider whom they represent and on whose behalf they seek aid.
ELMALILI:1:5#7/r4.anchor: Çünkü Cenâb-ı Allah ferdden sade vicdân-ı ferdîsiyle bir mîsâk istemiyor da vicdân-ı ictimâ‘î ile bir mîsâk istiyor

ELMALILI:1:5#7/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#7/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#7/r5.claim: If no actual worshipping congregation suffices, a Muslim should mentally join the existing congregation to the potential one, including God's angels.
ELMALILI:1:5#7/r5.anchor: mevcud olan cemaate kuvvedeki cemaati, Allah’ın melâikesini dahi zammetmeyi her hâlde unutmamalıdır

ELMALILI:1:5#7/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#7/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#7/r6.claim: Exegetes say the plural pronouns refer to the reciter together with guardian angels, the present congregation, or all monotheists.
ELMALILI:1:5#7/r6.anchor: müfessirîn buradaki “biz” zamirlerini okuyan kimse ile beraberindeki hafaza melâikesine veyahut cemâ‘at-i hâzıraya veyahut bütün muvahhidîne râci‘dir derler

ELMALILI:1:5#8/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#8/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#8/r1.claim: The verse entails both unity of Lordship, accepting God's unique real essence, and unity of worship, a pledge to form a unified community; the latter builds a relational unity on the former.
ELMALILI:1:5#8/r1.anchor: hem tevhîd-i rubûbiyete ve hem tevhîd-i ‘ubûdiyete delâlet etmektedir

ELMALILI:1:5#8/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#8/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#8/r2.claim: The verse renews a witnessed testimony that there is no deity besides God and a commitment to act on it; collective Qur'anic pledges can distribute rights and duties to every individual (an individual obligation) or assign them to the collective body (a communal obligation).
ELMALILI:1:5#8/r2.anchor: cemiyeti ferdde, ferdi cemiyette indirâc ettirerek her ferde ‘ale’s-seviyye hak ve vazife tevzî‘etmektir

ELMALILI:1:5#8/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#8/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#8/r3.claim: Here the individual sense is retained: each believer bears the individual obligation, while collective testimony is the aggregate of individual testimony; the two consciences mutually guarantee one another.
ELMALILI:1:5#8/r3.anchor: İslâm’da hem ferdin ve hem cemaatin vicdânî tevhîdi vardır. Ve bunlar mütekābilen yekdiğerinin kefîlidir

ELMALILI:1:5#8/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#8/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#8/r4.claim: The verse is pure monotheism and rejects every form of associating partners with God.
ELMALILI:1:5#8/r4.anchor: bunda envâ‘-i şirkin hepsini nefyeden bir cevâb-ı red vardır

ELMALILI:1:5#8/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#8/r5.speaker: امام فخرالدین رازی
ELMALILI:1:5#8/r5.claim: Razi classifies shirk by corporeal versus incorporeal partners: lower or celestial bodies, simple or composite bodies, and material idols, plants, animals, humans, heavenly bodies, or spirits.
ELMALILI:1:5#8/r5.anchor: İmam Fahreddin Râzî burada şu telhîsi yapmıştır: “Müşrikler bölük bölüktürler. Çünkü Allah teâlâ’ya karşı iddia edip taptıkları

ELMALILI:1:5#8/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#8/r6.speaker: امام فخرالدین رازی
ELMALILI:1:5#8/r6.claim: Razi includes worshippers of fire, the sun, moon, stars, and astrologers who attribute fortune and misfortune to the stars, as well as Manichaean light-and-dark dualists.
ELMALILI:1:5#8/r6.anchor: Ecsâm-ı ‘ulviyeden şerîk ittihaz edenler de Güneş, Ay ve sâir yıldızlar gibi kevâkibe tapan ve saâdet u nuhûseti onlara atfeden Sâbi’e ve ekser-i müneccimîndir

ELMALILI:1:5#8/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#8/r7.speaker: امام فخرالدین رازی
ELMALILI:1:5#8/r7.claim: Razi describes angel worshippers who assign cosmic and climatic governance to spirits and worship their images, and dualists who posit good and evil first principles such as Yazdan and Ahriman.
ELMALILI:1:5#8/r7.anchor: bunlara “‘abede-i melâike” denir. Bunlar mâneviyâtı sezmiş ve fakat ecsâm-perest, ‘abede-i esnâm menzilesinde kalmışlardır

ELMALILI:1:5#8/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#8/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#8/r8.claim: Two wholly disconnected first principles could not organize one world; if they share kinship or a higher principle, they cease to be first principles, which leads toward the Trinity and Christianity's developed form.
ELMALILI:1:5#8/r8.anchor: aralarında asla bir nokta-i ittisal ve iştirak bulunmayacak olan iki mebde’-i evvelin bir nizam tesis edemeyecekleri

ELMALILI:1:5#8/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#8/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#8/r9.claim: Humanity wandered from awareness of one God into multiplicity, reduced it to two and then Trinity; Islam restores true oneness, and the verse refutes shirk, uniting people who enter Islam while departure fragments and humiliates them.
ELMALILI:1:5#8/r9.anchor: nihâyet dîn-i İslâm ile tevhîd-i hakīkīyi kemâliyle bulmuş ve toplanmıştır

ELMALILI:1:5#9/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#9/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#9/r1.claim: After the covenant, the prayer for guidance begins as the most comprehensive practical application of seeking divine aid; it answers the worshipper's need, after pausing at “we seek aid,” to know where and how to begin.
ELMALILI:1:5#9/r1.anchor: Bu talep ve dua isti‘ânenin ehem ve eşmel bir sûret-i tatbîkiyesiyle beyânıdır

ELMALILI:1:5#9/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#9/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#9/r2.claim: Guidance is contained in seeking aid, which is contained in worship and praise; thus all of Fatiha unfolds as one complete الحمد لله sentence and unified discourse, so its first two pauses are complete but not obligatory.
ELMALILI:1:5#9/r2.anchor: bütün Fâtiha’nın bir اَلْحَمْدُ للّٰهِِّٰ cümle-i tâmmesinin inkişâfı olup sade başıyla değil hey’et-i mecmû‘asıyla kelâm-ı vâhid hâlinde

CORPUSCORANICUM:1:5:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:5:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:5:kommentar/r1.claim: The double first-person plural declaration explicitly makes the text a community prayer, reversing the usual sura pattern of God speaking to the Prophet or his community.
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:5:kommentar/r1.anchor: Mit dieser doppelten Wir-Aussage erweist sich der Text explizit als Gebet einer Glaubensgemeinde

CORPUSCORANICUM:1:5:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:5:kommentar/r2.speaker: Devin Stewart
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:5:kommentar/r2.claim: Stewart explains the marked object-first word order as a way to achieve the rhyme.
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:5:kommentar/r2.anchor: mit Devin Stewart (2016) ließe sich die besondere Wortstellung (ʾiyyāka nastaʿīn statt nastaʿīnuka als durch den nur so zu erreichenden Reim erklären

CORPUSCORANICUM:1:5:kommentar/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:5:kommentar/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:5:kommentar/r3.claim: The author favors liturgical convention over rhyme as the explanation for the two litany-like elements, comparing them with responses in the Chrysostom liturgy.
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:5:kommentar/r3.anchor: doch dürften die beiden Litanei-Elemente eher liturgischer Konvention geschuldet sein

CORPUSCORANICUM:1:5:kommentar/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:5:kommentar/r4.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:5:kommentar/r4.claim: Despite its litany-like phrases, the Fātiḥa as a whole resembles an Introit prayer; its placement and liturgical role are discussed elsewhere in the commentary.
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:5:kommentar/r4.anchor: doch entspricht die Fātiḥa als ganze eher einem Introitusgebet

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:5/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:5/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:5/r1.claim: After describing God’s attributes and relation to creation and judgment, the passage voices the believers’ response: worship and help-seeking belong exclusively to Him.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:5/r1.anchor: ibadetin ve yardım dilemenin O’na özgü kılınması da –kul açısından– tabii hale gelmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:5/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:5/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:5/r2.claim: Worship combines love, fear, and submission; it is humanity’s purpose but remains a free choice under life’s test, and worldly gifts are means for serving God rather than ends.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:5/r2.anchor: Bu kavramın içinde kâmil mânada “sevgi, korku ve boyun eğme” vardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:5/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:5/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:5/r3.claim: Human power and will cannot meet every need; reliance on people or superhuman powers without divine guidance has bred shirk and false systems, while this verse directs worship and reliance to the right source and establishes tawhid.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:5/r3.anchor: Bu âyet, ibadet ederken ve yardım isterken yöneleceğimiz doğru adresi bize göstermekte ve tevhidi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:5/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:5/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:5/r4.claim: The plural we marks believers as a community bound by faith and worship, balancing person and society; they help one another while knowing every blessing ultimately comes from God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:5/r4.anchor: Âyette “ederim, dilerim” yerine “ederiz, dileriz” şeklinin seçilmiş olması tevhid ehli müminlerin bir bütün teşkil ettiklerini

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:5/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:5/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:5/r5.claim: The hadith urging God’s servants to be brothers clarifies the communal bond; believers aid one another but know no one can give without God’s will.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:5/r5.anchor: “Allah’ın kulları! Kardeş olun” (Buhârî, “Nikâh”, 45; Müslim, “Birr”, 23, 28-32) meâlindeki hadis de bu mânaya açıklık getirmektedir

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p20/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p20/r2.speaker: الرازي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p20/r2.claim: Al-hamd may appear to apply to God or another, so naming God clarifies it; worship can only be for God, so fronting You in 1:5 prevents an implication of worshipping another.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p20/r2.anchor: جاء في تفسير الرازي ذِكْرُ الفرقِ بين قوله

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p23/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p23/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p23/r3.claim: Allah suits the following worship verse: on the prevalent etymology it derives from ilah, the worshipped, and the Qur'an often pairs this name with worship.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p23/r3.anchor: لأن هذا اللفظ على أشهر الأقوال مأخوذ من لفظ (الإله)

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p41/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p41/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p41/r3.claim: Fronting You in both verbs restricts worship and seeking aid to God alone, as also expressed in other calls to worship and trust in God.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p42/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p42/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p42/r1.claim: I worship you states an act but does not exclude worshipping others; fronting You states that worship is exclusive.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p42/r1.anchor: يفيد أنه خَصَّهُ بالإكرام فلم يُكْرِمْ أحداً غيره

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p42/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p42/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p42/r2.claim: Repeating You explicitly restricts seeking aid to God; without repetition it could leave the aid's recipient unspecified or suggest worship and aid occur only together.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p42/r2.anchor: في تكرير (إياك) من الاهتمام والقوة ما ليس في الحذف

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p42/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p42/r3.speaker: روح المعاني
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p42/r3.claim: The repetition emphasizes seeking aid from God, since without it the source of aid may remain unspecified; one pronoun could also imply the two acts occur only together.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p42/r3.anchor: جاء في (روح المعاني) : "في سر تكرار (إياك) فقيل: للتخصيص على طلبِ العون منه تعالى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p43/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p43/r1.speaker: التفسير القيم
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p43/r1.claim: Repeating the object pronoun gives worship and fear exclusive force and focus that omitting its repetition would lack.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p43/r1.anchor: ففي إعادة الضمير من قوة الاقتضاء لذلك ما ليس في حذفه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p43/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p43/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p43/r2.claim: Leaving the object of seeking aid unstated makes the request cover every worldly and otherworldly need, not only worship or obedience.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p43/r2.anchor: أراد إطلاق الاستعانة لتشمل كل شيء يريده الإنسان

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p43/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p43/r3.speaker: روح المعاني
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p43/r3.claim: The omitted object gives seeking aid general scope; otherwise the verse would leave aid for needs beyond worship unknown.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p43/r3.anchor: في سر إطلاق الاستعانة فقيل: ليتناول كلَّ مُستعانٍ فيه،

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p43/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p43/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p43/r4.claim: The plural verbs signal Islam’s communal character, reflected in congregational prayer, mosques, pilgrimage, charity, jihad, shared fasting and feasts, and visiting the sick.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p43/r4.anchor: وذلك إشارة إلى أهمية الجماعة في الإسلام

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p44/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p44/r1.speaker: author
