SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p44/r1.claim: The recurring plural prayer in every rakʿah reinforces collective worship; congregational prayer is worth twenty-seven times individual prayer.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p44/r1.anchor: وهذه السورة التي تتردد في كل ركعة من ركعات الصلاة فيها إشارة إلى أهمية الجماعة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p44/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p44/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p44/r2.claim: Islam’s communal practices include pilgrimage, social solidarity through alms, collective jihad, and fasting and feast days binding the Muslim community.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p44/r2.anchor: والحج أكبر مظهر جماعي، والزكاة والصدقات من أكبر مظاهر التكافل الاجتماعي

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p44/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p44/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p44/r3.claim: The plural form of worship and seeking aid extends the supplication beyond the speaker to all believers, as the author’s cited views explain.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p44/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p44/r4.speaker: الرازي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p44/r4.claim: The plural nūn encourages a person to perform prayer in congregation.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p44/r4.anchor: إن المراد من هذه النون نون الجمع، وهو تنبيه على أن الأولى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p44/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p44/r5.speaker: الرازي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p44/r5.claim: Because believers are siblings, saying we worship includes all believers across the world and seeks the Muslims’ common good.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p44/r5.anchor: كان قد ذكر عبادة نفسه وعبادة جميع المؤمنين، شرقاً وغرباً، فكأنه سعى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p44/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p44/r6.speaker: فتح القدير
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p44/r6.claim: The plural verbs let the supplicant speak for himself and the wider class of worshippers.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p44/r6.anchor: والمجيء بالنون في الفعلين لقصد الإخبار من الداعي عن نفسه، وعن جنسه من العباد.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p44/r7.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p44/r7.speaker: فتح القدير
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p44/r7.claim: Another view takes the plural as humility: the individual is too small for this great occasion, rather than as self-exaltation.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p44/r7.anchor: وقيل: إن المقام لما كان عظيماً لم يستقلّ به الواحد استقصاراً لنفسه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p45/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p45/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p45/r1.claim: Worship is impossible without God’s aid and enabling; seeking aid admits human inability and dependence, countering pride and arrogance.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p45/r1.anchor: لا يستطيع أن يقوم بعباة الله إلا بإعانة الله وتوفيقه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p45/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p45/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p45/r2.claim: The pairing joins what servants offer God in worship with what they need and ask from Him.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p45/r2.anchor: وليجمع بين ما يتقرب به العباد إلى ربهم وبين ما يطلبونه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p45/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p45/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p45/r3.claim: Worship precedes seeking aid because worship is the purpose for which humans and jinn were created, while aid is its means.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p45/r3.anchor: العبادة هي علة خلق الإنس والجن

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p45/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p45/r4.speaker: روح المعاني
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p45/r4.claim: Since worship is unavoidably obligatory for servants, it is more deserving of precedence than seeking aid.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p45/r4.anchor: إن العبادة واجبة حتماً لا مناص للعباد من الإتيان بها

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p45/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p45/r5.speaker: التفسير القيم
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p45/r5.claim: Putting worship before seeking aid follows the rule that ends precede means: worship is the end and aid its instrument.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p45/r5.anchor: إن تقديم العبادة على الاستعانة في الفاتحة من باب تقديم الغايات على الوسائل

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p45/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p45/r6.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p45/r6.claim: Worship is God’s due, whereas seeking aid is the servant’s request; offering submission first is fitting before asking for something.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p45/r6.anchor: أن العبادة قَسْمُ الربِّ وحَقُّه، وأن الاستعانة مرادُ العبد،

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p46/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p46/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p46/r1.claim: God’s right in worship takes precedence over the servant’s share in seeking aid.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p46/r1.anchor: العبادة حقُّ الله وقسمه والاستعانةُ قسمُ العبد، وحقُّ الله أولى بالتقديم.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p46/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p46/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p46/r2.claim: Worship suits mention of recompense, while seeking aid fits the ensuing request for guidance; each expression is placed beside what suits it.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p46/r2.anchor: ومنها: أنَّ العبادة أكثرُ مناسبةً للجزاء أعني

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p46/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p46/r3.speaker: روح المعاني
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p46/r3.claim: Worship is more apt beside the mention of recompense, and seeking aid joins more closely to the request for guidance.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p46/r3.anchor: أشد مناسبة بذكر الجزاء، والاستعانة أقوى التئاماً بطلب الهداية

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p46/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p46/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p46/r4.claim: Worship relates to God’s divinity and name Allah, while seeking aid relates to His lordship and the name Rabb, matching the opening order.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p46/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p46/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p46/r5.claim: Worship belongs to the God-praising half of the surah, whereas the servant’s request for aid belongs with the supplication beginning guide us.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p46/r5.anchor: فكان مع الشطر الذي له وهو {اهدنا الصراط المستقيم} إلى آخر السورة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p46/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p46/r6.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p46/r6.claim: The ordering parallels the command to worship God and then rely on Him.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p46/r6.anchor: وهذا التعبير هو نظير قوله تعالى: {فاعبده

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p46/r7.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p46/r7.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p46/r7.claim: Delaying the seeking-aid clause also matches the surah’s verse endings.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p46/r7.anchor: في تأخير فعل الاستعانة توافقاً مع خواتيم الآي في السورة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p47/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p47/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p47/r1.claim: The shift from speaking about God to addressing Him is iltifāt, a rhetorical turn between grammatical perspectives.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p47/r1.anchor: هذا يسمى التفاتاً في علم البلاغة، والالتفاتُ قد يكون عدولاً

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p47/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p47/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p47/r2.claim: A change of style refreshes the listener and awakens attention.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p47/r2.anchor: أن الكلام إذا نُقِلَ من أسلوب إلى أسلوب كان ذلك أحسن تطرية لنشاط السامع

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p47/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p47/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p47/r3.claim: After naming the One worthy of praise and describing His great attributes, direct address makes the exclusive worship and aid owed to Him more vivid.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p47/r3.anchor: فقيل: إياك يا مَنْ هذه صفاته نخص بالعبادة والاستعانة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p47/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p47/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p47/r4.claim: Calling God Rabb of all worlds establishes His presence everywhere and always, so addressing Him as present is apt.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p47/r4.anchor: لما وُصِفَ بأنه رب العالمين عُلِمَ أنه حاضرٌ في كل مكان وزمان

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p47/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p47/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p47/r5.claim: Addressing someone just described in the third person can express a tactful intimacy more strongly than saying of him, I seek him.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p47/r5.anchor: فتقول له: إياك أقصد، فيكون في هذا الخطاب من التلطف

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p48/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p48/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p48/r1.claim: The direct address prepares for the supplication that follows in guide us.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p48/r1.anchor: ذكر توطئةً للدعاء في قوله: اهدنا

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p48/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p48/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p48/r2.claim: A request made to someone present is stronger than one made about someone absent.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p48/r2.anchor: ثم إن الطلب من الحاضر أقوى من الطلب من الغائب

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p48/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p48/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p48/r3.claim: The opening praise is fittingly in the third person, while supplication from this point onward is fittingly direct address.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p48/r3.anchor: الكلام من أول السورة إلى هنا ثناءٌ، والثناء في الغيبة أَوْلى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p48/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p48/r4.speaker: قيل
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p48/r4.claim: Praise is fuller in the absent form, but worship is due to the ever-present God; hence praise uses third person and worship direct address.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p48/r4.anchor: كانت العبادة إنما يستحقها الحاضر الذي لا يغيب

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p56/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p56/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p56/r1.claim: Guide us matches we worship and we seek aid: once the speaker includes companions in worship, he asks guidance for all, needed to reach their aim.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p56/r1.anchor: لأنه لما أخبر المتكلم أنه هو ومن معه يعبدون الله ويستعينونه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p56/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p56/r2.speaker: الرازي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p56/r2.claim: Invoking the congregation’s mercy, the worshipper praises, worships, seeks help, asks guidance, follows the righteous, and flees the rejected as a group.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p56/r2.anchor: سمعت رسولك يقول: (الجماعة رحمة والفرقة عذاب) فلما أردت تحميدك

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p63/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p63/r1.speaker: التفسير القيم
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p63/r1.claim: Living out worship and seeking aid in knowledge, action, and inward state cures corruption of the heart and intention.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p63/r1.anchor: والتحقق بـ {إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ} علماً ومعرفة وعملاً وحالاً يتضمنُ الشفاءَ

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p63/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p63/r2.speaker: التفسير القيم
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p63/r2.claim: Exclusive worship is the remedy for ostentation, and seeking aid from God is the remedy for pride and vanity.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p63/r2.anchor: فدواء الرياء بـ {إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ} ودواء الكبر بـ {وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ}

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p71/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p71/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p71/r3.claim: The surah gathers the foundations of Islamic belief: God and His perfect attributes, monotheism, the Last Day, divine power, and the messengers and revelation.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p71/r3.anchor: إن هذه السورة جمعت أصول العقيدة الإسلامية

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p71/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p71/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p71/r4.claim: God’s lordship over all entails that He alone is Lord, while exclusive worship and reliance affirm that there is no deity but Him.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p71/r4.anchor: فإن كونه رباً للعالمين جميعاً، يعني: أنه لا رَبَّ سواه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p71/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p71/r6.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p71/r6.claim: Seeking aid from God affirms His unlimited power.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p71/r6.anchor: وقوله: {وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ} يعني: الإقرار بقدرته التي لا تُحَدُّ.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p71/r8.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p71/r8.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p71/r8.claim: The surah contains the religion’s two pillars, faith and righteous action; the faith section names belief in God, His messengers, and the Last Day.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p71/r8.anchor: وتضمنت دين الإسلام بركنيه، الإيمان والعمل الصالح.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p72/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p72/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p72/r1.claim: Righteous action appears in worship and seeking aid through the end of the surah.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p72/r1.anchor: وأما العمل الصالح فقد دخل في قوله: {إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ}

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p72/r7.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p72/r7.speaker: الرازي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p72/r7.claim: The servant’s deeds require worship and recognition that he cannot perform it without God’s aid.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p72/r7.anchor: أما الأعمال التي يأتي بها العبد فلها ركنان

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p72/r8.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p72/r8.speaker: الرازي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p72/r8.claim: The surah is truly the Mother of the Book because it contains both doctrinal foundations and the two pillars of action.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p72/r8.anchor: فهذه السورة هي أم الكتاب حقاً

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p14/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p14/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p14/r1.claim: The name Allah suits the move to worship because it denotes the deity to be worshipped, and the author says it is paired with worship more than fifty times in the Quran.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p14/r1.anchor: لفظ الجلالة (الله) يعنى الإله المعبود مأخوذة من أله

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p19/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p19/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p19/r2.claim: Fronting إياك restricts worship and reliance to God alone; the author compares this exclusive order with exclusive trust and turning in 60:4 and 14:12.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p19/r2.anchor: قدم المفعولين لنعبد ونستعين وهذا التقديم للاختصاص

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p19/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p19/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p19/r3.claim: In 67:29 faith is not exclusive to God, since believers also affirm messengers, books, angels, the Last Day, and destiny; reliance, by contrast, is exclusively on God.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p19/r3.anchor: الإيمان ليس محصورا بالله وحده فقط بل علينا الإيمان بالله ورسله وكتبه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p20/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p20/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p20/r1.claim: Repeating إياك explicitly restricts both worship and reliance independently; one pronoun could leave reliance unexpressed or imply that either depends on the other.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p20/r1.anchor: وجب التكرار في الضمير إياك نعبد وإياك نستعين

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p20/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p20/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p20/r2.claim: Reliance is left unrestricted so it includes every matter for which a person may seek God's help, rather than one worldly task.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p20/r2.anchor: أطلق سبحانه فعل الاستعانة ولم يحدد نستعين على شيء

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p20/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p20/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p20/r3.claim: The plural نعبد ونستعين emphasizes communal life: congregational prayer, pilgrimage, charity, jihad, festivals, fasting, and believers' shared brotherhood; it includes the speaker among them.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p20/r3.anchor: في هذا إشارة إلى أهمية الجماعة في الإسلام

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p21/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p21/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p21/r1.claim: Worship is possible only with God's aid and enabling; asking for help cures pride and admits human weakness and inability to bear the trust unaided.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p21/r1.anchor: الإنسان لا يستطيع أن يقوم بعبادة الله إلا بإعانة الله له وتوفيقه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p21/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p21/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p21/r2.claim: Worship precedes reliance because worship is the purpose of creating humans and jinn (51:56), while reliance is a means to worship; God's right also precedes a request.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p21/r2.anchor: العبادة هي علة خلق الإنس والجن (وما خلقت الجن والإنس إلا ليعبدون) (الذاريات 56)

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p21/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p21/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p21/r3.claim: The shift from third-person praise to direct address is iltifat; it renews attention and suits addressing God as present when worshippers pray.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p21/r3.anchor: في البلاغة يسمى هذا الانتقال من الغائب للمخاطب أو المتكلم أو العكس " الإلتفات "

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p25/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p25/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p25/r1.claim: Fronting إيانا would wrongly restrict guidance to us alone; unlike worship and reliance, guidance is not requested exclusively for the speaker's group.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p25/r1.anchor: ولا يجوز أن نقول إيانا اهدي بمعنى خصنا بالهداية ولا تهدي أحداً غيرنا

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p26/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p26/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p26/r1.claim: The guidance request ties the chapter together: Rabb guides, Rahman and Rahim show mercy, worship and reliance require the path, and the favored oppose the astray.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p26/r1.anchor: هذا الدعاء ارتبط بأول السورة وبوسطها وآخرها

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p31/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p31/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p31/r5.claim: Al-Fatiha contains faith and good works, affirming God, the Last Day, angels, messengers, and scriptures, and joins lordship's unity to the unity of worship; it is therefore the Mother of the Book.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p31/r5.anchor: وقد جمعت هذه السورة توحيد الربوبية

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p39/r1.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p39/r1.speaker: الفضل الرقاشي
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p39/r1.claim: Al-Faḍl al-Raqqāshī reads the pronoun with initial hamza opened; Ibn Jinnī treats this as a recognized dialectal variant, also heard with initial hāʾ.

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p39/r2.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p39/r2.speaker: عمرو بن فايد
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p39/r2.claim: ʿAmr b. Fāʾid lightens the doubled yāʾ in both pronouns; Ibn Jinnī analyzes īyā as faʿl, like riḍā, and links it with the word for the sun’s ray or sign.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p39/r2.anchor: بتخفيف الياء فيهما جميعا، فوزن إيا على هذا فعل

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p39/r3.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p39/r3.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p39/r3.claim: Abū Isḥāq glosses the address as worshipping God’s reality, deriving īyā from āya, ‘sign’; Ibn Jinnī says this derivation works only on Abū Isḥāq’s view that īyā is a special name for the pronoun.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p39/r3.anchor: كان أبو إسحاق يقول في قول الله سبحانه: "إياك نعبد" أي: حقيقتك نعبد

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p39/r4.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p39/r4.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p39/r4.claim: Ibn Jinnī rejects treating the lightened pronunciation as an established dialect: he finds no linguistic record for it and suspects ʿAmr reduced the yāʾs to avoid their heaviness.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p39/r4.anchor: لا ينبغي أن يحمل "إياك" بالتخفيف على أنها لغة، وذلك أنا لم نر

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p39/r5.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p39/r5.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p39/r5.claim: The cited verses of Ṭarafa and Dhū al-Rumma use iyā/iyāʾ for sunlight, supporting the form’s association with the sun’s visible sign.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p39/r5.anchor: قال طرفة: سقته إياة الشمس إلا لثاته ... أسف

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p40/r1.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p40/r1.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p40/r1.claim: Arabic has other attested lightening and consonant changes, illustrated by al-Farazdaq and other verse; Ibn Jinnī still says the Qurʾān should not adopt the unattested lightening of īyā.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p40/r1.anchor: كل واحد من هذه الحروف وغيرها قد سمع وشاع، فأما "إياك" بالتخفيف فلم يسمع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p40#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p40#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p40#2/r1.claim: Iyyā plus attached suffixes is an independent accusative pronoun, not a visible noun in construct; grammarians disagree about the status of the base and suffixes.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p40#2/r1.anchor: إيا تلحقه ياء المتكلم وكاف المخاطب وهاء الغائب وفروعها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p40#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p40#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p40#2/r2.claim: The pronoun has several reported pronunciations: kasra or fatḥa on the hamza with doubled yāʾ, light yāʾ, or replacement of hamza by hāʾ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p40#2/r2.anchor: وأما لغاته فبكسر الهمزة وتشديد الياء، وبها قرأ الجمهور

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p40#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p40#2/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p40#2/r3.claim: Abū ʿUbayda's derivation of iyyā is weak; Abū Ḥayyān says his expertise was languages and Arab history, not grammar.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p40#2/r3.anchor: وذهاب أبي عبيدة إلى أن إيا مشتق ضعيف، وكان أبو عبيدة لا يحسن النحو

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p40#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p40#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p40#2/r4.claim: Proposed derivations from words for refuge or a verse, along with several morphological reconstructions, are all judged weak.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p40#2/r4.anchor: أقاويل كلها ضعيفة، والكلام على تصاريفها حتى صارت إيا تذكر في علم النحو

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p40#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p40#2/r5.speaker: ابن السكيت
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p40#2/r5.claim: Ibn al-Sikkīt glosses ʿibāda as tajrīd, while the majority gloss it as humility and submission.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p40#2/r5.anchor: العبادة: التذلل، قاله الجمهور، أو التجريد، قاله ابن السكيت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p40#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p40#2/r6.speaker: الحسن، وأبو مجلز، وأبو المتوكل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p40#2/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Abū Majlaz, and Abū al-Mutawakkil read iyyāka yaʿbud in the passive voice.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p40#2/r6.anchor: وقرأ الحسن، وأبو مجلز، وأبو المتوكل: إياك يعبد بالياء مبنيا للمفعول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p40#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p40#2/r7.speaker: بعض أهل مكة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p40#2/r7.claim: Some Meccans read naʿbud with a quiescent dāl.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p40#2/r7.anchor: وعن بعض أهل مكة نعبد بإسكان الدال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p40#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p40#2/r8.speaker: زيد بن علي، ويحيى بن وثاب، وعبيد بن عمير الليثي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p40#2/r8.claim: Zayd ibn ʿAlī, Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, and ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr al-Laythī read naʿbud with a kasra on its nūn.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p40#2/r8.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي، ويحيى بن وثاب، وعبيد بن عمير الليثي: نعبد بكسر النون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p40#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p40#2/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p40#2/r9.claim: Istiʿāna means requesting help, and requesting is one of twelve meanings of the verb pattern istifʿāl, alongside the cited related semantic functions.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p40#2/r9.anchor: الاستعانة، طلب العون، والطلب أحد معاني استفعل، وهي اثنا عشر معنى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p42/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p42/r1.speaker: أبو الحسن بن سيده
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p42/r1.claim: Ibn Sīda records tamāsaktu, masaktu, and istamsaktu as equivalent expressions for holding onto something.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p42/r1.anchor: حكى أبو الحسن بن سيده في المحكم: تماسكت بالشيء ومسكت به واستمسك به

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p42/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p42/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p42/r2.claim: Including istifʿāl forms that match tafāʿala and tafaʿʿala raises the pattern's possible meanings from twelve to fourteen.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p42/r2.anchor: فتكون معاني استفعل حينئذ أربعة عشر لزيادة موافقة تفاعل وتفعل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p42/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p42/r3.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p42/r3.claim: The majority pronounce the nūn of nastaʿīn with fatḥa; Abū Ḥayyān calls this the eloquent Ḥijāzī form.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p42/r3.anchor: وفتح نون نستعين قرأ بها الجمهور، وهي لغة الحجاز، وهي الفصحى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p42/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p42/r4.speaker: عبيد بن عمير الليثي، وزر بن حبيش، ويحيى بن وثاب، والنخعي، والأعمش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p42/r4.claim: These readers use kasra on the nūn, a dialect attributed to Qays, Tamīm, Asad, and Rabīʿa; al-Ṭūsī attributes it to Hudhayl.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p42/r4.anchor: وقرأ عبيد بن عمير الليثي، وزر بن حبيش، ويحيى بن وثاب، والنخعي، والأعمش، بكسرها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p42/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p42/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p42/r5.claim: Istiʿāna is derived from the root for help, with regular vowel changes across forms, and takes either a direct object or the preposition bāʾ.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p42/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p42/r6.speaker: صاحب اللوامح
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p42/r6.claim: The author of al-Lawāmiḥ records a form wayyāka with wāw substituted for hamza, though he is unsure whether it comes from al-Farrāʾ or Arab usage.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p42/r6.anchor: وقال صاحب اللوامح: وقد جاء فيه وياك أبدل الهمزة واوا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p42/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p42/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p42/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says fronting iyyāka restricts worship to God alone, equivalent to saying We worship no one but You.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p42/r7.anchor: إياك مفعول مقدم، والزمخشري يزعم أنه لا يقدم على العامل إلا للتخصيص

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p42/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p42/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p42/r8.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects compulsory restriction from fronting: it may express attention and care for the object, as ordinary Arabic examples show.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p42/r8.anchor: فالتقديم عندنا إنما هو للاعتناء والاهتمام بالمفعول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p42/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p42/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p42/r9.claim: Iyyāka is an iltifāt from third-person reference to direct address; iltifāt shifts among absent, addressed, and speaker forms while the referent remains one.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p42/r9.anchor: وإياك التفات لأنه انتقال من الغيبة، إذ لو جرى على نسق واحد لكان إياه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p42/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p42/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p42/r10.claim: The shift draws the worshipper into direct address after praising God as Lord, Merciful, and King, and prepares the ensuing supplication for guidance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p42/r10.anchor: وفائدته في إياك نعبد أنه لما ذكر أن الحمد لله المتصف بالربوبية والرحمة والملك والملك لليوم المذكور

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p43/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p43/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p43/r1.claim: If malik is a vocative, iyyāka is not a shift from absence, since it continues direct address after direct address.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p43/r1.anchor: ومن ذهب إلى أن ملك منادى، فلا يكون إياك التفاتا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p43/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p43/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p43/r2.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects al-Zamakhsharī's three-iltifāt analysis of Imruʾ al-Qays's lines, finding two shifts and rejecting the proposed movement to presence.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p43/r2.anchor: ودعوى الزمخشري في أبيات امرئ القيس الثلاثة أن فيه ثلاثة التفاتات غير صحيح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p43/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p43/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p43/r3.claim: The passive reading iyyāka yuʿbadu is grammatically difficult because iyyāka is accusative; Abū Ḥayyān explains it through metaphorical pronoun substitution and an internal shift.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p43/r3.anchor: وقراءة من قرأ إياك يعبد بالياء مبنيا للمفعول مشكلة، لأن إياك ضمير نصب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p43#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p43#2/r1.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p43#2/r1.claim: Most interpret worship as submission and humility; other contextual senses include obedience, drawing near through obedience, supplication, and affirmation of divine unity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p43#2/r1.anchor: وفسرت العبادة في إياك نعبد بأنها التذلل والخضوع، وهو أصل موضوع اللغة أو الطاعة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p43#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p43#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p43#2/r2.claim: Worship is joined to seeking help because the verse combines what the servant offers God with what the servant asks from Him; worship comes first as a means before the request.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p43#2/r2.anchor: وقرنت الاستعانة بالعبادة للجمع بين ما يتقرب به العبد إلى الله تعالى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p43#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p43#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p43#2/r3.claim: Both worship and seeking help are unqualified so they include every act of worship and every matter for which help is sought.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p43#2/r3.anchor: وأطلق العبادة والاستعانة لتتناول كل معبود به وكل مستعان عليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p43#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p43#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p43#2/r4.claim: Repeating iyyāka makes worship and seeking help two deliberate clauses and explicitly identifies God as the one from whom help is requested.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p43#2/r4.anchor: وكرر إياك ليكون كل من العبادة والاستعانة سيقا في جملتين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p43#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p43#2/r5.speaker: بعض المنتمين للصلاح
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p43#2/r5.claim: Some spiritually inclined interpreters assign worship to knowledge and seeking help to mystical gnosis, but Abū Ḥayyān finds no textual indication for these restrictions.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p43#2/r5.anchor: كقول بعضهم: إياك نعبد بالعلم، وإياك نستعين عليه بالمعرفة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p43#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p43#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p43#2/r6.claim: Some say We worship answers the determinists and We seek help answers the advocates of free will.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p43#2/r6.anchor: وفي قوله: نعبد قالوا رد على الجبرية، وفي نستعين رد على القدرية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p43#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p43#2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p43#2/r7.claim: Worship is a noble station: scripture applies servant to prophets and places worship after monotheism, since worship follows the foundation of divine unity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p43#2/r7.anchor: فذكر العبادة عقيب التوحيد، لأن التوحيد هو الأصل، والعبادة فرعه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p43#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p43#2/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p43#2/r8.claim: Some read the direct address in iyyāka as an answer to deniers of time, God, or a creator, because it addresses a present existent.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p43#2/r8.anchor: وقالوا في قوله: إياك. رد على الدهرية والمعطلة والمنكرين لوجود الصانع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p54/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p54/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p54/r1.claim: The sūra uses fronting and delay in “we worship, we seek help” and in “those angered, those astray.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p54/r1.anchor: التقديم والتأخير، وهو في قوله نعبد، ونستعين، والمغضوب عليهم، والضالين،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p54/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p54/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p54/r3.claim: The shift to direct address in “You alone we worship,” “You alone we seek help,” and “guide us” is iltifāt.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p54/r3.anchor: النوع الثامن: الالتفات، وهو في إياك نعبد وإياك نستعين، اهدنا.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p54/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p54/r9.speaker: عمرو بن عبيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p54/r9.claim: In an anomalous count, ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd treats “You alone we worship” as a verse, giving eight verses.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p54/r9.anchor: وشذ عمرو بن عبيد، فجعل آية إياك نعبد، فهي على عده ثمان آيات،

ALUSI-FULL:v1p86/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p86/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p86/r1.claim: The five manifestations yield bodily worship, the devilish soul's request for help, the predatory soul's request for guidance, the animal soul's request for uprightness, and the holy spirit's request to join purified spirits; the pillars of Islam likewise correspond to the five names.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p86/r1.anchor: وآثار هذا التجلي طاعة الأبدان بالعبادة وطاعة النفس الشيطانية بطلب الإستعانة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p86/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p86/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p86/r2.claim: Because the Fatiha's praise reaches its limit here, the prayer turns to direct address in Iyyaka naʿbudu wa-iyyaka nastaʿīn.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p86/r2.anchor: ولما بلغ الثناء الغاية القصوى قال سبحانه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p86/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p86/r3.speaker: بعض النحاة
ALUSI-FULL:v1p86/r3.claim: Grammarians offer competing analyses of iyyāka: an independent accusative pronoun with added suffixes, a noun with attached pronouns, or a form whose support syllable carries the pronominal force.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p86/r3.anchor: إيا في المشهور ضمير نصب منفصل واللواحق حروف زيدت لبيان الحال

ALUSI-FULL:v1p86/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p86/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ALUSI-FULL:v1p86/r4.claim: Abu ʿUbayda proposed a derivation for iyyā, which al-Alusi dismisses as astonishing ignorance.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p86/r4.anchor: وزعم أبو عبيدة إشتقاقه وهو جهل عجيب

ALUSI-FULL:v1p86/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p86/r5.speaker: أبو الفضل الرقاشي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p86/r5.claim: Nonstandard readings include wayyāka with waw, ʾiyyāka with a light yāʾ, ʾayyāka with a doubled yāʾ, and hiyyāka with hāʾ; the majority use the familiar form.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p86/r5.anchor: وقد جاء وياك بقلب الهمزة واو ولا أدري أهو عن القراء أم عن العرب

ALUSI-FULL:v1p86/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p86/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p86/r6.claim: Worship is the highest degree of submission and is due only to God, who bestowed the greatest gifts of life and existence; therefore prostration to another is forbidden.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p86/r6.anchor: والعبادة أعلى مراتب الخضوع ولا يجوز شرعا ولا عقلا فعلها إلا لله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p86/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p86/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p86/r7.claim: Worship may mean submission, obedience, supplication, or affirming God's oneness; the meanings are close, and references to worshipping idols report the opponents' claim sarcastically.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p86/r7.anchor: وقيل لا تستعمل إلا في الخضوع له سبحانه وما ورد من نحو قوله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p86/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p86/r8.speaker: بعض المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v1p86/r8.claim: A scholar distinguishes three levels: worship from hope or fear, devotion through honor or accepting duties, and pure service recognizing God's intrinsic right; the first is spiritually lowest and the last highest.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p86/r8.anchor: وذكر بعض المحققين أن لها ثلاث درجات لأنه إما أن يعبد الله تعالى رغبة في ثوابه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p86/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p86/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p86/r9.claim: Prayer would be invalid if the worshipper explicitly prayed for reward or the prestige of worship, since its intention must be directed to God Himself.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p86/r9.anchor: وإليه الإشارة بقول المصلي أصلي لله تعالى فإنه لو قال أصلي لثوابه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p86/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p86/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p86/r10.claim: Istiʿāna means seeking assistance, and the yāʾ in its verb comes from a root wāw.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p86/r10.anchor: والإستعانة طلب المعونة وياء فعله منقلبة عن واو

ALUSI-FULL:v1p86/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p86/r11.speaker: الجبرية
ALUSI-FULL:v1p86/r11.claim: The Jabriyya argue that if humans acted independently, asking God for help with action would have no point.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p86/r11.anchor: أما الجبرية فقالوا لو كان العبد مستقلا لما كان للإستعانة على الفعل فائدة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p86/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p86/r12.speaker: القدرية
ALUSI-FULL:v1p86/r12.claim: The Qadariyya argue that asking help makes sense only if a person already has the capacity to perform the act.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p86/r12.anchor: وأما القدرية فقالوا السؤال إنما يحسن لو كان العبد متمكنا في أصل الفعل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p87/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p87/r1.speaker: ناصر الملة والدين البيضاوي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p87/r1.claim: Al-Bayḍāwī distinguishes necessary assistance, without which action cannot occur, from nonessential help that makes an already possible act easier; neither category entails compulsion or denies capacity.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p87/r1.anchor: قال وهي إما ضرورية أو غيرها والضرورية ما لا يتأتى الفعل دونه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p87/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p87/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p87/r2.claim: Al-Alusi reads the verse as affirming human capacity that has real effect only by God's permission, rejecting compulsion, inert capacity, and independent human control alike.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p87/r2.anchor: وعندى أن الآية إن إستدل بها على شيء من بحث خلق الأفعال

ALUSI-FULL:v1p87/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p87/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p87/r3.claim: The phrase Iyyaka naʿbudu entails that acts issue from people through an effective capacity; saying capacity is only nominal or equivalent to none contradicts necessity and reason.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p87/r3.anchor: إياك نعبد مشير إلى صدور الفعل من العباد وذلك يستدعي قدرة يكون بها الإيجاد

ALUSI-FULL:v1p87/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p87/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p87/r4.claim: Iyyaka nastaʿīn denies independence: human capacity and action depend on God's permission and aid, yielding neither compulsion nor delegation of control.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p87/r4.anchor: وقوله وإياك نستعين يدل على نفي الإستقلال فيه وأنه بإذن الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p87#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p87#2/r1.speaker: إبن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v1p87#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the fronted object as meaning that we worship no one besides You, repudiating idolatry and implicitly addressing polytheists.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p87#2/r1.anchor: قال إبن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما معناه لا نعبد غيرك

ALUSI-FULL:v1p87#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p87#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p87#2/r2.claim: Fronting You reflects God's precedence over worshippers and worship in existence, and immediately directs the worshipper's attention toward the true object of devotion.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p87#2/r2.anchor: وتقديم ما هو مقدم في الوجود فإنه تعالى مقدم على العابد والعبادة ذاتا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p87#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p87#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p87#2/r3.claim: The early explicit focus on God strengthens monotheism and guards against distraction, satanic whispering, and the thought that worship might be meant for someone else.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p87#2/r3.anchor: والتصريح من أول وهلة بأن العبادة له سبحانه فهو أبلغ في التوحيد

ALUSI-FULL:v1p87#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p87#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p87#2/r4.claim: The spiritual aspirant should regard God first and worship only as a vehicle toward Him, remaining absorbed in the vision of divine majesty and beauty.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p87#2/r4.anchor: والإشارة إلى حال العارف وأنه ينبغي أن يكون نظره إلى المعبود أولا وبالذات

ALUSI-FULL:v1p87#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p87#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p87#2/r5.claim: The cited contrasts distinguish the believers' remembrance of God and the Prophet's assurance of God's presence from Israel's remembrance of favors and Moses' assurance that his Lord will guide him.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p87#2/r5.anchor: وكم من فرق بين قوله تعالى للمحمديين

ALUSI-FULL:v1p87#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p87#2/r6.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v1p87#2/r6.claim: The plural naʿbudu can humbly join one's deficient worship to that of all worshippers instead of presenting one's own worship as worthy of mention.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p87#2/r6.anchor: فقد قيل هو الإشارة إلى حال العبد كأنه يقول إلهي ما بلغت عبادتي

ALUSI-FULL:v1p87#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p87#2/r7.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v1p87#2/r7.claim: Another explanation says the singular would risk a false claim of exclusive devotion, since people often submit to worldly powers and seek help from powerless creatures; the plural can include the righteous.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p87#2/r7.anchor: وقيل النكتة في العدول إلى الأفراد التحرز عن الوقوع في الكذب

ALUSI-FULL:v1p87#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p87#2/r8.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v1p87#2/r8.claim: A further explanation hears the plural as saying that the speaker is one servant among God's servants; a humble collective identity is contrasted with the singular claims of Ishmael and Moses.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p87#2/r8.anchor: وقيل لو قال إياك أعبد لكان ذلك بمعنى أنا العابد

ALUSI-FULL:v1p88/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p88/r1.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v1p88/r1.claim: The plural pronouns may include the reciter, guardian angels, and those present in congregational prayer.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p88/r1.anchor: وقيل الضمير في الفعلين للقاري ومن معه من الحفظة وحاضري الجماعة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p88/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p88/r2.speaker: الغزالي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p88/r2.claim: The plural may evoke congregational prayer, which al-Ghazali says is superior to an individual's prayer.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p88/r2.anchor: وقيل هو من باب صلاة الجماعة تفضل صلاة الفذ على ما ذكره الغزالي

ALUSI-FULL:v1p88/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p88/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p88/r3.claim: One reason to mention worship first is that it is a trust God offered to the heavens, earth, and mountains, so its discharge takes priority.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p88/r3.anchor: الأول أن العبادة أمانة كما قال تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p88/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p88/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p88/r4.claim: Saying I worship might sound self-congratulatory; immediately asking for help shows that worship itself depends on God's enabling and permission.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p88/r4.anchor: أنه لما نسب المتكلم العبادة إلى نفسه أوهم ذلك تبجحا وإعتدادا منه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p88/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p88/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p88/r5.claim: Worship brings the servant near to God, whereas requesting assistance does not itself do so, making worship more important.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p88/r5.anchor: أن العبادة مما يتقرب بها العبد إلى الله تعالى والإستعانة ليست كذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v1p88/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p88/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p88/r6.claim: Worship is a means, so it properly precedes the request for a need and may make that request more readily answered.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p88/r6.anchor: أنها وسيلة فتقدم على طلب الحاجة لأنه أدعى للإجابة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p88/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p88/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p88/r7.claim: Offering what the Master requires before asking what one wants from Him better demonstrates sincere servitude.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p88/r7.anchor: تقديم العبد ما يريده مولاه منه أدل على صدق العبودية

ALUSI-FULL:v1p88/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p88/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p88/r8.claim: Worship is an unavoidable duty and the stated purpose for creating humans and jinn, so it deserves precedence.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p88/r8.anchor: أن العبادة واجبة حتما لا مناص للعباد عن الإتيان بها

ALUSI-FULL:v1p88/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p88/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p88/r9.claim: Worship suits the preceding mention of recompense, while seeking help connects more directly with the coming request for guidance.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p88/r9.anchor: أنها أشد مناسبة بذكر الجزاء والإستعانة أقوى إلتئاما بطلب الهداية

ALUSI-FULL:v1p88/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p88/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p88/r10.claim: Islam begins by singling God out in worship and escaping shirk; explicit dependence on His aid comes after monotheism is established.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p88/r10.anchor: أن مبدأ الإسلام التخصيص بالعبادة والخلوص من الشرك

ALUSI-FULL:v1p88/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p88/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p88/r11.claim: Placing nastaʿīn second preserves the cadence of the verse endings.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p88/r11.anchor: أن في تأخير فعل الإستعانة توافق رؤوس الآي

ALUSI-FULL:v1p88/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p88/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p88/r12.claim: When two actions are linked, their order can sometimes be reversed, as with fulfilling a right and then showing kindness, or the reverse.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p88/r12.anchor: أن أحدهما إذا كان مرتبطا بالآخر لم يختلف التقديم والتأخير

ALUSI-FULL:v1p88/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p88/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p88/r13.claim: In the mystic's journey, worship marks the end of the station of seekers; after the heart is purified by praise, the soul turns to request spiritual empowerment.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p88/r13.anchor: أن مقام السالكين ينتهي عند قوله إياك نعبد وبعده يطلب التمكين

ALUSI-FULL:v1p89/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p89/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p89/r1.claim: One explanation of the shift to direct address is that divine attributes made God a particular known reality, moving the worshipper from proof and thought to immediate witnessing.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p89/r1.anchor: حقيقة العبادة إنقياد النفس الأمارة لأحكام الله تعالى وصورته وقالبه الإسلام ومعناه وروحه الإيمان ونوره ونوره الإحسان وفي نعبد والإلتفات تتم الأمور الثلاثة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p89/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p89/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p89/r2.claim: Another explanation is spiritual progress from Islam through accepted praise to ihsan, worshipping as if one sees God; the verse's worship and address bring together these levels.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p89/r2.anchor: ترقى بذريعة الحمد المستجاب لمزيد النعم إلى رتبة الإحسان وهو أن تعبد الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p89/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p89/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p89/r3.claim: Since past and future are alike to God, who owned all ages eternally, the shift from third person to direct address is fitting.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p89/r3.anchor: لما تبين أنه ملك في الأزل ما في أحايين الأبد علم أن الشاهد والغائب

ALUSI-FULL:v1p89/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p89/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p89/r4.claim: A structural explanation takes the first part as praise, naturally spoken about God, and the remainder as supplication, naturally spoken in His presence.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p89/r4.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون السر أن الكلام من أول السورة إلى هنا ثناء والثناء في الغيبة أولى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p89/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p89/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p89/r5.claim: Because worship belongs to the ever-present God, while praise can remain complete in His absence, each section receives the style suited to it; Abraham rejects what sets.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p89/r5.anchor: وكانت العبادة إنما يستحقها الحاضر الذي لا يغيب كما حكى سبحانه عن إبراهيم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p89/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p89/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p89/r6.claim: The worshipper imitates the faithful community in its speech and hopes that joining its worship will count him among the righteous.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p89/r6.anchor: فالعابد لما رام ذلك سلك مسلك القوم في الذكر ومزج عبادته بعبادتهم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p89/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p89/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p89/r7.claim: A person who recognizes his distance from God through humility is especially apt to receive mercy that draws him into intimacy and direct address.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p89/r7.anchor: من لزم جادة الأدب والإنكسار ورأى نفسه بعيدا عن ساحة القرب

ALUSI-FULL:v1p89#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p89#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p89#2/r1.claim: Because worship is demanding, the beloved's presence gives the servant energy to endure hardship without fatigue, as illustrated by a poetic appeal to sing before Saʿdā.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p89#2/r1.anchor: المحبوب قرن سبحانه العبادة بما يشعر بحضوره ليأتي بها العابد

ALUSI-FULL:v1p89#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p89#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p89#2/r2.claim: Praise addresses others while the mystic sees divine virtues among them; when remembrance removes the veils and all others vanish from awareness, speech necessarily turns directly to God.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p89#2/r2.anchor: وأما إذا آل أمره بملازمة الإذكار إلى إرتفاع الحجب والأستار

ALUSI-FULL:v1p89#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p89#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p89#2/r3.claim: Al-Alusi's own subtle reading links the turn after Judgment Day to the believer's future delight in God's presence, direct conversation, and unveiling, a mercy paired with the preceding warning.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p89#2/r3.anchor: وعندي وهو من نسائم الأسحار أن الله سبحانه بعد أن ذكر يوم الدين

ALUSI-FULL:v1p89#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p89#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p89#2/r4.claim: In Sufi symbolism, Judgment Day hints at annihilating the ego's desires and attachments; once the self dies, abiding in the garden of witnessing and union follows.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p89#2/r4.anchor: تلويح إلى مقام الفناء لأنه موت النفس عن شهواتها وخروجها عن جسد تعلقها بالأغيار

ALUSI-FULL:v1p89#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p89#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p89#2/r5.claim: Beyond that union lies a station that language cannot explain; al-Alusi prays for complete absorption in witnessing God alone.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p89#2/r5.anchor: وفوق هذا مقام آخر لا يفي بتقريره الكلام ولا تقدر على تحريره الأقلام

ALUSI-FULL:v1p89#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p89#2/r6.speaker: الإمام السيوطي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p89#2/r6.claim: Al-Suyuti, quoting Shaykh Bahāʾ al-Dīn, says there is agreement on one shift in person; al-Alusi argues that the count depends on whether one supplies the command Say and on rival definitions of iltifāt.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p89#2/r6.anchor: هذا وقد ذكر الإمام السيوطي نقلا عن الشيخ بهاء الدين أنه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p90/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p90/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p90/r1.claim: The earlier phrase al-ḥamdu lillāh itself may contain a shift depending on whether Say is supplied, so the dispute over one, two, or no shifts turns on grammatical and rhetorical assumptions.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p90/r1.anchor: إن كان التقدير قولوا الحمد لله ففي الكلام المأمور به إلتفاتان

ALUSI-FULL:v1p90/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p90/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p90/r2.claim: One explanation for repeating Iyyaka is to specify that help is sought from God, which might remain unspecified if only one object were used.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p90/r2.anchor: فقيل للتنصيص على طلب العون منه تعالى فإنه لو قال سبحانه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p90/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p90/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p90/r3.claim: Another explanation says a single object might imply that worship only draws one near when combined with asking assistance, which is not true.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p90/r3.anchor: وقيل أنه لو أقتصر على واحد ربما توهم أنه لايتقرب إلى الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p90/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p90/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p90/r4.claim: Repetition as mere emphasis is rejected because the second Iyyaka is the separate object of nastaʿīn, not a redundant object of the first verb.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p90/r4.anchor: وفيه أن التكرير إنما يكون تأكيدا إذا لم يكن معمولا لفعل ثان

ALUSI-FULL:v1p90/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p90/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p90/r5.claim: A further explanation treats the repetition as teaching believers to renew remembrance of God whenever they have a need.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p90/r5.anchor: وقيل أنه تعليم لنا في تجديد ذكره تعالى عند كل حاجة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p90/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p90/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p90/r6.claim: Al-Alusi says the repeated object marks different grounds of relation: worship is directed to God in itself, while asking assistance depends on an attribute of His.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p90/r6.anchor: وعندي أن التكرار للأشعار أن حيثية تعلق العبادة به تعالى غير حيثية

ALUSI-FULL:v1p90/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p90/r7.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v1p90/r7.claim: Some take the unexpressed object of seeking help universally, like an unrestricted verb of giving; al-Bayḍāwī's practice favors this, and it accords with a report from Ibn ʿAbbās.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p90/r7.anchor: فقيل ليتناول كل مستعان فيه فالحذف هنا مثله في قولهم فلان يعطى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p90/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p90/r8.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
ALUSI-FULL:v1p90/r8.claim: Al-Kashshaf considers it better to seek God's help and enabling specifically for worship, with Guide us to the straight path explaining the requested assistance.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p90/r8.anchor: الأحسن أن يراد الإستعانة به وبتوفيقه على أداء العبادة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p90/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p90/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p90/r9.claim: Al-Alusi prefers an unrestricted request for assistance because it unifies the surah's meaning and includes faith, worship, conduct, social dealings, salvation, and escape from every kind of error.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p90/r9.anchor: والإنصاف عندي أن الحمل على العموم أولى ليتوافق ألفاظ هذه السورة الكريمة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p90/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p90/r10.speaker: رسول الله
ALUSI-FULL:v1p90/r10.claim: A sound hadith to Ibn ʿAbbās commands him: when seeking help, seek God's help; al-Alusi sees it as evidence for the unrestricted reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p90/r10.anchor: وقد ثبت في الصحيح عنه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم أنه قال لإبن عباس

ALUSI-FULL:v1p90/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p90/r11.speaker: عبيد بن عمير الليثي وزيد بن حبيش ويحيى بن وثاب والنخعي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p90/r11.claim: They read naʿbudu with kasra on the initial nūn, a dialect found among Qays, Tamim, Asad, Rabīʿa, and Hudhayl; the same pattern applies to nastaʿīn.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p90/r11.anchor: وقد قرأ عبيد بن عمير الليثي وزيد بن حبيش ويحيى بن وثاب والنخعي نعبد بكسر النون

ALUSI-FULL:v1p90/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p90/r12.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v1p90/r12.claim: A few dialect forms also put kasra under the imperfect prefix in verbs such as yajillu and yaʿlamūn.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p90/r12.anchor: على أن بعضهم قال يجل بكسر ياء المضارعة من وجل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p90/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p90/r13.speaker: الحسن وإبن المتوكل وأبو محلف
ALUSI-FULL:v1p90/r13.claim: They read yuʿbadu in the passive, an unusual form.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p90/r13.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وإبن المتوكل وأبو محلف يعبد بالياء مبنيا للمفعول

ALUSI-FULL:v1p90/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p90/r14.speaker: بعض أهل مكة
ALUSI-FULL:v1p90/r14.claim: Some Meccans read naʿbud with a silent final dāl; the majority use the standard open nūn and damma on dāl of the Hijaz.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p90/r14.anchor: وعن بعض أهل مكة أنه قرأ نعبد بإسكان الدال وقرأ الجمهور نعبد بفتح النون وضم الدال

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p53#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p53#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p53#2/r1.claim: Iyyaka is a pronoun used before a verb, as in ‘you alone I mean’; after a verb it appears only independently, as in ‘I meant only you.’
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p53#2/r1.anchor: كلمة ضمير خصت بالإضافة إلى المضمر ويستعمل مقدما على الفعل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p53#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p53#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p53#2/r2.claim: Worship means making God one, obeying him with humility and submission; the word for servant reflects submission, as in a trodden path.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p53#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p53#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p53#2/r3.claim: Seeking help asks God’s aid for worship and all affairs; the order is challenged by those who require capacity before action, but al-Baghawi says divine enabling accompanies action.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p53#2/r3.anchor: فإن قيل: لم قدم ذكر العبادة على الاستعانة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p53#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p53#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p53#2/r4.claim: Because aid is itself a kind of worship, the verse can state worship generally and then name one of its details; on his view, the ordering poses no problem.

BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5/r1.claim: After identifying the one worthy of praise, the discourse turns from absence to direct address and from reasoning to witnessing: the servants reserve worship and seeking aid for Him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5/r1.anchor: يا من هذا شأنه نخصك بالعبادة والاستعانة

BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5/r2.claim: The shift of person is an Arabic device that refreshes speech and engages listeners, as in 10:22 and 35:9 and the cited poetry of Imruʾ al-Qays.
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5/r2.anchor: ومن عادة العرب التفنن في الكلام والعدول من أسلوب إلى آخر

BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5/r3.claim: إيا is the accusative pronoun stem and the attached letters distinguish speaker, addressee, and absent person; the attached forms have no grammatical case of their own.
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5/r3.anchor: وإيا ضمير منصوب من فصل، وما يلحقه من الياء والكاف والهاء حروف زيدت

BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5/r4.speaker: الخليل
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5/r4.claim: Al-Khalīl considered the following suffix to be annexed to إيا, citing a colloquial example; al-Bayḍāwī says this evidence is anomalous and unreliable.
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5/r4.anchor: وقال الخليل: إيا مضاف إليها، واحتج بما حكاه عن بعض العرب

BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5/r5.claim: Other grammatical analyses treat إيا as the pronoun with an added support element, or treat the entire form as the pronoun.
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5/r5.anchor: وقيل: هي الضمائر، وإيا عمدة فإنها لما فصلت عن العوامل

BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5/r6.claim: Readings include opening إيا's hamza and replacing it with hāʾ.
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5/r6.anchor: وقرىء { إياك } بفتح الهمزة و «هياك» بقلبها هاء.

BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5/r7.claim: ʿIbāda is the utmost submission and abasement, and is used only for submission to God.
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5/r7.anchor: والعبادة: أقصى غاية الخضوع والتذلل ومنه طريق معبد أي مذلل

BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5#2/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5#2/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5#2/r1.claim: Necessary aid makes action possible; nonessential aid makes it easier or encourages it, but is not required for moral responsibility.
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5#2/r1.anchor: طلب المعونة وهي: إما ضرورية، أو غير ضرورية والضرورية ما لا يتأتى

BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5#2/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5#2/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5#2/r2.claim: The request may seek help in all important matters or specifically in performing acts of worship; the pronoun can include the reciter, angels present, congregants, or all monotheists.
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5#2/r2.anchor: المراد طلب المعونة في المهمات كلها، أو في أداء العبادات

BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5#2/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5#2/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5#2/r3.claim: The speaker includes himself among worshippers to seek acceptance and response through their blessing, which helps explain the institution of congregational prayer.
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5#2/r3.anchor: أدرج عبادته في تضاعيف عبادتهم وخلط حاجته بحاجتهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5#2/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5#2/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5#2/r4.claim: Fronting إياك conveys honor, concern, and exclusivity; Ibn ʿAbbās glosses it “we worship You and worship no other.”
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5#2/r4.anchor: ولذلك قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما (معناه نعبدك ولا نعبد غيرك)

BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5#2/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5#2/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5#2/r5.claim: The worshipper should attend first to the worshipped and regard worship as a noble relation to God, not as a self-congratulatory act.
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5#2/r5.anchor: والتنبيه على أن العابد ينبغي أن يكون نظره إلى المعبود أولا وبالذات

BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5#2/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5#2/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5#2/r6.claim: The Prophet's statement “God is with us” is superior to Moses' “my Lord is with me” because the former loses sight of self in divine presence.
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5#2/r6.anchor: ولذلك فضل ما حكى الله عن حبيبه حين قال:

BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5#2/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5#2/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5#2/r7.claim: Repeating إياك explicitly reserves seeking help for God, while placing worship first preserves rhyme and teaches that presenting a means before one's request aids its acceptance.
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5#2/r7.anchor: وكرر الضمير للتنصيص على أنه المستعان به لا غير

BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5#2/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5#2/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5#2/r8.claim: Saying “we worship” might sound boastful, so “we seek Your help” clarifies that worship itself depends on God's aid and enabling.
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5#2/r8.anchor: فعقبه بقوله: { وإياك نستعين } ليدل على أن العبادة أيضا

BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5#2/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5#2/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5#2/r9.claim: The conjunction may instead express circumstance: “we worship You while seeking Your help.”
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5#2/r9.anchor: وقيل: الواو للحال والمعنى نعبدك مستعينين بك.

BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5#2/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5#2/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5#2/r10.claim: The imperfect verbs with kasra are a Tamīm dialect feature when the following consonant is not uḍamma.
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:5#2/r10.anchor: وقرىء بكسر النون فيهما وهي لغة بني تميم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r2.speaker: أبو الفضل محمد المشدالي المغربي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r2.claim: Al-Mashdali's method for Qur'anic coherence is to identify a surah's purpose, its prerequisites and their distance from the goal, then answer expectations raised as the discourse unfolds.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r2.anchor: قال شيخنا الإمام المحقق أبو الفضل محمد بن العلامة القدوة أبي عبد الله محمد ابن العلامة القدوة أبي القاسم محمد المشدالي المغربي

BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r3.claim: A surah's name summarizes its purpose, as a title signals the details within; Adam demonstrated this naming principle when he named things before the angels.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r3.anchor: أن اسم كل سورة مترجم عن مقصودها هلأن أسم كل شيء تظهر المناسبة بينه وبين مسماه عنوانه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r4.claim: The Fatiha's many titles converge on مراقبة: it is the Mother of the Book, foundation, oft-repeated, treasure, healing, sufficing, complete, protecting, incantation, praise, thanks, supplication and prayer.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r4.anchor: فمدار هذه الأسماء كما ترى على أمر خفي كاف لكل مراد وهو المراقبة التي سأقول إنها مقصودها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r5.claim: The Fatiha is a treasure, cure, sufficiency, fulfillment, protection and incantation; it gathers praise, gratitude and supplication, with prayer as their greatest assembly.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r5.anchor: فكل شيء لا يفتتح بها لا اعتداد به ، وهي كنز لكل شيء شافية لكل داء

BIQAI-FULL:v1p12/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p12/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p12/r1.claim: The Fatiha's purpose is to establish God's exclusive right to all praise and perfection, sovereignty over both worlds, worship and aid, and to ask for the path of the successful rather than the doomed; its center is مراقبة.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p12/r1.anchor: الغرض الذي سبقت له الفاتحة وه إثبات استحقاق الله تعالى لجميع المحامد وصفا الكمال ، واختصاصه بملك الدنيا والآخرة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p12/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p12/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p12/r2.claim: Prophets, scriptures and laws ultimately gather people to truth so they may know their sovereign and what pleases Him; knowledge and practice together serve the Qur'an's purpose.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p12/r2.anchor: لأن المقصود منت إرسال الرسل وإنزال الكتب نصب الشرائع ، والمقصود من نصب الشرائع جمع الخلق على الحق

BIQAI-FULL:v1p13/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p13/r2.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p13/r2.claim: The basmala relates to the Fatiha as the Fatiha relates to the Qur'an: each is a compact synthesis of what the larger whole details.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p13/r2.anchor: وأشد منه أنه لما كانت نسبة البسملة من الفاتحة نسبة الفاتحة من القرآن صدرت بها الفاتحة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r1.claim: After establishing God's worthiness and prompting hope and fear, the recitation turns from third person to direct address and puts the means before the request.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r1.anchor: فلما استجمع الأمر استحقاقا وتحبيبا وترغيبا وترهيبا كان من شأن كل ذي لب الإقبال إليه وقصر الهمم عليه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r2.claim: Iyyaka addresses the possessor of these attributes, and worship means reaching the utmost abasement; repeating the pronoun intensifies the request for aid.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r2.anchor: أي يا من هذه الصفات صفاته { نعبد } كما قال الحالي : تبلغ الغاية في أنحاء التذلل

BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r3.claim: Worship is possible only through God's aid, and guidance lies in His hand; the sequence moves from essence to acts to attributes and back to essence, teaching dependence after recognizing God's right.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r3.anchor: إشارة إلى أن عبادته لا تتهيأ إلا بمعونته وإلى أن ملاك الهداية بيده

BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r4.speaker: عائشة
BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r4.claim: Aisha reports the Prophet seeking refuge in God's pardon from punishment, pleasure from anger, and God from God, then admitting he cannot enumerate His praise.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r4.anchor: والنسائى وهذا لفظة في التعود عن عائشة رضى الله عنها : ( أعوذ بعوفك من عقوبتك , وبرضاك من سخطك

BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r5.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r5.claim: Al-Harali says all Qur'an is God's speech, but some verses voice what creatures at different levels ought to say yet cannot express; God teaches them words that fulfill their duty.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r5.anchor: قال الحرالي : وهذه الآيات أى هذه وما بهدها مما جاء كلام الله فيه جارياعلى لسان خلقه فإن القرآن كله كلام الله

BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r6.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r6.claim: Al-Harali explains the sound report that God divided prayer between Himself and His servant: the first three verses are God's praise, which He accepts from the reciting servant as praise and glorification.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r6.anchor: وتلك هي صلاتهم المقسمة التى عبر عنها فيما صح عنه علية الصلاة والسلام من قوله تعالى : ( قسمت الصلاة بيني وبين عبدي نصفين )

BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r7.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r7.claim: Al-Harali says the paired verse belongs between God and servant: worship is the servant's commitment, aid is God's gift, and aid precedes and enables worship.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r7.anchor: فكان ظاهرهاغ التزام عهد العبادة وهو ما يرجع إلى العبد وعمادها طلب المعونة من الله سبحانه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r8.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r8.claim: Whoever asks God for aid with a genuine task receives help proportionate to it; failure comes from neglecting God's due, misunderstanding the verse or forgetting its favor, and the plural nun signals congregational prayer.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r8.anchor: فمن كانت عليه مؤنة شىء فاستعان الله فيهالا على مقتضى هذه الآية جاءته المعونة على قدر مؤنته

BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r9.claim: The verse teaches confession of inability, need and reliance on God's power; that dependence leads directly to asking for guidance along the necessary path.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r9.anchor: وفي الآية ندب إلى اعتقاد العجز واستشعار الافتقار والاعتصام بحوله وقوته

BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r3.claim: The Qur'an's arrangement is miraculous, so the Fatiha must retain its required order in prayer; rearrangement or insertion of foreign material invalidates it. Al-Isfahani locates its clearest inimitability in order.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r3.anchor: قال الأصبهاني : فإن القرآن معجز والركن الأبين الإعجاز يتعلق بالنظم والترتيب

BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r4.claim: The spiritual seeker passes through awe of God's attributes, recognizes many perilous paths and the lack of guidance or safety apart from God, then asks for the straight path, its blessed companions and protection from both condemned groups.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r4.anchor: فلما أشرف وستنار وعرف مواقع الأسرار بالأقدار كأنه قيل له : ماذا تطلب وفي أي مذهب تذهب ؟

BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r5.speaker: مسعود التفتازاني
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r5.claim: Al-Taftazani maps the Fatiha's blessings to two creations and two preservations: creation in Rabb al-alamin, preservation in mercy, second creation in judgment, and afterlife preservation in worship onward.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r5.anchor: كما قال العلامة سعد الدين مسعود ابن عمرو التفتازاني الشافعي . إلى جميع النعم فغنها ترجع إلى إيجاد وإبقاء ثانيافي دار الفناء والبقاء

BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r7.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r7.claim: Al-Harali says the seven repeated verses are the Qur'an's gathered essence and its contents will be disclosed at creation's completion; earlier scriptures progress from changeable scrolls and lasting books to the Qur'an, which completes religion.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r7.anchor: قال الأستاذ أبو الحسن الحرالي في مفتاح الباب القفل لفهم القرآن المنزل في أخر الباب التاسع منه : ولننه هذه الأبواب

BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r1.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r1.claim: Al-Harali contrasts the Qur'an's detailed, dispersed sequence with the Fatiha's seven complete universals, and makes the Fatiha a mirror of the servant's move from misguidance to guidance.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r1.anchor: ووجه فوت أم القرآن مقصود تنزيله التفصيل والجوامع , فيه نجوم مبثوثة غير منتظمة , وحداة إثر واحدة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r2.claim: A Prophetic report says he was sent to complete noble character; the author links this completion with the Fatiha's comprehensive opening and the Qur'an's culmination.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r2.anchor: بعثت لأتمم مكارم الأخلاق . أن إلى ربك المنتهى .

BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r3.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r3.claim: Al-Harali describes the Qur'an's majesty through rulings spanning immediate and deferred realities, witnessed experience, and reports of the past and patterns that recur in time.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r3.anchor: ومن مجيده وهو ما حربت أحكامه من بين عاجل ما شهد وآجل ما علم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r4.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r4.claim: Al-Harali distinguishes gradual descent that moves understanding between states and rulings from descent from high to low, which may occur with or without intermediaries.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r4.anchor: وما كان منه بتدريج وتقريب للأفهام ففاءت من حال إلى حال

BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r5.claim: The passage names al-Baqara 2:281 as the last revealed verse and says its recitation position between the debt verse and the verse before it shows revelation and recitation order can differ.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r5.anchor: وجعلوها بين آية الدين والآية قبلها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r1.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r1.claim: Al-Harali says the Qur'an's sevenfold gathering in Muhammad's heart relates to the Mother of Qur'an's universals as the Qur'an's gathering in his heart relates to the Mother.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r1.anchor: وأما الجمع ففي قلبه نسبة جوامعه السبع في أم القرآن إلى القرآن بمنزلة نسبة جمعه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r2.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r2.claim: Al-Harali says the Qur'an reached the Prophet on his tongue over the span of the prophetic mission, after its descent to the lowest heaven.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r2.anchor: وعلى لسانه في أمد أيام النبوة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r3.speaker: عائشة
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r3.claim: Aisha reports that Muhammad's character was the Qur'an, making his conduct the visible form of its inner reality.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r3.anchor: قالت عائشة رضى الله عنها : كان خلقه القرآن

BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r4.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r4.claim: Al-Harali says the Fatiha is the Qur'an's mother: its first three verses encompass the divine names and attributes, while its last three cover the creature's way to God, mercy or failure.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r4.anchor: فالآيات الثلاث الول قال شاملة لكل معنى تضمنته الأسماء الحسنى والصفات العلى

BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r5.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r5.claim: Recitation order can differ from revelation chronology; the verse allowing the Prophet to marry certain women was placed before a later restriction.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r5.anchor: فقد يتطابق قرآن الأمر وتطور الخلق وقد لا يتابق والله يتولى إقامتها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r6.claim: In the authentic report in Muslim and the four Sunan, God says the Fatiha is divided between Himself and His servant: He answers praise, glorification and worship, and grants the servant's final requests.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r6.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضى الله عنه قال : سمعت زسول الله صلى اله عليه وسلم يقول

BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r1.claim: Al-Baqara aims to prove the Book is guidance to follow; belief in the unseen, especially resurrection and the afterlife, is its greatest guidance and organizing theme.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r1.anchor: مقصودها إقامة الدليل على أن الكتاب هدى ليتبع يفي كل ما قال ، وأعظم ما يهدي إليه الإيمالن بالغيب

BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r2.claim: The cow story makes the surah's title apt because resurrection occurs through an apparently slight human cause; it is a clearer sign of divine power than Abraham's story or earlier Israelite resurrections.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r2.anchor: فلذلك سميت بها السورة وكانت بذلك أحق من قصة إبراهيم عليه الصلاة والسلام لأنها في نوع البشر

BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r3.claim: The following comparison of hearts and stones shows the guided and astray: hearts become hard and wretched, while stones display fear and yield benefit that reaches God's servants.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r3.anchor: ولا سيما وقد اتبعت بوصف القلوب والحجارة بما عم اللمهتدين بالكتاب والضالين فوصفها بالقسوة الموجبة للشقوة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r4.claim: The Book functions like a caliph from the resolute messengers, guiding every matter to the right exit: rejecting it fails, hesitation nearly perishes, and accepting it brings piety and excellence.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r4.anchor: وفيها إشارة إلى أن هذا الكتاب فينا كما لو كان فينا خليفة من أولي العزم من الرسل يرشدنا في كل أمر

BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r5.claim: Al-Baqara is also called the Radiant and the Hump: it illuminates guidance and sufficiency, brightens believers' faces at judgment, and exalts belief in the afterlife above every other good after monotheism.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r5.anchor: وسميت الزهراء لإنارتها طريق الهداية والكفاية في الدنيا والآخرة ، ولأيجابها إسفار الوجوه يفي يوم الجزاء

BIQAI-FULL:v1p28/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p28/r1.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p28/r1.claim: Because praise is the seventh inclusive letter, the Fatiha begins with it and gathers the seven universals diffused through the Qur'an, as the Qur'an gathers earlier scriptures.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p28/r1.anchor: ولما كان حرف الحمد هو سابعها الجامع افتتح الله به سبحانه وتعالى الفاتحة أم القرآن وأم الكتاب

BIQAI-FULL:v1p28/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p28/r5.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p28/r5.claim: The fourth verse contains the clear letter in worship and the ambiguous letter in seeking help; because it is intimate direct address, its request is not repeated.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p28/r5.anchor: والرابعة تشتمل على حرفي المحكم في قوله ^ ( إياك نعبد ) ^ [ الفاتحة : 5 ]

BIQAI-FULL:v1p28/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p28/r6.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p28/r6.claim: The fifth verse's request returns to praise, the sixth to the grace of lawful and forbidden provisions, and the seventh to the sovereign's command; together these complete all seven letters.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p28/r6.anchor: وعادتت مسألة الآيةى الخاتمسة على حرف الحمد ومسألة الآية السادسة على آية النعمة من حرفي الحلال والحرام

BIQAI-FULL:v1p31/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p31/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p31/r3.claim: Baqara answers the Fatiha's plea for guidance by directing worshippers to the Book, describing the guided and denied groups as patterns to follow or avoid; its pious are the straight path and its others the path of ruin.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p31/r3.anchor: وأما منسبة ما بعد ذلك للفاتحة فهو أنه لما أخبلا سبحانه وتعالى أن عباده المخلصين سألوا في الفاتحة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p31/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p31/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p31/r4.claim: Alternatively, the surah's purpose is solely to describe the Book; it establishes the truth of its meaning, exposes disbelief and hypocrisy to show that inward faith matters, then proves its inimitable form and authority for teaching law.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p31/r4.anchor: وإن شئت قلت : مقصود هذه السورة وصف الكتاب فقط وما عدا ذلك فتوابع ولوازم

DURR-FULL:v1p25/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p25/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p25/r1.claim: “You alone we worship” means worshipping and affirming God's oneness; “You alone we ask for help” is the servant's part after asking.
DURR-FULL:v1p25/r1.anchor: إياك نعبد} يعني الله أعبد وأوحد {وإياك نستعين} قال الله: هذا بيني وبين عبدي إياي يعبد

DURR-FULL:v1p34/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p34/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v1p34/r7.claim: Qatada says “You alone we worship” indicates God's oneness.
DURR-FULL:v1p34/r7.anchor: هكذا فقولوا {إياك نعبد وإياك نستعين} قال: دل على نفسه

DURR-FULL:v1p34/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p34/r9.speaker: أم سلمة
DURR-FULL:v1p34/r9.claim: Aisha reports that the Prophet counted the basmala as verse one, al-hamd as two, al-Rahman al-Rahim as three, Malik yawm al-din as four, then indicated five for the next verse.
DURR-FULL:v1p34/r9.anchor: عن أم سلمة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قرأ في الصلاة {بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم} فعدها آية {الحمد لله رب العالمين} آيتين

DURR-FULL:v1p36/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p36/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p36/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas explains “You alone we worship” as worshipping, affirming God's oneness, fearing and hoping in Him alone, and seeking His help for obedience and all affairs.
DURR-FULL:v1p36/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {إياك نعبد} يعني إياك نوحد ونخاف ونرجو ربنا لا غيرك

DURR-FULL:v1p37/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p37/r1.speaker: علي
DURR-FULL:v1p37/r1.claim: Ali recited “You alone we worship … guide us” with both verbs raised; another report says he used hamza, lengthening, and shadda in “iyyaka.”
DURR-FULL:v1p37/r1.anchor: عن أبي رزين قال: سمعت عليا قرأ هذا الحرف وكان قرشيا عربيا فصيحا {إياك نعبد وإياك نستعين اهدنا

DURR-FULL:v1p37/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p37/r2.speaker: أبو طلحة
DURR-FULL:v1p37/r2.claim: In battle, Abu Talha heard the Prophet recite “Master of Judgment, You alone we worship and seek help”; he saw men fall as angels struck them from front and behind.
DURR-FULL:v1p37/r2.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك عن أبي طلحة قال: كنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في غزو فلقي العدو

RAZI-FULL:v25p74/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p74/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p74/r5.claim: The verse’s mention of God’s servants already contains the aid sought in 1:5, because Satan is barred from them.
