RAZI-FULL:v25p74/r5.anchor: لأن المذكور بعبادي لما كان الشيطان مسدود السبيل عليه مسدود القبيل عنه كان في غاية الإعانة

RAZI-FULL:v25p74/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p74/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p74/r6.claim: Human assistance-seeking serves an aim, so the aim comes first mentally, as the intention to live in a house precedes its construction.
RAZI-FULL:v25p74/r6.anchor: فإن الغرض سابق على الفعل في الإدراك ، وذلك لأن من يبني بيتا للسكنى يدخل في ذهنه أولا فائدة السكنى فيحمله على البناء

RAZI-FULL:v25p74/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p74/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p74/r7.claim: Since God does not act for a purpose, He follows the order of existence, with assistance preceding worship.

RAZI-FULL:v1p15/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p15/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p15/r5.claim: Worship and seeking aid concern carrying out the whole range of religious obligations.

RAZI-FULL:v1p19/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p19/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p19/r8.claim: Worship is performing an act commanded by the one obeyed, out of reverence for that commander.
RAZI-FULL:v1p19/r8.anchor: العبادة عبارة عن الإتيان بالفعل المأموز به على سبيل التعظيم للآمر

RAZI-FULL:v1p19/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p19/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p19/r9.claim: Worship presupposes proof that the world has one God, with unlimited power and knowledge and no needs, who commands and forbids and must be obeyed.
RAZI-FULL:v1p19/r9.anchor: فما لم يثبت بالدليل أن لهذا العالم إلها واحدا قادرا على مقدورات لا نهاية لها عالما بمعلومات لا نهاية لها غنيا عن كل الحاجات

RAZI-FULL:v1p19/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p19/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p19/r10.claim: The verse opens an immense inquiry into God's commands and prohibitions, including this community's law, earlier prophetic laws, and the obligations imposed on angels.
RAZI-FULL:v1p19/r10.anchor: وجميع ما صنف في الدين من كتب الفقه يدخل فيه تكاليف الله ثم كما يدخل فيه تكاليف الله تعالى بحسب هذه الشريعة

RAZI-FULL:v1p19/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p19/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p19/r11.claim: Fiqh addresses obligations of bodily acts, while obligations of the heart are greater and nobler and are treated in ethics and political writings across different communities.
RAZI-FULL:v1p19/r11.anchor: وأيضا فكتب الفقه مشتملة على شرح التكاليف المتوجهة في أعمال الجوارح اما أقسام التكاليف الموجودة في أعمال القلوب فهي أكبر وأعظم وأجل

RAZI-FULL:v1p19/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p19/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p19/r12.claim: The verse contains such an ocean of questions that human intellect and reflection reach only a small portion.
RAZI-FULL:v1p19/r12.anchor: علم حينئذ أن المسائل التي اشتملت هذه الآية عليها كالبحر المحيط الذي لا تصل العقول والأفكار إلا إلى القليل منها

RAZI-FULL:v1p63/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p63/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p63/r1.claim: A person cannot resolve a doubtful proposition by seeking a middle term: if known, the conclusion is already present; if unknown, it cannot be sought, leaving the person unable to escape perplexity.
RAZI-FULL:v1p63/r1.anchor: الحد الأوسط إن كان حاضرا في عقله كان القياس منعقدا والنتيجة لازمة . فحينئذ لا يكون العقل متوقفا في تلك القضية

RAZI-FULL:v1p63/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p63/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p63/r2.claim: The Prophet's unrestricted prayer for refuge from satanic promptings illustrates the servant's inability to secure beliefs and knowledge independently.
RAZI-FULL:v1p63/r2.anchor: أنه تعالى قال لرسوله عليه الصلاة والسلام ﴿ وقل رب أعوذ بك من همزات الشياطين ﴾ [ المؤمنون : 97 ] فهذه الاستعاذة مطلقة

RAZI-FULL:v1p63/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p63/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p63/r3.claim: The body resembles Hell with nineteen gatekeepers: five outer senses, five inner senses, desire, anger, and seven natural faculties, each multiplying into countless individual obstacles.
RAZI-FULL:v1p63/r3.anchor: أن هذا البدن يشبه الجحيم وانكشف لهم أنه جلس على باب هذا الجحيم تسعة عشر نوعا من الزبانية

RAZI-FULL:v1p63/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p63/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p63/r4.claim: Sight's effects pull the heart from the spiritual heights to bodily lowliness; amid innumerable obstacles, only God's aid can free it, so refuge is needed at every moment and at the start of each act.
RAZI-FULL:v1p63/r4.anchor: وذلك الأثر يجر القلب من أوج عالم الروحانيات إلى حضيض عالم الجسمانيات وإذا عرفت هذا ظهر أن مع كثرة هذه العوائق والعلائق

RAZI-FULL:v1p63/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p63/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p63/r5.claim: Sensual and imaginative pleasures, including leadership, intensify desire as they are experienced; each attainment increases craving for further perfection without limit, a sickness the servant cannot cure alone.
RAZI-FULL:v1p63/r5.anchor: الحاصل أن الإنسان كلما كان أكثر فوزا بالمطالب كان أعظم حرصا وأشد رغبة في تحصيل الزائد عليها

RAZI-FULL:v1p63/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p63/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p63/r6.claim: Rāzī supports dependence on God with the command to seek help through patience and prayer and Moses' command to seek God's aid and be patient; a divine-book saying warns against hoping in anyone else.
RAZI-FULL:v1p63/r6.anchor: في تقرير ما ذكرناه قوله تعالى ﴿ إياك نعبد وإياك نستعين ﴾ وقوله : ^ { واستعينوا بالصبر والصلاة } [ البقرة : 45 ] وقول موسى لقومه : ^ { استعينوا بالله واصبروا

RAZI-FULL:v1p63/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p63/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p63/r7.claim: A saying in some divine books says God will disappoint, humiliate, and distance from Himself those who place their hopes in others, while His door remains open to those who call on Him.
RAZI-FULL:v1p63/r7.anchor: وفي بعض الكتب الإلهية أن الله تعالى يقول : وعزتي وجلالي لأقطعن امل كل مؤمل غيري باليأس ولألبسنه ثوب المذلة عند الناس

TAB:1:2/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:2/r11.speaker: author
TAB:1:2/r11.claim: God speaks both clauses: He praises Himself, then teaches and obliges His servants to recite them as a test, with an understood command to say them signaled by “You alone we worship.”
TAB:1:2/r11.anchor: بل ذلك كله كلام الله جل ثناؤه ولكنه جل ذكره حمد نفسه وأثنى عليها

TAB:1:2/r12.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:2/r12.speaker: author
TAB:1:2/r12.claim: The command “say” is omitted because Arabic speakers omit words recoverable from context; here the following worship clause reveals that the praise clause is also an instruction to servants.
TAB:1:2/r12.anchor: أغنت دلالة ما ظهر عليه من القول عن إبداء ما حذف

TAB:1:5/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:5/r1.speaker: author
TAB:1:5/r1.claim: Al-Tabari interprets “You alone we worship” as humbling, abasing, and submitting ourselves to God alone, acknowledging His lordship.
TAB:1:5/r1.anchor: لك اللهم نخشع ،  ونذلّ ،  ونستكين ،  إقرارا لك يا ربنا بالربوبية لا لغيرك

TAB:1:5/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:5/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:1:5/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports Gabriel's gloss that worship means to affirm God's oneness, fear Him, and hope in Him alone.
TAB:1:5/r2.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عباس ،  قال :  قال جبريل لمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم :  قل يا محمد :  إياك نعبد

TAB:1:5/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:5/r3.speaker: author
TAB:1:5/r3.claim: Al-Tabari prefers humility and submission to fear and hope because worship in Arabic fundamentally means abasement; the road called muʿabbad is trodden and subdued, as in Ṭarafa's verse, and a ridden camel is also muʿabbad.
TAB:1:5/r3.anchor: قول طَرَفة بن العبد :  تُبَارِي عِتَاقا ناجياتٍ وأتْبَعَتْ

TAB:1:5/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:5/r4.speaker: author
TAB:1:5/r4.claim: The servants seek God's aid for worship, obedience, and all their affairs, relying on no one else, unlike disbelievers who seek aid from the idols they worship.
TAB:1:5/r4.anchor: وإياك ربنا نستعين على عبادتنا إياك وطاعتنا لك وفي أمورنا كلها لا أحد سواك

TAB:1:5/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:5/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:1:5/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas glosses the request as seeking God's aid for obedience and all one's affairs.
TAB:1:5/r5.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عباس :  وإياك نستعين قال :  إياك :  نستعين على طاعتك وعلى أمورنا كلها

TAB:1:5/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:5/r6.speaker: author
TAB:1:5/r6.claim: The believer asks for help with obedience during the remaining life, not past deeds; God's enabling of the limbs and gift of guidance are grace, not an obligation, and granting or withholding aid entails neither injustice nor faulty governance.
TAB:1:5/r6.anchor: داعٍ أن يعينه فيما بقي من عمره على ما كلفه من طاعته ،  دون ما قد تَقَضّى ومضى

TAB:1:5/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:5/r7.speaker: القائلين بالتفويض من أهل القدر
TAB:1:5/r7.claim: Al-Tabari rejects the Qadari delegation claim that God may command a duty only after making its performance and omission possible through necessary aid; the verse teaches believers to ask for assistance as a divine favor.
TAB:1:5/r7.anchor: أدل الدليل على فساد قول القائلين بالتفويض من أهل القدر

TAB:1:5/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:5/r8.speaker: author
TAB:1:5/r8.claim: He argues that the Qadari premise makes asking for aid equivalent to asking God not to act unjustly, but Muslims approve the former supplication and reject the latter, exposing the premise's error.
TAB:1:5/r8.anchor: وفي إجماع أهل الإسلام جميعا على تصويب قول القائل :  اللهم إنا نستعينك وتخطئتهم قول القائل

TAB:1:5/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:5/r9.speaker: author
TAB:1:5/r9.claim: Worship precedes the request for aid because each entails the other: a servant cannot worship without God's aid, and aid for worship is realized in the servant's act; either order conveys the relation.
TAB:1:5/r9.anchor: كان سواء تقديم ما قدم منهما على صاحبه ،  كما سواء قولك للرجل إذا قضى حاجتك فأحسن إليك

TAB:1:5/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:5/r10.speaker: بعض أهل الغفلة
TAB:1:5/r10.claim: Some inattentive readers took the verse as an instance of fronting and delaying the intended order, like Imruʾ al-Qays's line about enough money and seeking more.
TAB:1:5/r10.anchor: وقد ظن بعض أهل الغفلة أن ذلك من المقدم الذي معناه التأخير

TAB:1:5/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:5/r11.speaker: author
TAB:1:5/r11.claim: Al-Tabari rejects the delayed-order analogy: having enough money does not prevent seeking more, whereas worship and divine aid entail one another, so their stated order is sound.
TAB:1:5/r11.anchor: ومن مشابهة بيت امرىء القيس بمعزلٍ من أجل أنه قد يكفيه القليل من المال ويطلب الكثير

TAB:1:5/r12.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:5/r12.speaker: author
TAB:1:5/r12.claim: The fronted object pronoun is repeated with each verb because each verb governs its own object; Arabic speech is more eloquent when the object is repeated, though omission is permissible when the pronoun follows the verb.
TAB:1:5/r12.anchor: كان الأفصح إعادتها مع كل فعل .  كما كان الفصيح من الكلام إعادتها مع كل فعل

TAB:1:5/r13.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:5/r13.speaker: بعض من لم يمعن النظر
TAB:1:5/r13.claim: Some who did not examine closely compared the repeated “You alone” to the repeated “between” in verses by ʿAdī ibn Zayd and al-Aʿshā of Hamdān.
TAB:1:5/r13.anchor: ظن بعض من لم يمعن النظر أن إعادة «إياك » مع «نستعين » بعد تقدمها

TAB:1:5/r14.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:5/r14.speaker: author
TAB:1:5/r14.claim: Al-Tabari rejects the analogy: “between” requires two complements and is incomplete when one is omitted, but “You alone we worship” is already a complete clause, and each verb properly takes the repeated object.
TAB:1:5/r14.anchor: حاجة كل كلمة كانت نظيرة «إياك نعبد » إلى «إياك » كحاجة «نعبد » إليها

TAB:1:7/r54.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r54.speaker: أهل الإلحاد الطاعنون في القرآن
TAB:1:7/r54.claim: Critics ask why al-Fātiḥa has seven verses when, they argue, the meaning of its remaining verses is already contained in “Master of Judgment Day” and “You alone we worship and ask for help.”
TAB:1:7/r54.anchor: فما الوجه إذ كان الأمر على ما وصفت في إطالة الكلام بمثل سورة أم القرآن بسبع آيات

TAB:1:7/r55.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r55.speaker: author
TAB:1:7/r55.claim: Earlier scriptures each contain some meanings found together in the Qur'an: the Torah gives admonitions and detail, the Psalms praise and glorify, and the Gospel admonishes and reminds; the Qur'an gathers these and adds more.
TAB:1:7/r55.anchor: كالتوراة التي هي مواعظ وتفصيل ، والزّبور الذي هو تحميد وتمجيد ، والإنجيل الذي هو مواعظ وتذكير

TAB:1:7/r56.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r56.speaker: author
TAB:1:7/r56.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says the prior books lack a miracle certifying their recipients, whereas the Qur'an's unmatched composition defeats all attempts to produce even a short surah and proves Muhammad's prophethood.
TAB:1:7/r56.anchor: نظمه العجيب ، ورصفه الغريب ، وتأليفه البديع ، الذي عجزت عن نظم مثل أصغر سورة منه الخطباء

TAB:1:7/r57.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r57.speaker: author
TAB:1:7/r57.claim: The Qur'an's varied contents—encouragement, warning, commands, prohibitions, stories, argument, and parables—also make its extended expression purposeful.

TAB:1:7/r58.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r58.speaker: author
TAB:1:7/r58.claim: Al-Fātiḥa's inimitable arrangement proves prophethood, while its praise and glorification direct people to recognize God's greatness, sovereignty, power, and dominion and to thank Him for His favors.
TAB:1:7/r58.anchor: ليذكروه بآلائه ويحمدوه على نعمائه ، فيستحقوا به منه المزيد ويستوجبوا عليه الثواب الجزيل

TAB:1:7/r59.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r59.speaker: author
TAB:1:7/r59.claim: The account of those favored through knowledge of God and His enabling teaches that every religious and worldly blessing comes from Him, directing requests to God rather than idols or rivals.
TAB:1:7/r59.anchor: تعريف عباده أن كل ما بهم من نعمة في دينهم ودنياهم فمنه ، ليصرفوا رغبتهم إليه

TAB:1:7/r60.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r60.speaker: author
TAB:1:7/r60.claim: Recounting punishments for disobedience warns people away from sin and from incurring God's anger, whose consequences lead to destruction.
TAB:1:7/r60.anchor: ترهيب عباده عن ركوب معاصيه ، والتعرض لما لا قبل لهم به من سخطه

TAB:1:7/r61.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r61.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB:1:7/r61.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that the Prophet said God answers the worshipper's recitation: He calls al-ḥamdu praise, al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm commendation, Mālik Yawm al-Dīn glorification, and the rest of the surah the servant's share.
TAB:1:7/r61.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : «إذا قال العبد : الحمد لله رب العالمين ، قال الله : حمدني عبدي

TAB:1:7/r62.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r62.speaker: أبو هريرة
TAB:1:7/r62.claim: A second Abū Hurayra version gives the same recitation exchange but is not attributed to the Prophet.
TAB:1:7/r62.anchor: عن أبي هريرة ، قال : إذا قال العبد : الحمد لله ، فذكر نحوه ، ولم يرفعه

TAB:1:7/r63.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r63.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB:1:7/r63.claim: Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh reports the divine saying that the prayer is divided between God and His servant, with the servant receiving what he asks; the first three praises are God's, and what follows is for the servant.
TAB:1:7/r63.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : «قال الله عز وجل : قسمت الصلاة بيني وبين عبدي نصفين وله ما سأل

TABATABAI:2:21-25#11/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:21-25#11/r2.speaker: بعض النصارى
TABATABAI:2:21-25#11/r2.claim: He also quotes a Christian's parody of al-Fatiha as another failed counter-imitation.

ELMALILI:v1p85/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:v1p85/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:v1p85/r1.claim: Elmalılı dedicates his words to God's praise, his heart to God's remembrance, and his own path to God's Book.
ELMALILI:v1p85/r1.anchor: Hamdini sözüme sertâc ettim, zikrini kalbime mi‘râc ettim, kitâbını kendime minhâc ettim

ELMALILI:v1p85/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:v1p85/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:v1p85/r2.claim: He credits God with bringing him into existence and awareness, and with making his heart restless through divine love.
ELMALILI:v1p85/r2.anchor: Ben yoktum vâr ettin, varlığından haberdâr ettin, aşkınla gönlümü bî-karâr ettin

ELMALILI:v1p85/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:v1p85/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:v1p85/r3.claim: He seeks refuge in God's grace and guidance and asks for mercy because he has failed to worship adequately.
ELMALILI:v1p85/r3.anchor: İnâyetine sığındım kapına geldim, hidâyetine sığındım lütfuna geldim. Kulluk edemedim affına geldim

ELMALILI:v1p85/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:v1p85/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:v1p85/r5.claim: Human hearing, speech, and ability to make others love depend on God's enabling; Elmalılı says he cannot do these without God.
ELMALILI:v1p85/r5.anchor: Sen sevdirmezsen ben sevdiremem. Sevdir bize hep sevdiklerini

BURHAN:v1p16/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p16/r1.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر بن العربي
BURHAN:v1p16/r1.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī estimates the Qurʾānic sciences at fifty categories and a further vast total calculated by multiplying the Qurʾān’s words by four.
BURHAN:v1p16/r1.anchor: ذكر القاضي أبو بكر بن العربي في كتاب قانون التأويل إن علوم القرآن خمسون علما

BURHAN:v1p16/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p16/r2.speaker: بعض السلف
BURHAN:v1p16/r2.claim: Some early authorities say each Qurʾānic word has an outward sense, an inward sense, a limit, and a point of departure; relations among words exceed human enumeration.
BURHAN:v1p16/r2.anchor: قال بعض السلف إذ لكل كلمة ظاهر وباطن وحد ومقطع

BURHAN:v1p16/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p16/r3.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر بن العربي
BURHAN:v1p16/r3.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī groups the Qurʾān’s core subjects into monotheism, reminder—including promise, warning, Paradise, Hell, and purification—and rulings, including duties and commands.
BURHAN:v1p16/r3.anchor: قال وأم علوم القرآن ثلاثة أقسام توحيد وتذكير وأحكام

BURHAN:v1p16/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p16/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p16/r4.claim: Al-Fātiḥa is the Mother of the Book because it contains all three fields: monotheism through 1:4, rulings in 1:5, and reminder from 1:6 onward.
BURHAN:v1p16/r4.anchor: ولهذا المعنى صارت فاتحة الكتاب أم الكتاب لأن فيها الأقسام الثلاثة

BURHAN:v1p16/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p16/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p16/r5.claim: The claim that Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ equals a third of the Qurʾān is explained either as a reward granted by God or as a meaning-based division, since it contains monotheism.
BURHAN:v1p16/r5.anchor: وقيل ثلثه فى المعنى لأن القرآن ثلاثة أقسام كما ذكرنا وهذه السورة اشتملت على التوحيد

BURHAN:v1p16/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p16/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p16/r6.claim: One explanation for the title “Mother of the Book” is that al-Fātiḥa precedes the rest of the Qurʾān as a mother precedes a daughter.
BURHAN:v1p16/r6.anchor: وقيل صارت أما لأنها مقدمة على القرآن بالقبلية والأم قبل البنت

BURHAN:v1p16/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p16/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p16/r7.claim: Another explanation of “Opening” is that al-Fātiḥa opens the gates of Paradise, as discussed elsewhere.
BURHAN:v1p16/r7.anchor: وقيل سميت فاتحة لأنها تفتح أبواب الجنة على وجوه مذكورة فى مواضعها

BURHAN:v1p16/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p16/r8.speaker: أبو الحكم بن برجان
BURHAN:v1p16/r8.claim: Ibn Barrajān divides Qurʾānic knowledge into God’s names and attributes, prophethood and its proofs, and legal obligation and trial; the last is hardest because it is unfamiliar and neglected.
BURHAN:v1p16/r8.anchor: وقال أبو الحكم بن برجان في كتاب الإرشاد وجملة القرآن تشتمل على ثلاثة علوم

BURHAN:v1p63/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p63/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p63/r1.claim: One explanation for putting the request for help after worship, though help precedes worship in sense, is that the order suits the sūrah’s verse endings.
BURHAN:v1p63/r1.anchor: ومنه تأخير الاستعانة عن العبادة فى قوله تعالى

BURHAN:v1p359/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p359/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p359/r1.claim: The author says the familiar labels for stop quality are not a complete, sound classification and have produced confusion in books on pauses.
BURHAN:v1p359/r1.anchor: فالوجه أن يقال الوقف ضربان اضطرارى واختيارى

BURHAN:v1p359/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p359/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p359/r2.claim: A forced pause is caused only by running out of breath and is not restricted to particular places; examples include Ḥamza pausing within words or before a genitive complement.
BURHAN:v1p359/r2.anchor: فالاضطرارى ما يدعو إليه انقطاع النفس فقط وذلك لا يخص موضعا دون موضع

BURHAN:v1p359/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p359/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p359/r3.claim: An optional pause is preferable and is classified by how the two parts of the statement depend on each other.
BURHAN:v1p359/r3.anchor: والاختيارى وهو أفضلهما هو الذى لا يكون باعتبار انفصال ما بين جزأى القول

BURHAN:v1p359/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p359/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p359/r4.claim: A complete pause leaves both adjoining parts independently sufficient; stopping at “we ask for help” is complete because the following request also stands alone.
BURHAN:v1p359/r4.anchor: الأول التام وهو الذى يكون بحيث يستغنى كل واحد من جزأى القولين

BURHAN:v1p436/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p436/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p436/r1.claim: These insights benefit only someone sincere, reflective, and shaped by the Qurʾān in heart and action; otherwise conduct contradicts professed words.
BURHAN:v1p436/r1.anchor: هذا النوع والذى قبله لن ينتفع به إلا من أخلص لله قلبه ونيته وتدبر الكتاب

BURHAN:v1p436/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p436/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p436/r2.claim: A spiritual adept feared that relying on another person after praying “You alone we ask for help” would make his prayer a lie; likewise, following Satan’s counsel contradicts seeking refuge from him.
BURHAN:v1p436/r2.anchor: كما روى أن عارفا وقعت له واقعة فقال له صديق له نستعين بفلان فقال أخشى أن تبطل صلاتى

BURHAN:v2p320/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p320/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p320/r7.claim: The supplicatory meaning of “we ask for help” is “help us in Your worship.”
BURHAN:v2p320/r7.anchor: ومنها الدعاء كقوله تعالى ﴿ إياك نعبد وإياك نستعين ﴾ 5 أي أعنا على عبادتك

BURHAN:v3p10/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p10/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p10/r3.claim: One explanation for repeating “You alone” is emphasis, like repeating “between” in “between Zayd and between ʿAmr.”
BURHAN:v3p10/r3.anchor: فقيل إنما كررت للتأكيد كما تقول بين زبد وبين عمرو مال

BURHAN:v3p10/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p10/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p10/r4.claim: Another explanation is that omission would attach a following pronoun to the second verb and lose the intended emphasis created by placing its object first.
BURHAN:v3p10/r4.anchor: وقيل إنما كررت لارتفاع أن يتوهم إذا حذفت أن مفعول نستعين ضمير متصل

BURHAN:v3p10/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p10/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p10/r5.claim: The author says no explanation for the repeated object is needed: two different verbs each require an object, so stating both is normal and deletion would be exceptional.
BURHAN:v3p10/r5.anchor: والتحقيق أن السؤال غير متجه لأن هنا عاملين متغايرين كل منهما يقتضي معمولا

BURHAN:v3p235/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p235/r1.speaker: سيبويه
BURHAN:v3p235/r1.claim: Sībawayh says that when coordinated matters are both important, Arabic speakers put first the one that matters more or deserves greater attention; the conjunction itself does not order them.
BURHAN:v3p235/r1.anchor: قال سيبويه كأنهم يقدمون الذي شأنه أهم لهم وهم ببيانه أعنى

BURHAN:v3p235/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p235/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p235/r2.claim: Worship precedes the request for help because worship is the more important matter.
BURHAN:v3p235/r2.anchor: وقال تعالى ﴿ إياك نعبد وإياك نستعين ﴾ 5 فقدم العبادة للاهتمام بها

BURHAN:v3p235/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p235/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p235/r7.claim: Fronting the object in “You alone we worship” expresses exclusive worship: we worship You and no one else.
BURHAN:v3p235/r7.anchor: السابع الاختصاص وذلك بتقديم المفعول والخبر والظرف والجار

BURHAN:v3p247/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p247/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p247/r3.claim: Worship comes before seeking aid because it is the cause of receiving aid.
BURHAN:v3p247/r3.anchor: ومنه قوله ﴿ إياك نعبد وإياك نستعين ﴾ 2 قدمت العبادة لأنها سبب حصول الإعانة

BURHAN:v3p322/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p322/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p322/r2.claim: Al-Fātiḥa begins in third-person style through “Master of the Day of Judgment,” then turns to direct address with “You alone we worship.”
BURHAN:v3p322/r2.anchor: فإن من أولها إلى قوله ﴿ مالك يوم الدين ﴾ 2 أسلوب غيبة

BURHAN:v3p325/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p325/r5.speaker: البيانيون
BURHAN:v3p325/r5.claim: Rhetoricians say changing a style after a long stretch refreshes the listener, draws attention, broadens expression, and eases meter and rhyme.
BURHAN:v3p325/r5.anchor: وقال البيانيون إن الكلام إذا جاء على أسلوب واحد وطال حسن تغيير الطريقة

BURHAN:v3p325/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p325/r6.speaker: القاضي شمس الدين بن الجوزي
BURHAN:v3p325/r6.claim: Ibn al-Jawzī argues that stylistic variation alone does not explain appropriateness, since a long Qurʾānic list in 33:35 maintains one style throughout.
BURHAN:v3p325/r6.anchor: ونازعهم القاضي شمس الدين بن الجوزي وقال الظاهر أن مجرد هذا لا يكفي في المناسبة

BURHAN:v3p325/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p325/r7.speaker: القاضي شمس الدين بن الجوزي
BURHAN:v3p325/r7.claim: Ibn al-Jawzī explains the shift from praise to direct address by the listener’s changing attention: the praise awakens the heart, making “You alone” apt.
BURHAN:v3p325/r7.anchor: فإنه يكون غائبا فيحضر بكلمة واحدة وآخر يكون حاضرا فيغيب

BURHAN:v3p325/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p325/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p325/r8.claim: The particular reasons for a shift of style depend on its setting and on the speaker’s purpose.
BURHAN:v3p325/r8.anchor: وأما الخاصة فتختلف 4 باختلاف محاله ومواقع الكلام فيه

BURHAN:v3p327/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p327/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p327/r1.claim: Human beings begin distant from God behind the veil of majesty; knowing and praising Him and worshipping as befits them makes them ready to address Him directly.
BURHAN:v3p327/r1.anchor: فإذا عرفوه بما هو له وتوسلوا للقرب بالثناء عليه وأقروا بالمحامد له وتعبدوا له بما يليق بهم تأهلوا

BURHAN:v3p327/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p327/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p327/r2.claim: Before prayer and intimate address, worshippers should present God’s attributes with reverence, rather than pray carelessly, playfully, or without intention.
BURHAN:v3p327/r2.anchor: وفيه أنهم يبدون بين يدي كل دعاء له سبحانه ومناجاة له صفات عظمته لمخاطبته على الأدب والتعظيم

BURHAN:v3p327/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p327/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p327/r3.claim: Intimate prayer rises only after purification from ignorance of God, analogously to bodily prayer after ritual purification; this explains placing refuge-seeking before recitation.
BURHAN:v3p327/r3.anchor: ومنه أن مناجاته لا تصعد إلا إذا تطهر من أدناس الجهالة به كما لا تسجد الأعضاء إلا بعد التطهير

BURHAN:v3p326/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p326/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p326/r1.claim: The successive praises intensify the servant's attention: God's exclusive praise, universal lordship, gifts of mercy, and command of judgment prepare the worshipper to approach and seek help.
BURHAN:v3p326/r1.anchor: فإن العبد إذا افتتح حمد مولاه بقوله الحمد لله الدال على اختصاصه بالحمد وجد من نفسه التحرك للإقبال عليه

BURHAN:v3p326/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p326/r2.speaker: قيل
BURHAN:v3p326/r2.claim: One explanation says praise uses third person because it ranks below worship, while direct address elevates the worshipper's encounter; similarly, blessing is explicitly attributed to God but anger is phrased obliquely as a matter of etiquette.
BURHAN:v3p326/r2.anchor: وقيل إنما اختير للحمد لفظ الغيبة وللعبادة الخطاب للإشارة إلى أن الحمد دون العبادة في الرتبة

BURHAN:v3p326/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p326/r3.speaker: قيل
BURHAN:v3p326/r3.claim: Another explanation says that after describing God with magnificent attributes, the discourse directly addresses the clearly identified one worthy of exclusive worship and reliance.
BURHAN:v3p326/r3.anchor: وقيل لأنه لما ذكر الحقيق بالحمد وأجرى عليه بالصفات العظيمة من كونه ربا للعالمين ورحمانا ورحيما

BURHAN:v1p260#2/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p260#2/r2.speaker: بعض الأئمة
BURHAN:v1p260#2/r2.claim: Some imams say al-Fatiha affirms lordship, seeks guidance in Islam, and asks protection from Judaism and Christianity.
BURHAN:v1p260#2/r2.anchor: قال بعض الأئمة وسورة الفاتحة تضمنت الإقرار بالربوبية والالتجاء إليه فى دين الإسلام

ITQAN:v1p102#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p102#2/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p102#2/r5.claim: The worshippers speak this supplication; an implied “say” can be supplied, as with the two earlier human utterances, unlike Gabriel’s and the angels’ speech.
ITQAN:v1p102#2/r5.anchor: إلا أنه يمكن هنا تقدير القول أي قولوا وكذا الآيتان الأوليان يصح أن يقدر فيهما قل بخلاف الثالثة والرابعة

ITQAN:v1p150#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p150#2/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p150#2/r1.claim: The Fatiha is also called al-Nur, al-Hamd, al-Shukr, al-Hamd al-Ula, and al-Hamd al-Qusra.
ITQAN:v1p150#2/r1.anchor: ثاني عشرها وثالث عشرها سورة الحمد وسورة الشكر

ITQAN:v1p150#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p150#2/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p150#2/r2.claim: The Fatiha is named al-Ruqya, al-Shifa, and al-Shafiya in view of reports about its special virtues.
ITQAN:v1p150#2/r2.anchor: سادس عشرها وسابع عشرها وثامن عشرها الرقية والشفاء والشافية للأحاديث الآتية في نوع الخواص

ITQAN:v1p150#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p150#2/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p150#2/r3.claim: It is called the Surah of Prayer because prayer depends on it.
ITQAN:v1p150#2/r3.anchor: تاسع عشرها سورة الصلاة لتوقف الصلاة عليها

ITQAN:v1p150#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p150#2/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p150#2/r4.claim: It is also said to be called al-Salah, as in the hadith “I divided the prayer between Me and My servant,” where “the prayer” means this surah.
ITQAN:v1p150#2/r4.anchor: وقيل إن من أسمائها الصلاة أيضا لحديث قسمت الصلاة بيني وبين عبدي نصفين أي السورة

ITQAN:v1p150#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p150#2/r5.speaker: المرسي
ITQAN:v1p150#2/r5.claim: Al-Mursi explains the name al-Salah as naming the surah after something necessary to it, namely prayer.
ITQAN:v1p150#2/r5.anchor: قال المرسي لأنها من لوازمها فهو من باب تسمية الشيء باسم لازمه

ITQAN:v1p150#2/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p150#2/r9.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p150#2/r9.claim: It is the Surah of Intimate Discourse because the servant privately addresses the Lord in this verse.
ITQAN:v1p150#2/r9.anchor: الرابع والعشرون سورة المناجاة لأن العبد يناجي فيها ربه

ITQAN:v1p150#2/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p150#2/r10.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p150#2/r10.claim: It is the Surah of Entrusting because the verse expresses reliance and entrusting oneself to God.
ITQAN:v1p150#2/r10.anchor: الخامس والعشرون سورة التفويض لاشتمالها عليه

ITQAN:v1p150#2/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p150#2/r11.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p150#2/r11.claim: The author says this collection of Fatiha names had not previously been gathered in a book.
ITQAN:v1p150#2/r11.anchor: فهذا ما وقفت عليه من أسمائها ولم تجتمع في كتاب قبل هذا

ITQAN:v1p226/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p226/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p226/r5.claim: Both stops are complete, but the stop after “Master of the Day of Judgment” is more complete because the next clause shares the direct address, unlike the first.
ITQAN:v1p226/r5.anchor: كلاهما تام إلا أن الأول أتم من الثاني لاشتراك الثاني فيما بعده في معنى الخطاب

ITQAN:v1p226/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p226/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p226/r6.claim: Some call the less complete of two complete stops “resembling complete.”
ITQAN:v1p226/r6.anchor: وهذا هو الذي سماه بعضهم شبيها بالتام

ITQAN:v1p226/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p226/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p226/r7.claim: A “necessary” stop is strongly recommended to make the intended meaning clear, even though a relation to what follows remains.
ITQAN:v1p226/r7.anchor: ومنه ما يتأكد استحسانه لبيان المعنى المقصود به وهو الذي سماه السجاوندي باللازم

ITQAN:v3p140/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p140/r1.speaker: أهل البيان
ITQAN:v3p140/r1.claim: Rhetoricians generally say fronting an object, adverbial, or prepositional phrase conveys restriction; thus the verse means that worship and help are directed to God alone.
ITQAN:v3p140/r1.anchor: كاد أهل البيان يطبقون على أن تقديم المعمول يفيد الحصر سواء كان مفعولا أو ظرفا أو مجرورا ولهذا قيل في

ITQAN:v3p140/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p140/r3.speaker: ابن الحاجب
ITQAN:v3p140/r3.claim: Ibn al-Hajib rejects the usual restrictive reading of a fronted complement as an illusion, citing the command to worship God sincerely and then the fronted “rather, worship God.”
ITQAN:v3p140/r3.anchor: وخالف في ذلك ابن الحاجب فقال في شرح المفصل الاختصاص الذي يتوهمه كثير من الناس من تقديم المعمول وهم

ITQAN:v3p140/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p140/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p140/r4.claim: The author answers that “sincerely devoting religion to Him” already implies restriction; even without it, a clause may name the restricted object without restrictive syntax, while “rather worship God” strongly implies exclusivity after the warning against shirk.
ITQAN:v3p140/r4.anchor: أغنى عن إفادة الحصر في الآية الأولى ولو لم يكن فما المانع من ذكر المحصور في محل بغير صيغة الحصر

ITQAN:v3p232/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p232/r2.speaker: قيل
ITQAN:v3p232/r2.claim: One explanation says that after God is described as Lord, Merciful, and Master of Judgment, the worshipper addresses Him alone as worthy of worship and reliance.
ITQAN:v3p232/r2.anchor: وقيل لأنه لما ذكر الحقيق بالحمد وأجرى عليه الصفات العظيمة من كونه ربا للعالمين ورحمانا ورحيما ومالكا ليوم الدين تعلق العلم بمعلوم عظيم الشأن

ITQAN:v3p232/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p232/r3.speaker: قيل
ITQAN:v3p232/r3.claim: A spiritual explanation sees a movement from creatures’ initial distance and inability to converse with God to readiness for intimate address after knowing, praising, and worshipping Him.
ITQAN:v3p232/r3.anchor: ومن لطائفه التنبيه على أن مبتدأ الخلق الغيبة منهم عنه سبحانه وتعالى وقصورهم عن محاضرته ومخاطبته وقيام حجاب العظمة عليهم

ITQAN:v3p293/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p293/r1.speaker: ابن الأثير
ITQAN:v3p293/r1.claim: Ibn al-Athir calls this transition a form of separation better than conjunction: a strong connection between moving from one kind of speech to another.
ITQAN:v3p293/r1.anchor: قال ابن الأثير هذا في هذا المقام من الفصل الذي هو أحسن من الوصل وهي علاقة أكيدة بين الخروج من كلام إلى آخر

ITQAN:v3p293/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p293/r2.speaker: الزنجاني والطيبي
ITQAN:v3p293/r2.claim: Al-Zanjani and al-Tibi define a good transition to the request as stating the means before reaching the intended aim; the verse moves from praise to the request for help and guidance.
ITQAN:v3p293/r2.anchor: قال الزنجاني والطيبي وهو أن يخرج إلى الغرض بعد تقدم الوسيلة

ITQAN:v4p420/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p420/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ITQAN:v4p420/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the Fatiha encompasses praise, worship through commands and prohibitions, and promise and warning; every Qur’anic verse falls under one of these topics.
ITQAN:v4p420/r1.anchor: وبيان اشتمالها على علوم القرآن قرره الزمخشري باشتمالها على الثناء على الله تعالى بما هو أهله وعلى التعبد بالأمر والنهي وعلى الوعد والوعيد

ITQAN:v4p420/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p420/r2.speaker: الإمام فخر الدين
ITQAN:v4p420/r2.claim: Fakhr al-Din maps the Qur’an’s four aims—God, resurrection, prophethood, and divine decree—onto the Fatiha: praise, Judgment Day, worship and reliance, and guidance through the surah’s end; this supports its name Umm al-Qur’an.
ITQAN:v4p420/r2.anchor: وقال الإمام فخر الدين المقصود من القرآن كله تقرير أمور أربعة الإلهيات والمعاد والنبوات وإثبات القضاء والقدر لله تعالى

ITQAN:v4p420/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p420/r3.speaker: البيضاوي
ITQAN:v4p420/r3.claim: Al-Baydawi says the Fatiha contains theoretical wisdom, practical rulings in walking the straight path, and knowledge of the ranks of the blessed and abodes of the wretched.
ITQAN:v4p420/r3.anchor: وقال البيضاوي هي مشتملة على الحكم النظرية والأحكام العملية التي هي سلوك الطريق المستقيم والاطلاع على مراتب السعداء ومنازل الأشقياء

ITQAN:v4p420/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p420/r4.speaker: الطيبي
ITQAN:v4p420/r4.claim: Al-Tibi divides the Fatiha’s religious knowledge into foundations (God and attributes, prophethood, resurrection), branches (worship), ethical perfection and seeking the path, and accounts of earlier peoples with promise and threat.
ITQAN:v4p420/r4.anchor: وقال الطيبي هي مشتملة على أربعة أنواع من العلوم التي هي مناط الدين

ITQAN:v4p421/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p421/r1.speaker: الغزالي
ITQAN:v4p421/r1.claim: Al-Ghazali lists three essential Qur’anic aims—knowing God, the straight path, and the return in the Hereafter—and three supplementary aims: the obedient, deniers’ speech, and the stations of the path, all signaled by the Fatiha.
ITQAN:v4p421/r1.anchor: وقال الغزالي مقاصد القرآن سنة ثلاثة مهمة وثلاثة متمة الأولى تعريف المدعو إليه كما أشير إليه بصدرها

ITQAN:v4p421/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p421/r2.speaker: الزركشي وناصر الدين بن الميلق
ITQAN:v4p421/r2.claim: They reconcile the hadith calling the Fatiha two-thirds of the Qur’an by saying it indicates all Qur’anic aims through inclusion and implication, but not direct correspondence; those are two of three modes of indication.
ITQAN:v4p421/r2.anchor: ذكره الزركشي في شرح التنبيه وناصر الدين بن الميلق قال وأيضا الحقوق ثلاثة حق الله على عباده

ITQAN:v4p421/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p421/r3.speaker: ناصر الدين بن الميلق
ITQAN:v4p421/r3.claim: A second explanation counts three kinds of rights—God’s claim on servants, servants’ claim on God, and people’s claims on one another—and says the Fatiha explicitly covers the first two, hence two-thirds.
ITQAN:v4p421/r3.anchor: قال وأيضا الحقوق ثلاثة حق الله على عباده وحق العباد على الله وحق بعض العباد على بعض وقد اشتملت الفاتحة صريحا على الحقين الأولين فناسب كونها بصريحها ثلثين

ITQAN:v4p421/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p421/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p421/r4.claim: The hadith “I divided the prayer between Me and My servant in two halves” supports the Fatiha’s two-thirds description.
ITQAN:v4p421/r4.anchor: وحديث ( قسمت الصلاة بيني وبين عبدي نصفين ) شاهد لذلك

ITQAN:v4p421/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p421/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p421/r5.claim: There is no conflict between hadiths calling the Fatiha the greatest surah and al-Baqara the greatest: al-Baqara is greatest among surahs other than the Fatiha because of its detailed laws, parables, and arguments.
ITQAN:v4p421/r5.anchor: قلت ولا تنافي أيضا بين كون الفاتحة أعظم السور وبين الحديث الآخر أن البقرة أعظم السور

ITQAN:v4p421/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p421/r6.speaker: ابن العربي
ITQAN:v4p421/r6.claim: Ibn al-Arabi quotes a teacher saying the Fatiha contains a thousand commands, prohibitions, rulings, and reports; Ibn Umar spent eight years teaching it because of its jurisprudential depth.
ITQAN:v4p421/r6.anchor: قال ابن العربي في أحكامه سمعت بعض أشياخي يقول فيها ألف أمر وألف نهي وألف حكم وألف خبر

ITQAN:v4p490/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p490/r5.speaker: ابن أبي جمرة
ITQAN:v4p490/r5.claim: Commentary on the verse requires explaining God’s majesty, worship, its forms and performance, the worshipper’s qualities, and the nature and manner of seeking aid.
ITQAN:v4p490/r5.anchor: يحتاج إلى بيان المعبود من جلالته والعبادة وكيفيتها وصفتها وأدائها على جميع أنواعها والعابد في صفته

ITQAN:v3p284/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p284/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p284/r1.claim: The Fatiha points to all major Qur’anic disciplines: knowledge of God and attributes, prophecy, resurrection, worship, ethical conduct and the straight path, and stories teaching the outcomes of obedience and disobedience.
ITQAN:v3p284/r1.anchor: وقد وجه ذلك بأن العلوم التي احتوى عليها القرآن قامت بها الأديان أربعة علم الأصول ومداره على معرفة الله وصفاته

ITQAN:v3p284/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p284/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p284/r2.claim: By signaling all Qur’anic aims, the Fatiha achieves an exemplary opening and combines beautiful words, pleasing cadence, and rhetorical forms.
ITQAN:v3p284/r2.anchor: فنبه في الفاتحة على جميع مقاصد القرآن وهذا هو الغاية في براعة الاستهلال مع ما اشتملت عليه من الألفاظ الحسنة والمقاطع المستحسنة وأنواع البلاغة

ITQAN:v3p204#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p204#2/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p204#2/r3.claim: Declarative form can express supplication: ask for help, curse Abu Lahab, or invoke ruin and a curse on others.
ITQAN:v3p204#2/r3.anchor: وبمعنى الدعاء نحو ﴿ وإياك نستعين ﴾ أي أعنا ومنه ﴿ تبت يدا أبي لهب وتب ﴾ فإنه دعاء عليه

ITQAN:v3p154/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p154/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p154/r4.claim: An omitted complement can express generality: 'You alone we ask for help' means in worship and all our affairs, while God's call to the Abode of Peace addresses each person.
ITQAN:v3p154/r4.anchor: أي على العبادة وعلى أمورنا كلها

ITQAN:v3p85#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p85#2/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p85#2/r5.claim: Exclusive wording implies exclusion of all others: there is no god or guardian besides God, and worship is directed to God alone.
ITQAN:v3p85#2/r5.anchor: وحصر نحو ﴿ لا إله إلا الله ﴾ ﴿ إنما إلهكم الله ﴾ أي فغيره ليس بإله

ITQAN:v1p47#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p47#2/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p47#2/r3.claim: One view says half of al-Fatiha was revealed in Medina, apparently its second half, but the author says this view has no evidence.
ITQAN:v1p47#2/r3.anchor: الفاتحة تقدم قول أن نصفها نزل بالمدينة والظاهر أنه النصف الثاني ولا دليل لهذا القول

ITQAN:v3p38/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p38/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p38/r5.claim: Sequence can mark causation: worship brings aid, repentance brings purification, slander causes sin, and the gaze can lead to sexual desire.
ITQAN:v3p38/r5.anchor: ومنه تقديم العبادة على الاستعانة في سورة الفاتحة لأنها سبب حصول الإعانة

ZAJJAJ:v1p47/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p47/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p47/r4.claim: ʿIbāda means obedience together with humility; the phrase means that we obey God with submission.
ZAJJAJ:v1p47/r4.anchor: معنى العبادة في اللغة الطاعة مع الخضوع، يقال هذا طريق معبد

ZAJJAJ:v1p47/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p47/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p47/r5.claim: A road is called maʿbad when much foot traffic has subdued it, and a camel is maʿbad when coated with tar.
ZAJJAJ:v1p47/r5.anchor: وبعير معبد، إذا كان مطليا بالقطران

ZAJJAJ:v1p47/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p47/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p47/r6.claim: Iyyāka is the accusative object, while its kāf is genitive through annexation to iyyā; iyyā is a noun used for accusative pronouns and may take any such pronoun.

ZAJJAJ:v1p47/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p47/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p47/r7.claim: Adding iyyā to an overt noun, as in iyyā Zayd, is inelegant because it is reserved for pronouns.
ZAJJAJ:v1p47/r7.anchor: كان قبيحا لأنه خص به المضمر

ZAJJAJ:v1p47/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p47/r8.speaker: الخليل
ZAJJAJ:v1p47/r8.claim: Al-Khalīl transmits an Arab expression warning a man over sixty to beware of young women, with iyyā used before a noun.
ZAJJAJ:v1p47/r8.anchor: رواه الخليل: (إذا بلغ الرجل الستين فإياه وإيا الشواب

ZAJJAJ:v1p47/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p47/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p47/r9.claim: He rejects the claim that iyyāka is one indivisible noun: nouns do not take annexation this way, while Arabic treats the hāʾ of iyyāhu like that in ʿaṣāhu.
ZAJJAJ:v1p47/r9.anchor: ومن قال إن إياك بكماله الاسم، قيل له:

ZAJJAJ:v1p49/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p49/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p49/r1.claim: Nastaʿīnu originally was nastaʿūnu, from maʿūna and ʿawn; wāw became yāʾ under the weight of kasra, the kasra moved to ʿayn, and the resulting sound changes follow examples like aʿāna/yaʿīnu.
ZAJJAJ:v1p49/r1.anchor: الأصل في نستعين: نستعون لأنه إنما معناه من المعونة والعون.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4/r1.claim: Samarrāʾ distinguishes fronting a word before its own governor from reordering words relative to each other.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4/r2.claim: Fronting before a word's governor usually marks exclusivity: ‘I helped Khālid’ does not, while ‘Khālid I helped’ singles him out.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4/r2.anchor: وهذا التقديم في الغالب يفيد الاختصاص

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4/r3.claim: The object ‘You’ is fronted with worship and seeking help because these belong exclusively to God; worship is similarly exclusive in 39:66 and 2:172.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4/r3.anchor: على فعل العبادة وعلى فعل الاستعانة دون فعل الهداية

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4/r12.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4/r12.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4/r12.claim: Fronting may also serve praise, glorification, magnification, or disparagement, although exclusivity is its most common effect.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4/r12.anchor: وقد يكون التقديم من هذا النوع لغرض آخر كالمدح والثناء والتعظيم والتحقير وغير ذلك من الأغراض

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p24/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p24/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p24/r1.claim: Fronting can place a word before its governing verb, as in “You alone we worship”; it can also reorder words that are not the verb’s object.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p24/r1.anchor: تقديم اللفظ على عامله نحو قوله تعالى (إياك نعبد وإياك نستعين)

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p25/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p25/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p25/r1.claim: Fronting an object usually conveys exclusivity: “I helped Khalid” permits helping others too, while “Khalid I helped” singles him out.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p25/r1.anchor: وهذا التقديم في الغالب يفيد الإختصاص فقولك (أنجدت خالداً) يفيد أنك أنجدت خالداً

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p25/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p25/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p25/r2.claim: Fronting “You” before worship and seeking help makes both acts exclusive to God; the verse does not front the object of guidance because guidance is not requested exclusively for oneself.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p25/r2.anchor: على فعل العبادة وعلى فعل الإستعانة دون فعل الهداية قلم يقل إيانا اهد كما قال في الأوليين

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p25/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p25/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p25/r3.claim: The fronted phrases “upon God” and “to Him” in commands to trust and turn back likewise signal that trust and repentance belong to God alone.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p25/r3.anchor: فقدم الجار والمجرور للدلالة على الإختصاص وذلك لأن التوكّل لا يكون إلا على الله وحده

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p476/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p476/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p476/r1.claim: Preposing includes placing a word before its governing word, such as fronting the object before its verb; other examples include fronted circumstantials and adverbial phrases.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p476/r1.anchor: تقديم اللفظ على عامله نحو قوله تعالى (إياك نعبد وإياك نستعين)

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p476/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p476/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p476/r2.claim: This kind of preposing usually conveys restriction: Khalid I helped restricts the help to Khalid, unlike I helped Khalid.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p476/r2.anchor: وهذا التقديم في الغالب يفيد الإختصاص فقولك (أنجدت خالداً) يفيد أنك أنجدت خالداً ولا يفيد أنك

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p476/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p476/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p476/r3.claim: Fronted إياك restricts worship and seeking help to God alone, as do other Quranic frontings that restrict worship, gratitude, trust, and turning back to Him.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p476/r3.anchor: وسبب ذلك أن العبادة والإستعانة مختصتان بالله تعالى فلا يعبد أحد غيره ولا يستعان به

NASHR:v1p47/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p47/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p47/r1.claim: He rejects the claim that the seven ahruf mean following seven famous imams; readings must be received reliably, word by word, through successive imams to the Prophet.
NASHR:v1p47/r1.anchor: يتوهمون أن معنى السبعة الأحرف المذكورة في الخبر اتباع هؤلاء الأئمة السبعة وليس ذلك على ما توهموه

NASHR:v1p47/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p47/r8.speaker: عمرو بن فائد الإسواري
NASHR:v1p47/r8.claim: Amr b. Fa'id reads both instances of iyyāka with a light yā'; some later scholars disliked it because it sounds like iyā, the sun's light.
NASHR:v1p47/r8.anchor: عمرو بن فائد الإسواري (إياك نعبد وإياك) بتخفيف الياء فيهما، وقد كره ذلك بعض المتأخرين

NASHR:v1p47/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p47/r9.speaker: يحيى بن وثاب
NASHR:v1p47/r9.claim: Yahya b. Waththab reads the first nūn of nastaʿīn with kasra, a well-known and good dialect.
NASHR:v1p47/r9.anchor: يحيى بن وثاب (نستعين) بكسر النون الأولى وهي لغة مشهورة حسنة

NASHR:v1p47/r12.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p47/r12.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p47/r12.claim: Maki deems these noncanonical-imam readings permissible when reliably transmitted, since each has a sound Arabic analysis and agrees with the codex spelling; Ibn al-Jazari says others also share some forms.
NASHR:v1p47/r12.anchor: القراءة به لمن رواه عن الثقات جائزة لصحة وجهه في العربية وموافقته الخط إذا صح نقله

NASHR:v1p48/r11.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p48/r11.speaker: الفضل بن محمد الرقاشي
NASHR:v1p48/r11.claim: Al-Fadl b. Muhammad al-Raqashi reads both instances with fatḥa on the hamza; the source also transmits it from Ali through Sufyan al-Thawri.
NASHR:v1p48/r11.anchor: الفضل بن محمد الرقاشي (أياك نعبد وأياك) بفتح الهمزة فيهما، وهي لغة ورواها سفيان الثوري عن علي أيضا

NASHR:v1p48/r12.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p48/r12.speaker: أبو عمرو
NASHR:v1p48/r12.claim: Abu Amr, through Abd Allah b. Dawud al-Khuraybi, reads the alif of both instances of iyyāka with imāla because of the preceding kasra.
NASHR:v1p48/r12.anchor: (وعن) أبي عمرو في رواية عبد الله بن داود الخريبي إمالة الألف منهما ووجه ذلك الكسرة من قبل

NASHR:v1p48/r13.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p48/r13.speaker: بعض أهل مكة
NASHR:v1p48/r13.claim: Some Meccans read naʿbud with a still dāl for lightening, or treat it as a verse ending and carry a pause into connected recitation.
NASHR:v1p48/r13.anchor: وعن بعض أهل مكة (نعبد) بإسكان الدال ووجهها التخفيف كقراءة أبي عمرو (يأمركم) بالإسكان

NASHR:v1p226/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p226/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p226/r1.claim: A complete stop commonly comes at verse ends and story endings; he illustrates one at māliki yawm al-dīn, followed by the start iyyāka naʿbudu.
NASHR:v1p226/r1.anchor: نحو الوقف على مالك يوم الدين والابتداء إياك نعبد وإياك نستعين

NASHR:v1p227/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p227/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p227/r1.claim: Both māliki yawm al-dīn and iyyāka naʿbudu permit a complete stop, but the first is more complete because the second shares the address's meaning with what follows.
NASHR:v1p227/r1.anchor: مالك يوم الدين، وإياك نعبد، وإياك نستعين كلاهما تام، إلا أن الأول أتم من الثاني

NASHR:v1p49/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p49/r7.speaker: قتيبة عن الكسائي، كردم عن نافع، ورش
NASHR:v1p49/r7.claim: The author adds unlisted transmissions: Qutayba from al-Kisa'i has imāla in al-ʿālamīn and al-raḥmān; Kurram from Nafi and al-Ahwazi from Warsh lengthen vowels in mālik, naʿbudu, and iyyāka.
NASHR:v1p49/r7.anchor: وبقي منها روايات أخرى رويناها منها إمالة (العالمين والرحمن) بخلاف لقتيبة عن الكسائي، ومنها إشباع الكسرة من (ملك يوم الدين)

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r1.claim: Iyyā takes attached first, second, or third person pronouns and forms an independent accusative pronoun, not an overt noun with an annexed suffix, contrary to an unnamed claimant.
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r1.anchor: فيكون ضمير نصب منفصلاً لا اسماً ظاهراً أضيف خلافاً لزاعمه

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r2.claim: Grammarians differ over whether the pronoun is the whole form or only part of it, whether the suffixes are letters or nouns, and whether iyyā is added solely to host pronouns.
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r2.anchor: وهل الضمير هو مع لواحقه أو هو وحده

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r3.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r3.claim: The majority read iyyā with a kasra on hamza and a doubled yāʾ.
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r3.anchor: وأما لغاته فبكسر الهمزة وتشديد الياء

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r4.speaker: الفضل الرقاشي
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r4.claim: Al-Faḍl al-Ruqāshī reads it with a fatḥa on hamza and a doubled yāʾ.
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r4.anchor: وبفتح الهمزة وتشديد الياء ، وبها قرأ الفضل الرقاشي

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r5.speaker: عمرو بن فائد
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r5.claim: ʿAmr ibn Fāʾid, transmitting from Ubayy, reads it with kasra on hamza and an undoubled yāʾ.

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r6.speaker: ابن السوار الغنوي
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r6.claim: Ibn al-Sawwār al-Ghanawī reads the forms with either a kasra or fatḥa hamza replaced by hāʾ.

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r7.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r7.claim: Abū ʿUbayda’s derivation of iyyā is weak; Abū Ḥayyān says he was poor at grammar despite mastery of lexicon and Arab history.
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r7.anchor: وكان أبو عبيدة لا يحسن النحو

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r8.claim: If iyyā is derived, proposed sources include the word in a poetic line and āya, with the latter analysis making its root consonant yāʾ.

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r9.claim: Several competing root and pattern analyses are proposed for iyyā, but Abū Ḥayyān judges them all weak.
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r9.anchor: وهل وزنه إفعل وأصله إ أو و أو إ أو ي أو فعيل فأصله أو يو

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r10.claim: Annexing iyyā to an overt noun is rare, or a poetic necessity; the text gives examples of both.

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r11.claim: In the familiar warning use, iyyā can contain a nominative pronoun that is followed by a nominative emphatic pronoun.
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r11.anchor: واستعماله تحذيراً معروف فيحتمل ضميراً مرفوعاً

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r12.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r12.claim: The majority explain worship as humility and submission, which Abū Ḥayyān later identifies as the basic lexical sense.

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r13.speaker: ابن السكيت
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r13.claim: Ibn al-Sikkīt gives tajrīd, stripping or devotion, as an alternative meaning of worship.
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r13.anchor: أو التجريد ، قاله ابن السكيت ، وتعديه

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r14.claim: The transitive sense changes with form: ʿabadt al-rajul means I humbled the man, while ʿabadt Allāh means I humbled myself to God.
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r14.anchor: عبدت الرجل ذللته ، وعبدت الله ذللت له

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r15.speaker: الحسن، وأبو مجلز، وأبو المتوكل
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r15.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Abū Majliz, and Abū al-Mutawakkil read iyyāka yaʿbudu with yāʾ and a passive verb.
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r15.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ، وأبو مجلز ، وأبو المتوكل

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r16.speaker: بعض أهل مكة
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r16.claim: Some Meccans read naʿbud with the dāl unvowelled.
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r16.anchor: وعن بعض أهل مكة نعبد بإسكان الدال

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r17.speaker: زيد بن علي، ويحيى بن وثاب، وعبيد بن عمير الليثي
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r17.claim: Zayd ibn ʿAlī, Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, and ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr al-Laythī read naʿbud with kasra on its initial nūn.
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r17.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي ، ويحيى بن وثاب ، وعبيد بن عمير الليثي

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r18.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r18.claim: Istiʿāna means seeking aid; the form istifʿala has twelve uses, including request, transformation, treating something as something, and several forms of equivalence or substitution.

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r19.speaker: صاحب اللوامح
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r19.claim: The author of al-Lawāmiʿ reports a form wayyāka, with hamza changed to wāw, but is unsure whether it came from al-Farrāʾ or Arab usage.
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r19.anchor: وقال صاحب اللوامح : وقد جاء فيه وياك

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r20.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r20.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r20.claim: The change to wāw reflects aversion to hamza; this reverses the alternative tendency to replace a kasra-bearing wāw with hamza.
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r20.anchor: وفي وياك فروا من الهمزة إلى الواو

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r21.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r21.speaker: أبو الحسن بن سيده
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r21.claim: Ibn Sīda says tamāsaktu, masaktu, amsaktu, and istamsaktu bi-shayʾ have the same sense, holding fast to something; this adds two equivalence uses to istifʿala.
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r21.anchor: أبو الحسن بن سيده في المحكم

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r22.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r22.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r22.claim: Istiʿāna means asking for help, as in other verbs of request.

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r23.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r23.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r23.claim: The majority pronounce the initial nūn of nastaʿīn with fatḥa, the Hijazi and most correct form.
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r23.anchor: وفتح نون نستعين قرأ بها الجمهور

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r24.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r24.speaker: عبيد بن عمير الليثي، وزر بن حبيش، ويحيى بن وثاب، والنخعي، والأعمش
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r24.claim: These readers pronounce the initial nūn of nastaʿīn with kasra, matching Qays, Tamīm, Asad, and Rabīʿa; similar imperfect forms follow the same rule.
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r24.anchor: وقرأ عبيد بن عمير الليثي ، وزر بن حبيش

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r25.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r25.speaker: أبو جعفر الطوسي
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r25.claim: Abū Jaʿfar al-Ṭūsī identifies the kasra on the initial nūn as the dialect of Hudhayl.
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r25.anchor: أبو جعفر الطوسي : هي لغة هذيل

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r26.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r26.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r26.claim: In these forms wāw shifts to alif in istaʿāna and mustaʿān, and to yāʾ in nastaʿīn and mustaʿīn; deletion in istiʿāna belongs to morphology.
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r26.anchor: وانقلاب الواو ألفاً في استعان ومستعان

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r27.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r27.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r27.claim: Istaʿāna can take a direct object or the preposition bi-; its verbal noun also shows morphological deletion.

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r28.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r28.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r28.claim: Iyyāka is the fronted direct object of naʿbud.

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r29.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r29.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r29.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes object fronting to mean exclusivity, as though the verse said only you we worship; Abū Ḥayyān says it instead signals care and attention to the object.
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r29.anchor: والزمخشري يزعم أنه لا يقدم على العامل إلا للتخصيص

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r30.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r30.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r30.claim: An Arab addressed an insulter with iyyāka aʿnī; the reply wa-ʿanka aʿriḍ shows that speakers front what matters most.
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r30.anchor: وسب أعرابي آخر فأعرض عنه وقال

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r31.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r31.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r31.claim: Iyyāka is an iltifāt from third-person reference, since a consistent third-person construction would say iyyāhu.
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r31.anchor: وإياك التفات لأنه انتقال من الغيبة

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r32.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r32.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r32.claim: Iltifāt shifts among third person, address, and first person, in any direction; the same referent must remain in view, whether named or pronominal.
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r32.anchor: والانتقال من فنون البلاغة ، وهو الانتقال من الغيبة للخطاب

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r33.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r33.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r33.claim: Rhetoricians cite iltifāt as a display of command over expression; some also seek a distinct local effect, and Ibn al-Athīr wrote notably on the device.
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r33.anchor: فائدة هذا الالتفات إظهار الملكة في الكلام

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r34.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r34.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r34.claim: After praising God for lordship, mercy, and kingship in 1:2–4, the speaker turns to address Him and says that he and others worship and submit to Him.
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r34.anchor: أقبل الحامد مخبراً بأثر ذكره الحمد المستقر له منه ومن غيره

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r35.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r35.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r35.claim: The first-person plural nūn includes the speaker and others, just as the preceding praise encompasses all who praise.
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r35.anchor: وكذلك أتى بالنون التي تكون له ولغيره

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r36.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r36.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r36.claim: Addressing a present person directly is more tactful and effective than referring to him as absent with iyyāhu.
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r36.anchor: ونظير هذا أنك تذكر شخصاً متصفاً بأوصاف جليلة

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r37.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r37.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r37.claim: The direct address in iyyāka naʿbud is a preparation for the supplication ihdinā that follows.
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r37.anchor: ولأنه ذكر ذلك توطئة للدعاء في قوله اهدنا

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r38.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r38.speaker: من ذهب إلى أن ملك منادى
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r38.claim: If malik is taken as a vocative, iyyāka continues address rather than making an iltifāt; shifts to third person can nevertheless follow a vocative, as the cited poems show.
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r38.anchor: ومن ذهب إلى أن ملك منادى

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r39.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r39.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r39.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī counts three iltifāts in Imruʾ al-Qays’s lines, but Abū Ḥayyān identifies only two: address to third person, then third person to first person.
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r39.anchor: ودعوى الزمخشري في أبيات امرئ القيس الثلاثة

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r40.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r40.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r40.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects identifying the first shift by inferred presence: iltifāt concerns actual wording, and inserting an unspoken say before either phrase would remove the shift.
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r40.anchor: إن الأول هو الانتقال من الغيبة إلى الحضور أشد خطأ

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r41.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r41.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r41.claim: The passive reading iyyāka yuʿbadu seems to lack a governor for the accusative pronoun; Abū Ḥayyān explains it as a metaphorical substitution of nominative anta, followed by an unusual shift to third person.
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r41.anchor: وقراءة من قرأ إياك يعبد بالياء مبنياً للمفعول

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r42.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r42.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r42.claim: Worship can also mean obedience, as in the command not to worship Satan.
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r42.anchor: أو الطاعة ، كقوله تعالى : { لا تعبد الشيطان }

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r43.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r43.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r43.claim: Some interpret worship here as drawing near to God through obedience.

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r44.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r44.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r44.claim: Worship is also interpreted as supplication, as in the warning against those who disdain worship.
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r44.anchor: أو الدعاء أن الذين يستكبرون عن عبادتي

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r45.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r45.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r45.claim: Worship is also explained as affirming God's oneness, as in the statement that jinn and humankind were created only to worship.

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r46.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r46.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r46.claim: The meanings offered for worship—humility, obedience, drawing near, supplication, and affirming oneness—are close in sense.
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r46.anchor: وفسرت العبادة في إياك نعبد بأنها التذلل والخضوع

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r47.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r47.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r47.claim: Joining worship to seeking help combines what the servant offers God with what the servant asks from Him.
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r47.anchor: وقرنت الاستعانة بالعبادة للجمع بين ما يتقرب به العبد إلى الله تعالى

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r48.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r48.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r48.claim: Worship precedes the request for aid because the means is presented before the need, so the request may be answered.
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r48.anchor: وقدمت العبادة على الاستعانة لتقديم الوسيلة قبل طلب الحاجة

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r49.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r49.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r49.claim: The unqualified terms worship and seeking help encompass every act of worship and every matter for which help is sought.
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r49.anchor: وأطلق العبادة والاستعانة لتتناول كل معبود به

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r50.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r50.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r50.claim: Repeating iyyāka makes worship and seeking help two independently intended sentences.
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r50.anchor: وكرر إياك ليكون كل من العبادة والاستعانة

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r51.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r51.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r51.claim: The repeated iyyāka explicitly identifies God as the one from whom aid is sought; without it, the wording could leave the source unspecified.

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r52.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r52.speaker: بعض المنتمين للصلاح
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r52.claim: Some pious interpreters restrict worship to knowledge and seeking help to gnosis, but Abū Ḥayyān says the wording gives no evidence for these restrictions.
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r52.anchor: ونقل عن المنتمين للصلاح تقييدات مختلفة

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r53.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r53.speaker: قالوا
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r53.claim: They say naʿbud refutes the determinists while nastaʿīn refutes the Qadarites.

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r54.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r54.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r54.claim: Worship is an exalted station, commanded in scripture and used as an honorific for the most excellent creatures, including the Prophet and Jesus.
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r54.anchor: ومقام العبادة شريف ، وقد جاء الأمر به

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r55.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r55.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r55.claim: The verse God gives in 20:14 places worship after exclusive monotheism, because monotheism is the foundation and worship its branch.
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r55.anchor: لأن التوحيد هو الأصل ، والعبادة فرعه

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r56.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r56.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r56.claim: Directly addressing God as present refutes materialists, atheists, and those who deny a creator.
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r56.anchor: وقالوا في قوله : إياك . رد على الدهرية

ALUSI:1:5/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:5/r1.claim: When praise reaches its highest limit, the discourse turns to direct address to God.
ALUSI:1:5/r1.anchor: لما بلغ الثناء الغاية القصوى قال سبحانه

ALUSI:1:5/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:5/r2.claim: The well-known grammatical analysis treats iyyā as a separate accusative pronoun and the attached elements as letters added to clarify its form.
ALUSI:1:5/r2.anchor: إيا في المشهور ضمير نصب منفصل واللواحق حروف زيدت لبيان الحال

ALUSI:1:5/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r3.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:1:5/r3.claim: One analysis treats the attached elements as nouns to which iyyā is annexed.

ALUSI:1:5/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r4.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:1:5/r4.claim: Another analysis takes the attached elements themselves as the pronoun and iyyā as a supporting element.
ALUSI:1:5/r4.anchor: وقيل الضمير هي تلك اللواحق وإيا دعامة

ALUSI:1:5/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:1:5/r5.claim: A further analysis identifies the pronoun with the whole compound.

ALUSI:1:5/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:1:5/r6.claim: Another analysis treats iyyā as an indefinite, ambiguous noun annexed to the attached elements.
ALUSI:1:5/r6.anchor: وقيل إيا مظهر مبهم مضاف إلى اللواحق

ALUSI:1:5/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r7.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ALUSI:1:5/r7.claim: Abū ʿUbayda claims that iyyā is derived by word formation; al-Ālūsī calls this astonishing ignorance and refers the discussion to grammar.
ALUSI:1:5/r7.anchor: وزعم أبو عبيدة اشتقاقه وهو جهل عجيب والبحث مستوفى في علم النحو

ALUSI:1:5/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:5/r8.claim: The form wayyāka, with hamza changed to wāw, occurs, but al-Ālūsī cannot tell whether it comes from readers or Arab usage.
ALUSI:1:5/r8.anchor: وقد جاء وياك بقلب الهمزة واواً ولا أدري أهو عن القراء أم عن العرب

ALUSI:1:5/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r9.speaker: عمرو بن فائد عن أبيّ
ALUSI:1:5/r9.claim: ʿAmr ibn Fāʾid, reporting from Ubayy, reads iyyāka with a kasra on the hamza and a light yāʾ.
ALUSI:1:5/r9.anchor: قرأ عمرو بن فائد عن أبيّ ( إياك ) بكسر الهمزة وتخفيف الياء

ALUSI:1:5/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r10.speaker: علا وأبو الفضل الرقاشي
ALUSI:1:5/r10.claim: ʿAlā and Abū al-Faḍl al-Raqāshī read ayyāka with an open hamza and doubled yāʾ.
ALUSI:1:5/r10.anchor: وعلى وأبو الفضل الرقاشي ( أياك ) بفتح الهمزة والتشديد

ALUSI:1:5/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r11.speaker: أبو السوار الغنوي
ALUSI:1:5/r11.claim: Abū al-Sawwār al-Ghanawī replaces the hamza with hāʾ, using either its kasra or its fatḥa.
ALUSI:1:5/r11.anchor: وأبو السوار الغنوي ( هياك ) بإبدال الهمزة مكسورة ومفتوحة هاء

ALUSI:1:5/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r12.speaker: الجمهور
ALUSI:1:5/r12.claim: The majority read iyyāka with a kasra on the hamza and a doubled yāʾ.

ALUSI:1:5/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:5/r13.claim: Worship is the highest degree of submissive humility.

ALUSI:1:5/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:5/r14.claim: Only God may rightly receive worship, in law and reason, because He grants the greatest blessings, beginning with life and existence and all that follows from them.
ALUSI:1:5/r14.anchor: ولا يجوز شرعاً ولا عقلاً فعلها إلا لله تعالى لأنه المستحق لذلك لكونه مولياً لأعظم النعم من الحياة والوجود وتوابعهما

ALUSI:1:5/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:5/r15.claim: Prostration to anyone besides God is forbidden: placing the noblest body parts on earth, the lowest object and a place trodden by feet and shoes, expresses the utmost humiliation.
ALUSI:1:5/r15.anchor: ولذلك يحرم السجود لغيره سبحانه لأن وضع أشرف الأعضاء على أهون الأشياء وهو التراب وموطئ الأقدام والنعال غاية الخضوع

ALUSI:1:5/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r16.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:1:5/r16.claim: Some restrict the word worship to submission directed to God; references to people worshipping other things describe their own false assumption and rebuke their stupidity.
ALUSI:1:5/r16.anchor: وقيل لا تستعمل إلا في الخضوع له سبحانه

ALUSI:1:5/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:5/r17.claim: Worship can mean obedience, as in the command not to worship Satan.
ALUSI:1:5/r17.anchor: وتستعمل بمعنى الطاعة ومنه : { أَن لاَّ تَعْبُدُواْ الشيطان }

ALUSI:1:5/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:5/r18.claim: Worship can also mean supplication, as in the warning against those who are too proud to worship God.
ALUSI:1:5/r18.anchor: وبمعنى الدعاء ومنه : { إِنَّ الذين يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ عَنْ عِبَادَتِي }

ALUSI:1:5/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:5/r19.claim: Worship may mean affirming divine oneness, as in the stated purpose for creating jinn and humankind.
ALUSI:1:5/r19.anchor: وبمعنى التوحيد ومنه : { وَمَا خَلَقْتُ الجن والإنس إِلاَّ لِيَعْبُدُونِ }

ALUSI:1:5/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r20.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:5/r20.claim: These senses of worship—submission, obedience, supplication, and affirming oneness—are close in meaning.

ALUSI:1:5/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r21.speaker: بعض المحققين
ALUSI:1:5/r21.claim: Some careful scholars distinguish three levels: worship for reward or fear of punishment (the lower level, called ʿibāda); worship as honor, acceptance of duties, or affiliation (the middle level, ʿubūdiyya); and submission solely because God deserves it (the highest, ʿubūda).
ALUSI:1:5/r21.anchor: ذكر بعض المحققين أن لها ثلاث درجات

ALUSI:1:5/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r22.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:5/r22.claim: The prayer formula must express worship of God Himself; al-Ālūsī says a prayer would be invalid if its intention were merely to gain reward or the honor of worshipping Him.
ALUSI:1:5/r22.anchor: وإليه الإشارة بقول المصلي أصلي لله تعالى فإنه لو قال أصلي لثوابه تعالى مثلاً أو للتشرف بعبادته فسدت صلاته

ALUSI:1:5/r23.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r23.speaker: الإمام الرازي
ALUSI:1:5/r23.claim: Al-Rāzī does not name the middle level in his commentary; he calls the highest level ʿubūdiyya, unlike al-Ālūsī’s terminology.
ALUSI:1:5/r23.anchor: والإمام الرازي في التفسير لم يضع للثانية اسما وسمى الثالثة بالعبودية

ALUSI:1:5/r24.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r24.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:5/r24.claim: Al-Ālūsī’s note says his three-level account answers the objection that, if worship is the highest submission, most believers would not count as worshippers.
ALUSI:1:5/r24.anchor: وبما ذكرنا سقط ما قبل أن العبادة إذا كانت أعلى مراتب الخضوع يلزم أن لا يكون أكثر المؤمنين عابدين

ALUSI:1:5/r25.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r25.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:5/r25.claim: Seeking aid means requesting assistance; the yāʾ in the verb is changed from an original wāw.
ALUSI:1:5/r25.anchor: والاستعانة طلب المعونة وياء فعله منقلبة عن واو

ALUSI:1:5/r26.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r26.speaker: الجبرية
ALUSI:1:5/r26.claim: The Jabriyya argue that if a servant acted independently, asking God for help in acting would serve no purpose.
ALUSI:1:5/r26.anchor: أما الجبرية فقالوا : لو كان العبد مستقلاً لما كان للاستعانة على الفعل فائدة

ALUSI:1:5/r27.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r27.speaker: القدرية
ALUSI:1:5/r27.claim: The Qadariyya argue that asking for aid makes sense only if the servant already has some capacity to act; without it, aid would be pointless.
ALUSI:1:5/r27.anchor: وأما القدرية فقالوا السؤال إنما يحسن لو كان العبد متمكناً في أصل الفعل فيطلب الإعانة من الغير

ALUSI:1:5/r28.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r28.speaker: البيضاوي
ALUSI:1:5/r28.claim: Al-Bayḍāwī distinguishes necessary aid, such as power, understanding, tools, and material, from nonessential aids that ease or encourage action; the latter are not required for liability.
ALUSI:1:5/r28.anchor: وقد أشار ناصر الملة والدين البيضاوي بيض الله تعالى وجه حجته ببيان المعونة

ALUSI:1:5/r29.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r29.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:5/r29.claim: On al-Bayḍāwī’s distinction, neither faction can use this verse to establish its doctrine: necessary aid permits action and liability, while helpful extras merely ease action.
ALUSI:1:5/r29.anchor: وحاصله أن الاستعانة طلب ما يتمكن به العبد من الفعل أو يوجب اليسر عليه وشيء منهما لا يوجب الجبر ولا القدر

ALUSI:1:5/r30.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r30.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:5/r30.claim: If the verse bears on created acts, al-Ālūsī takes it to affirm that people have real capacity to act, effective by God’s permission but not independent of Him.
ALUSI:1:5/r30.anchor: أن للعباد قدراً مؤثرة بإذن الله تعالى لا بالاستقلال كما عقدت عليه خنصر عقيدتي

ALUSI:1:5/r31.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r31.speaker: الجبرية
ALUSI:1:5/r31.claim: Al-Ālūsī rejects the Jabriyya claim that people have no capacity and all their acts resemble the involuntary twitch of a trembling person; necessary capacity contradicts this.
ALUSI:1:5/r31.anchor: بل جميع أفعالهم كحركة المرتعش كما يقوله الجبرية ؛ إذ الضرورية تكذبه

ALUSI:1:5/r32.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r32.speaker: الأشاعرة
ALUSI:1:5/r32.claim: Al-Ālūsī also rejects the common Ashʿarite position that human capacity never affects action, likening it to a paralyzed hand and saying it amounts in effect to Jabriyya doctrine.
ALUSI:1:5/r32.anchor: ولا أن لهم قدرة غير مؤثرة أبداً كاليد المشلولة كما هو الشائع من مذهب الأشاعرة إذ هو في المآل كقول الجبرية

ALUSI:1:5/r33.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r33.speaker: المعتزلة
ALUSI:1:5/r33.claim: He rejects the Muʿtazilite claim that people act independently, so that God wills what they do not do and they do what God does not will, because decisive texts refute it.
ALUSI:1:5/r33.anchor: ولا أن لهم قدرة مستقلة بالأفعال يفعلون بها ما شاءوا

ALUSI:1:5/r34.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r34.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:5/r34.claim: Al-Ālūsī says the worship clause presupposes an effective human capacity: one cannot be told to produce an act without some capacity that contributes to its occurrence; kasb alone does not satisfy him.
ALUSI:1:5/r34.anchor: ووجه الاستدلال أن { إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ } مشير إلى صدور الفعل من العباد وذلك يستدعي قدرة

ALUSI:1:5/r35.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r35.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:5/r35.claim: The aid clause denies independent human action and affirms action through God’s permission and assistance; al-Ālūsī calls this the middle way between compulsion and absolute delegation.
ALUSI:1:5/r35.anchor: وقوله { وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ } يدل على نفي الاستقلال فيه

ALUSI:1:5/r36.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r36.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:5/r36.claim: Fronting the object signals restriction and exclusivity, a marked departure from ordinary order; Ibn ʿAbbās glosses it as worshipping no one else.
ALUSI:1:5/r36.anchor: ولذلك قال ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما : معناه لا نعبد غيرك

ALUSI:1:5/r37.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r37.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:5/r37.claim: The restriction is real rather than merely a reply correcting an interlocutor; it renounces idolatry and implicitly rebukes idolaters.
ALUSI:1:5/r37.anchor: وهو حقيقي لا يستدعي رد خطأ المخاطب والمقصود منه التبرئة عن الشرك وتعريض بالمشركين

ALUSI:1:5/r38.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r38.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:5/r38.claim: The object comes first because God precedes worshipper and worship in being, so the sentence order mirrors reality.
ALUSI:1:5/r38.anchor: وتقديم ما هو مقدم في الوجود فإنه تعالى مقدم على العابد والعبادة ذاتاً فقم وضعاً ليوافق الوضع الطبع

ALUSI:1:5/r39.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r39.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:5/r39.claim: Putting God first directs the worshipper’s attention to the true object, strengthens reverence, counters distraction and lethargy, and excludes any opening for association.
ALUSI:1:5/r39.anchor: وتنبيه العابد من أول الأمر على أن المعبود هو الله تعالى الحق فلا يتكاسل في التعظيم ولا يلتفت يميناً وشمالاً

ALUSI:1:5/r40.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r40.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:5/r40.claim: For the gnostic, God is the first and primary object of attention; worship is only a vehicle of approach, leaving the seeker absorbed in divine majesty and beauty.
ALUSI:1:5/r40.anchor: والإشارة إلى حال العارف وأنه ينبغي أن يكون نظره إلى المعبود أولاً وبالذات

ALUSI:1:5/r41.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r41.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:5/r41.claim: Al-Ālūsī contrasts the direct remembrance given to Muḥammad’s community with Israel’s remembrance of divine favors, and contrasts Muḥammad’s assurance of God’s presence with Moses’ assurance of future guidance.
ALUSI:1:5/r41.anchor: وكم من فرق بين قوله تعالى للمحمديين : { فاذكروني أَذْكُرْكُمْ }

ALUSI:1:5/r42.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r42.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:1:5/r42.claim: One explanation for saying we worship rather than I worship is humility: the speaker’s own service is too deficient to cite alone, so he joins it with the worship of all worshippers.
ALUSI:1:5/r42.anchor: فقد قيل هو الإشارة إلى حال العبد كأنه يقول :

ALUSI:1:5/r43.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r43.speaker: قيل
