ALUSI:1:5/r43.claim: Another explanation is that the singular would falsely claim personal devotion despite worldly submission and dependence; the plural lets the speaker include exemplary saints and the devout.
ALUSI:1:5/r43.anchor: وقيل : النكتة في العدول إلى الإفراد التحرز عن الوقوع في الكذب

ALUSI:1:5/r44.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r44.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:1:5/r44.claim: A third explanation says the plural presents the speaker humbly as one among God’s servants, unlike the singular claim to be the worshipper; al-Ālūsī illustrates the contrast with Ishmael and Moses.
ALUSI:1:5/r44.anchor: وقيل : لو قال إياك أعبد لكان ذلك بمعنى : أنا العابد

ALUSI:1:5/r45.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r45.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:1:5/r45.claim: Some say the plural pronoun includes the reciter, the guardian angels, and those present in congregational prayer.
ALUSI:1:5/r45.anchor: وقيل : الضمير في الفعلين للقاري ومن معه من الحفظة وحاضري الجماعة

ALUSI:1:5/r46.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r46.speaker: الغزالي
ALUSI:1:5/r46.claim: Al-Ghazālī’s analogy treats the plural as the merit of congregational prayer over an individual prayer.
ALUSI:1:5/r46.anchor: وقيل هو من باب : «صلاة الجماعة تفضل صلاة الفذ » على ما ذكره الغزالي

ALUSI:1:5/r47.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r47.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:5/r47.claim: Al-Ālūsī gives eleven reasons for putting worship before seeking aid: its status as a trust, its priority to requests, obligation, relation to reward and guidance, rhetorical cadence, and the spiritual progression of the worshipper.
ALUSI:1:5/r47.anchor: الثالث : في سر تقديم فعل العبادة على فعل الاستعانة وله وجوه

ALUSI:1:5/r48.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r48.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:5/r48.claim: Since worship is a trust, al-Ālūsī says concern for fulfilling it warrants placing it first.

ALUSI:1:5/r49.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r49.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:5/r49.claim: After attributing worship to oneself, the worshipper immediately asks for God’s help to show that worship itself depends on His help, enabling grace, and permission.
ALUSI:1:5/r49.anchor: الثاني : أنه لما نسب المتكلم العبادة إلى نفسه أوهم ذلك تبجحاً

ALUSI:1:5/r50.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r50.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:5/r50.claim: Worship is a means of drawing near to God, whereas seeking aid is not; the more important act therefore comes first.
ALUSI:1:5/r50.anchor: أن العبادة مما يتقرب بها العبد إلى الله تعالى والاستعانة ليست كذلك فالأول أهم

ALUSI:1:5/r51.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r51.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:5/r51.claim: Worship is a means, so placing it before the request for aid is like offering a means before asking for what one needs.
ALUSI:1:5/r51.anchor: أنها وسيلة فتقدم على طلب الحاجة لأنه أدعى للإجابة

ALUSI:1:5/r52.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r52.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:5/r52.claim: Putting first what the Master asks of the servant, before what the servant requests from the Master, better displays sincere servitude.
ALUSI:1:5/r52.anchor: الخامس : أنها مطلوبة لله تعالى من العبادة

ALUSI:1:5/r53.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r53.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:5/r53.claim: Worship is an inescapable duty and is presented as the purpose for which humans and jinn were created, so it has priority.
ALUSI:1:5/r53.anchor: أن العبادة واجبة حتماً لا مناص للعبادة عن الإتيان بها حتى جعلت كالعلة لخلق الإنس والجن

ALUSI:1:5/r54.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r54.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:5/r54.claim: Worship accords more closely with mention of recompense, while seeking aid fits more closely with the later request for guidance.
ALUSI:1:5/r54.anchor: أنها أشد مناسبة بذكر الجزاء والاستعانة أقوى التئاماً بطلب الهداية

ALUSI:1:5/r55.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r55.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:5/r55.claim: Islam begins by restricting worship to God and escaping idolatry; exclusive reliance on God follows once that commitment is established.
ALUSI:1:5/r55.anchor: أن مبدأ الإسلام التخصيص بالعبادة والخلوص من الشرك والتخصيص بالاستعانة بعد الرسوخ

ALUSI:1:5/r56.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r56.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:5/r56.claim: Delaying the request for aid also preserves the end-rhyme of the verses.
ALUSI:1:5/r56.anchor: أن في تأخير فعل الاستعانة توافق رءوس الآي

ALUSI:1:5/r57.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r57.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:5/r57.claim: When two linked actions are mentioned, reversing their order can leave the relation intact, as in saying either that one paid a debt and then did a kindness or vice versa.
ALUSI:1:5/r57.anchor: أن أحدهما إذا كان مرتبطاً بالآخر لم يختلف التقديم والتأخير كما يقال قضيت حقي فأحسنت إلي

ALUSI:1:5/r58.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r58.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:5/r58.claim: In al-Ālūsī’s Sufi progression, the wayfarer reaches the station of true servitude at this clause after praise, remembrance, recognition of divine favor, and longing for release from attachment to other things.
ALUSI:1:5/r58.anchor: الحادي عشر : أن مقام السالكين ينتهي عند قوله

ALUSI:1:5/r59.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r59.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:5/r59.claim: The Prophet’s description as God’s servant during the Night Journey exemplifies this station; he then seeks firmness and guidance and protection from spiritual change, completing the ascent and return.
ALUSI:1:5/r59.anchor: ألا يرى إلى سيد الخلق وحبيب الحق كيف عبر عن مقامه هذا بقوله :

ALUSI:1:5/r60.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r60.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:5/r60.claim: The general function of shifting from absence to direct address is variation of style, refreshing the discourse and engaging the listener.
ALUSI:1:5/r60.anchor: وهي التفنن في الكلام والعدول من أسلوب إلى آخر تطرية له وتنشيطاً للسامع

ALUSI:1:5/r61.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r61.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:1:5/r61.claim: After God is identified by distinguishing attributes and becomes a definite object of knowledge, direct address marks greater exclusivity and a rise from inference to vision and presence.
ALUSI:1:5/r61.anchor: فقيل لما ذكر الحقيق بالحمد ووصف بصفات عظام تميز بها عن سائر الذوات وتعلق العلم بمعلوم معين خوطب بذلك

ALUSI:1:5/r62.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r62.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:1:5/r62.claim: Another explanation is that praise and divine favor elevate the servant to ihsan, worshipping as if seeing God; the direct address and worship express Islam’s outward form, faith’s meaning, and ihsan’s light.
ALUSI:1:5/r62.anchor: وقيل : لما شرح الله تعالى صدر عبده وأفاض على قلبه وقالبه نور الإيمان والإسلام

ALUSI:1:5/r63.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r63.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:1:5/r63.claim: Since God is King throughout all time and sees past and future equally, the shift to address is fitting.
ALUSI:1:5/r63.anchor: وأيضاً لما تبين أنه ملك في الأزل ما في أحايين الأبد علم أن الشاهد والغائب والماضي والمستقبل بالنسبة إليه على حد سواء

ALUSI:1:5/r64.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r64.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:1:5/r64.claim: Another view says praise belongs naturally to the language of absence, while prayer belongs to presence and direct address, since God is living and generous.
ALUSI:1:5/r64.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون السر أن الكلام من أول السورة إلى هنا ثناء والثناء في الغيبة أولى ومن هنا إلى الآخر دعاء وهو في الحضور أولى

ALUSI:1:5/r65.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r65.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:1:5/r65.claim: Another explanation assigns absence to praise, which is complete even at a distance, and direct address to worship, which is due to the ever-present God; Abraham’s rejection of setting stars illustrates the latter.
ALUSI:1:5/r65.anchor: وقيل : إنه لما كان الحمد لا يتفاوت غيبة وحضوراً بل هو مع ملاحظة الغيبة

ALUSI:1:5/r66.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r66.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:1:5/r66.claim: By joining the plural voice of the devout, a worshipper imitates them and hopes to be counted among their company; the source cites a couplet on imitating the noble.
ALUSI:1:5/r66.anchor: وأيضاً من تشبه بقوم فهو منهم ، فالعابد لما رام ذلك سلك مسلك القوم في الذكر

ALUSI:1:5/r67.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r67.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:1:5/r67.claim: One explanation sees direct address as a gift to the modest person who feels far from God: divine mercy brings that person into closeness and intimate presence.
ALUSI:1:5/r67.anchor: وأيضاً فيه إشارة إلى أن من لزم جادة الأدب والانكسار ورأى نفسه بعيداً عن ساحة القرب لكمال الاحتقار فهو حقيق أن تدركه رحمة إلهية

ALUSI:1:5/r68.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r68.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:1:5/r68.claim: Since worship is harder than praise, placing it in the language of presence helps the lover perform it energetically and without weariness; a poem pictures the beloved seeing and hearing.
ALUSI:1:5/r68.anchor: وأيضاً إنه لما لم يكن في الحمد مزيد كلفة بخلاف العبادة فإن خطبها عظيم ، ومن دأب المحب تحمل المشاق العظيمة

ALUSI:1:5/r69.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r69.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:1:5/r69.claim: When veils and otherness vanish from the seeker’s view, only God remains, so speech turns entirely to direct address; the explanation cites the verse that wherever one turns is God’s face.
ALUSI:1:5/r69.anchor: وأما إذا آل أمره بملازمة الأذكار إلى ارتفاع الحجب والأستار واضمحلال جميع الأغيار لم يبق في نظره سوى المعبود الحق

ALUSI:1:5/r70.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r70.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:5/r70.claim: Al-Ālūsī’s own allusion is to the Resurrection: believers will attain the joy of divine presence, private audience without an interpreter, and unveiled intimate address; this mercy follows the warning of Judgment.
ALUSI:1:5/r70.anchor: وعندي وهو من نسائم الأسحار أن الله سبحانه بعد أن ذكر يوم الدين وهو يوم القيامة التفت إلى الخطاب للإشارة إلى أنه إذا قامت القيامة

ALUSI:1:5/r71.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r71.speaker: السيوطي عن الشيخ بهاء الدين
ALUSI:1:5/r71.claim: Al-Suyūṭī transmits from Shaykh Bahāʾ al-Dīn that scholars agree there is one shift in this passage.
ALUSI:1:5/r71.anchor: هذا وقد ذكر الإمام السيوطي نقلاً عن الشيخ بهاء الدين أنه قال اتفقوا على أن فيما نحن فيه التفاتاً واحداً

ALUSI:1:5/r72.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r72.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:5/r72.claim: Al-Ālūsī questions that consensus: on al-Zamakhsharī and al-Sakkākī’s account, supplying an implied say can yield two shifts, while other assumptions yield none; the count depends on the analysis.
ALUSI:1:5/r72.anchor: وفيه نظر لأن الزمخشري ومن تابعه على أن الالتفات خلاف الظاهر مطلقاً فإن كان التقدير قولوا الحمد لله

ALUSI:1:5/r73.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r73.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:1:5/r73.claim: One view explains the repeated object as explicitly identifying God as the one from whom help is requested; without it, the helper could remain unspecified.
ALUSI:1:5/r73.anchor: فقيل للتنصيص على طلب العون منه تعالى

ALUSI:1:5/r74.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r74.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:1:5/r74.claim: Another view says repetition prevents the mistaken implication that one draws near to God only by combining worship with asking for aid.
ALUSI:1:5/r74.anchor: وقيل إنه لو اقتصر على واحد ربما توهم أنه لا يتقرب إلى الله تعالى إلا بالجمع بينهما

ALUSI:1:5/r75.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r75.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:1:5/r75.claim: A third view treats the repetition as emphasis, by analogy with saying a house is between Zayd and ʿAmr.
ALUSI:1:5/r75.anchor: وقيل إنه جمع بينهما للتأكيد كما يقال الدار بين زيد وبين عمرو

ALUSI:1:5/r76.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r76.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:5/r76.claim: Al-Ālūsī rejects the emphasis account: the second object is governed by a separate verb, so it is not merely emphatic repetition.
ALUSI:1:5/r76.anchor: وفيه أن التكرير إنما يكون تأكيداً إذا لم يكن معمولاً لفعل ثان وإياك الثاني في الآية معمول لنستعين

ALUSI:1:5/r77.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r77.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:1:5/r77.claim: Another reported purpose is to teach worshippers to renew mention of God whenever they have a need.
ALUSI:1:5/r77.anchor: وقيل إنه تعليم لنا في تجديد ذكره تعالى عند كل حاجة

ALUSI:1:5/r78.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r78.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:5/r78.claim: Al-Ālūsī prefers the view that repetition marks two different relations: worship relates to God directly, while seeking aid relates through an attribute or means.
ALUSI:1:5/r78.anchor: وعندي أن التكرار للإشعار أن حيثية تعلق العبادة به تعالى غير حيثية تعلق طلب الاستعانة منه سبحانه

ALUSI:1:5/r79.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r79.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:5/r79.claim: The unexpressed object of seeking aid may be unrestricted, like an omitted object that implies generality; choosing only some needs would require an arbitrary preference.
ALUSI:1:5/r79.anchor: فقيل ليتناول كل مستعان فيه فالحذف هنا مثله

ALUSI:1:5/r80.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r80.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI:1:5/r80.claim: The unrestricted object is transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās, the Qurʾān’s interpreter; al-Ālūsī says that total scope signifies renouncing one’s own power and relying entirely on God.
ALUSI:1:5/r80.anchor: وبأنه المروي عن ترجمان القرآن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما وبأن عموم المفعول متضمن لنفي الحول والقوة عن نفسه

ALUSI:1:5/r81.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r81.speaker: البيضاوي
ALUSI:1:5/r81.claim: Al-Ālūsī says al-Bayḍāwī’s presentation also points toward preferring an unrestricted object of aid.
ALUSI:1:5/r81.anchor: وإلى ترجيحه يشير صنيع العلامة البيضاوي

ALUSI:1:5/r82.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r82.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
ALUSI:1:5/r82.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī prefers aid specifically for performing worship; the following request for guidance specifies that aid and fits the passage closely, while worship is contrary to the self’s inclinations.
ALUSI:1:5/r82.anchor: وقال صاحب «الكشاف » : الأحسن أن يراد الاستعانة به وبتوفيقه على أداء العبادة

ALUSI:1:5/r83.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r83.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:5/r83.claim: Al-Ālūsī nevertheless prefers the unrestricted sense: seeking aid through worship can serve every legitimate purpose, and the straight path embraces all religious and worldly affairs and ultimate salvation.
ALUSI:1:5/r83.anchor: والإنصاف عندي أن الحمل على العموم أولى ليتوافق ألفاظ هذه السورة الكريمة في المعنى المطلوب منها

ALUSI:1:5/r84.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r84.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:5/r84.claim: The unrestricted request includes all help needed for worship, its prerequisites, and associated matters, just as God’s bestowed favor is described without restriction.
ALUSI:1:5/r84.anchor: وأيضاً لا يخفى أن المراد بالعبادة في إياك نعبد

ALUSI:1:5/r85.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r85.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:5/r85.claim: Limiting the request to aid in worship would leave the Qurʾān’s opening chapter silent about seeking God’s aid for other needs, a conclusion al-Ālūsī will not accept.
ALUSI:1:5/r85.anchor: يبقى حكم الاستعانة في غيرها غير معلوم في أم الكتاب

ALUSI:1:5/r86.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r86.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI:1:5/r86.claim: In an authentic report, the Prophet tells Ibn ʿAbbās: when you seek aid, seek it from God; al-Ālūsī sees this as supporting unrestricted reliance and thinks it likely explains Ibn ʿAbbās’s view of the verse.
ALUSI:1:5/r86.anchor: وقد ثبت في الصحيح عنه صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال لابن عباس

ALUSI:1:5/r87.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r87.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:5/r87.claim: Al-Ālūsī concludes that no one but God is the true source of help: asking needy people for what they lack is folly, and he quotes a poem on reliance upon God alone.
ALUSI:1:5/r87.anchor: فمن استعان بغيره في المهمات بل وفي غيرها فقد استسمن ذا ورم ونفخ في غير ضرم

ALUSI:1:5/r88.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r88.speaker: عبيد بن عمير الليثي وزيد بن حبيش ويحيى بن وثاب والنخعي
ALUSI:1:5/r88.claim: ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr al-Laythī, Zayd ibn Ḥubaysh, Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, and al-Nakhaʿī read the initial nūn of naʿbudu with a kasra, a dialect of Qays, Tamīm, Asad, Rabīʿa, and Hudhayl.
ALUSI:1:5/r88.anchor: وقد قرأ عبيد بن عمير الليثي وزيد بن حبيش ويحيى بن وثاب والنخعي ( نعبد ) بكسر النون

ALUSI:1:5/r89.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r89.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:5/r89.claim: The same kasra on the imperfect prefix occurs in comparable verbs such as nastaʿīnu, except where the following sound makes the kasra difficult; some also say yijillu for yajalu.
ALUSI:1:5/r89.anchor: وكذلك حكم حروف المضارعة في هذا الفعل وما أشبهه كنستعين مما لم ينضم ما بعدها فيه سوى الباء

ALUSI:1:5/r90.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r90.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI:1:5/r90.claim: Some also read yaʿlamūn with a kasra on the imperfect prefix.
ALUSI:1:5/r90.anchor: على أن بعضهم قال يجل بكسر ياء المضارعة من وجل ، وقرأ بعضهم يعلمون

ALUSI:1:5/r91.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r91.speaker: الحسن وابن المتوكل وأبو محلف
ALUSI:1:5/r91.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Ibn al-Mutawakkil, and Abū Miḥlaf read yuʿbadu in the passive; al-Ālūsī calls this unusual.
ALUSI:1:5/r91.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وابن المتوكل وأبو محلف يعبد بالياء مبنياً للمفعول ، وهو غريب

ALUSI:1:5/r92.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r92.speaker: بعض أهل مكة
ALUSI:1:5/r92.claim: Some people of Mecca read naʿbud with a quiescent dāl.
ALUSI:1:5/r92.anchor: وعن بعض أهل مكة أنه قرأ ( نعبد ) بإسكان الدال

ALUSI:1:5/r93.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:5/r93.speaker: الجمهور
ALUSI:1:5/r93.claim: The majority read naʿbudu with an open nūn and a ḍamma on the dāl; al-Ālūsī identifies this as the eloquent Hijazi form.
ALUSI:1:5/r93.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور ( نعبد ) بفتح النون وضم الدال وهي لغة أهل الحجاز وهي الفصحى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r1.speaker: الفخر
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r1.claim: Al-Fakhr argues that the surah's omission of seven letters that begin words for punishment signals that its faithful readers are safe from Hell's seven levels, matching its seven gates.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r1.anchor: أنه قال في صفة جهنم ( لها سبعة أبواب لكل باب منهم جزء مقسوم ) ثم أنه تعالى أسقط سبعة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r2.claim: Alusi calls the letter-count argument arbitrary: seven other omitted letters also begin words for Hell and punishment, so the same reasoning could be applied to them.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r2.anchor: فلتسقط الذال والواو والنون والحاء والعين والميم والغين إذ الواو من الويل والذال من الذلة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r3.claim: Alusi says the story crediting Ali with solving the letter puzzle for the Roman Caesar after Muawiya failed has no basis.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r3.anchor: وأما نسبته لأمير المؤمنين علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه حين سأل قيصر الروم معاوية عن ذلك فلم يجب فسأل عليا فأجاب فلا أصل له

ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r4.claim: Even if the Ali story were accepted, Alusi says Ali meant only to direct the questioner toward the surah's deeper meanings.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r4.anchor: وعلى تقدير التسليم فما مرام الأمير بالإكتفاء على هذا المقدار إلا التنبيه للسائل على ما لا يخفى عليك من الأسرار

ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r5.claim: Other names are al-Kanz, al-Wafiya, and al-Kafiya: the surah contains treasured meanings and is complete and sufficient, with no other surah sufficing in prayer.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r5.anchor: الكنز والوافية والكافية لما مر من إشتمالها على الجواهر المكنوزة فتفي وتكفي أو لأنها لا تنصف في الصلاة ولا يكفي فيها غيرها

ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r6.claim: Al-Asas is a name because al-Fatiha is the Quran's foundation and its first surah.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r6.anchor: لأنها أصل القرآن وأول سورة فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r7.claim: Names nine through thirteen include al-Hamd, al-Shukr, al-Duʿa, Taʿlim al-Masʾala, and al-Suʾal, reflecting praise, gratitude, supplication, and asking.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r7.anchor: سورة الحمد وسورة الشكر وسورة الدعاء وسورة تعليم المسألة وسورة السؤال لاشتمالها على الحمد

ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r8.claim: Alusi finds the claim that the surah contains supplication or asking more difficult than the claim about gratitude; it begins with praise before the request.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r8.anchor: وأما الاشتمال على الثالث فكالإشكال على الأول بل أظهر وأما تعليم المسألة فلأنها بدئت بالثناء قبله

ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r9.claim: Munajat and Tafwid are names because the servant converses with God in this verse and thereby entrusts matters to Him.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r9.anchor: العبد يناجي ربه بقوله إياك نعبد وإياك نستعين

ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r10.claim: The authentic hadiths imply the names al-Ruqya, al-Shifa, and al-Shafiya, identifying the surah as a protective recitation and healing.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r10.anchor: الرقية والشفاء والشافية والأحاديث الصحيحة مشعرة بذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r11.claim: The name al-Salah reflects that reciting the surah in prayer is obligatory or required; some jurists hold it recommended, with a transmitted report supporting that view.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r11.anchor: سورة الصلاة لأنها واجبة أو فريضة فيها والاستحباب مذهب بعض المجتهدين ورواية عن البعض في النقل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r12.claim: The hadith God divided the prayer between Himself and His servant uses prayer to mean this surah; Alusi allows a whole-for-part figure or a literal sense by implication.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r12.anchor: لحديث قسمت الصلاة بيني وبين عبدي نصفين وأراد السورة والمجاز اللغوي لعلاقة الكلية والجزئية

ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r13.claim: Al-Nur may refer to the surah's widespread use, its illumination of hearts, or its meanings as an embodiment of the Quranic light.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r13.anchor: النور لظهورها بكثرة إستعمالها أو لتنويرها القلوب لجلالة قدرها أو لأنها لما أشتملت عليه من المعاني عبارة عن النور

ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r14.claim: Al-Quran al-Azim is another self-evident name for the surah.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r14.anchor: القرآن العظيم وهو ظاهر مما قدمناه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r15.claim: Al-Sabʿ al-Mathani is explained by the surah's seven verses, whose count is agreed; the only other seven-verse surah he knows is Arayta.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r15.anchor: لأنها سبع آيات باتفاق وما رأينا مشاركا لها سوى ( أرأيت )

ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r16.claim: Eight- or nine-verse counts are anomalous or a narrator's mistake; authorities differ over counting the basmala versus Anʿamta ʿalayhim, and the latter count's cadence objection is answered by a parallel in al-Nasr.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r16.anchor: والقول بأنها ثمان كالقول بأنها تسع شاذ لا يعبأ به أو وهم من الراوي إلا أن منهم من عد التسمية آية دون ( أنعمت عليهم )

ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r17.claim: It is called oft-repeated because it recurs in each rakah; the common sense of prayer avoids objections about one-rakah and funeral prayers, while the latter is technically supplication rather than prayer.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r17.anchor: وتثنى وتكرر في كل ركعة وصلاة ذات ركوع أو المراد المتعارف الأغلب من الصلاة فلا ترد الركعة الواحدة ولا صلاة الجنازة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r18.claim: Alternative derivations of mathani are repetition with another surah, two revelations, its two parts of supplication and praise, or God's response after each verse; it may also derive from praise or divine selection for this community.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r18.anchor: وقيل وصفت بذلك لأنها تثنى بسورة أخرى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r19.claim: Dividing the Quran into surahs renews a reader's energy, makes each memorized portion feel complete and valuable, and demonstrates that every surah is independently miraculous; the reason for varying their lengths is obvious.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p37/r19.anchor: أن يكون أنشط للقاريء وأبعث على التحصيل كالمسافر إذا قطع ميلا أو فرسخا نفس ذلك منه ونشط للمسير

BAGHAWI:1:5/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:5/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:1:5/r1.claim: Iyyā is a pronoun used with an attached object pronoun before a verb, while after the verb it occurs only detached, as in “I intended only you.”
BAGHAWI:1:5/r1.anchor: ( إيا ) كلمة ضمير خصت بالإضافة إلى المضمر ، ويستعمل مقدماً على الفعل ، فيقال : إياك أعني

BAGHAWI:1:5/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:5/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:1:5/r2.claim: “We worship” means we affirm God's oneness and obey Him humbly; worship is obedience with humility and submission, as a slave is compliant and a road is leveled.
BAGHAWI:1:5/r2.anchor: { نعبد } أي نوحدك ونطيعك خاضعين ، والعبادة الطاعة مع التذلل والخضوع ؛

BAGHAWI:1:5/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:5/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:1:5/r3.claim: “We seek help” asks God to aid us in worship and in all our affairs.
BAGHAWI:1:5/r3.anchor: نطلب منك المعونة على عبادتك وعلى جميع أمورنا .

BAGHAWI:1:5/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:5/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:1:5/r4.claim: The question why worship precedes seeking aid matters to those who place ability before action; Baghawi says divine enabling and aid accompany the act, so the order makes no difference.
BAGHAWI:1:5/r4.anchor: فإن قيل : لم قدم ذكر العبادة على الاستعانة والاستعانة تكون قبل العبادة ؟ فلهذا يلزم من يجعل الاستطاعة قبل الفعل . ونحن نحمد الله نجعل التوفيق والاستعانة مع الفعل ،

BAGHAWI:1:5/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:5/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:1:5/r5.claim: Another explanation says seeking aid is itself a kind of worship, so the verse gives the general act of worship before one of its details.
BAGHAWI:1:5/r5.anchor: ويقال : الاستعانة نوع تعبد ، فكأنه ذكر جملة العبادة أولاً ثم ذكر ما هو من تفاصيلها .

BAGHAWI:1:7/r36.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:7/r36.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI:1:7/r36.claim: In a qudsi report, God divides prayer between Himself and His servant and answers each part of al-Fatiha; Baghawi grades it sahih.
BAGHAWI:1:7/r36.anchor: قال الله عز وجل : قسمت الصلاة بيني وبين عبدي نصفين ، نصفها لي ونصفها لعبدي ولعبدي ما سأل ،

BAYDAWI:1:5/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:5/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:5/r1.claim: After naming the one deserving praise and describing His distinguishing attributes, the discourse directly addresses Him; this moves from proof and absence to presence and witnessing, the knower's culmination after reflection on God's names, gifts, and works.
BAYDAWI:1:5/r1.anchor: ثم إنه لما ذكر الحقيق بالحمد ،   ووصف بصفات عظام تميز بها عن سائر الذوات

BAYDAWI:1:5/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:5/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:5/r2.claim: Arabs vary person and address to refresh speech and engage listeners; Bayḍāwī illustrates the shift with Qur'anic examples and Imruʾ al-Qays's changing pronouns.
BAYDAWI:1:5/r2.anchor: ومن عادة العرب التفنن في الكلام والعدول من أسلوب إلى آخر تطرية له وتنشيطا للسامع

BAYDAWI:1:5/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:5/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:5/r3.claim: Iyyā is a detached accusative pronoun; attached yāʾ, kāf, or hāʾ marks person and has no syntactic position, like tāʾ in anta and kāf in araʾaytaka.
BAYDAWI:1:5/r3.anchor: وإيا ضمير منصوب منفصل ،   وما يلحقه من الياء والكاف والهاء حروف زيدت لبيان

BAYDAWI:1:5/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:5/r4.speaker: الخليل
BAYDAWI:1:5/r4.claim: Al-Khalīl analyzes iyyā as a noun to which attached pronouns are genitive, citing an Arab saying about a man reaching sixty and young women.
BAYDAWI:1:5/r4.anchor: وقال الخليل إيا مضاف إليها ،   واحتج بما حكاه عن بعض العرب

BAYDAWI:1:5/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:5/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:5/r5.claim: Bayḍāwī dismisses al-Khalīl's evidence as anomalous and unreliable.

BAYDAWI:1:5/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:5/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:5/r6.claim: One analysis makes suffixes the pronouns and iyyā their support because pronouns detached from governors cannot be pronounced alone.
BAYDAWI:1:5/r6.anchor: وقيل هي الضمائر ،   وإيا عمدة فإنها لما فصلت عن العوامل تعذر النطق بها

BAYDAWI:1:5/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:5/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:5/r7.claim: Another analysis treats the whole form—iyyā plus suffix—as the pronoun.

BAYDAWI:1:5/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:5/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:5/r8.claim: Reported readings include iyyāka with fatḥa on hamza and hiyyāka with hamza changed to hāʾ.
BAYDAWI:1:5/r8.anchor: وقرئ { إياك } بفتح الهمزة و " هياك "

BAYDAWI:1:5/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:5/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:5/r9.claim: ʿIbāda is utmost submission and humility, from maʿbad, a smoothed road, and a garment of exceptional thickness; thus it is used only for submission to God.
BAYDAWI:1:5/r9.anchor: والعبادة : أقصى غاية الخضوع والتذلل ومنه طريق معبد

BAYDAWI:1:5/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:5/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:5/r10.claim: Istiʿāna is seeking help. Necessary assistance includes capacity, conceiving the act, tools, and material; when these obtain, one can be morally commanded.

BAYDAWI:1:5/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:5/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:5/r11.claim: Nonessential help makes an act easier or motivates it, like a mount for one able to walk; it is not required for valid moral responsibility.
BAYDAWI:1:5/r11.anchor: وغير الضرورية تحصيل ما يتيسر به الفعل ويسهل كالراحلة في السفر

BAYDAWI:1:5/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:5/r12.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:5/r12.claim: The request may concern every important matter or specifically performance of worship.
BAYDAWI:1:5/r12.anchor: والمراد طلب المعونة في المهمات كلها ،   أو في أداء العبادات

BAYDAWI:1:5/r13.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:5/r13.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:5/r13.claim: The implicit “we” may include reciter, guardian angels, and those at congregational prayer, or all monotheists; sharing their worship and need seeks acceptance through their blessing and explains communal prayer.
BAYDAWI:1:5/r13.anchor: والضمير المستكن في الفعلين للقارئ ومن معه من الحفظة ،   وحاضري صلاة الجماعة

BAYDAWI:1:5/r14.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:5/r14.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:5/r14.claim: Fronting the object signals reverence, importance, and exclusivity; Ibn ʿAbbās glosses it “We worship You and no other.”
BAYDAWI:1:5/r14.anchor: ولذلك قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما ( معناه نعبدك ولا نعبد غيرك )

BAYDAWI:1:5/r15.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:5/r15.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:5/r15.claim: The worshipper attends first to God and views worship as a noble relation, not personal achievement; the gnostic reaches communion through total attention to God and loss of self-awareness.
BAYDAWI:1:5/r15.anchor: ومنه إلى العبادة لا من حيث إنها عبادة صدرت عنه بل من حيث إنها نسبة شريفة إليه

BAYDAWI:1:5/r16.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:5/r16.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:5/r16.claim: Bayḍāwī prefers the beloved Prophet's “Do not grieve; God is with us” to Moses's “My Lord is with me and will guide me,” because the first foregrounds God's presence.
BAYDAWI:1:5/r16.anchor: ولذلك فضل ما حكى الله عن حبيبه حين قال { لا تحزن إن الله معنا } على ما حكاه عن كليمه

BAYDAWI:1:5/r17.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:5/r17.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:5/r17.claim: Repeating iyyāka makes explicit that God alone is sought for help.
BAYDAWI:1:5/r17.anchor: وكرر الضمير للتنصيص على أنه المستعان به لا غير

BAYDAWI:1:5/r18.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:5/r18.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:5/r18.claim: Worship comes first to preserve verse endings and because presenting the means before requesting a need makes a response more likely.
BAYDAWI:1:5/r18.anchor: ويعلم منه أن تقديم الوسيلة على طلب الحاجة أدعى إلى الإجابة

BAYDAWI:1:5/r19.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:5/r19.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:5/r19.claim: Ascribing worship to oneself might imply pride, so the following request shows worship cannot occur or endure without God's aid and enabling grace.
BAYDAWI:1:5/r19.anchor: وأقول : لما نسب المتكلم العبادة إلى نفسه أوهم ذلك تبجحا واعتدادا منه

BAYDAWI:1:5/r20.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:5/r20.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:5/r20.claim: Another analysis takes the conjunction as circumstantial: “We worship You while seeking Your help.”
BAYDAWI:1:5/r20.anchor: وقيل : الواو للحال والمعنى نعبدك مستعينين بك

BAYDAWI:1:5/r21.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:5/r21.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:5/r21.claim: Kasra on both nūns follows Tamim dialect, which kasras imperfect prefixes other than yāʾ if the following vowel is not ḍamma.
BAYDAWI:1:5/r21.anchor: وقرئ بكسر النون فيهما وهي لغة بني تميم

BIQAI:1:5/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:5/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:1:5/r1.claim: After God's entitlement and mercy have been established, a rational person turns to Him alone; the passage shifts from speaking about Him to addressing Him directly.
BIQAI:1:5/r1.anchor: كان من شأن كل ذي لب الإقبال إليه وقصر الهمم عليه

BIQAI:1:5/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:5/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:1:5/r2.claim: The direct address names the possessor of the preceding attributes; putting the means of worship before the requested need is more likely to bring a response.
BIQAI:1:5/r2.anchor: للوسيلة على طلب الحاجة لأنه أجدر بالإجابة

BIQAI:1:5/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:5/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:1:5/r3.claim: The phrase guides people toward worshipping God.

BIQAI:1:5/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:5/r4.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI:1:5/r4.claim: Al-Ḥarālī defines worship as reaching the utmost degree in all forms of humble submission.
BIQAI:1:5/r4.anchor: ومعنى { نعبد } كما قال الحرالي : تبلغ الغاية في أنحاء التذلل

BIQAI:1:5/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:5/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI:1:5/r5.claim: Repeating the object pronoun urges earnestness in asking for help; the wording also declares that worship is possible only through God's aid and that guidance rests in His hand.
BIQAI:1:5/r5.anchor: إشارة إلى أن عبادته لا تتهيأ إلا بمعونته وإلى أن ملاك

BIQAI:1:5/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:5/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI:1:5/r6.claim: The sūra begins with God's essence, points to His acts, rises to His attributes, and returns to His essence, signaling that He encompasses beginning and end.
BIQAI:1:5/r6.anchor: ثم دل عليه بالأفعال ، ثم رقي إلى الصفات ، ثم رجع إلى الذات

BIQAI:1:5/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:5/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI:1:5/r7.claim: Knowledge of God's acts and attributes establishes His right to exclusive worship and then reveals the worshipper's inability to fulfill that right, prompting the request for aid.
BIQAI:1:5/r7.anchor: فطلبت الإعانة ، فهو كقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم

BIQAI:1:5/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:5/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI:1:5/r8.claim: As an analogy, the Prophet, reporting from ʿĀʾisha, sought refuge in God's pardon from punishment, pleasure from wrath, and God Himself from God; al-Nasāʾī adds his confession that he cannot enumerate God's praise. Biqāʿī gives no grading.
BIQAI:1:5/r8.anchor: فيما رواه مسلم وأبو داود في الصلاة والترمذي وابن ماجه في الدعاء والنسائي وهذا لفظه في التعوذ عن عائشة رضى الله عنها

BIQAI:1:5/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:5/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI:1:5/r9.claim: Biqāʿī points to his discussion at the end of Sūrat Iqraʾ for a fuller explanation of this hadith.
BIQAI:1:5/r9.anchor: وفي آخر سورة اقرأ شرح بديع لهذا الحديث

BIQAI:1:5/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:5/r10.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI:1:5/r10.claim: Al-Ḥarālī says all Qur'an is God's speech: some speaks about God Himself, while other passages express what people at varying levels and in varying states ought to say.
BIQAI:1:5/r10.anchor: قال الحرالي : وهذه الآيات أي هذه وما بعدها

BIQAI:1:5/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:5/r11.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI:1:5/r11.claim: Because creatures cannot reach the full truth of what they owe, God, the trustee over all things, informs them of it and makes their recitation equivalent to their own utterance, completing His grace to them.
BIQAI:1:5/r11.anchor: قال الحرالي : وهذه الآيات أي هذه وما بعدها

BIQAI:1:5/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:5/r12.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI:1:5/r12.claim: Left to themselves, people could not say what would mend their worldly and religious condition or adequately thank God; He teaches them words that fulfill their duty, so their sole connection is reciting His sublime speech, with or without understanding.
BIQAI:1:5/r12.anchor: قال الحرالي : وهذه الآيات أي هذه وما بعدها

BIQAI:1:5/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:5/r13.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI:1:5/r13.claim: Al-Ḥarālī cites the authenticated report in which the Prophet conveys God's statement that prayer is divided equally between God and His servant, then recites this sūra.
BIQAI:1:5/r13.anchor: من قوله تعالى : " قسمت الصلاة بيني وبين عبدي نصفين "

BIQAI:1:5/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:5/r14.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI:1:5/r14.claim: Al-Ḥarālī says the first three verses praise God Himself; when the servant recites them, God accepts that recitation as the servant's praise, eulogy, and glorification.
BIQAI:1:5/r14.anchor: قال الحرالي : وهذه الآيات أي هذه وما بعدها

BIQAI:1:5/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:5/r15.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI:1:5/r15.claim: For al-Ḥarālī, the following verses are voiced on the creatures' tongues: worship is the servant's duty, while asking for aid belongs to God; the passage is shared between them.
BIQAI:1:5/r15.anchor: قال الحرالي : وهذه الآيات أي هذه وما بعدها

BIQAI:1:5/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:5/r16.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI:1:5/r16.claim: God's side comes first because His assistance precedes worship and makes it possible.
BIQAI:1:5/r16.anchor: قال الحرالي : وهذه الآيات أي هذه وما بعدها

BIQAI:1:5/r17.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:5/r17.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI:1:5/r17.claim: Al-Ḥarālī says whoever seeks God's aid for a burden according to this verse receives help proportionate to it; failure comes from forfeiting one's share of God, ignorance of the verse's implications, or heedlessness of its blessing.
BIQAI:1:5/r17.anchor: قال الحرالي : وهذه الآيات أي هذه وما بعدها

BIQAI:1:5/r18.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:5/r18.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI:1:5/r18.claim: The first-person plural nūn in naʿbudu signals that prayer is founded on congregational worship.
BIQAI:1:5/r18.anchor: وفي قوله : { نعبد } بنون الاستتباع إشعار بأن الصلاة بنيت على الاجتماع

BIQAI:1:5/r19.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:5/r19.speaker: author
BIQAI:1:5/r19.claim: The verse teaches believers to acknowledge incapacity, feel their need, and rely on God's power; this directs their desires toward asking Him for guidance on the straight path.
BIQAI:1:5/r19.anchor: وفي الآية ندب إلى اعتقاد العجز واستشعار الافتقار والاعتصام بحوله وقوته

BIQAI:1:7/r29.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:7/r29.speaker: العلامة سعد الدين مسعود ابن عمرو التفتازاني الشافعي
BIQAI:1:7/r29.claim: The second preservation is signaled by worship through the end of the sūra, whose benefits return to the afterlife.
BIQAI:1:7/r29.anchor: وأما الإبقاء الثاني فبقوله : { إياك نعبد } إلى آخرها ،   فإن منافع ذلك تعود إلى الآخرة

DURR:1:1/r116.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:1/r116.speaker: الله
DURR:1:1/r116.claim: Worship means worshipping and unifying God, while the request for help is the servant's share in the shared verse.
DURR:1:1/r116.anchor: { إياك نعبد } يعني الله أعبد وأوحد { وإياك نستعين } قال الله : هذا بيني وبين عبدي

DURR:1:3/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:3/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR:1:3/r3.claim: In Qatada's sequential gloss, the Day of Recompense is when creatures are repaid; the worship-prayer is what people should say and directs them to God; the straight path is named, the favored are prophets, the objects of anger are Jews, and the astray are Christians.
DURR:1:3/r3.anchor: عن قتادة في قول الله { الحمد لله رب العالمين } قال : ما وصف من خلقه . وفي قوله { الرحمن الرحيم } قال : مدح نفسه { ملك يوم الدين }

DURR:1:5/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:5/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:1:5/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses worship as affirming God's oneness, fearing and hoping in Him as Lord, and worshipping no other.
DURR:1:5/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله { إياك نعبد } يعني إياك نوحد ونخاف ونرجو ربنا لا غيرك

DURR:1:5/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:5/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:1:5/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the servant seeks God's help for obedience and for all affairs.
DURR:1:5/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله { إياك نعبد } يعني إياك نوحد ونخاف ونرجو ربنا لا غيرك { وإياك نستعين } على طاعتك وعلى أمورنا كلها

DURR:1:5/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:5/r3.speaker: علي
DURR:1:5/r3.claim: Abu Razin says Ali read the worship and help clauses, followed by ihdina, in the raised form; he characterizes Ali as a fluent Qurayshi Arab.
DURR:1:5/r3.anchor: عن أبي رزين قال : سمعت عليا قرأ هذا الحرف وكان قرشيا عربيا فصيحا { إياك نعبد وإياك نستعين ، اهدنا } يرفعهما جميعا

DURR:1:5/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:5/r4.speaker: علي
DURR:1:5/r4.claim: Abu Razin reports Ali's pronunciation of this phrase with hamza, lengthening, and gemination.
DURR:1:5/r4.anchor: عن أبي رزين أن عليا قرأ { إياك نعبد وإياك نستعين } فهمز ، ومد ، وشد

DURR:1:5/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:5/r5.speaker: رسول الله
DURR:1:5/r5.claim: During a campaign against the enemy, Abu Talha heard the Prophet invoke the Lord of Judgment and recite this worship-prayer; he saw men fall, struck by angels from before and behind.
DURR:1:5/r5.anchor: عن أبي طلحة قال :  " كنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في غزو ، فلقي العدو فسمعته يقول

ABUDAWUD:821/r1.author: ABUDAWUD
ABUDAWUD:821/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABUDAWUD:821/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet saying a prayer without Umm al-Qur'an is deficient, and advises a worshipper praying behind the imam to recite it silently.
ABUDAWUD:821/r1.anchor: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا هُرَيْرَةَ، يَقُولُ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم

ABUDAWUD:821/r2.author: ABUDAWUD
ABUDAWUD:821/r2.speaker: الله تعالى
ABUDAWUD:821/r2.claim: In a hadith qudsi transmitted by Abu Hurayra, God divides al-Fatiha between Himself and the servant: praise and glorification receive divine responses, worship is mutual, and the guidance petition belongs to the servant.
ABUDAWUD:821/r2.anchor: قَالَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى قَسَمْتُ الصَّلاَةَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَ عَبْدِي

DURR-FULL:v1p12/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p12/r2.speaker: أم سلمة
DURR-FULL:v1p12/r2.claim: Umm Salama reports that the Prophet recited the Fātiḥa including the basmala and called it seven verses.
DURR-FULL:v1p12/r2.anchor: عن أم سلمة قالت قرأ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم {بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين

DURR-FULL:v1p12/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p12/r3.speaker: أبو سعيد بن المعلى
DURR-FULL:v1p12/r3.claim: Abū Saʿīd b. al-Muʿallā reports that the Prophet cited 8:24 when he failed to answer his call in prayer, then taught him al-Fātiḥa as the greatest sūra, the seven oft-repeated, and the great Qur'an.
DURR-FULL:v1p12/r3.anchor: عن أبي سعيد بن المعلى قال: كنت أصلي فدعاني النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فلم أجبه

DURR-FULL:v1p12/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p12/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p12/r5.claim: The Prophet tells Ubayy that no sūra like the Fātiḥa was revealed in the Torah, Gospel, Psalms, or Qur'an, and identifies it as the seven oft-repeated.
DURR-FULL:v1p12/r5.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: كيف تقرأ في الصلاة فقرأ بأم الكتاب

DURR-FULL:v1p18/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p18/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v1p18/r1.claim: Abū Hurayra tells Abū al-Sāʾib to recite the Fātiḥa silently to himself when praying behind the imam.
DURR-FULL:v1p18/r1.anchor: قال أبو السائب: فقلت ياأبا هريرة إني أحيانا أكون وراء الإمام فغمز ذراعي وقال: اقرأ بها يا فارسي في نفسك

DURR-FULL:v1p18/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p18/r2.speaker: الله عز وجل
DURR-FULL:v1p18/r2.claim: In Abū Hurayra's report, God says the prayer is divided between Him and His servant: the opening praise is His, the middle is shared, and the servant receives what he asks in the remainder.
DURR-FULL:v1p18/r2.anchor: فإني سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: قال الله عز وجل قسمت الصلاة بيني وبين عبدي نصفين

DURR-FULL:v1p18/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p18/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v1p18/r3.claim: A weakly transmitted version from Abū Hurayra adds that God acknowledges the basmala as remembrance and answers the Fātiḥa's successive praises, calling its middle verse shared and its ending the servant's.
DURR-FULL:v1p18/r3.anchor: بسند ضعيف عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول الله تعالى: قسمت هذه الصلاة بيني وبين عبدي نصفين

DURR-FULL:v1p18/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p18/r4.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
DURR-FULL:v1p18/r4.claim: Jābir reports a version in which God answers that the servant praised Him at al-ḥamdu and extolled Him at al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm, then says the rest belongs to the servant.
DURR-FULL:v1p18/r4.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال الله: قسمت الصلاة بيني وبين عبدي نصفين وله ما سأل

DURR-FULL:v1p18/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p18/r5.speaker: أبي بن كعب
DURR-FULL:v1p18/r5.claim: Ubayy b. Kaʿb reports that God calls the Fātiḥa seven verses, beginning a division of three for God, three for the servant, and one shared between them.
DURR-FULL:v1p18/r5.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب قال: قرأ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فاتحة الكتاب ثم قال قال ربكم: ابن آدم أنزلت عليك سبع آيات

DURR-FULL:v1p19/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p19/r1.speaker: ربكم
DURR-FULL:v1p19/r1.claim: The continuation of Ubayy b. Kaʿb's report assigns the first three Fātiḥa verses to God, the middle verse to both, and the final three to the servant; worship is the servant's and aid comes from God.
DURR-FULL:v1p19/r1.anchor: ثلاث لي وثلاث لك وواحدة بيني وبينك

DURR-FULL:v1p13/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p13/r1.speaker: أبي بن كعب
DURR-FULL:v1p13/r1.claim: Ubayy b. Kaʿb reports that no equivalent of the Fātiḥa occurs in the Torah, Gospel, Psalms, or Qur'an; it is the seven oft-repeated and the great Qur'an. Al-Tirmidhī graded the report ḥasan and al-Ḥākim ṣaḥīḥ.
DURR-FULL:v1p13/r1.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ما أنزل الله في التوراة

DURR-FULL:v1p13/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p13/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p13/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that Gabriel announced two lights never given to an earlier prophet: the Fātiḥa and the closing verses of al-Baqara; every letter recited brings its promised gift.
DURR-FULL:v1p13/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال بينما رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم جالس وعنده جبريل إذ سمع نقيضا من السماء من فوق فرفع جبريل بصره

DURR-FULL:v1p13/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p13/r3.speaker: أبو زيد
DURR-FULL:v1p13/r3.claim: Abū Zayd, a Companion, reports that the Prophet listened to a man reciting the Fātiḥa in night prayer and said nothing on earth is like it; al-Ṭabarānī's chain is weak.
DURR-FULL:v1p13/r3.anchor: عن أبي زيد وكانت له صحبة قال كنت مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في بعض فجاج المدينة فسمع رجلا يتهجد ويقرأ بأم القرآن

DURR-FULL:v1p13/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p13/r4.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
DURR-FULL:v1p13/r4.claim: Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī reports reciting the Fātiḥa seven times as a healing spell for a scorpion sting; the chief recovered, and the Prophet approved the sheep payment and a share for himself.
DURR-FULL:v1p13/r4.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال: بعثنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في سرية ثلاثين راكبا

DURR-FULL:v1p16/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p16/r1.speaker: أبو الدرداء
DURR-FULL:v1p16/r1.claim: Abū al-Dardāʾ reports the Prophet said the Fātiḥa suffices where nothing else does and, weighed against the Qur'an, outweighs it sevenfold.
DURR-FULL:v1p16/r1.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فاتحة الكتاب تجزىء مالا يجزىء شيء من القرآن

DURR-FULL:v1p16/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p16/r2.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v1p16/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan attributes to the Prophet the claim that reciting the Fātiḥa is like reciting the Torah, Gospel, Psalms, and Qur'an.
DURR-FULL:v1p16/r2.anchor: عن الحسن قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من قرأ فاتحة الكتاب فكأنما قرأ التوراة

DURR-FULL:v1p16/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p16/r3.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v1p16/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan reports a teaching that knowledge of all revealed books was condensed through the Qur'an and its shorter sūras into the Fātiḥa, so understanding its interpretation is like understanding all revealed books.
DURR-FULL:v1p16/r3.anchor: عن الحسن قال: أنزل الله مائة وأربعة كتب أودع علومها أربعة منها التوراة والإنجيل والزبور والفرقان

DURR-FULL:v1p16/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p16/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v1p16/r4.claim: Mujāhid says Iblīs groaned four times: when the Fātiḥa descended, when he was cursed, when he fell to earth, and when Muhammad was sent.
DURR-FULL:v1p16/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: رن إبليس أربعا حين نزلت فاتحة الكتاب وحين لعن وحين هبط إلى الأرض وحين بعث محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v1p16/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p16/r6.speaker: عبد العزيز بن ربيع
DURR-FULL:v1p16/r6.claim: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz b. Rabīʿ says Iblīs groaned at the Fātiḥa's revelation as he had on the day he was cursed.
DURR-FULL:v1p16/r6.anchor: عن عبد العزيز بن ربيع قال: لما نزلت فاتحة الكتاب رن إبليس كرنته يوم لعن

DURR-FULL:v1p16/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p16/r7.speaker: مكحول
DURR-FULL:v1p16/r7.claim: Makḥūl characterizes the Mother of the Qur'an as recitation, request, and supplication.
DURR-FULL:v1p16/r7.anchor: عن مكحول قال: أم القرآن قراءة ومسألة ودعاء

DURR-FULL:v1p16/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p16/r8.speaker: عطاء
DURR-FULL:v1p16/r8.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says that whoever wants a need fulfilled should recite the Fātiḥa to its end, and it will be fulfilled, God willing.
DURR-FULL:v1p16/r8.anchor: عن عطاء قال: إذا أردت حاجة فاقرأ بفاتحة الكتاب حتى تختمها تقضى إن شاء الله

IBNASHUR:1:2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:2/r2.claim: The first purification is rejecting denial of God and associating partners with Him, expressed by worshipping Him alone.
IBNASHUR:1:2/r2.anchor: أولها التخلية عن التعطيل والشرك بما تضمنه { إياك نعبد }

IBNASHUR:1:2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:2/r3.claim: Seeking God's help frees the worshipper from imagining self-sufficiency and from reliance on personal power before His greatness.
IBNASHUR:1:2/r3.anchor: الثاني التخلي عن خواطر الاستغناء عنه بالتبرىء من الحول والقوة تجاه عظمته بما تضمنه { وإياك نستعين }

IBNASHUR:1:5/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:5/r1.claim: After completing praise, the reciter turns to God to express exclusive sincerity, moving from stating the Lord’s due to affirming what the servant owes Him.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r1.anchor: إذا أتم الحامد حمد ربه يأخذ في التوجه إليه بإظهار الإخلاص له انتقالا من الإفصاح عن حق الرب إلى إظهار مراعة ما يقتضيه حقه

IBNASHUR:1:5/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:5/r2.claim: Addressing a great person with praise before speaking to him is an established Arab convention.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r2.anchor: ومفاتحة العظماء بالتمجيد عند التوجه إليهم قبل أن يخاطبوا طريقة عربية

IBNASHUR:1:5/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r3.speaker: حسان بن ثابت
IBNASHUR:1:5/r3.claim: Abu al-Faraj al-Isfahani transmits Hassan ibn Thabit’s account: at al-Nuʿman’s gathering, a man’s rajaz outside the tent prompted al-Nuʿman to recognize al-Nabigha and admit him; no grading is given.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r3.anchor: روى أبو الفرج الأصفهاني عن حسان بن ثابت قال :  كنتُ عند النعمان

IBNASHUR:1:5/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r4.speaker: الجمهور من أئمة البلاغة
IBNASHUR:1:5/r4.claim: Most rhetoricians define iltifāt as switching the mode used for the same referent after first expressing it through one of speech, absence, or address.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r4.anchor: أحدهما رأي من عدا السكاكي من أئمة البلاغة وهو أن المتكلم بعد أن يعبر عن ذات

IBNASHUR:1:5/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r5.speaker: السكاكي
IBNASHUR:1:5/r5.claim: Al-Sakkaki defines iltifāt as choosing a mode of speech, address, or absence other than the mode most fitting at that point.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r5.anchor: وخالفهم السكاكي فجعل مسمى الالتفات أن يعبر عن ذات بطريق من طرق التكلم أو الخطاب

IBNASHUR:1:5/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r6.speaker: الجمهور والسكاكي
IBNASHUR:1:5/r6.claim: Alqama’s opening line addresses the speaker’s own heart by tajrīd; the majority do not count this as iltifāt, while al-Sakkaki does.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r6.anchor: مثل قول علقمة بن عبده في طالع قصيدته :  طَحَا بكَ قلبٌ في الحسان طروب

IBNASHUR:1:5/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:5/r7.claim: The majority’s name for iltifāt likens changing expression to a viewer turning away; al-Sakkaki likely retained the established label although tajrīd does not fit the usual image.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r7.anchor: فتسمية الالتفات التفاتا على رأي الجمهور باعتبار أن عدول المتكلم عن الطريق الذي سلكه إلى طريق آخر

IBNASHUR:1:5/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:5/r8.claim: Iltifāt refreshes expression of the same meaning, renewing the listener’s attention instead of repeating one style until it becomes tedious; al-Sakkaki likens this to varying hospitality for souls.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r8.anchor: ولأهل البلاغة عناية بالالتفات لأن فيه تجديد أسلوب التعبير عن المعنى بعينه تحاشيا من تكرر الأسلوب

IBNASHUR:1:5/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r9.speaker: السكاكي
IBNASHUR:1:5/r9.claim: Al-Sakkaki says Arabs vary the styles with which they entertain souls just as they vary colors and tastes in entertaining bodies.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r9.anchor: قال السكاكي في « المفتاح » بعد أن ذكر أن العرب يستكثرون من الالتفات :  « أفتراهم يحسنون قِرى الأشباح

IBNASHUR:1:5/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:5/r10.claim: Here the praiser’s thought reaches its limit after praising God’s attributes, imagines himself in the divine presence, and turns directly to his Lord; this is a striking iltifāt.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r10.anchor: وما هنا التفات بديع فإن الحامد لما حمد الله تعالى ووصفه بعظيم الصفات بلغت به الفكرة منتهاها

IBNASHUR:1:5/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:5/r11.claim: The reverse shift appears in Muhammad ibn Bashir al-Khariji’s poem: it opens by addressing someone, then uses a feminine absent pronoun as the addressee seems to shrink from view.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r11.anchor: كعكس هذا الالتفاتتِ في قول محمد بن بشير الخارجي ( نسبَة إلى بني خارجة قبيلة ) :  ذُممتَ ولم تُحمد

IBNASHUR:1:5/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:5/r12.claim: Qur’an 29:23 similarly moves from describing disbelievers in the absent form to God’s first-person ‘My mercy,’ underscoring the severity of their disbelief against the named Lord.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r12.anchor: وبعكس ذلك قوله تعالى :  { والذين كفروا بآيات الله ولقائه أولئك يئسوا من رحمتي }  [ العنكبوت :  23 ] لاعتبار تشنيع

IBNASHUR:1:5/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:5/r13.claim: The shift to direct address also moves from praise into supplication, which naturally calls for address and leads into the request for guidance in 1:6.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r13.anchor: ومما يزيد الالتفات وقعا في الآية أنه تخلص من الثناء إلى الدعاء ولا شك أن الدعاء يقتضي الخطاب

IBNASHUR:1:5/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r14.speaker: أبو الفتح ابن جني
IBNASHUR:1:5/r14.claim: Ibn Jinni calls iltifāt ‘the bravery of Arabic,’ treating it as evidence of a rhetorician’s agility in directing speech as he wishes.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r14.anchor: وأبو الفتح ابن جني يسمى الالتفات « شَجاعة العربية » كأنه عنى أنه دليل على حدة ذهن البليغ

IBNASHUR:1:5/r15.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r15.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:5/r15.claim: Iyyāka is a detached accusative address pronoun; the stronger analysis is that iyyā supports an otherwise detached pronoun, as in iyyāya and iyyāhum.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r15.anchor: و ( إياك ) ضمير خطاب في حالة النصب . والأظهر أن كلمة إيا جعلت ليَعْتَمِد عليها الضمير

IBNASHUR:1:5/r16.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r16.speaker: النحاة
IBNASHUR:1:5/r16.claim: Grammarians variously analyze iyyā as a fixed-form detached pronoun with an emphatic suffix, the pronoun itself followed by clarifying particles, a pronoun support, or a noun annexed to pronouns.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r16.anchor: ومن النحاة من جعل ( إيَّا ) ضميراً منفصلاً ملازماً حالة واحدة وجعل الضمائر التي معه أضيفت إليه للتأكيد .

IBNASHUR:1:5/r17.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r17.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:5/r17.claim: Worship ordinarily denotes an act of submission or reverence exceeding what is customary between people; using it for obedience alone is metaphorical.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r17.anchor: والعبادة فعل يدل على الخضوع أو التعظيم الزائدين على المتعارف بين الناس . وأما إطلاقها على الطاعة فهو مجاز .

IBNASHUR:1:5/r18.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r18.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:5/r18.claim: In religious usage worship is doing what pleases the Lord through submission, compliance, and avoidance, or a morally accountable person’s action against personal desire in reverence for God.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r18.anchor: والعبادة في الشرع أخص فتُعرّف بأنها فعل ما يرضي الرب من خضوع وامتثال واجتناب

IBNASHUR:1:5/r19.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r19.speaker: الرازي
IBNASHUR:1:5/r19.claim: Al-Razi’s explanation of worship in 51:56 encompasses compliance with the whole body of religious law.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r19.anchor: وقال الرازي في تفسير قوله تعالى :  { وما خلقت الجن والإنس إلا ليعبدون }  [ الذاريات :  56 ] > ا هـ فهي بهذا التفسير تشمل الامتثال

IBNASHUR:1:5/r20.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r20.speaker: الصوفية
IBNASHUR:1:5/r20.claim: Sufis distinguish worship as doing what pleases God from servitude as contentment with what God does; they also define servitude as keeping covenants and limits, accepting what is present, and bearing what is lost.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r20.anchor: وقد فسر الصوفية العبادة بأنها فعل ما يرضي الرب ،  والعبودية بالرضا بما يفعل الرب . فهي أقوى .

IBNASHUR:1:5/r21.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r21.speaker: الفخر
IBNASHUR:1:5/r21.claim: Fakhr al-Din ranks worship for reward or fear as lowest, worship for the honor of serving God as higher but incomplete, and worship because God alone deserves it as the highest station, servitude.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r21.anchor: قال الفخر :  ( ( مراتب العبادة ثلاث :  الأولى أن يعبد الله طمعاً في الثواب وخوفاً من العقاب وهي العبادة

IBNASHUR:1:5/r22.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r22.speaker: ابن سينا
IBNASHUR:1:5/r22.claim: Ibn Sina describes the highest station as seeking God for no other end, serving Him because He deserves worship and because relation to Him is noble, without hope or fear.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r22.anchor: لأن الشيخ ابن سينا قال في « الإشارات » :  ( ( العارف يريد الحق لا لشيء غيره ولا يُؤْثِر شيئاً على

IBNASHUR:1:5/r23.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r23.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:5/r23.claim: The author identifies Ibn Sina’s God-directed devotion with Fakhr’s highest station of servitude, treating its two stated motives as one state.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r23.anchor: لا لرغبة أو رهبة ) ) ا هـ فجعلهما حالة واحدة .

IBNASHUR:1:5/r24.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r24.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:5/r24.claim: The author rejects Fakhr’s dismissal of reward-and-fear worship as a low, fallen grade: Islam itself teaches it, most believers practice it, and it is the aim of obligation; higher stations are rare and even the devout still hope and fear.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r24.anchor: وما ادعاه الفخر في سقوط الدرجة الأولى ونزول مرتبتها قد غلب عليه فيه اصطلاح غلاة الصوفية

IBNASHUR:1:5/r25.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r25.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR:1:5/r25.claim: Asked why he exerted himself in worship after God had forgiven his past and future sins, the Prophet replied, ‘Should I not be a grateful servant?’; the author sees this as the highest station without hope of more reward.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r25.anchor: والمرتبة الثالثة هي التي أشار لها قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم لمن قال له كيف تُجهد نفسك في العبادة وقد غَفَر لك الله

IBNASHUR:1:5/r26.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r26.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:5/r26.claim: Worship’s purpose is human perfection: God made the world display His attributes, endowed people with spirit and intellect to ascend, guided them through revelation, and prescribed repeated worship to recall judgment, discipline the self, sustain social order, and develop individual and communal virtues.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r26.anchor: واعلم أن من أهم المباحث البحث عن سر العبادة وتأثيرها وسر مشروعيتها لنا وذلك أن الله تعالى خلق هذا العالم

IBNASHUR:1:5/r27.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r27.speaker: ابن سينا
IBNASHUR:1:5/r27.claim: Ibn Sina explains that human interdependence requires exchange, justice, and a divinely prescribed law; a lawgiver and just recompense require knowledge of God, preserved by repeated worship.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r27.anchor: وقريب من هذا التقرير الذي نحوناه وأقل منه قول الشيخ ابن سينا في « الإشارات » :  ( ( لما لم يكن الإنسان بحيث يستقل

IBNASHUR:1:5/r28.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r28.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:5/r28.claim: Worship is driven by reverence, either from love or bare fear; love is more important because it pleases the worshipper, and it entails fearing the beloved’s displeasure.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r28.anchor: لا شك أن داعي العبادة التعظيم والإجلال وهو إما عن محبة أو عن خوف مجرد ،  وأهمه ما كان عن محبة لأنه يرضي نفس فاعله

IBNASHUR:1:5/r29.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r29.speaker: محمود الوراق أو منصور الفقيه
IBNASHUR:1:5/r29.claim: A couplet attributed uncertainly to Mahmud al-Warraq or Mansur al-Faqih argues that claiming to love God while disobeying Him is strange, since a true lover obeys the beloved.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r29.anchor:
قال محمود الوراق أو منصور الفقيه :
تَعصي الإله وأنتَ تُظهر حبَّه

IBNASHUR:1:5/r30.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r30.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:5/r30.claim: Qur’an 3:31 links following the Prophet’s law with God’s love, supporting the claim that love of God leads to obedience and the wish to be loved in return.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r30.anchor: ولذلك قال تعالى :  { قل إن كنتم تحبون الله فاتبعوني يحببكم الله }  [ آل عمران :  31 ] فذلك يشعر بأن اتباع الشريعة

IBNASHUR:1:5/r31.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r31.speaker: المعري
IBNASHUR:1:5/r31.claim: Al-Maʿarri’s couplet presents Ahriman as evil and darkness, born from a malign thought that crossed Yazdan, the deity of good, unawares.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r31.anchor:
قال المعري :
فَكَّرَ يَزْدَانُ على غِرة

IBNASHUR:1:5/r32.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r32.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:5/r32.claim: Most nations’ worship, including worship prescribed in revealed laws, is founded on love of God; polytheists likewise love their idols as they love God, as 2:165 says.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r32.anchor: وإلى هذا النوع ترجع عبادة أكثر الأمم ،  ومنها العبادة المشروعة في جميع الشرائع لأنها مبنية على حب الله تعالى ،  وكذلك عبادة المشركين أصنامهم قال تعالى :  { ومن الناس من يتخذ من دون الله أنداداً يحبونهم كحب الله }

IBNASHUR:1:5/r33.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r33.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:5/r33.claim: Some peoples worshipped from fear alone to avert harm: examples include some devil worshippers and Manichaeans, who worshipped Ahriman as lord of evil and harm.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r33.anchor: ومن الأمم من عبدت عن خوف دون محبة وإنما هو لاتقاء شر كما عبدت بعض الأمم الشياطين وعبدت المانوية

IBNASHUR:1:5/r34.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r34.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:5/r34.claim: Fronting the object in ‘You alone we worship’ gives true restriction: the believers taught this praise worship none but God.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r34.anchor: والحصر المستفاد من تقديم المعمول في قوله تعالى :  { إياك نعبد } حصر حقيقي لأن المؤمنين الملقَّنين لهذا الحمد لا يعبدون

IBNASHUR:1:5/r35.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r35.speaker: ابن الحاجب
IBNASHUR:1:5/r35.claim: Ibn al-Hajib argues that fronting the object conveys emphasis but not restriction, and reads 1:5 as emphasis rather than exclusivity; he cites the wording of 39:2 against relying on 39:66.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r35.anchor: وزعم ابن الحاجب في « إيضاح المفصل » في شرح ديباجة « المفصل » عند قول الزمخشري « اللهََ أحمد » أن التقديم لا يفيد إلا الاهتمام

IBNASHUR:1:5/r36.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r36.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:5/r36.claim: The author rejects Ibn al-Hajib’s argument from 39:2: expressions cannot be treated as identical across contexts, and the rebuttal is established in works on semantics.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r36.anchor: وأنا أرى استدلاله بورود قوله تعالى :  { فاعبد الله } لا يليق بمقامه العلمي إذ لا يظن أن محامل الكلام متماثلة

IBNASHUR:1:5/r37.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r37.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:5/r37.claim: The clause ‘and You we ask for help’ is coordinated with worship; it is not separated by the repetition common in supplicatory enumeration, emphasizing that both acts matter under this restriction.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r37.anchor: بطريقة تعداد الجمل مقام التضرع ونحوه من مقامات التعداد والتكرير

IBNASHUR:1:5/r38.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r38.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:5/r38.claim: Seeking help is requesting assistance; assistance makes a difficult act easier through tools, bodily participation, guidance or teaching, counsel, or money, as illustrated by al-Hariri’s ‘my character is a fine helper.’
IBNASHUR:1:5/r38.anchor: والاستعانة طلب العون . والعون والإعانة تسهيل فعلِ شيء يشق ويعسر على المستعين وحده

IBNASHUR:1:5/r39.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r39.speaker: الحريري
IBNASHUR:1:5/r39.claim: Al-Hariri writes in the Maqāma, ‘My character is a fine helper,’ using ʿawn in the ordinary sense of aid.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r39.anchor: قال الحريري في المقامة :  « وخُلُقي نعم العون »

IBNASHUR:1:5/r40.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r40.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:5/r40.claim: Seeking God’s help means exerting one’s own capacity while asking God to facilitate what a person cannot accomplish alone; this is the religious sense of divine assistance.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r40.anchor: وأما الاستعانة بالله فهي طلب المعونة على ما لا قبل للبشر بالإعانة عليه ولا قبل للمستعين بتحصيله بمفرده

IBNASHUR:1:5/r41.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r41.speaker: العلماء
IBNASHUR:1:5/r41.claim: Scholars define necessary aid as creating what completes an act: the agent’s capacity, awareness of the act, its material, and its tool; together these are ability or sound means and tools, enabling moral obligation.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r41.anchor: وقد فسرها العلماء بأنها هي خَلْق ما به تمامُ الفعل أو تيسيرُه ،  فتنقسم قسمين ضرورية أي ما يتوقف الفعل عليها

IBNASHUR:1:5/r42.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r42.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:5/r42.claim: Nonessential aid provides something that eases an act, such as arranging a mount for someone able to walk; together with necessary aid it completes tawfīq, creating capacity and the impulse to obey.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r42.anchor: القسم الثاني المعونة غير الضرورية وينبغي أن تخص باسم الإعانة وهي إيجاد المعين ما يتيسر به الفعل

IBNASHUR:1:5/r43.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r43.speaker: الراغب
IBNASHUR:1:5/r43.claim: Al-Raghib calls the second, easing kind of aid tawfīq; the author says this does not conflict with scholars’ definition because it follows the necessary aid that first makes tawfīq possible.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r43.anchor: وسمى الراغب هذا القسم الثاني بالتوفيق ولا تعارض بين كلامه وبين تعريفهم إياه لما علمت

IBNASHUR:1:5/r44.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r44.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:5/r44.claim: The omitted object of ‘we seek help’ is deliberately general: it includes important acts, especially receiving religion and overcoming the self’s resistance to virtue, as indicated by the sūrah’s opening and the placement after worship.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r44.anchor: والمقصود هنا الاستعانة على الأفعال المهمة كلها التي أعلاها تلقي الدين وكل ما يعسر على المرء تذليله

IBNASHUR:1:5/r45.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r45.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:5/r45.claim: The complement governed by ‘seek help’ is omitted; its normal construction would name the object after ʿalā, and omission makes the request general while reserving it to God out of reverence.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r45.anchor: ولذلك حذف متعلق { نستعين } الذي حقه أن يذكر مجروراً بعلى ،  وقد أفاد هذا الحذف الهام عموم الاستعانة

IBNASHUR:1:5/r46.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r46.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:5/r46.claim: Knowledge, guidance, revelation, and sciences are also requested aids from God: 90:8–10 points to perception, speech and instruction, and revealed law.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r46.anchor: ومن توابع ذلك وأسبابه وهي المعارف والإرشادات والشرائع وأصول العلوم فكلها من الإعانة المطلوبة

IBNASHUR:1:5/r47.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r47.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:5/r47.claim: Fronting the object in seeking help gives an assertive, rhetorical restriction, since ordinary mutual assistance exists; the restriction means reliance on God for grave matters beyond human help.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r47.anchor: والحصر المستفاد من التقديم في قوله :  { وإياك نستعين } حصر ادعائي للمبالغة لعدم الاعتداد بالاستعانات المتعارفة

IBNASHUR:1:5/r48.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r48.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:5/r48.claim: The two restrictions indirectly rebuke polytheists: some worshipped other gods while forgetting God, including Sabaʾ and groups among Persians, Egyptians, and peoples of Sudan.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r48.anchor: ويفيد هذا القصر فيهما التعريض بالمشركين الذين يعبدون غير الله ويستعينون بغيره لأنهم كانوا فريقين منهم من عبد

IBNASHUR:1:5/r49.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r49.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:5/r49.claim: Many Arabs combined worship of God with idols or celestial bodies; named tribes worshipped the sun, moon, Sirius, Aldebaran, or Pleiades, treating these beings as intermediaries and thus as sources of help.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r49.anchor: ومن المشركين من أشرك مع عبادة الله عبادة غيره وهذا حال معظم العرب ممن عبد الأصنام أو عبد الكواكب

IBNASHUR:1:5/r50.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r50.speaker: السلكوتي
IBNASHUR:1:5/r50.claim: Al-Salkuti notes that true restriction cannot directly refute an opposing belief, since its literal meaning is true; the rebuke of polytheists therefore works by implication (taʿrīḍ).
IBNASHUR:1:5/r50.anchor: لأن القصر الحقيقي لا يصلح أن يكون لرد الاعتقاد إلا تعريضا لأن معناه حاصل على الحقيقة كما أشار إليه السلكوتي

IBNASHUR:1:5/r51.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r51.speaker: الشيخ الجد
IBNASHUR:1:5/r51.claim: In his note on the Ibn ʿAbbas hadith, the author’s grandfather says its lack of an explicit restrictive form hints that asking belongs only to the all-powerful, all-knowing God; rhetoricians can omit restriction when exclusivity is intrinsic.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r51.anchor: قلت قد ذكر الشيخ الجد قدس الله روحه في تعليقه على هذا الحديث أن ترك طريقة القصر إيماء إلى أن المقام لا يقبل الشركة

IBNASHUR:1:5/r52.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r52.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR:1:5/r52.claim: The Prophet teaches Ibn ʿAbbas: ‘If you ask, ask God; if you seek help, seek God’; the wording has no explicit object-fronting restriction.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r52.anchor: فإن قلت كيف أمرنا بأن لا نعبد إلا الله ولا نستعين إلا به حسبما تشير إليه هذه الآية ،  وقد ورد في الصحيح أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لما علَّم عبد الله بن عباس قال له «  إذا سألت فاسأل الله وإذا استعنت فاستعن بالله  »

IBNASHUR:1:5/r53.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r53.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:5/r53.claim: The hadith teaches an already established Muslim, so it can assume exclusivity; this sūrah opens revelation and legislation and rebukes shirk, making explicit restriction apt, while its conditional wording also implies disavowal of divination at idols.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r53.anchor: وأقول تقفية على أثره إن مقام الحديث غير مقام الآية فمقام الحديث مقام تعليم خاص لمن نشأ وشب

IBNASHUR:1:5/r54.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r54.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:5/r54.claim: The plural ‘we’ in worship and seeking help includes the reciter with the community of believers; it displays their collective strength to polytheists and makes their shared praise more eloquent than an individual’s testimony.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r54.anchor: وضميرا { نعبد ونَستعين } يعودان إلى تالي السورة ذاكراً معه جماعة المؤمنين . وفي العدول عن ضمير الواحد

IBNASHUR:1:5/r55.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r55.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:5/r55.claim: The plural worshippers’ testimony itself praises God: the speaker moving from praise to intimate address takes every chance to show that many recognize the praised one’s merit.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r55.anchor: ولأنه أبلغ في الثناء من أعبد وأستعين لئلا تخلو المناجاة عن ثناء أيضا بأن المحمود المعبود المستعان

IBNASHUR:1:5/r56.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r56.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:5/r56.claim: Al-Nabigha’s elegy lists Ghassan, Turks, and other peoples hoping for al-Nuʿman’s return to imply his greatness and the size of his realm, like the communal praise here.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r56.anchor: وقريب من هذا قول النابغة في رثاء النعمان بن الحارث الغساني :  قعوداً له غسان يرجون أوبة

IBNASHUR:1:5/r57.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r57.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:5/r57.claim: Worship precedes seeking help because it draws the servant near God, is the worshipper’s own commitment before a request for aid, is presupposed by divine assistance, and is itself among the acts aided.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r57.anchor: ووجهه تقديم قوله { إياك نعبد } على قوله :  { وإياك نستعين } أن العبادة تقرُّب للخالق تعالى فهي أجدر بالتقديم

IBNASHUR:1:5/r58.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r58.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:5/r58.claim: The order also preserves the sūrah’s cadence, whose endings use the same or a nearby consonant of the tongue’s articulation.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r58.anchor: وقد حصل من ذلك التقديم أيضا إيفاء حق فواصل السورة المبنية على الحرف الساكن المتماثل

IBNASHUR:1:5/r59.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r59.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:5/r59.claim: Repeating ‘You’ before seeking help marks a different restriction from worship: people may assist one another, as 5:2 commands, but only God is relied on for grave matters and counts as true aid.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r59.anchor: وأعيد لفظ { إياك } في الاستعانة دون أن يعطف فعل { نستعين } على { نعبد } مع أنهما مقصودان جميعاً

IBNASHUR:1:5/r60.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r60.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:5/r60.claim: The author’s note adds that ‘servitude’ can be more emphatic than ‘worship’ because the relational formation is intensified by the nisba suffix, as in asḥamī versus asḥam.
IBNASHUR:1:5/r60.anchor: كأنهم اصطلحوا على أن العبودية أبلغ من العبادة لما فيها من النسب لأن الأوصاف التي تلحق ياء النسب

IBNASHUR:1:5/r61.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:5/r61.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:5/r61.claim: The author’s note adds that gratitude benefits its recipient as praise adorns the praised one, citing al-Nabigha’s line ‘I thanked you for the bounty.’
IBNASHUR:1:5/r61.anchor: واعلم أن كون الشكر يشتمل على حظ للمشكور قد تقرر في بحث الحمد إذ بينا أن الحمد والشكر

IBNHIBBAN:776/r1.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:776/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNHIBBAN:776/r1.claim: The Prophet calls a prayer without reciting the Fatiha deficient and incomplete.
IBNHIBBAN:776/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، قال: «من صلى صلاة

IBNHIBBAN:776/r2.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:776/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNHIBBAN:776/r2.claim: When a follower says he sometimes prays behind the imam, Abu Hurayra tells him to recite the Fatiha silently to himself.
IBNHIBBAN:776/r2.anchor: فقال رجل: يا أبا هريرة إني أحيانا أكون وراء الإمام، قال: فغمز ذراعي

IBNHIBBAN:776/r3.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:776/r3.speaker: الله تبارك وتعالى
IBNHIBBAN:776/r3.claim: The hadith divides the prayer between God and the servant: this verse is their shared exchange, while the remaining request for guidance belongs to the servant.
IBNHIBBAN:776/r3.anchor: قال الله تبارك وتعالى: قسمت الصلاة بيني وبين عبادي نصفين، فنصفها لعبدي ونصفها لي

IBNHIBBAN:1784/r1.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:1784/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNHIBBAN:1784/r1.claim: The Prophet calls a prayer without Umm al-Qur'an deficient and incomplete.
IBNHIBBAN:1784/r1.anchor: سمعت أبا هريرة يقول: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "من صلى صلاة لم يقرأ فيها بأم القرآن

IBNHIBBAN:1784/r2.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:1784/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNHIBBAN:1784/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra advises the man who prays behind an imam to recite the Fatiha quietly to himself.
IBNHIBBAN:1784/r2.anchor: فقلت: يا أبا هريرة إني أحيانا أكون وراء الإمام قال: فغمز ذراعي وقال: اقرأ بها يا فارسي

IBNHIBBAN:1784/r3.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:1784/r3.speaker: الله جل وعلا
IBNHIBBAN:1784/r3.claim: God describes the prayer as divided between Him and the servant; the quoted verse is the shared portion, and the servant receives what follows as a request.
IBNHIBBAN:1784/r3.anchor: "قال الله جل وعلا: قسمت الصلاة بيني وبين عبدي نصفين

IBNHIBBAN:1795/r1.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:1795/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNHIBBAN:1795/r1.claim: The Prophet says that a prayer without Umm al-Qur'an is deficient.
IBNHIBBAN:1795/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "من صلى صلاة لم يقرأ فيها بأم القرآن فهي خداج

IBNHIBBAN:1795/r2.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:1795/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNHIBBAN:1795/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra tells a follower behind the imam to recite the Fatiha inwardly.
IBNHIBBAN:1795/r2.anchor: قلت: يا أبا هريرة إني أحيانا أكون وراء الإمام قال: يا ابن الفارسي اقرأ بها في نفسك

IBNHIBBAN:1795/r3.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:1795/r3.speaker: الله تبارك وتعالى
IBNHIBBAN:1795/r3.claim: The hadith divides the prayer between God and the servant, placing this verse between them and the rest of the sura among the servant's requests.
IBNHIBBAN:1795/r3.anchor: قال الله تبارك وتعالى: قسمت الصلاة بيني وبين عبدي نصفين فنصفها لي ونصفها لعبدي ولعبدي ما شاء

IBNMAJAH:3784/r1.author: IBNMAJAH
IBNMAJAH:3784/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNMAJAH:3784/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra transmits a divine report that al-Fatiha is divided between God and servant: this middle declaration belongs to both, and the servant receives what he asks.
IBNMAJAH:3784/r1.anchor: عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، قَالَ سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ـ صلى الله عليه وسلم ـ يَقُولُ ‏"‏ قَالَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ قَسَمْتُ الصَّلاَةَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَ عَبْدِي شَطْرَيْنِ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r16.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r16.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r16.claim: For Ibn Ashur, glossing iyyaka naʿbudu merely as we worship You misses its full intent because fronting the object signals exclusivity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r16.anchor: فمن يفسر قوله تعالى ) إياك نعبد ( بإنا نعبدك لم يطلع على تمام المراد

IBNATIYYA:1:5/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r1.claim: The believer's declaration confesses God's lordship, expresses humility, and affirms worship of God, unlike people who worship idols.
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r1.anchor: نطق المؤمن به إقرار بالربوبية وتذلل وتحقيق لعبادة الله ،   إذ سائر الناس يعبدون سواه من أصنام وغير ذلك

IBNATIYYA:1:5/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r2.claim: The object is placed before the verb for emphasis and importance, following the Arabic tendency to put what matters first.
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r2.anchor: وقدم المفعول على الفعل اهتماماً( {[66]} ) ،   وشأن العرب تقديم الأهم

IBNATIYYA:1:5/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r3.claim: An anecdote illustrates fronting what matters: an abused man answers “I turn away from you” after being told “You are whom I mean.”
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r3.anchor: فقال له السابُّ : «إياك أعني » فقال الآخر : «وعنكَ أُعرِضُ » فقدَّما الأهم

IBNATIYYA:1:5/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r4.speaker: الفضل الرقاشي
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r4.claim: Al-Faḍl al-Raqāshī reads ayyaka with fatḥa on the hamza, a well-known dialect form.
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r4.anchor: وقرأ الفضل الرقاشي( {[67]} ) : «أياك » بفتح الهمزة ،   وهي لغة مشهورة

IBNATIYYA:1:5/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r5.speaker: عمرو بن فائد
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r5.claim: ʿAmr ibn Fāʾid reads īyāka with a light yāʾ, avoiding the heavy doubled yāʾ after kasra.
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r5.anchor: وقرأ عمرو بن فائد : «إيَاك » بكسر الهمزة وتخفيف الياء ،   وذاك أنه كره تضعيف الياء

IBNATIYYA:1:5/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r6.speaker: أبو السوار الغنوي
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r6.claim: Abū al-Sawwār al-Ghanawī reads hayyāka naʿbudu and hayyāka nastaʿīnu with initial hāʾ, an Arabic dialect.
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r6.anchor: وقرأ أبو السوار الغنوي( {[69]} ) : «هيّاك نعبد وهيّاك نستعين » بالهاء ،   وهي لغة

IBNATIYYA:1:5/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r7.speaker: الخليل
