IBNATIYYA:1:5/r7.claim: Al-Khalīl analyzes iyā as a pronoun with the following suffix added for clarification, not to make it definite.
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r7.anchor: فقال الخليل : إيّا اسم مضمر أضيف إلى ما بعده للبيان لا للتعريف

IBNATIYYA:1:5/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r8.speaker: المبرد
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r8.claim: Al-Mubarrad calls iyā an indefinite, ambiguous noun specified by the following suffix rather than made definite.
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r8.anchor: وقال المبرد : إيّا اسم مبهم أضيف للتخصيص لا للتعريف

IBNATIYYA:1:5/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r9.speaker: بعض الكوفيين
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r9.claim: Some Kufan grammarians treat iyāka as a single pronoun, uniquely among pronouns changing its ending.
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r9.anchor: وحكي ابن كيسان عن بعض الكوفيين أنّ { إيّاك } بكماله اسم مضمر ،   ولا يعرف اسم مضمر يتغير آخره غيره

IBNATIYYA:1:5/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r10.speaker: بعضهم
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r10.claim: Another analysis treats kāf, hāʾ, and yāʾ as the pronouns, unable to stand alone; iyā supports them before verbs while suffixes attach directly after them.
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r10.anchor: وحكي عن بعضهم أنه قال : الكاف والهاء والياء هي الاسم المضمر ،   لكنها لا تقوم بأنفسها ولا تكون إلا متصلات

IBNATIYYA:1:5/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r11.speaker: بعضهم
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r11.claim: A further view takes iyā as an ambiguous accusative pronoun base; its suffixes distinguish addressee, absent person, and speaker and have no syntactic case of their own.
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r11.anchor: وحكي عن بعضهم أن أيا اسم مبهم يكنى به عن المنصوب ،   وزيدت الكاف والياء والهاء تفرقة بين المخاطب والغائب والمتكلم

IBNATIYYA:1:5/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r12.claim: Naʿbudu means to uphold the law and commands with humility and submission; maʿbad likewise names a smoothed path or camel.
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r12.anchor: و { نعبد } معناه نقيم الشرع والأوامر مع تذلل واستكانة ،   والطريق المذلل يقال له معبد

IBNATIYYA:1:5/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r13.speaker: طرفة
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r13.claim: Ṭarafa's phrase “over a smoothed path” supports the lexical sense of maʿbad as something made smooth.
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r13.anchor:
وقال طرفة : [ الطويل ] .
تباري عتاق الناجيات وأتبعت  .   .   .   وظيفاً

IBNATIYYA:1:5/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r14.claim: Iyyāka is repeated because the two different verbs each need emphasis and focused attention.
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r14.anchor: وتكررت { إياك } بحسب اختلاف الفعلين ،   فاحتاج كل واحد منهما إلى تأكيد واهتمام

IBNATIYYA:1:5/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r15.claim: Nastaʿīnu means asking God for help in all affairs; the declaration as a whole disavows idols.
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r15.anchor: معناه نطلب العون منك في جميع أمورنا ،   وهذا كله تبرؤ( {[73]} ) من الأصنام

IBNATIYYA:1:5/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r16.speaker: الأعمش وابن وثاب والنخعي
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r16.claim: Al-Aʿmash, Ibn Waththāb, and al-Nakhaʿī read wa-nistaʿīnu with kasra on the initial nūn, a dialect of some Qurashīs.
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r16.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش وابن وثاب والنخعي : «ونستعين » بكسر النون ،   وهي لغة لبعض قريش

IBNATIYYA:1:5/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r17.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r17.claim: The kasra dialect affects nūn, tāʾ, and hamza, not third-person yāʾ; it occurs with prefixed forms and certain Form I verbs, including hollow verbs.
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r17.anchor: ولا يقولونها في ياء الغائب وإنما ذلك في كل فعل سمي فاعله فيه زوائد أو فيما يأتي من الثلاثي

IBNATIYYA:1:5/r18.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r18.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r18.claim: In nastaʿīnu, the vowel of the original wāw moves to ʿayn, and the wāw becomes yāʾ because the preceding consonant has kasra.
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r18.anchor: و { نستعين } أصله نستعون نقلت حركة الواو إلى العين وقلبت ياء لانكسار ما قبلها

IBNATIYYA:1:5/r19.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r19.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r19.claim: The verbal noun istiʿāna derives from istiʿwānan: the wāw's vowel moves to ʿayn, then the wāw becomes alif after fatḥa.
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r19.anchor: والمصدر استعانة أصله استعواناً نقلت حركة الواو إلى العين فلما انفتح ما قبلها وهي في نية الحركة انقلبت ألفاً

IBNATIYYA:1:5/r20.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r20.speaker: بعضهم
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r20.claim: One analysis deletes the second of the two adjacent quiescent alifs because it was added for grammatical meaning and is more expendable.
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r20.anchor: فقيل حذفت الأولى لأن الثانية مجلوبة لمعنى ،   فهي أولى بالبقاء

IBNATIYYA:1:5/r21.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r21.speaker: بعضهم
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r21.claim: Another analysis deletes the first alif because it is original and more deserving of preservation; the final hāʾ compensates for the deletion.
IBNATIYYA:1:5/r21.anchor: وقيل حذفت الثانية لأن الأولى أصلية فهي أولى بالبقاء ،   ثم لزمت الهاء عوضاً من المحذوف

MALIK:187/r1.author: MALIK
MALIK:187/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
MALIK:187/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that the Prophet calls prayer without Umm al-Qur’an deficient and tells a questioner to recite it silently behind the imam.
MALIK:187/r1.anchor: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول

MALIK:187/r2.author: MALIK
MALIK:187/r2.speaker: الله تبارك وتعالى
MALIK:187/r2.claim: In the qudsi report, this verse is the shared exchange between God and the servant, who receives what he asks.
MALIK:187/r2.anchor: فهذه الآية بيني وبين عبدي ولعبدي ما سأل

MUSLIM:878/r1.author: MUSLIM
MUSLIM:878/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MUSLIM:878/r1.claim: The Prophet calls a prayer without Umm al-Qurʾān deficient and incomplete; when asked about praying behind an imam, Abu Hurayra tells them to recite it quietly.
MUSLIM:878/r1.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

MUSLIM:878/r2.author: MUSLIM
MUSLIM:878/r2.speaker: الله تعالى
MUSLIM:878/r2.claim: In the divine report, Allah says the central declaration of worship and request for help belongs jointly to Him and the servant, who receives what he asks.
MUSLIM:878/r2.anchor: قال الله تعالى قسمت الصلاة بيني وبين عبدي نصفين ولعبدي ما سأل

MUSNAD-AHMAD:7291/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:7291/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي
MUSNAD-AHMAD:7291/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra relates that the Prophet called a prayer without al-Fatiha defective and told a Persian worshipper to recite it.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:7291/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة: أيما صلاة لا يقرأ فيها بفاتحة الكتاب، فهي خداج

MUSNAD-AHMAD:7291/r2.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:7291/r2.speaker: النبي
MUSNAD-AHMAD:7291/r2.claim: In a divine report, God says the prayer is divided between Him and the servant; this verse is shared, and the servant receives what he asks in the following supplication.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:7291/r2.anchor: فإني سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: " قال الله عز وجل: قسمت الصلاة بيني وبين عبدي

MUSNAD-AHMAD:7836/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:7836/r1.speaker: النبي
MUSNAD-AHMAD:7836/r1.claim: God calls the opening praises acknowledgments from the servant, makes this verse the shared portion, and grants the servant's requests in the closing supplication.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:7836/r1.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " اقرءوا، يقول: فيقول العبد: {الحمد لله رب العالمين}

MUSNAD-AHMAD:7836/r2.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:7836/r2.speaker: النبي
MUSNAD-AHMAD:7836/r2.claim: The Prophet calls prayer without al-Fatiha incomplete; Abu Hurayra tells a worshipper behind the imam to recite it inwardly.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:7836/r2.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " من صلى صلاة لم يقرأ فيها بأم القرآن، فهي خداج

MUSNAD-AHMAD:9932/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:9932/r1.speaker: النبي
MUSNAD-AHMAD:9932/r1.claim: The divine report assigns the opening praise to God, this verse to both God and servant, and the requests in the final verses to the servant.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:9932/r1.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " اقرءوا: يقول العبد: {الحمد لله رب العالمين}

MUSNAD-AHMAD:9932/r2.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:9932/r2.speaker: النبي
MUSNAD-AHMAD:9932/r2.claim: The Prophet says prayer without al-Fatiha is deficient; Abu Hurayra instructs a follower behind the imam to recite it to himself.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:9932/r2.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " من صلى صلاة لم يقرأ فيها بأم القرآن فهي خداج

NASAI:909/r1.author: NASAI
NASAI:909/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
NASAI:909/r1.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that the Prophet calls prayer without Umm al-Qurʾān deficient and tells a Persian worshipper to recite it silently, even behind the imam.
NASAI:909/r1.anchor: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا هُرَيْرَةَ، يَقُولُ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم

NASAI:909/r2.author: NASAI
NASAI:909/r2.speaker: رسول الله
NASAI:909/r2.claim: Abū Hurayra transmits a qudsī report in which God divides al-Fātiḥa between Himself and the servant; the declaration of worship and plea for help is shared, and God grants what is asked.
NASAI:909/r2.anchor: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم

KASHSHAF:1:5/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:5/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:1:5/r1.claim: Iya is a separate accusative pronoun; suffixes mark address, absence, and speaker without independent syntactic position.
KASHSHAF:1:5/r1.anchor: واللواحق التي تلحقه من الكاف والهاء والياء

KASHSHAF:1:5/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:5/r2.speaker: الأخفش والمحققون
KASHSHAF:1:5/r2.claim: Al-Akhfash and careful grammarians hold that suffixes are not independent pronouns, like the kاف in araʾaytaka.

KASHSHAF:1:5/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:5/r3.speaker: الخليل وبعض العرب
KASHSHAF:1:5/r3.claim: Al-Khalil reports an anomalous expression using iya without a suffix, which al-Zamakhshari says should not be relied on.
KASHSHAF:1:5/r3.anchor: ما حكاه الخليل عن بعض العرب

KASHSHAF:1:5/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:5/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:1:5/r4.claim: Fronting the object gives exclusive force, as in 39:64 and 6:164.
KASHSHAF:1:5/r4.anchor: وتقديم المفعول لقصد الاختصاص ، كقوله تعالى : { قل أفغير الله تأمروني أعبد }

KASHSHAF:1:5/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:5/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:1:5/r5.claim: The speakers devote worship and request help exclusively to God, seeking neither from anyone else.

KASHSHAF:1:5/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:5/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:1:5/r6.claim: A reading weakens the yā in iyaaka.

KASHSHAF:1:5/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:5/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:1:5/r7.claim: Another reading has fatḥa on the hamza and a geminated yā.

KASHSHAF:1:5/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:5/r8.speaker: طفيل الغنوي
KASHSHAF:1:5/r8.claim: A reading changes initial hamza to hāʾ; Tufayl al-Ghanawi's verse witnesses hiyyaka.
KASHSHAF:1:5/r8.anchor: وهياك بقلب الهمزة هاء . قال طفيل الغنوي

KASHSHAF:1:5/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:5/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:1:5/r9.claim: Worship is utmost submission and abasement; related ʿabada describes thick, strongly woven cloth.

KASHSHAF:1:5/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:5/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:1:5/r10.claim: Worship is reserved for God because He gives the greatest blessings and deserves highest submission.
KASHSHAF:1:5/r10.anchor: لأنه مولى أعظم النعم فكان حقيقا بأقصى غاية الخضوع

KASHSHAF:1:5/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:5/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:1:5/r11.claim: The shift from third-person to address is iltifat; the Quran also shifts in 10:22 and 35:9.
KASHSHAF:1:5/r11.anchor: هذا يسمى الالتفات في علم البيان قد يكون من الغيبة إلى الخطاب

KASHSHAF:1:5/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:5/r12.speaker: امرؤ القيس
KASHSHAF:1:5/r12.claim: Imru al-Qays shifts perspective three times over three lines, illustrating varied discourse mode.
KASHSHAF:1:5/r12.anchor: وقد التفت امرؤ القيس ثلاث التفاتات في ثلاثة أبيات

KASHSHAF:1:5/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:5/r13.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:1:5/r13.claim: Changing discourse mode refreshes attention and awakens listening; this placement has additional benefits.
KASHSHAF:1:5/r13.anchor: ولأن الكلام إذا نقل من أسلوب إلى أسلوب

KASHSHAF:1:5/r14.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:5/r14.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:1:5/r14.claim: After praising God and listing His attributes, the speech directly addresses the one worthy of worship and help.
KASHSHAF:1:5/r14.anchor: تعلق العلم بمعلوم عظيم الشأن حقيق بالثناء

KASHSHAF:1:5/r15.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:5/r15.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:1:5/r15.claim: Worship and help are paired to join what servants offer their Lord with what they request from Him.
KASHSHAF:1:5/r15.anchor: ليجمع بين ما يتقرب به العباد إلى ربهم وبين ما يطلبونه ويحتاجون إليه

KASHSHAF:1:5/r16.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:5/r16.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:1:5/r16.claim: Worship comes before asking for help because offering the means before the request merits a response.
KASHSHAF:1:5/r16.anchor: تقديم الوسيلة قبل طلب الحاجة ليستوجبوا الإجابة إليها

KASHSHAF:1:5/r17.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:5/r17.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:1:5/r17.claim: Seeking help is unqualified so it covers every matter in which help is needed.

KASHSHAF:1:5/r18.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:5/r18.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:1:5/r18.claim: Best is asking God and His enabling grace for help in worship; 1:6 specifies aid as guidance.
KASHSHAF:1:5/r18.anchor: والأحسن أن تراد الاستعانة به وبتوفيقه على أداء العبادة

KASHSHAF:1:5/r19.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:5/r19.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:1:5/r19.claim: The request for guidance explains what help is sought and coheres with the preceding words.
KASHSHAF:1:5/r19.anchor: ويكون قوله : { اهدنا } بيانا للمطلوب من المعونة

KASHSHAF:1:5/r20.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:5/r20.speaker: ابن حبيش
KASHSHAF:1:5/r20.claim: Ibn Hubaysh reads nastaʿinu with kasra on its initial nūn.
KASHSHAF:1:5/r20.anchor: وقرأ ابن حبيش :  "  نستعين  "  ، بكسر النون

TIRMIDHI:2953/r1.author: TIRMIDHI
TIRMIDHI:2953/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
TIRMIDHI:2953/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra transmits the Prophet’s ruling that a prayer without reciting the Opening is deficient, and tells one praying behind an imam to recite it silently to himself.
TIRMIDHI:2953/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

TIRMIDHI:2953/r2.author: TIRMIDHI
TIRMIDHI:2953/r2.speaker: الله تعالى
TIRMIDHI:2953/r2.claim: In the divine report the Opening is divided into halves: praise belongs to God, the central pledge of worship and seeking help is shared, and its closing requests belong to the worshipper, who receives what he asks.
TIRMIDHI:2953/r2.anchor: قال الله تعالى قسمت الصلاة بيني وبين عبدي نصفين فنصفها لي ونصفها لعبدي ولعبدي ما سأل

TIRMIDHI:2953/r3.author: TIRMIDHI
TIRMIDHI:2953/r3.speaker: أبو عيسى
TIRMIDHI:2953/r3.claim: Tirmidhi grades the report hasan; Abu Zurʿa says both transmission versions are sound.
TIRMIDHI:2953/r3.anchor: قال أبو عيسى هذا حديث حسن

MAWARDI:1:5/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:1:5/r1.speaker: الخليل
MAWARDI:1:5/r1.claim: Al-Khalil says the divine name is annexed to the pronoun kaf in iyyaka.
MAWARDI:1:5/r1.anchor: أن اسم الله تعالى مضاف إلى الكاف ،   وهذا قول الخليل

MAWARDI:1:5/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:1:5/r2.speaker: الأخفش
MAWARDI:1:5/r2.claim: Al-Akhfash takes iyyaka as a single pronoun for God, not an annexation, because a pronoun is not annexed.
MAWARDI:1:5/r2.anchor: أنها كلمة واحدة كُنِّيَ بها عن اسم الله تعالى ،   وليس فيها إضافة لأن المضمر لا يضاف ،   وهذا قول الأخفش

MAWARDI:1:5/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:1:5/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI:1:5/r3.claim: The clearest sense of worship is humility, the highest form of submission, owed only to God as giver of the greatest gifts such as life, reason, hearing, and sight.
MAWARDI:1:5/r3.anchor: أن العبادة الخضوع ،   ولا يستحقها إلا الله تعالى ،   لأنها أعلى مراتب الخضوع ،   فلا يستحقها إلا المنعم بأعظم النعم

MAWARDI:1:5/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:1:5/r4.speaker: unattributed
MAWARDI:1:5/r4.claim: A second interpretation takes worship to mean obedience.

MAWARDI:1:5/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:1:5/r5.speaker: unattributed
MAWARDI:1:5/r5.claim: A third interpretation takes worship to mean drawing near through obedience.

MAWARDI:1:5/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:1:5/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI:1:5/r6.claim: Humility is clearest because Christians worshipped Jesus without obeying him through worship, while the Prophet is obeyed but is not thereby worshipped.
MAWARDI:1:5/r6.anchor: لأن النصارى عبدت عيسى عليه السلام ،   ولم تطعه بالعبادة ،   والنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مطاع ،   وليس بمعبودٍ بالطاعة

NASAFI:1:1/r12.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:1:1/r12.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي
NASAFI:1:1/r12.claim: Abu Hurayra reports God’s dialogue dividing the Fatiha between Himself and the servant: praise, glorification, and exaltation belong to God; the worshipper’s request for guidance and the response to it belong to the servant, while worship and aid are shared.
NASAFI:1:1/r12.anchor: قال الله تعالى قسمت الصلاة أي الفاتحة بيني وبين عبدي نصفين ولعبدي ما سأل

NASAFI:1:5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:1:5/r1.speaker: الخليل وسيبويه
NASAFI:1:5/r1.claim: Al-Khalil and Sibawayh parse iyya as an independent pronoun; for Sibawayh the kaf is an uninflected address particle, while for al-Khalil it is an attached pronoun in annexation to iyya.
NASAFI:1:5/r1.anchor: «إيا » عند الخليل وسيبويه اسم مضمر ، والكاف حرف خطاب عند سيبويه ولا محل له من الإعراب

NASAFI:1:5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:1:5/r2.speaker: الكوفيون
NASAFI:1:5/r2.claim: The Kufans regard iyaka as a complete pronoun rather than dividing it into iyya and the kaf.
NASAFI:1:5/r2.anchor: وقال للكوفيون : إياك بكمالها اسم وتقديم المفعول لقصد الاختصاص

NASAFI:1:5/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:1:5/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI:1:5/r3.claim: Putting the object before the verb expresses exclusivity: worshippers devote worship, the utmost humility and submission, and their request for aid to God alone.
NASAFI:1:5/r3.anchor: والمعنى نخصك بالعبادة وهي أقصى غاية الخضوع والتذلل ، ونخصك بطلب المعونة

NASAFI:1:5/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:1:5/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI:1:5/r4.claim: The verse shifts from speaking about God in the third person to addressing Him directly after praise establishes His attributes and greatness; the worshipper turns to the uniquely worthy addressee to worship and seek help from no other.
NASAFI:1:5/r4.anchor: ومما اختص به هذا الموضع أنه لما ذكر الحقيق بالحمد والثناء ، وأجرى عليه تلك الصفات العظام

NASAFI:1:5/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:1:5/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI:1:5/r5.claim: Iltifat can shift from third person to address, address to third person, or third person to first person; Nasafi illustrates the pattern with shifts in Qur’an 10:22 and 35:9 and Imru’ al-Qays’s poem, where the speaker changes person across its three lines.
NASAFI:1:5/r5.anchor: وهو قد يكون من الغيبة إلى الخطاب ومن الخطاب إلى الغيبة ومن الغيبة إلى التكلم

NASAFI:1:5/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:1:5/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI:1:5/r6.claim: Arabs favor shifts of style because they engage listeners, renew attention, and make listening more pleasurable; particular placements also carry subtleties recognized by expert scholars.
NASAFI:1:5/r6.anchor: والعرب يستكثرون منه ويرون الكلام إذا انتقل من أسلوب إلى أسلوب

NASAFI:1:5/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:1:5/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI:1:5/r7.claim: Worship precedes asking for aid either because presenting a means before asking for a need makes a response likelier, or to preserve the verse order, as with al-Rahman’s precedence despite the greater rhetorical force of the other name.
NASAFI:1:5/r7.anchor: وقدمت العبادة على الاستعانة لأن تقديم الوسيلة قبل طلب الحاجة أقرب إلى الإجابة

NASAFI:1:5/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:1:5/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI:1:5/r8.claim: The unqualified request for aid embraces every kind of help; alternatively, it asks God’s help and enabling for worship, with ‘guide us’ specifying the requested assistance.
NASAFI:1:5/r8.anchor: ويكون قوله : «اهدنا » بيانا للمطلوب من المعونة كأنه قيل : كيف أعينكم

QURTUBI:1:2/r43.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:2/r43.speaker: author
QURTUBI:1:2/r43.claim: Qurtubi treats the implied command to say as a common Arabic ellipsis whose context supplies the omitted words, and says the same construction applies to the later address, as though it said, Say, You alone we worship.
QURTUBI:1:2/r43.anchor: وعلى هذا يجيء قولوا إياك . وهذا من حذف العرب ما يدل ظاهر الكلام عليه

QURTUBI:1:5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:5/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:1:5/r1.claim: The wording shifts from third-person report and praise of God to direct address, an iltifāt; Qurtubi compares the shift in 76:21 and its reverse in 10:22.
QURTUBI:1:5/r1.anchor: رجع من الغيبة إلى الخطاب على التلوين ؛ لأن من أول السورة إلى ههنا خبرا عن الله تعالى وثناء عليه

QURTUBI:1:5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:5/r2.speaker: الهروي
QURTUBI:1:5/r2.claim: Naʿbud means we obey; worship is obedience joined with humility. Al-Harawī compares a trodden, smoothed road called muʿabbad.
QURTUBI:1:5/r2.anchor: و " نعبد " معناه نطيع والعبادة الطاعة والتذلل . وطريق معبد إذا كان مذللا للسالكين قاله الهروي

QURTUBI:1:5/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:5/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI:1:5/r3.claim: A responsible speaker’s recitation affirms God’s lordship and realizes worship of God, since other people worship idols and other objects instead.
QURTUBI:1:5/r3.anchor: ونطق المكلف به إقرار بالربوبية وتحقيق لعبادة الله تعالى ؛ إذ سائر الناس يعبدون سواه من أصنام

QURTUBI:1:5/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:5/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI:1:5/r4.claim: We seek God’s help, support, and enabling success.
QURTUBI:1:5/r4.anchor: " وإياك نستعين " أي نطلب العون والتأييد والتوفيق

QURTUBI:1:5/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:5/r5.speaker: أبو حفص الفرغاني
QURTUBI:1:5/r5.claim: Al-Sulamī transmits from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shādhān, from Abū Ḥafṣ al-Farghānī, that affirming this verse frees one from both determinism and Qadarism.
QURTUBI:1:5/r5.anchor: قال السلمي في حقائقه : سمعت محمد بن عبدالله بن شاذان يقول : سمعت أبا حفص الفرغاني يقول : من أقر

QURTUBI:1:5/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:5/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI:1:5/r6.claim: The object is brought before the verb because Arabs place what matters first; this also puts the worshiped before mention of the worshiper and worship, following the Qur’anic wording.
QURTUBI:1:5/r6.anchor: قيل له : قدم اهتماما ، وشأن العرب تقديم الأهم

QURTUBI:1:5/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:5/r7.speaker: أعرابي
QURTUBI:1:5/r7.claim: A Bedouin exchange illustrates foregrounding what matters: when a man said You are the one I mean, the other replied that he was turning away from him.
QURTUBI:1:5/r7.anchor: يذكر أن أعرابيا سب آخر فأعرض المسبوب عنه ، فقال له الساب : إياك أعني

QURTUBI:1:5/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:5/r8.speaker: العجاج
QURTUBI:1:5/r8.claim: Al-ʿAjjāj’s line uses the fronted object in I call upon You, illustrating the Qur’anic word order.
QURTUBI:1:5/r8.anchor: وقال العجاج : إياك أدعو فتقبل مَلَقي *** واغفر خطاياي وكثّر ورِقي

QURTUBI:1:5/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:5/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI:1:5/r9.claim: The poetic phrase ilayka ḥattā balaghat iyyāka is anomalous and cannot serve as a model; wariq with kasra means dirhams and with fatḥa means wealth.
QURTUBI:1:5/r9.anchor: وأما قول الشاعر{[98]} : إليك حتى بلغت إياكا فشاذ لا يقاس عليه . والورق بكسر الراء من الدراهم

QURTUBI:1:5/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:5/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI:1:5/r10.claim: Repeating iyyāka prevents anyone from supposing that while worship is directed to God, help is sought from someone else.
QURTUBI:1:5/r10.anchor: وكرر الاسم لئلا يتوهم إياك نعبد ونستعين غيرك

QURTUBI:1:5/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:5/r11.speaker: الجمهور من القراء والعلماء
QURTUBI:1:5/r11.claim: The majority of readers and scholars pronounce the yāʾ in both instances of iyyāka with a shadda.
QURTUBI:1:5/r11.anchor: الجمهور من القراء والعلماء على شد الياء من " إياك " في الموضعين

QURTUBI:1:5/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:5/r12.speaker: عمرو بن فائد
QURTUBI:1:5/r12.claim: ʿAmr ibn Fāʾid reads iyyāka with kasra on the hamza and a light yāʾ to avoid doubling a yāʾ after kasra; Qurtubi rejects it because it would mean your sun or its light.
QURTUBI:1:5/r12.anchor: وقرأ عمرو بن فائد : " إياك " بكسر الهمزة وتخفيف الياء ، وذلك أنه كره تضعيف الياء

QURTUBI:1:5/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:5/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI:1:5/r13.claim: Īāya means the sun’s light or its halo-like ring; a verse attributed to Ṭarafa describes the sun’s light on a tooth, and dropping the final hāʾ lengthens the word.
QURTUBI:1:5/r13.anchor: وقال{[99]} : سقته إِيَاةُ الشمس إلا لِثَاتِه

QURTUBI:1:5/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:5/r14.speaker: الفضل الرقاشي
QURTUBI:1:5/r14.claim: Al-Faḍl al-Raqāshī reads iyyāka with fatḥa on the hamza, which Qurtubi calls a familiar dialect.
QURTUBI:1:5/r14.anchor: وقرأ الفضل الرقاشي : " أياك " ( بفتح الهمزة ) وهي لغة مشهورة

QURTUBI:1:5/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:5/r15.speaker: أبو السوار الغنوي
QURTUBI:1:5/r15.claim: Abū al-Sawwār al-Ghanawī reads hiyyāka in both places as a dialect, citing a line of verse.
QURTUBI:1:5/r15.anchor: وقرأ أبو السوار الغنوي : " هياك " في الموضعين وهي لغة قال : فهياك والأمر الذي

QURTUBI:1:5/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:5/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI:1:5/r16.claim: The clause wa-iyyāka nastaʿīn is coordinated with the preceding clause.
QURTUBI:1:5/r16.anchor: قوله تعالى : " وإياك نستعين " عطف جملة على جملة

QURTUBI:1:5/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:5/r17.speaker: يحيى بن وثاب والأعمش
QURTUBI:1:5/r17.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb and al-Aʿmash read nistaʿīn with kasra on the nūn, a dialect of Tamīm, Asad, Qays, and Rabīʿa that signals derivation from istaʿāna.
QURTUBI:1:5/r17.anchor: وقرأ يحيى بن وثاب والأعمش : " نِستعين " بكسر النون وهي لغة تميم وأسد وقيس وربيعة

QURTUBI:1:5/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:5/r18.speaker: author
QURTUBI:1:5/r18.claim: The form nastaʿīn derives from nastaʿwinu: the vowel of wāw transfers to ʿayn and turns to yāʾ; the verbal noun derives from istaʿwana, where transferred wāw becomes alif and one of two meeting alifs is deleted, with disagreement over which, while tāʾ compensates.
QURTUBI:1:5/r18.anchor: وأصل " نستعين " نستعون قلبت حركة الواو إلى العين فصارت ياء ، والمصدر استعانة والأصل استعوان

RAZI:1:1/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:1:1/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:1:1/r1.claim: Razi sketches the sūra’s sequence: seek refuge from sins, begin good works in God’s name, praise and recognize his lordship and mercy, heed judgment, worship and seek help, ask guidance, and avoid ignorance and error.
RAZI:1:1/r1.anchor: بسم الله الرحمان الرحيم } نشرع في أداء كل الخيرات والمأمورات

RAZI:1:5/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:1:5/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:1:5/r1.claim: Worship is performing an act that has been commanded, out of reverence for the commander.
RAZI:1:5/r1.anchor: العبادة عبارة عن الإتيان بالفعل المأمور به على سبيل التعظيم للآمر

RAZI:1:5/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:1:5/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:1:5/r2.claim: Worship requires proving that the world has one God, able to do all possible things, knowing all knowable things, and free of need; He commands and forbids, so creatures must obey and submit.
RAZI:1:5/r2.anchor: قادرا على مقدورات لا نهاية لها ،   عالما بمعلومات لا نهاية لها ،   غنيا عن كل الحاجات

RAZI:1:5/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:1:5/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:1:5/r3.claim: To fulfill “You alone we worship,” one must then detail all commands and prohibitions; the religious law books cover the obligations of the present dispensation.
RAZI:1:5/r3.anchor: لابد من تفصيل أقسام تلك التكاليف ،   وبيان أنواع تلك الأوامر والنواهي

RAZI:1:5/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:1:5/r4.speaker: author
RAZI:1:5/r4.claim: The obligations encompassed by worship also include those God revealed through earlier prophets and those He assigned to the angels in heaven from their creation.
RAZI:1:5/r4.anchor: تكاليف الله تعالى بحسب الشرائع التي قد كان أنزلها الله تعالى على الأنبياء المتقدمين

RAZI:1:5/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:1:5/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:1:5/r5.claim: Legal works explain bodily duties, while duties of the heart are greater, weightier and more elevated; books of ethics and statecraft address them across different religions and peoples.
RAZI:1:5/r5.anchor: أما أقسام التكاليف الموجودة في أعمال القلوب فهي أكبر وأعظم وأجل

RAZI:1:5/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:1:5/r6.speaker: author
RAZI:1:5/r6.claim: All these fields of law, worship, ethics and governance fall under “You alone we worship”; the verse contains an ocean of questions that human reason reaches only slightly.
RAZI:1:5/r6.anchor: علم حينئذ أن المسائل التي اشتملت هذه الآية عليها كالبحر المحيط الذي لا تصل العقول والأفكار إلا إلى القليل منها
